2026-09-02 — Batch EP: THE SECOND RUNG IS THE SAME FIGHT, TWICE AS HARD

A measurement batch. Nothing was retuned, nothing was authored and nothing was ruled. Rung 2 does not scale enemy HEALTH at all any more — Batch EO's floor made rung 1's health and rung 2's health bit-identical — so the two rungs run fights of the same LENGTH, asking the same questions, and rung 2 simply doubles what a wrong answer costs. And the brief's headline figure was wrong: rung 2 with the rows rung 1 unlocks reads 22%, not the 7% Batch EO measured at n=30. Full working: docs/reports/EP.md.

§1 — WHAT RUNG 2 CHANGES, DERIVED FROM THE CODE. IT IS ATTACK, AND ALMOST NOTHING ELSE. Both spawn multipliers at both rungs across all three zones: the HEALTH row is bit-identical on 3 of 3 products and the ATTACK row doubles on 3 of 3. zone_base_mult_hp is _zone_ladder(slot) * maxf(difficulty_mult(), 1.0), and maxf returns rung 1's ×0.50 and rung 2's ×1.00 as the same 1.00. Config-diffed through Enemies.config, 1 of 21 enemy kinds differs between rung 1 and rung 2 — the end boss gains Sundering Decree — and 48 of 48 rung-1 abilities are field-for-field identical at rung 2 (delay, pressure, statuses, chances, cooldowns, damage). Enemy stability reads a flat 100 on all 21 kinds. Encounter counts, elite and boss composition, gold and loot read no rung at all. So the fights are the same length and the measurement says so: rounds to resolution 7.8 at rung 1 against 7.4 at rung 2 on the same loadout.

§1b — THE THIRD LEVER, AND IT INVERTS AT RUNG 3. The severity floor rises 2→3 between rungs 1 and 2, which does work: measured over 400 offers a rung, mean severity offered goes 2.83 → 3.29. But at rung 3 the floor of 4 leaves the gamble pool empty, both gambles fall through roll_offer's guard clause, and all three options are drawn from the whole twenty-modifier table — rung 3's bargains come out MILDER than rung 1's, at 2.31. The source comment claimed the high pool “holds seven and needs to supply two, so this is a guard, not a path”; it holds 8 / 4 / 0 and at rung 3 the guard is the path. The comment is corrected and nothing else is touched — rung 3 is not this brief's rung and no ruling is made on it.

§1c — WHERE THE RUNS ARE LOST: ATTRITION, NOT A WALL, AND NOT A BOSS. Four arms at --run 100 each, DOD_SIM_ROUTE=balanced: rung 1 with rows 1–3 completes 95% (±4.3); rung 2 with the same three rows completes 22% (±8.1); rung 2 untalented 3% (±3.3); rung 2 fully talented 90% (±5.9). The like-for-like pair is 95% → 22%, 73 points at 15.6 standard errors. Of the 78 wipes at rung 2 with rows 1–3, only 14 (18%) happen at a node the route cannot duck and 56 (72%) happen at ordinary fights in slots 10–15. No single fight is a wall — the worst printed per-fight win rate is 88% — and the run ends because a party takes about twenty-six fights and the per-fight loss rate is 3.9% at rung 2 against 0.19% at rung 1 on the same loadout, a factor of twenty-one. THE HARNESS'S OWN WIPE TABLE WOULD HAVE GIVEN THE OPPOSITE ANSWER: it bands tier >= 11 as “boss” and its per-tier table loops range(1, 12), but a zone has held SIXTEEN slots since Batch BK — so the band is six slots (reading 57 where the true zone-boss count is 7) and the table silently drops slots 12–16, which is where most wipes happen. The true distribution came from the per-run progress line, which carries the exact slot. Named as the next instrument, not fixed.

§1d — WHAT ROWS 1–3 ARE WORTH: NINETEEN POINTS AND A SEVENFOLD MULTIPLE. They move rung 2 from 3% to 22%, at 4.2 standard errors. And the arm is exactly the first-clear player rather than an approximation of one: Profile.award_zone_boss_points pays 1 point per ZONE boss and the end boss pays none, so clearing rung 1 banks exactly 3 points; rows 1–3 hold 9 cells at 1 point each; and DOD_SIM_ROWS=3 equips exactly 3 nodes. 22% is a FLOOR — a player who took three attempts banks nine points and can fill all nine cells, which this harness cannot express.

§2 — FIVE OPTIONS, COSTED, AND NONE TAKEN. Tune the damage scale (one number, teaches nothing new); make the Break gate rung-aware (small, and the measured risk is that pressure is unevenly distributed — the Sharpshooter carries 6 pressure-bearing draft cards and the Inquisitor carries none, so a Break gate would quietly become a spec gate); add rung-tagged abilities (zero code — Enemies.config already filters on rung — and it is the only option that changes the QUESTION rather than the price); change the encounter shape rather than the enemies (respecting BK §5's boss-band collision and compose's elite floor of 6); or make the severity twist that exists actually work. ×0.50 is still untouched and still unplayed.

§3 — THE 22% IS A BOT FLOOR. Eleven decisions the bot's policies exclude, each read off the code rather than the document: a fixed per-spec rotation identical on turn 1 and turn 30; drafted cards taken as the first usable one in slot order, and only once the rotation has fallen through to the basic attack; one item behaviour in battle (a Health Potion below 35% HP — bomb, revive, defense and mana items are never used at all) and no pre-emptive or offensive use; routing one tier ahead; shop rune picks that ignore build synergy; severity-extreme bargains that never read what the modifier does; first-in-pool ability picks; first-valid events; one talent lane of the thirty-six; and a timing bar rolled at 20% Perfect with no mitigation taken at all on defence.

§4 — THE FOUR RUNE ITEMS, RE-PRESENTED, AND TWO NEW FACTS. The floors are re-derived through Runes.eligible_ids rather than quoted and reproduce Batch EO: 65 authored, 12 retired, 53 offerable; drawable 9, spec-scoped 2, rare shelf 5, against 3 slots. (1) Every talent node the three Beastmaster runes mirror sits in rows 1–3 — Wild Communion (row 1), Absolute Devotion (row 3), Quick Whistle (row 1), Feral Momentum (row 2), The Wild Within (row 2) — so a 100g rare buys between an eighth and a third of a node a single rung-1 clear already opens. (2) The Bared Guard's cost is 80% refundable by one row-1 talent node: its −0.15 exactly cancels Defensive Stance's 0.85 mitigation (→1.00 on the nose), and sm_def_stance — Poise, row 1 — writes +0.12 back into the same subtraction. AND ONE CORRECTION TO BATCH EO: retiring it would NOT leave the Swordmaster “the only spec with no Scarred rune”. There are 17 Scarred runes — 2 universal, 3 class-scoped (there is no class:warrior one) and exactly 1 per spec — so the three Warrior specs draw 3 where the other nine draw 4, and retiring the Bared Guard leaves the Swordmaster 2. He would be the only spec with no spec-scoped Scarred rune and would hold the thinnest shelf in the game. Nothing authored, nothing retired, nothing ruled.

WHAT MOVED. One comment in scripts/run_state.gd — a comment-stripped diff of that file reads 1429 code lines before and after and zero differences, and the instrument was armed on a swallowed code line and bit. docs/master.html gains the rung-2 health note and this batch's measurements; docs/state.md is rewritten; docs/reports/EP.md is the working. Batch EO's entry above is left exactly as it stands — its 7% is the honest record of what n=30 read, and superseding it here rather than editing it is what a changelog is for.

2026-09-02 — Batch EO: THE STARTER RUNG TEACHES THE REAL GAME

The starter rung was ruled to keep the full game and soften only its blows. The measurement that decides the batch came first, and it made the batch small: rung 1 strips no abilities, no intents, no statuses and no Break gates — it only scales numbers. What it scaled was health as well as damage, and health is the fight's LENGTH, which is the only thing that lets an enemy ask a question. The rung now scales damage alone. Twelve of the sixteen runes the charter emptied are RETIRED — kept, and said to be kept. Full working: docs/reports/EO.md.

§1 — WHAT A RUNG ACTUALLY CHANGES, DERIVED FROM THE CODE RATHER THAN THE DOCUMENT. The ladder carries exactly four fields with a consequence — rung, mult, severity_floor, fixed_modifier — and every reader of each was swept. THE QUESTION THAT MATTERED: does rung 1 strip enemy ABILITIES, or only scale NUMBERS? It only scales numbers. Config-diffed at rung 1 against rung 3, 20 of the 21 enemy kinds are identical, and 48 of the 50 authored abilities carry no rung tag at all. The two that do are both on the end boss (Sundering Decree at 2, The Long Dark at 3) and are an authored ESCALATION added above rung 1, not a starter-rung gutting — Enemies.config defaults an untagged ability to rung 1. Encounter counts, elite and boss composition, gold and the relic ladder read no rung at all. Enemy stability, armor, speed, ability delays, statuses and pressure are flat at every rung.

§2 — THE RUNG SCALES DAMAGE, NOT HEALTH. The multiplier reached the game through one door and applied to max_hp AND attack together. Halving the health pool is not forgiveness — it ends the fight before the question is posed. Stability is a flat 100 and ab.pressure is flat, so the Break gate needs the SAME number of hero turns at rung 1 as at rung 3; the same half took the 2.5–4.0 telegraphs, the statuses worth cleansing and the turn of pressure an item is for. Run.zone_base_mult_hp floors the rung out of the health path. Rungs 2 and 3 are untouched BY CONSTRUCTION — maxf(mult, 1.0) returns ×1.00 and ×1.30 unchanged, proved bit-identical on 6 of 6 products, and the attack path is bit-identical on 9 of 9. THE VERIFICATION IS A LIVE UNTALENTED MEASUREMENT (DOD_SIM_ROWS=0, --run 30 a rung): completion 97% → 77% at rung 1, 0% → 0% at rungs 2 and 3, and a rung-1 trash fight ran 5.7 → 9.2 rounds, elite 5.5 → 8.5, boss 7.8 → 12.3. A two-armed re-run at n=100 — because a completion figure at n=30 carries a ±12-point band and cannot carry the claim — reads 92% → 73% and trash rounds 5.7 → 9.1 over ~1,130 fights an arm: 19 points at 3.7 standard errors. The ×0.50 damage scale was NOT tuned and is flagged as the designer's.

§3 — TWELVE RUNES RETIRED; 65 AUTHORED, 53 OFFERABLE. The sixteen were re-derived off LANE_TREES and runes.json and reproduce EM §3 name for name — but only once a UNIT_MATH clause counts as a rune SURVIVING: excluding those nine from the denominator returns twenty-two and sweeps in six runes EN's own threshold table names as survivors. Three are held back for re-authoring (the Beastmaster's, whose retirement would leave no rune in the game touching a companion) and are PRESENTED AS OPTIONS with nothing authored; the Bared Guard is reported apart and ruled on nowhere, because its two clauses ARE the trade and retiring it removes the cost with the upside. RETIRED MEANS KEPT — the Melted Armor contract: the entry stays in runes.json with a retired string naming what is lost, config / build still resolve it, and one continue in Runes.eligible_ids — the only door both offer paths use — stops it being offered. It cannot blank an offer: measured floors are 9 drawable, 2 spec-scoped and 5 on the rare shelf against 3 slots.

§4 — RUNG 2's GAP DOES NOT CLOSE WHEN ROWS 1–3 OPEN, AND THAT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN FIXED. Rung 1 unlocks rows 1–3; measured with exactly those rows equipped (DOD_SIM_ROWS=3, n=30), rung 2 reads 7% against 0–3% untalented, and rung 3 stays at 0%. The second rung is the next problem, and this batch deliberately did not touch it. Per-hero relics stay unbuilt and belong to the relic family's batch.

THE SUITES THAT MOVED, AND WHY EACH MOVED THE WAY IT DID. test_runes asserts the retirement in BOTH directions now — a retired rune must roll for nobody — rather than being exempted, because a one-armed version reads green on the day the whole file stops rolling; and its grant loop asks for the number of spec runes that SURVIVE rather than the literal 4, so a further retirement needs no edit there (3125 → 3101 checks). test_rune_battle now walks Runes.ids() instead of eligible_ids: it tests whether clauses PAY, not whether they are offered, and walking the offer pool stops driving all twelve on the day they are retired. It does not fail silently — armed, the control reads 17 failures, because the clause assertions name specific runes and values; the hazard is the REPAIR, since deleting those assertions is the other way to green and is the tempting one. Kept content that nothing drives is content that rots.

2026-09-01 — Batch EN: THE LAST THREE CLAUSES, AND THE RUNG THAT IS A DOOR

The rune charter finishes at 59 of 59. The lowest difficulty rung was ruled removed and was not removed, because it is the only thing that opens a player's first talent row — reported and stopped, as the brief instructed. Per-hero relics never landed, and CLAUDE.md now says what a relic is FOR as distinct from a talent. The sixteen runes the charter empties are split, derived and PRESENTED; nothing was authored. Full working: docs/reports/EN.md.

§1 — THE THREE HOMELESS CLAUSES GET RUNE-OWNED FIELDS, AND THE RUNE PAYS WHAT IT PAID. divine_presence_pct, entropy_ranks and pleasure_pct now write rune_ fields of their own, and each drip's EXISTING per-turn tick sums the pair. There is no second tick and there must not be one — a hero holding the rune AND the node would be paid twice, which is a magnitude moving. All three are payouts and all three guards are presence tests, read at their own sites rather than taken by analogy from EM's 56; AL's MAX rule has zero applications across all 59.

AND IT WAS MEASURED LIVE, BEFORE AND AFTER, ON SEEDED BATTLES. A drip that stops dripping passes every static check. On a hero holding the rune and no talents at all, across 24 seeded autoplay battles an arm: Divine Presence 81 fires / 255 health, Entropy 130 / 694 Break, Pleasure from Pain 76 / 166 health — and every one of the nine readings reproduced EXACTLY after the re-key, not approximately. The negative control bit in three directions at once: with the read sites taking the node's half alone, all three rune-only arms went to 0, the node-only arms did not move a single fire, and the hero holding both lost precisely the rune's share of the sum (17.18 → 13.39, 26.48 → 21.37, 12.55 → 10.66).

§2 — THE SIXTEEN, DERIVED RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE BRIEF, AND PRESENTED AS OPTIONS. The sixteen wholly talent-keyed runes were re-derived from LANE_TREES and runes.json and reproduce EM's list exactly. Every spec has 4 spec-scoped runes and 12 drawable (4 spec + 3 class-wide + 5 universal), so the retirement never blanks an offer — an exhausted rarity widens, then falls back to the generated Common family. The threshold is stated and it is content, not a count: a spec is GUTTED when nothing surviving touches its own engine. Exactly one spec fails it — the Beastmaster, who would keep one rune whose only upside is Quick Shot, leaving no rune anywhere in the game that touches a companion. Nothing was authored.

§3 — THE RUNG STAYS, AND THIS IS THE STOP THE BRIEF ASKED FOR. Profile.note_end_boss(Run.difficulty_rung()) sets the talent tier to the rung cleared, and Talents.TIER_ROWS is [0, 3, 6, 9] — tier 0 opens no rows at all, so clearing rung 1 is the only thing in the game that opens rows 1–3 of all twelve trees, for every spec at once. Re-measured on the live tree with BN's own instrument (untalented, n=30 a rung): 97% / 3% / 0%. Removing the rung moves a new player's first talent row from a one-attempt clear to roughly a thirty-attempt one. The 100% bot completion that motivated the removal is a FULLY TALENTED party — already through the door the rung is. Relics would have survived it (unlock_random fires at every rung); talents would not. Every site that reads a rung by index is listed in the report.

§4 — PER-HERO RELICS NEVER LANDED, AND THE DOCUMENT WAS NOT WRONG. Run.active_relics is still a flat list of up to 3 ids with no hero key, and both accessors take a hook and nothing else — party-wide at all 25 read sites. master.html's "up to 3 equipped per run at the draft" was ACCURATE; what was missing is that a ruling points the other way and is unbuilt, which it now says. And CLAUDE.md gains the division of labour, derived from the read site: every relic hook is read at run start, battle SPAWN, the victory screen, gold awards, rest nodes, shop prices or elite spoils — not one while a turn resolves — and the category relics.gd declares OUT is exactly the in-combat one. A relic sets up the run; a talent changes what a spec does in a fight; a rune is this run's kit.

§5 — TWO ACCEPTANCES RECORDED, AND ONE STALE CAVEAT RETIRED. Elites stay the shortest fight at every rung and that is accepted by design — but the figures to quote are EN's, not CY's: re-measured at --run 30 a rung, elite 3.4 / 3.7 / 4.0 against trash 3.9 / 4.3 / 4.4 and boss 3.8 / 4.4 / 5.4. DA's "no longer holds at rung 3" caveat does not reproduce and is retired; the elite is shortest at all three rungs again. The tags stay mechanically inert and check_ek §3's game-side population stays at THREE.

§6 — ONE GATE SECTION INVERTED RATHER THAN DELETED. check_em §4 said "the day one is answered this gate reds and the answer is to delete its row". All three were answered at once, and deleting the table outright would have left the section looping over nothing and printing exactly like a clean run. It asserts the CLOSURE now and walks EN's three in both directions over a live population, printing CHECKED n of m. And a documentation error in that gate's own header was corrected: it read "crit_bonus, speed, armor and seven others" and "the TEN fields", where UNIT_MATH holds NINE and armor is not one of them — EJ's off-by-one arriving in the gate whose §1 found it.

2026-09-01 — Batch EM: THE RUNES GET THEIR OWN FIELDS

The mechanical half of the designer's rune charter, and only the mechanical half. 56 of the 59 clauses that wrote a live talent node's own counter now write a rune-owned field, read beside the node's at the same site. Not one magnitude moved. The three that had nowhere to go, the sixteen runes the charter empties, and what severing the lane rule deletes are REPORTED and unruled. Full working: docs/reports/EM.md.

§0 — THE TAGS STAY INERT AND THE POPULATION DID NOT MOVE. No rune keys to a tag in this batch; check_ek §3's game-side population is still THREE. The differential mechanism — a rune worth more to a hero pointed the same way — waits for a real draft screen. This batch did the work that has to happen under any answer.

§1 — 56 CLAUSES RE-KEYED, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A PAYOUT. Each writes rune_X now instead of the node's X, and every read site sums the pair — 47 new BattleUnit fields and 97 reading statements across nineteen scripts, derived by check_em §2 rather than counted by hand. AL's rule was applied and its answer is uniform: a THRESHOLD takes the MAX and a PAYOUT SUMS, and all 56 are payouts. The > 0 tests beside them are presence tests, not thresholds; On the Edge is still the only threshold any rune shares and it is still AL's. Four clauses are named in the report as arguable — the contagion CHANCE, the Focus conversion-point DROP, a cooldown shave with a floor at zero, and the Bared Guard's NEGATIVE scarred term.

AND THE GUARD IS THE DANGEROUS HALF, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. if occ.spread_ranks > 0 is FALSE for an Occultist holding the Rune of the Whispering Dark and not the node, so a 100g rune's clause pays nothing and nothing throws. Driven live on a rune-only hero with the guard reading the node's counter alone, that mark spread 0 times in 400; with the pair summed, 55–66. This is DP's Whispering Dark dud arriving through the repair for it, and it is why check_em §2 asserts that every STATEMENT reading X also reads rune_X.

§2 — THREE CLAUSES HAVE NO HOME AND NOTHING WAS INVENTED FOR THEM. divine_presence_pct (the Sleepless Vigil), entropy_ranks (the Deepening Ruin) and pleasure_pct (the Whispering Dark) are per-turn drips that exist only as their node. All three still write the node's counter, check_em §4 names them as an EQUALITY, and the options — a rune-owned implementation, a re-point onto something adjacent, or a deliberate retirement — are priced in the report with what each rune is worth before and after. Each of the three loses one clause of three or four.

§3 — SIXTEEN RUNES ARE WHOLLY TALENT-KEYED AND THE CHARTER EMPTIES THEM. All sixteen are mechanically whole after the re-key and all sixteen have lost the argument for existing, because each was nothing but your lane, but more. Every one is listed by name in the report with what it does, what it costs and its lane. Exactly one is Scarred — the Rune of the Bared Guard, 75g, whose two clauses are a trade — and retiring a Scarred rune removes both halves at once. The distribution is uneven and it matters to the ruling: all 59 clauses sat in the 48 spec runes, the 5 universal and 12 class-wide carried none, and the Warden is 0-of-7 against the Beastmaster's 8-of-9.

§4 — BOTH DOCUMENTS CORRECTED, AND WHAT IS LOST IS RECORDED BESIDE WHAT CHANGED. master.html and design-notes.md both stated the lane rule as CURRENT and both were accurate descriptions of the authored pool. They now say the rule was how the sets were AUTHORED and no longer describes what the runes do. The cost is stated because it was measured: 48 of the 65 runes were built on "worth more to a hero whose points went elsewhere", a rune with its own field is worth the same to every hero of its spec, and the 12 splashes lose most — with no lanes to reach across, a splash is three unrelated numbers in a bundle. The AA-era paragraphs in design-notes.md are kept in place and annotated, because they are the argument the charter overrules.

§5 — THE RUNE OF THE STANDING VOW IS ON THE RECORD. DO cut the unity half of Healing Pulse's trigger and it appeared in no report, no changelog entry and no state file; EJ found it by grepping. Confirmed live and by the guard chain: the drip fires on CONSECRATED GROUND alone (guard_cons_ground=true, guard_unity=false), and the rune's three clauses read 2 / 4 / 5 on an Inquisitor holding it and no talents. It is a quiet weakening rather than a mis-sale — the desc named only holy ground before and after, so the code moved TOWARD the card — but an undocumented change to a shipped item is what the report convention exists to prevent.

§6 — A GATE THE BRIEF DID NOT ASK FOR, BECAUSE EJ SAID THIS IS ITS BATCH. EJ §5 recorded that the property no rune writes a live node's counter "belongs in the batch that takes the charter". check_em is that gate: 210 checks, four sections, five negative controls all of which bit. §1 derives the charter property from LANE_TREES and runes.json and names the nine unit-math exemptions as an EQUALITY; §2 is the statement sweep; §3 asserts every rune_ field survives the JSON load as the type its partner is declared; §4 pins the three with no home. check_dp §4's two Whispering Dark rows were repaired to intent rather than loosened — they pinned the field the rune SHARED with the node, which is exactly what the charter removes, and left as they were they would have called a live rune dead.

AND EJ'S REPORT SAID NINE AND LISTED TEN. Its §1 names the fields classed STAT despite having a node; armor is the tenth and no live talent node writes it at all, so it needed no exemption. The gate's equality found that on its first run.

2026-09-01 — Batch EL: THE TAGS GET THEIR REAL NAMES, AND MARK IS THE SEVENTH

EK shipped six tag words chosen under a collision. EL freed the word that caused it, gave the vocabulary its plain names, and added the seventh — derived from a list the game had already written down. Still mechanically inert: no clause reads a tag, no card's behaviour changes and no magnitude moves. Full working: docs/reports/EL.md.

§1 — Tempo IS FREE, AND IT WAS SIX SURFACES RATHER THAN FOUR. EK renamed TEMPO to CLOCK because Tempo was a live status chip and three talent nodes. It was also the Sharpshooter's third talent LANE, in nine nodes, and one rune's lane — a surface EK's own sweep could not see, because _collect_names walks "name" keys and a lane lives under "lane". The cheap side moved, as the brief ruled: the chip is PIVOT (its legend already read "the pivot's momentum"), sm_deep_thrust is Pivot, cr_icy_veins is Shockwave (battle.gd's own log line already said "the shockwave sets the field back"), dv_crusade is Crusade — the name its own crusade_ranks counter always carried, which is CK's Ironclad precedent exactly, so no new word entered the game — and the lane is Pace. The status IDS did not move: the collision was the LABEL, and each declaration in unit.gd now names its display word so the id stays traceable.

§2 — THE SIX RENAMES, AND THE COST WAS 292 ROWS. AFFLICTION → DEBUFF, SHELTER → DEFENSE, METER → RESOURCE, AMP → OFFENSE, CLOCK → TEMPO; BREAK is unchanged. Every one-line meaning was rewritten to fit the new word rather than carried over — two were circular under the new names (a RESOURCE tag reading "moves a resource" defines the word with the word) and both now name the meters. The brief believed the 292 rows referenced TAG_ORDER; they hold the words as literals, so every row moved, and that is a finding about EK's design rather than about this batch. What DID hold is the half that mattered: no reader outside CARD_TAGS and RUNE_TAGS names a tag word, so the rename never left two files and not one clause in the game had to be read.

§2b — MARK, AND ITS POPULATION WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THE CODE. EK sized MARK at six cards by reading the six card texts that say "one mark at a time". battle.DISPEL_NEVER's own comment names the marks — "the five MARKS the party applies — covenant, quarry, snare_line, feinted, hunt_mark", with blood_debt, vendetta and reacquire named the same way — and off that list the population is TEN cards, nine of them in the draft: EK missed Covenant of Ash, Snare Line and Feint, none of which says "mark" in its own text. EIGHT TAKE MARK AS THEIR PRIMARY, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A RELABEL — each was tagged for what its mark PAYS, which is a reading of the payoff and not of the card. Snare Line keeps DEBUFF (it marks the whole FIELD, not one enemy) and Feint keeps BREAK (it marks on one of its two stance branches); both carry MARK second. No rune gains it: not one rune payload field reads a mark, and that is measured rather than assumed.

§2c — SEVEN IS THE CEILING, AND IT IS RECORDED SO AN EIGHTH NEEDS AN ARGUMENT. A tag only means something if holding two is notable. Every word added divides the corpus finer, and the point at which a pool of ten to thirteen cards stops producing a repeated combination is the point at which a second card on a tag stops being a signal. Seven is where the next one starts costing meaning.

§3 — THE SWEEP RAN ON ALL SEVEN, AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS THE THING THAT WAS WRONG. DEBUFF, RESOURCE and OFFENSE collide with nothing across 1,551 authored strings. BREAK is unchanged and still clean. TEMPO is clean because §1 freed it. Two collide and both ship, named: MARK meets Hunter's Mark, Quarry's Mark, Mark of the Hunt and the party_mark chip labelled "Hunter's Mark" — and all four MEAN what the tag means, which is not what happened to WARD (a chip meaning takes 50% less Break damage); DEFENSE meets the Defense Potion, whose pouch button renders Defense on the same screen the draft card is drawn on, though never in the same visible frame. A same-meaning collision ships and is named; a different-meaning one is renamed. check_ek §4 holds both as an EQUALITY against a named list, so a fifth collision still trips.

§3b — THREE HOLES IN THE SWEEP WERE FOUND AND CLOSED. It could not see talent or rune LANES, it could not see items, and its status-LABEL arm asked the wrong question: it tested whether battle.gd contained ["Ward", — an exact whole label — so it was blind to every label merely CONTAINING the word, which is precisely why the party_mark chip went unseen. Every label is word-boundary matched now, lanes, items and relics joined the population, and both new arms assert their own size.

§4 — WHAT DID NOT MOVE. No clause reads a tag; no rune was re-keyed (EJ sized that at 59 clauses across 32 runes and it is the next batch); no card's behaviour changed and no magnitude moved. The count of files in the SHIPPED GAME that name a tag is still THREE — but check_ek §3's population assertion rolled the game and the targets into one number, so writing a new gate was indistinguishable from breaking the rule. The two halves fail separately now, and only the targets' half moved.

§5 — VERIFIED. check_el is new and carries three rulings: MARK's population is derived live out of battle.gd's apply sites rather than listed; master.html §6c's tag table is required to equal the code's word for word (EH proved that document's prose is asserted by nothing); and the widest tag line is measured here so text-standard.html §4.8a quotes a live number rather than a transcribed one (DJ §3). The display was driven live — check_map_screen renders 12 tag lines for 12 offered cards in the new vocabulary.

2026-09-01 — Batch EK: ARCHETYPE TAGS

A shared vocabulary that names what a card is FOR, carried by every ability in the corpus and every authored rune, and shown to the player on the draft card. MECHANICALLY INERT AS SHIPPED: no clause reads a tag, no card's behaviour changes and no magnitude moves. The vocabulary was MEASURED out of the corpus rather than proposed — and the measurement overturned the brief's own example. Full working: docs/reports/EK.md.

§1 — THE SIX, AND WHY THEY ARE MECHANICS RATHER THAN STATUS NAMES. The brief's example vocabulary was the status one ("the Pyromancer's Fireball is a Burn card"), and the corpus was measured before anything was authored. IT DOES NOT SUPPORT SIX STATUS NAMES. Grouped into families, the six biggest status systems in the game — Burn, Frost, Bleed, Poison, Ruin, Mark — reach 40 of the 154 draft cards, leaving 114 under no tag at all, and the brief's own test says a vocabulary with a large remainder is the wrong vocabulary. The reason is structural rather than accidental: a status system belongs to ONE spec, so inside the pool a player is actually drafting from it does not vary — the Pyromancer's pool is 12 Burn cards of 13, and a tag on twelve of the thirteen cards on offer tells the player nothing. The six shipped are AFFLICTION, SHELTER, BREAK, METER, AMP and CLOCK, they cover 154 of 154, and they vary inside every pool — five to ten distinct tag combinations against ten to thirteen cards. The status-family option is priced in the report so the designer can overturn this.

§1b — TWO OF THE SIX WERE RENAMED BEFORE SHIPPING, ON CJ's PRECEDENT. The BR §1 sweep ran against every ability, talent node, status label and rune name. AFFLICTION, BREAK, METER and AMP collide with nothing. WARD became SHELTER — Ward is a live status chip and the Rune of the Triage Ward carries the word — and TEMPO became CLOCK, because Tempo is a live chip AND three talent nodes. That is CJ's Iron Will collision exactly, and CJ's answer was to rename. A new vocabulary is free to move today and costs 227 rows to move later. And the engine check the brief asked for is clean: none of the six is one of DR's engine names, so an engine and a tag can never collapse into one word.

§2 — EVERY CARD TAGGED, DERIVED FROM THE READ SITE. 227 abilities and 65 runes, at most two tags each with the first the primary. The fields are useless on this corpus and that is CN's rule biting hard: heal is 0 on all 154 draft cards and 123 of them carry a special. A card's read site is its arm in battle._resolve_special, PLUS every block keyed on its display_name in the hero strike loop (58 abilities carry one, and Blood Debt's whole payload is one of them), PLUS the card-specific helpers those call, PLUS — for a setup card that resolves nothing at cast — whatever reads the status it lays. Aegis Wall applies aegis_wall and does nothing else; its healing lives in the BLOCK handler, and without that last hop it reads as untagged along with 39 others.

§3 — SHOWN ON THE DRAFT CARD, WHICH IS WHERE THE DECISION HAPPENS. One line under the card's own button and above the description, in its own tint, built by Classes.card_tag_line — CK §1's one-builder rule, one layer down. The layout cost is measured and not papered over: one 11px line a card, three cards a column, +42px on a column CK already measured at 557–671px against a 388px viewport. Nothing is clipped; the font was not shrunk and the computed block was not truncated. Where else they should appear is REPORTED and not done — the hero sheet, the battle tooltip, the rune offer and the blacksmith, each with its cost, in docs/reports/EK.md §3.

§4 — INERT BY DECISION, AND THE DECISION IS ASSERTED. No clause reads a tag count. No card's behaviour changes. No magnitude moves. Ship the vocabulary, let the designer see it on a card, then build on it — every alternative bets that the tag set is right before anyone has seen it in play, and 227 rows is an expensive bet to unwind. Inertness is the one property nothing else in the tree would notice losing, so check_ek §3 sweeps every .gd in the repo comment-stripped and requires the set of files naming a tag to be EXACTLY five, with ZERO asserted separately in the six files a mechanic would have to live in.

§5 — THE GATE, AND THE LIVE HALF THAT IS NOT IN IT. check_ek is new and joins GATES: coverage over Classes.ability_corpus(), the vocabulary pinned at six, inertness, the BR §1 sweep re-run LIVE so a future collision trips, and CK's one-builder rule. §1's population is the corpus walk and that is DA §3's rule applied rather than exempted — the first draft read both draft-pool accessors, check_da called it correctly, and the exemption was NOT taken: the corpus is a superset of the draft, the boss pools and the cores, so one assertion answers four questions and WALK_EXEMPT stays at two. A vocabulary that renders on nothing passes every static check in the tree (DS's Heads Down shape), so the draft card's tag line is driven live in check_map_screen, which now withholds its check_map_screen: OK verdict on a mismatch — that target carries no failure counter, so taking the pinned line away is the only way to turn its report into an assertion.

2026-09-01 — Batch EJ: THE RUNES AGAINST A CHARTER THEY WERE NOT WRITTEN FOR

A REPORT. No rune was re-keyed, re-authored, retuned or retired; no lane field was removed; no magnitude moved and no document was corrected. The designer's new charter says runes are disconnected from talents — run-specific items that modify stats and resources, and the mechanics and values of core abilities, draft abilities and passives. The 65 authored runes were written to a different rule, and this sizes the gap. The answer is 59 of 135 clauses across 32 of 65 runes, and it is a RE-KEY rather than a rewrite — 56 of the 59 already modify a passive, a stat, a core ability or a draft ability at their read site and need only a field of their own. Three do not. Full working: docs/rune-audit.html and docs/reports/EJ.md.

§1 — WHAT EACH RUNE ACTUALLY MODIFIES, DERIVED FROM THE READ SITE. Not from the rune's text and not from its lane field. 65 runes carry 135 clauses (116 stat fields across 84 distinct names, 15 ability add/set terms, 4 grants), and the two figures differ because a rune may sit in several categories at once — the Rune of the Whispering Dark writes four fields in three of them. Talent-keyed: 59 clauses, 32 runes. Permitted unchanged: 46 STAT/RESOURCE, 15 CORE-ABILITY value edits, 5 CORE, 5 PASSIVE. All 15 ability runes name a PROTECTED CORE or a class kit ability, so that whole family is already charter-clean. THE UNEVENNESS IS THE FINDING, AS IT WAS AT DO: the 5 universal and 12 class-wide runes carry ZERO talent clauses, and every one of the 59 lives in the 48 spec runes — the Warden's four are 0-for-7 and the Beastmaster's are 8-of-9. Per class the talent share runs Warrior 5/27, Mage 11/33, Cleric 21/33, Hunter 22/34. 16 runes are WHOLLY talent-keyed and would be empty rather than trimmed.

§2 — THE REBUILD TOUCHED TWO RUNES, ONE OF THEM UNRECORDED UNTIL NOW. Every one of the 84 rune stat fields was compared at its READ SITE and at its enclosing GUARD CHAIN against the tree as it stood before DN. Five moved; three are unrelated widenings (DU, DS) and two are the rebuild. The Rune of the Whispering Dark is DP's known case — spread_ranks and spread_ruin survived, and DP re-wrote the rune's description with the node, so it sells what it now buys. THE RUNE OF THE STANDING VOW IS NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE. DO cut the unity half of Healing Pulse's trigger — if u.has_status("unity") or u.has_status("cons_ground") became cons_ground alone — and the rune rides pulse_ranks, so its third clause has fired under strictly fewer conditions ever since. DO reported the node cut in its own §3 table; the rune consequence appears in no report, no changelog entry and no gate. It is a quiet weakening rather than a mis-sale: the rune's description named only holy ground both before and after, so the code moved TOWARD the card. And oc_spread is the sharpest lesson in the batch — its node dictionary changed by DESCRIPTION ONLY at DP while battle.gd's read site moved 7,225 lines and changed from a party-wide _max_hero_rank to the Occultist's own field. A node-dictionary diff would have called it a documentation edit.

§2b — THREE RUNE-ONLY EFFECTS ANNOUNCE THEMSELVES TO THE PLAYER AS TALENTS. Derived, not assumed: beacon_ranks, capacitor_ranks and mindfulness_ranks are written by a rune and by nothing else — no live node carries any of those three names — and their read sites log "→ Talent: Beacon", "→ Talent: Holy Capacitor banks…" and "→ Talent: Mindfulness". The Capacitor also raises a status chip under that name. The newer rune-only sites already say "→ Rune:" (Exsanguination, Critical Mass, the Reaper, the Cinder Trail), so the convention exists and these three predate it. Reported, not fixed — a log string is player-facing text and this batch changes none.

§3 — THE SLOT LADDER IS WRONG IN THE BRIEF FOR THE FOURTH TIME, AND master.html HAS NEVER CARRIED IT. The brief quoted two contradictory descriptions as both live in that document. Only one of them is in it. Swept on UNWRAPPED text (EI's method): "Three equip slots, flat, from run start — no growth ladder" at line 2444, and four more that all agree — five sites, of which a line-anchored grep sees only three. Zero hits for "Equip slots", for "2 → 3 → 4" and for "starts the run choosing a rune". The code agrees: Run.rune_slots() returns a flat 3 and never grows — its only other arm is RICH_SLOTS = 4, gated on sim_run and a DOD_SIM_RUNE_ECON=rich environment flag, and that is a flat 4 from tier 1 rather than a ladder. The refutation has been sitting in battle.gd's own comment since CT: "Batch AN §9 deleted the rune ladder outright and rune_slots() has been flat 3 ever since." The confusion has a source and it is worth naming: there IS a live growth ladder beside the runes — the ITEM pouch (ITEM_SLOTS_BY_ZONE), kept at CT for the opposite reason the rune ladder was deleted at AN, and design-notes.md sets the two side by side. NO DOCUMENT WAS CORRECTED, because none is wrong.

§4 — HOW BIG IT IS, WITHOUT SOFTENING. Mechanically it is a re-key and it has a shipped precedent. Of the 59 talent clauses, 56 ride something the charter permits anyway — 31 a spec passive, 15 a stat, 8 a protected core, 2 a draft card — so each needs a field of its own read at the site that is already there. Batch AL did exactly this three times (rune_grudge_bonus, rune_vigil_bonus, rune_on_edge_ranks), for the same reason and with the method in the source comments, and no rune payload anywhere carries a condition or has_node gate, so the coupling is additive and never conditional. THREE CLAUSES HAVE NO HOME — divine_presence_pct, entropy_ranks and pleasure_pct are per-turn effects that exist only as their node, and each needs an effect invented, not moved. AND THE REAL COST IS NOT THE CODE. master.html and design-notes.md both state the authoring rule as current — one rune per talent lane plus one splash, "worth more to a hero whose points went elsewhere" — and 36 lane runes and 12 splash runes are built on it. Severing them makes each a flat power increment, which is the thing design-notes says the rule exists to prevent. The re-key costs 59 clauses of data work; the charter costs the design premise of 48 of the 65 runes, and that is the decision, not the code.

§5 — THE ONE FILE THIS BATCH CHANGED THAT IS NOT A DOCUMENT. baselines.json's test_batch_bk row was widened from 129–130 to 128–130, which is what its own note said to do "when a reading demands it". The battery read 128 checks / 0 failures there. It is not a regression and that is proved twice rather than argued: this batch changed four files, all under docs/, and that suite reads seven res:// paths all under scripts/ and scenes/ — the intersection is EMPTY; and the count is stochastic by construction, because run._generate_map() is never seeded anywhere in the tree and the assertions loop over the nodes the roll produced. A fall there is a thinner map, not a lost assertion. Two standalone re-runs on the frozen tree read 129. baselines.json has exactly ONE reader in code — check_de.gd, proved comment-stripped; the four other files naming it mention it only in comments — so check_de alone re-certifies, and it reads 346 / 0 / 0 notices.

2026-09-01 — Batch EI: THE FLOOR THAT DID NOT COVER THE FLOOR

Two items, both about the verification floor itself. §1 — check_parse.gd walked res://scripts and res://scenes only, so the floor procedure every implement-only batch has run since CG was blind to the 39 gates, the 47 suites and both fixtures: at EH a duplicate var in gate_fixture.gd left the stderr grep CLEAN while 23 gates could not load. The walk is 41 files → 158, and its population is DERIVED from run_battery.sh rather than from a list of directories — a directory list is what went stale all three times this gate has been found short. §2 — a brief's PRECEDENT is now a claim that gets checked, written down because three errors in one lineage all propagated through briefs, which nothing sweeps. No game code moved, no magnitude changed and no card was touched. Full report: docs/reports/EI.md.

§1 — THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, IN FOUR LAYERS, AND NO LAYER IS A DIRECTORY. The gate reads the battery script's own SUITES and GATES arrays, every literal --script target, every run_one and every res:// scene run — 82 targets. It then follows their preload / load / ext_resource / change_scene_to_file edges to closure, seeded also by project.godot's three autoloads and its main scene — 57 more, and this is how gate_fixture.gd and suite_fixture.gd arrive: nothing NAMES them and 60 files depend on them. What is left in scripts/ and scenes/ is the old gate's territory and is kept for exactly the files it was right about — 11 more, reachable only by a class_name identifier, which no textual closure can follow. And res://data/*.json, which reach the game through a DATA_PATH string constant — 4 more. A target added to the battery is covered the same day, with no edit to that gate.

THE RESIDUE IS NAMED IN THE OUTPUT EVERY RUN, BECAUSE A FLOOR THAT IS NEARLY COMPLETE IS THE ONE THAT GETS TRUSTED. Four files are in the tree, spawned by nothing and reached by nothing — check_ck_width, check_cu, check_cv and check_dn, the four docs/state.md already records as running nowhere. They are loaded like everything else and reported as a separate population, so “covered” can never quietly mean “reachable”. What is still outside the gate is stated in its own output: the two .py instruments, the shell scripts, shaders/outline.gdshader (a shader compiles on the rendering server, which is a stub under --headless, so load() there would prove only that the file exists) and the assets/ binaries no dependency edge reaches.

THE GATE PRELOADS NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. A floor that preloads gate_fixture.gd cannot report that gate_fixture.gd is broken: it fails to load itself, prints a Parse Error, runs not one line and exits 0. And a gate that can only pass is a gap, so three things are hard failures rather than quiet skips — run_battery.sh unreadable, either battery array parsing to nothing, and a name in the battery with no file behind it. Each would otherwise shrink the population toward zero and print success. Both guards were armed and both red: hiding the script reads 3 failures, renaming SUITES=( reads 1. Coverage does not shrink when the derivation breaks — the residue layer catches whatever falls out, so all three armed runs still checked 159 files; only the LABELLING moves, and the guards say so.

IT PRINTS A CHECK COUNT NOW, AND THE COUNT IS THE COVERAGE. For its whole life this gate read checks=?, so the only number it published was a failure total that reads zero whether the walk covers 158 files or 41 — which is exactly how it was short three times with nothing going red. baselines.json pins the floor at 158, written before the battery off three identical standalone readings, so a walk that quietly stops covering something is a FALL and check_de reds, while a batch that adds a suite is a RISE and reads as a notice. Eight targets could not report a check count; seven can not.

AND A MALFORMED DATA FILE IS THE ONE POPULATION THE ENGINE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT. Armed, a broken runes.json reddened the tally and left the stream CLEAN — a floor that is right only if you read it the way the standing rule says NOT to. The JSON failure goes to stderr naming itself a Parse Error now, so the one floor procedure covers the one floor.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS — NINE ARMS, EACH TWO-ARMED AGAINST HEAD'S OWN COPY OF THE GATE, because an arm that only reds the new gate proves that a broken file is broken rather than that the widening works. Disarmed, both gates read 0 failures and 0 stderr hits. Armed: gate_fixture.gd 24 failures / 74 stderr hits against HEAD's 0 / 0 — the 24 are the fixture and the 23 gates EH counted; suite_fixture.gd 38 / 39 against 0 / 0; a gate (check_dk), a suite (test_batch_bf), the run harness, a scene-run script (check_map_screen), a residue file (check_dn) and data/runes.json each 1 / 1 against 0 / 0. Every one reproduces EH's exact failure on HEAD: the tally clean AND the stderr grep clean, with the tree broken. A tenth arm is the positive control — scripts/talents.gd, which the OLD gate already covered, reds both (59 against HEAD's 10), so the new walk is a superset rather than a replacement.

§2 — A BRIEF'S PRECEDENT IS A CLAIM, AND CLAIMS GET CHECKED. Recorded in CLAUDE.md: when a brief cites a precedent — a prior ruling, a mechanism, an existing ladder or convention — the batch VERIFIES it against the code before building on it, and reports if it does not hold. A wrong precedent is worse than a wrong number: a number gets re-derived, and a precedent gets inherited. The standing rules already say to derive a FIGURE from the file — but a precedent is not a figure, and nothing told a batch to check one. Documents get swept and briefs do not, so a false precedent has no instrument between it and the next batch. THE LINEAGE IS THREE ERRORS DEEP AND EVERY ONE OF THEM LIVED IN A BRIEF: CT asserted a rune equip ladder deleted at AN §9 and caught it itself; eleven batches later EG's brief asserted the same ladder; EH's brief then blamed master.html, which has never carried the claim. It is forward-looking only — past briefs are history and are not swept.

§3 — ONE OF THE TWO CONFIRMATIONS DID NOT CONFIRM, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The enabler count holds: PROTECTED_CORES names sixteen across nine specs, derived live, and every record that reasons from it — CLAUDE.md, this file's EH entry, docs/state.md and check_eh §3's live enablers == 16 — says sixteen. The one surviving “seven” is EG's own changelog entry, which is an accurate record of what EG did and is corrected by the entry fifty lines above it. The section lag does NOT hold. A third section carries it, and two more sites beside.

§10 SAID THERE IS NO CAP ON HOW MANY ABILITIES A HERO HOLDS — the same claim EH repaired in §6a, 1,450 lines away, and a line-based sweep cannot see it because the sentence wraps. BO §2 gave earned abilities a cap and EG made it a ladder (ABILITY_SLOTS_BY_BOSS = 7/8/9/10). The words are true of the POOL and false of the surface they explain: the ability menu is built from equipped_ability_names, so it shows the LOADOUT. Derived rather than asserted: the widest menu any of the twelve can raise is ELEVEN entries, so §10's promised range of 10–18 reaches ⇧Q and ⇧W and the rest is headroom. TWO SOURCE COMMENTS CARRIED THE SAME CLAIM, both in battle.gd and both attributed to Batch AH — corrected with it, and proved comment-only by a comment-stripped diff against HEAD: 0 differing code lines.

§6.4 STILL SAID SMOKE BOMB AND FIELD DRESSING “LAND LATER”, AND §13 SAYS THEY ARE SPENT. Field Dressing shipped at BR as a Hunter class-wide draft card and Smoke Bomb's function shipped at BO as Choking Smoke — both verified live in the pools rather than read off the document. Only Blight is still owed. This is the §6a/§6b shape again: DS swept §13 and not the section 975 lines above it. The Sharpshooter's list beside it names Disengage, Suppressing Fire and Piercing Arrow, and all three really are still owed — checked, not assumed.

AND §11b DESCRIBED A FIRST-RUN CARD THE GAME NO LONGER SHOWS. It summarised the framing card as teaching “the two ability picks a zone pays out”; the card's own text in map_screen.gd names no ability pick at all, and does name four node types, the three bargains and the 15% clear heal that the summary omits. Rewritten from the card. Line 1511's “the only Break lever” is deliberately left standing — the code cannot settle whether a lever DEALS Break or AMPLIFIES it, and a claim no instrument can check is not repaired by asserting it harder.

2026-08-31 — Batch EH: THE THIRD TIER, AND A SWEEP FOR PRECEDENT THAT WAS NEVER TRUE

Batch EA gave a spent zone-boss award a fallback and chose a spec-draft card because that pool could not itself empty. Batch EG broke that arithmetic one batch later — the slot cap became a ladder to ten and a benched card is now KEPT, so the floor fell from six to three, and to two for the Occultist. The award chain gains a third tier: boss pool → spec draft pool → class-wide draft pool, and every spec is now offered a full three under a fully-held loadout. No ability magnitude moved, no card was authored, no pool gained or lost an entry, and EA's second tier is byte-unchanged. §2 then swept master.html for claims of fact the code had stopped honouring and found sixteen sites across twelve claims. Full report: docs/reports/EH.md.

§1 — THE THIRD TIER. Run.roll_class_fallback_offer() reads the hero's own CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS entry, filtered by owned_ability_names, and is reached only when both pools above it come back empty. It is not the thing DY §3 forbade, which is worth naming because it looks like it: that rule says do not re-create the deleted 61-entry CLASS_POOLS, and its own next sentence says a re-opened class draw reads CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS — which is live, curated, and what this reads. EA's ruling is overturned in its second tier only and not in its reasoning: a zone-boss award must always pay something real, and the baseline it replaced was silence — _award_ability_picks skipped the hero with no acknowledgement at all. That requirement carries here and is driven live.

AND THE CLASS-WIDE POOL CAN EMPTY, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHY IT WAS CHOSEN. The brief held that it cannot — six cards per class, shared across three specs, and no hero can hold another spec's picks. The second half is true and the first does not follow from it. No SIBLING drains it, because every hero filters it against what he himself owns; but roughly one draft card in four is class-wide and draft_card_is_class returns true unconditionally once the spec side is dry, so a hero who takes at every offer drains his spec pool and then this one. What holds the floor up is arithmetic, not structure: emptying the chain means owning every card in both draft pools — fifteen at the cheapest spec, twenty at the Pyromancer — and an offer pays at most one card. Stated plainly, because EA's identical claim about the tier above was true when written and false one batch later: under a fully-held LOADOUT no hero can be paid nothing; under a fully-held POOL every hero still can. The loadout bound is asserted and the pool bound is printed.

THE DEPTH, ACROSS ALL THREE TIERS. The chain's floor under the loadout bound runs 8 to 13 against an award that asks for three — Occultist 8, the Pyromancer 13 — where the two-tier floor ran 2 to 6. No rune grants a class-wide card, derived rather than assumed, so the one term that could push the third tier below its arithmetic reads zero on all twelve. check_ea §1 keeps EG's split intact and adds the chain as a third question rather than widening either half: floor >= 1 per spec is still the RULE, [occultist] is still the named short set, and floor_all >= awards is new.

§2 — THE DOCUMENT SWEEP, AND THE BRIEF'S OWN PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE IT. The brief held that the false rune-equip-ladder precedent misled two briefs eleven batches apart through master.html. It did not: master.html has never carried that claim. It says “three flat slots”, “no runes and three empty slots” and “three rune slots” in the four places it mentions them. The false ladder lived in the BRIEFS, and the correction has been in CLAUDE.md since EG. The second seed was real and is the pattern's genuine instance: master.html said Guard Change is “the only stance swap in the game” in two places, and BP corrected the code nineteen batches ago and never swept the document — and left a third copy in classes.gd's own comment, one screen from the why it did fix.

SIXTEEN SITES, AND THE LARGEST GROUP WAS NOT A SUPERLATIVE AT ALL. §6a of the document still described the game before Batch BO: “There is no cap and no swap step”, “a full run ends at core + 3 + 2 = 6 abilities”, and two boss picks a run from “zone 1's boss and zone 2's” when BM §6 made all three zone bosses pay. The same section still carried EA's “the fallback pool cannot itself run out… which floors the fallback at six cards”, false since EG. §6b, fifty lines below, was current the whole time — EG swept its own section and not the one above it. Every site is corrected toward the code, per the standing rule.

AND TWO SOURCE COMMENTS WERE SWEPT WITH IT. classes.gd's third copy of the stance-swap claim, and unit.gd's “Both ends are uncapped and nothing removes stacks” — two earned cards remove Resonance: Stabilize floors the meter at 2, and Arcane Bolt halves it. The document made the same mistake in two places and now names both.

CAN IT BE AN INSTRUMENT? REPORTED, RULED ON NOWHERE. check_eh §4 counts the document's uniqueness claims and how many name a live ability: 56 claims, 12 nameable. A TWO-ARMED CONTROL SETTLES WHY THE DEFECT SURVIVED — putting the false stance-swap sentence back leaves all five master.html readers green, while breaking a literal a suite demonstrably reads turns test_batch_ah red. The prose is unasserted, and that is the finding rather than a proposal.

§3 — AND ONE OF EG'S THREE CONFIRMATIONS DID NOT CONFIRM. The record reads “all seven named enablers are in protected_names for their spec”, and every word of it is true — it audited the seven the brief named. PROTECTED_CORES names SIXTEEN, across nine specs. All sixteen are protected, so the conclusion held; what did not is the sweep, and CLAUDE.md's own rule names the shape: a named list cannot audit itself. The other two confirm: the ladder and the cap both read core_slots and protected_names has exactly one live reader outside its own definition (the loadout panel's CORE rows), and decline_draft is the ledger's only writer with benching writing none, driven live.

2026-08-31 — Batch EG: THE DRAFT STAYS LIVE ALL RUN

Four draftable slots against roughly thirty-seven draft offers a run, 63% of them arriving at a hero already at the cap — so the draft was effectively over after zone one and every offer after it was refuse-or-swap, with a swap costing the card for the rest of the run. Two changes: a hero gains an ability slot after every zone boss (7 → 10 across a run), and a drafted card is never lost — benching one is free and reversible. The protected core does not change and does not become benchable. No ability magnitude moved, no card was authored, the spec passive is untouched and the talent charter holds unchanged. Full report: docs/reports/EG.md.

§1 — ABILITY SLOTS GROW ON A ZONE BOSS. ABILITY_SLOTS_BY_BOSS is [7, 8, 9, 10] and Run.ability_slot_cap() is its only reader, following the pouch's ITEM_SLOTS_BY_ZONE and announced on the zone-victory screen beside it. THE BRIEF NAMED A SECOND PRECEDENT THAT DOES NOT EXIST — the rune equip ladder was deleted at AN §9 and rune_slots() has returned a flat 3 ever since, which is the identical false claim Batch CT's brief made about the same ladder eleven batches ago. AND THE LADDER IS NOT INDEXED BY THE ZONE. BM §6 put the end boss on the third zone's own board, so has_next_zone() is already false when the third ZONE boss dies and zone_idx stays at 2 — a ladder read off it would stop at nine. A run-level zone_bosses_cleared counts the event instead, and it is reset where zone_idx is reset, because a second run in one session would otherwise open every hero at ten (Batch CT's pouch scar, at a second ladder).

THE SLOT ARRIVES BEFORE THE AWARD, AND SEPARATELY FROM IT. It is granted by the boss dying rather than by the award being offered, so a hero whose pools are both dry still gains it — and granting it first is what makes a hero at the cap able to receive both, because the pick is resolved later against a cap that has already moved. Driven live through three real zone bosses, the cap reads 7 → 8 → 9 → 10, and the end boss grants nothing.

§2 — A DRAFTED CARD IS NEVER LOST, AND THE POOL IS NOT THE LOADOUT. Every card a hero takes is kept for the run; what the cap limits is how many are CARRIED. bm_abilities keeps its name and is the POOL; bm_equipped is new and is the LOADOUT, and it defaults to the whole pool, which is why every existing save and every test fixture means exactly what it meant before. Swapping happens on the hero card on the map, through the rune pouch's own shape — one writer, as party_screen.gd already says of equipped.

THE NO-RETURN LEDGER STILL BITES AND IT HAS ONE WRITER NOW INSTEAD OF TWO. A DROP used to write it, because a drop was permanent; a BENCH does not, because the card is still owned and owned_ability_names is what keeps it off the offer. Declining still refuses the whole offer for the run. The pool is still exactly what the run dealt you.

ALL SEVEN NAMED ENABLERS ARE PROTECTED, CONFIRMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — Quick Shot, Consecrated Ground, Heal, the three summons and Guard Change are each in Classes.protected_names for their spec, so none is a live brick.

§3 — WHAT IT TOUCHED THAT IS NOT THE DRAFT. The save moves v11 → v12 and is TOLERANT, and the refusal threshold is deliberately unmoved at pre-v10: a v11 save loads with zone_bosses_cleared defaulting to zone_idx (not to zero, which would take a resumed zone-3 run back to seven slots) and every hero carrying his whole pool. The hero sheet's ability chips are in a scroller now, because the absolute layout put a fifth row through the RUNES header — an overflow a Beastmaster already reached before this batch, since his protected core is six display names in three slots. test_batch_bp §7 is the one fixture in the tree that had to learn the split.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, AND THE FIGURE IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE BATCH. See the report for the re-measurement.

§4 — FOUR INSTRUMENT REPAIRS BATTERY 1 FOUND, AND TWO OF THEM ARE ONE DEFECT IN TWO COPIES. test_batch_bm and test_run_harness gate 2 each slice battle.gd from func _resolve_boss for a fixed 2400 characters and look for the # The end boss. anchor inside it; §1's comment block pushed that anchor from character 2130 to 2955 and both went red. AND BATCH EE §4's GUARD IS THE ONLY REASON EITHER SURFACED: without its half_at >= 0 check the slice would have been EMPTY, the negative assertions would have held for every needle, and both targets would have gone green while neither read anything — which in the harness is the only assertion on that slice.

AND check_ct PINNED THE SAVE VERSION LITERAL, WHICH IS THE RULE CT ITSELF SET. A suite must not pin the save version literal (BK §6 / CT) — and check_ct asserted == 11, so it went red the first time anybody bumped it. The pin manifest could never have warned anyone: build_pin_manifest.py indexes string literals, and a version pin written as an INTEGER comparison is invisible to it. WHAT IS REPORTED AND NOT RULED ON. The slot ladder alone drops the zone-boss fallback's floor to 3 for seven specs and to 2 for the Occultist, so check_ea §1's one assertion — which was asking two questions at once — is split into the rule (an award always pays, floor >= 1) and the stricter claim (every award offers three), the second as a NAMED SET. Closing that is a design decision Batch EA priced and did not take, and it is the designer's.
