2026-08-30 — Batch EA: A ZONE-BOSS AWARD ALWAYS PAYS

Three sections. The fallback DZ priced is BUILT and it is a spec-draft card the hero does not hold; six assertions pinning a batch code inside CLAUDE.md are re-pointed at the rules they were reaching for; and every protected core is measured against the draft cards that do comparable work. NO ABILITY MAGNITUDE MOVED, NO CARD WAS AUTHORED AND Ability.PURE_BUFFS WAS NOT WIDENED. Full report: docs/reports/EA.md.

§1 — THE FALLBACK IS BUILT, AND 14 OF THE GAME'S 36 ZONE-BOSS AWARDS GO TO 0. Run.award_ability_pick used to return false when a hero's spec boss pool came back empty, and battle._award_ability_picks then skipped that hero without a word — the baseline was not a weak reward, it was silence: the boss died and the victory card did not name them. It now falls back to a card from that hero's own SPEC DRAFT pool that they do not already hold, three offered, announced exactly like any other award. The boss-pool draw above it is untouched, so AN §4's spec-lock ruling stands and the fallback is spec-locked too.

THE DEPTH TABLE AFTER THE FIX, DERIVED LIVE: no spec can be paid nothing, and the worst-case fallback pool is SIX cards by slot arithmetic alone — a hero earns at most ABILITY_SLOT_CAP − core_slots = 4 (3 for the Holy Cleric) against spec draft pools of 10 to 13. The eight emptiable BOSS pools did not move and are not supposed to: what changed is what an emptied pool costs.

AND THE FLOOR IS FIVE, NOT SIX, FOR ONE SPEC — MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. owned_ability_names cannot see an ability a RUNE grants, because the grant lands on the battle cfg and never on the member dict. Four runes grant an ability and two of the four name a card in the same hero's draft pool — the Rune of Binding Souls (Sacred Resolve, the Devout) and the Rune of the Flayed Mind (Mind Flay, the Occultist) — which takes the Occultist's fallback floor to FIVE. Both names are also in their own spec's BOSS pool, so the fallback exposes nothing the existing channel did not, and five still fills a three-card offer twice over. Pre-existing, shared by roll_spec_ability_offer and draft_pool_left alike, and reported rather than fixed.

THE FALLBACK DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONSULT draft_refused. The boss channel never has either, refusal is the DRAFT channel's own memory, and a run that declined enough offers could drain the floor back below three — which is the defect the fallback exists to close. The reason is at the site.

§2 — SIX ASSERTIONS PINNED A BATCH CODE INSIDE CLAUDE.md, NOT THREE. DZ found three by reading and predicted a fourth it would not find. The fourth is BATCH CG, one line below the third, in test_batch_ce — and a mechanical sweep found two more of a different shape: rule pins whose LITERAL still carried a code ("BATCH BN §2 — WAS x0.70" and "REWRITTEN AT BATCH BS, NOT AMENDED"). All six are re-pointed at the rule each was reaching for — the difficulty ladder's standing heading and its rung-1 number, the uncapped-meter governor table and its ceiling-not-a-cost sentence, the re-point-in-place discipline, and the content-batch convention. None was deleted: every one of the six had a live rule behind it.

AND EVERY ONE OF THE SIX WAS PASSING OFF A DIFFERENT SENTENCE THAN ITS MESSAGE CLAIMED. There is no BATCH BS block and no BATCH CE block; the strings were satisfied by standing rules that name the batch in passing. A check that passes for a reason other than the one it states has stopped asking its question — and it reads green while it does it. The rule is in CLAUDE.md.

§3 — THE PROTECTED CORES ARE SYSTEMATICALLY CHEAPER THAN COMPARABLE DRAFT CARDS. MEASURED. RULED ON NOWHERE. DZ found Blessing of Zeal — a protected core — sitting ON its family's line on initiative and UNDER it on both cost and cooldown. It is not one card. Controlled three ways — same spec (so the resource is one currency), same role (derived from the ability's own fields), same initiative, and PURE_BUFFS members excluded from both sides because a clamped initiative is not a price anyone chose — there are 17 comparable pairs, and in 13 of the 17 the core is cheaper on an axis and dearer on neither. Resource: core cheaper 10, dearer 2. Cooldown: core shorter 13, longer 1. Both counter-cases are the same draft card — Divine Plea against Holy's Heal and Renewal — and it costs 0 Mana.

AND THE CAP BINDS THE TWO LAYERS AT DIFFERENT RATES, WHICH EXTENDS DZ's STRUCTURAL FINDING RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. Ability.BUFF_DELAY_CAP is the only instrument in the project that prices an initiative and it binds by table membership: it reaches 29.5% of the draft layer against 12.8% of the cores. The counter-argument is recorded with the number so it travels with it: a protected core arrives free with the spec and a draft card costs a pick, so a core being cheaper to CAST is not by itself a defect. This is a balance finding across twelve specs and it needs the designer. Nothing was retuned and Ability.PURE_BUFFS was not widened.

§4 — VERIFICATION. A new gate, check_ea, and its §2 drives a real zone boss in two arms and reads the announcement off the end card's own Label: arm A empties the boss pools only and requires the card to NAME every hero; arm B empties both pools and requires the announcement ABSENT while the end card is still present, which is what proves arm B's absence is the award's and not a probe that stopped working. The needle verifier's extractor is fixed — DZ's took only the first literal of an and compound — and the fix found a second, larger hole in EA's own instrument: it read 32 asserted literals where there are 95, because it counted brackets inside string literals and glued every statement after a "(" into one. A sweep now asserts its own population, and that rule is in CLAUDE.md because EA's own rune control failed the same way: it read runes.json as an Array, the walk never ran, and it printed "0 granting runes" where the answer is four.

2026-08-30 — Batch DZ: THE FALLBACK, THE PRICING, AND THE PRUNE

Three sections. The zone-boss fallback is priced as four options and nothing is authored; Divine Wrath, Blessing of Zeal and Arcane Surge are measured against each other and ruled on nowhere; and CLAUDE.md is pruned to the rule Batch CW wrote for it. NO CODE MOVED, NO MAGNITUDE MOVED AND NO CARD WAS AUTHORED. CLAUDE.md goes 261.77 KiB → 210.59 KiB and the knowledge-sync ratio 3.639% → 2.948% — under CW's 3% target for the first time since it was set. Full report: docs/reports/DZ.md.

§1 — A ZONE-BOSS AWARD THAT PAYS NOTHING: FOUR OPTIONS, PRICED AT 154, NOTHING AUTHORED. The award count is THREE, derived from Run.SLOT_COUNT, and both channels write the same bm_abilities list — so a drafted card removes itself from the boss offer. Eight of the twelve specs can lose an award, and the figure nobody had put a number on is that 14 OF THE GAME'S 36 ZONE-BOSS AWARDS CAN PAY NOTHING in a run where every hero drafts against their own boss pool. What happens today is not a weak reward, it is no acknowledgement at all: award_ability_pick returns false and _award_ability_picks silently skips the hero, so the victory card does not name them. The four candidates are re-priced against the live game, each with what it feels like as the boss dies, and the depth table is re-derived for every spec AFTER each fallback: under a spec-draft card or a class-wide card no spec can lose an award and the fallback pool's own worst case is six cards and two cards respectively; under a rune the same, except that roll_rune_candidates returns empty in a runes-off run, so that option needs its own fallback; under gold all fourteen awards are still lost as ability awards and the table does not move at all. Nothing was authored and the decision is the designer's.

§1b — AND THE ARGUMENT THAT MADE THE CARD-SHAPED OPTIONS LOOK WORST BROKE AT DY, WHICH THIS IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT TO SAY. Batch DV recorded that the spec most likely to need a fallback also had the fewest slots to receive one — true while the Holy Cleric's boss pool was one card. After DY she can lose ONE award of three and the Devout can lose ALL THREE, and the Devout carries the normal four earnable slots against her three. The deepest hole is now on a spec with as much room as anybody, so that objection applies to Holy's single award rather than to the fix in general. docs/state.md carried the old coupling as current and is corrected.

§2 — DIVINE WRATH AGAINST BLESSING OF ZEAL: THE INITIATIVE IS NOT A PRICE, IT IS A CLAMP. divine_wrath is a member of Ability.PURE_BUFFS and Ability.make() clamps every member to BUFF_DELAY_CAP — the definition even writes the constant rather than a number. Whatever anyone typed there, the card reads 1.0, so Divine Wrath was never priced against the Devout's protected core; it was never priced at all. AND BOTH MEMBERSHIPS ARE CORRECT, DRIVEN LIVE RATHER THAN ARGUED: cast in a real battle with cooldowns snapshotted, Blessing of Zeal moves the target's COOLDOWNS at cast (the same exclusion the table's own header already names for Blink) and Arcane Surge moves the caster's Resonance 0 → 2 (the exclusion it names for Stabilize), while Divine Wrath writes one status to four heroes and moves nothing else. So there is no membership error and no magnitude error — what there is, is that the cap is the only instrument in the project that prices an initiative, and it binds by table membership, so a card excluded for carrying a second payload gets no price at all. That is why Arcane Surge's open 3.0 is the same question asked twice.

§2b — SO THE FAMILY PRICES THEM, AND IT IS ARCANE SURGE THAT BREAKS THE PATTERN, NOT ZEAL. Across the eleven second-payload exclusions ability.gd's own header names, Mana rises with initiative — and Arcane Surge carries the family's TOP initiative (3.0) on 15 Mana and cooldown 3, against Hold the Line's 30 and 6 at the same 3.0. It is priced like a 1.5 card on Mana and a 3.0 card on tempo. Blessing of Zeal sits ON the line on initiative and UNDER it on the other two axes — cheapest at its tempo and by far the shortest cooldown there — so if either of the two is mispriced it is the protected core, and it is mispriced LOW. AND THE TWO DAMAGE TERMS STACK, MEASURED: they are adjacent if blocks in the hero strike loop with no elif between them, and twelve seeded blows read 1.1509 / 1.1509 / 1.3333 against the arithmetic 1.15 / 1.15 / 1.3225 — a Devout who drafts Divine Wrath and casts Zeal on the same hero pays both. Speed reads 95.000 → 109.250, exactly ×1.15. Reported; nothing was retuned and PURE_BUFFS was not widened.

§3 — CLAUDE.md IS PRUNED, AND THE TEST WAS CW'S OWN. Does this line tell a future session what to do or not to do? Every rule stayed; every batch narrative attached to one went, with the reason kept to a sentence. 261.77 → 210.59 KiB, a cut of 51.2 KiB (19.6%), taking the sync ratio to 2.948%. The arithmetic of the target is worth recording because it is not obvious: pruning the file shrinks the denominator too, so clearing 3% needed more than 47.8 KiB rather than the 46.4 the naive subtraction gives.

§3b — THE SAME TRAP APPLIED AGAIN AND THE GATHER FOUND MORE THAN THE BRIEF NAMED. Twelve rules were stated inside a narrative and would have gone with it, and they are in the file's own voice now — among them a standing block states a number once (buried in the paragraph explaining how a superseded snapshot survived CW's split, inside the very block that then restated the draft total six times at four historical values), write a suite's refusal setup relative to the LIVE pool size, to find the next hole in a fingerprint ask what the rule is about and re-derive it, and an exemption is keyed file::func, never by file. TWO THINGS THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME: the file stated six rules TWICE — "Verify before shipping" and "THE TRAPS" each carried the same six — so the file enforcing "one authored copy" was carrying six second copies of its own rules; and it carried live counts that had gone stale against its own rule that live counts belong in docs/state.md (the corpus at 216 where it is 227, RECAST_GATED at 59 where it is 64, CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS at 24 where it is 25, and five more). Those were removed rather than corrected, because correcting them creates the second copy again; each is a pointer now.

§3c — HOW IT WAS PROVED SAFE, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT FOUND WHAT THE OTHERS COULD NOT. Roughly thirty-five suites assert against this file. A needle verifier built from the tree and green at HEAD before a line was cut — every literal any suite asserts against CLAUDE.md, plus test_batch_cd's structural slice — was re-run after every edit and caught two real breaks, both a needle split across a line wrap, which is invisible to reading and fatal to a contains. A literal sweep at a four-character floor over 10,948 literals read 174 lost, 0 gained. AND BOTH WERE GREEN WHEN A 17-SUITE SUBSET BATTERY, RUN BEFORE THE CERTIFICATION RUN, CAME BACK WITH test_batch_ce AT 1114 / 1. The extractor had taken only the FIRST literal out of each contains( call and ce's assertion is an AND of two; the first survived the rewrite and the second did not. Restored, and ce re-reads 1114 / 0. A sweep is only as wide as the convention it matches, and neither hole was knowable from inside the instrument — the run is what finds them, and a subset costs minutes against the thirty-five a full battery costs.

2026-08-30 — Batch DY: THE VAULT IS EMPTIED

Six sections. The seven abilities no run could reach are re-homed into live pools, CLASS_POOLS is retired, Holy's empty boss awards close as a consequence, the last unseeded flake is seeded, and the draft audit's arithmetic is re-derived. NOT ONE CARD WAS AUTHORED AND NOT ONE MAGNITUDE MOVED — every card moved already had its handler, its text and its Perfect. The draft goes 149 → 154 and the ability corpus reads 227 on both sides of the batch.

§0 — THE ORDER WAS THE WHOLE OF IT. Re-home first, retire the container second. All seven lived in ability_corpus() through CLASS_POOLS alone, so deleting the container first would have dropped the corpus 227 → 220 mid-batch and moved the printed population of roughly fifteen gates for no reason. Done in this order the corpus never moved, and that was stated as the expected result before the run rather than discovered after it. It is recorded in CLAUDE.md as a rule: re-home what is reachable only through a structure before you delete the structure.

§1 — FIVE CARDS INTO DRAFT POOLS. Each home was verified against the LIVE pool before it was taken, because the pools had moved twice since the homes were priced. RALLYING SHOUT → the Warden (9 → 10, the shallowest pool in the game): its two clauses exist separately in his TALENT TREE and its refuel clause on a boss card, but nothing in his draft pool did either. MANA SHIELD → the MAGE CLASS pool (6 → 7): untied, general, reads no passive, and derived over the whole corpus it is the only ability in the game that converts damage taken into Mana. ARCANE SURGE and REALITY FRACTURE → the Arcanist (10 → 12): Reality Fracture is the only ability in the 227-card corpus carrying a non-zero delay_push, an axis nothing else touches. DIVINE WRATH → the Devout (10 → 11).

THE THREE PRICING QUESTIONS SHIP AS AUTHORED AND ARE FLAGGED RATHER THAN RETUNED. Nothing was re-priced in this batch. (1) Arcane Surge's 3.0 initiative is three times BUFF_DELAY_CAP and has never been priced against it; it sits outside PURE_BUFFS legitimately, because its Resonance bank is a second cast-time payload, but "legitimately outside the cap" is not "priced". (2) Divine Wrath is party-wide +15% damage and +15% speed at initiative 1.0 — and the sharper comparison is not the one on record. BLESSING OF ZEAL IS THE DEVOUT'S OWN PROTECTED CORE: +15% damage on ONE ally at initiative 2.0. Divine Wrath is that card made party-wide at HALF the initiative, in the same hero's kit. DS's BRING IT DOWN is priced at 2.0 for being party-wide, but it is a BEASTMASTER card, so the two are not siblings and never meet in one offer — the brief's claim that they would is corrected. (3) SANCTUARY OVERLAPS HYMN OF HOPE, Holy's protected core party-heal: a different shape (12% of max against 20/35%, Mana against Mercy) doing the same job. All three are reported in docs/reports/DY.md §1 with options. Ruled on nowhere.

§2 — HOLY'S BOSS POOL GOES 1 → 3, AND THE GENERAL PROBLEM SURVIVES IT. DV §2 measured it: three zone bosses award one pick each from this pool, and the pool held ONE card — so two of her three awards paid nothing, and all three paid nothing if she drafted Divine Plea, which is also draftable. DAWNBREAK and SANCTUARY join it, both Cleric heals out of the vault with handlers, text and a Perfect apiece. The four fallback candidates DV priced are no longer needed for Holy. BUT THE QUESTION IS NOT CLOSED AND EVERY SPEC WAS RE-MEASURED. THE DEVOUT IS THE SHARPEST CASE NOW: his pool is TWO against three awards, and both of his two are also draftable, so all three of his awards can pay nothing — worse than Holy's position ever was. EIGHT of the twelve specs can be short of a full award set once drafting is accounted for; the three Hunter specs and the Warden are the only four that cannot. check_dv §2 derives both ends every run and went red on Holy's fix, which is exactly what that tripwire is for. AND THE SHARP POINT: ABILITY_SLOT_CAP is 7 and the Holy Cleric carries FOUR protected cores, the only spec that does — so the spec with the emptiest pool also had the fewest slots to receive a card.

§3 — CLASS_POOLS IS DELETED, NOT ZEROED. 61 entries across four classes, every one authored and resolving, feeding an award Batch AN §4 re-pointed away eighteen batches ago. pool_ability() never read it, so all seven of its exclusive entries still resolve with it gone; what was lost is the MANIFEST — the only place they were enumerated as a group — and that is the point: they are no longer a group. THE READERS WERE THE REAL COST, AND A GREP FOR THE CONSTANT FOUND ONLY SOME OF THEM. Eighteen suites and gates read it, and class_pool() — its accessor — had callers the constant's name never appears beside: test_batch_ah, ah_battle, ak, an, au, bp and check_dn among them. Each is re-pointed at the live structure that answers the same question, or inverted to assert the container's ABSENCE off the source — test_batch_an's idiom for roll_ability_offer. A check that survives a deletion by asking an empty dict a question is worse than a red. vault_ability()'s HEADER IS HISTORY NOW RATHER THAN A PLAN: it promised its entries would "return as earnable picks without a line of new mechanics", and all ten have returned. AND ITS OWN COUNT WAS WRONG ON RECORD — DX §3 and state.md both said the vault held 38 definitions with 31 re-homed; the live function holds TEN, seven of which were the orphans. §4 — THE LAST UNSEEDED FLAKE IS SEEDED, AND IT SETTLED AT ZERO. test_batch_at §1's live damage-curve ratio drew off whatever the startup RNG happened to be: the file calls seed() in four places and every one of them is downstream of this check. Seeded per-pair — DD's method, the same two lines the TAKEN loop twelve lines below has used since DD — so both arms of a pair draw one identical stream and the only difference left between them is the Resonance stack count. One row carries a flake field now and it is a seeded one. Its own text still read "calls seed() ZERO times", false since DF; corrected toward the code.

§5 — THE DRAFT AUDIT'S ARITHMETIC IS RE-DERIVED. docs/draft-audit.html §2 and §2b were marked STALE at DT and have been passed by DR, DS and this batch. NINE OF THE SIXTEEN POOL ROWS MOVED AND SEVEN DID NOT. THE WARDEN IS THE SHARPEST RESULT AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE BATCH SET OUT TO GET: he was the shallowest pool in the game, and he now holds the joint-widest decision spread in it — ten decisions across ten cards, the only pool where every card makes a different decision. AND TWO COUNTS IN THAT DOCUMENT WERE PRODUCED BY DIFFERENT METHODS: DR reported its own repair as taking the Swordmaster "four → eight decisions"; by DQ's method it is seven, because DR counted Wheeling Cut's self-mitigation as a second axis on one card. Recorded rather than smoothed over. Reported. Ruled on nowhere — DQ's value was that it changed nothing and DR then ruled.

2026-08-29 — Batch DX: A SIXTH INSTANCE EARNS A CONSTRUCTION RULE

Three items. A rule, its first sweep, and the thirty-one sites that sweep found; the project's second unseeded flake, seeded; and a decision the designer is owed. No ability magnitude moved and the draft is untouched at 149.

§1 — NEVER ASSERT AN EQUALITY AGAINST A COLLECTION THAT GROWS. check_dv §4 asserted live_span == 16 against a changelog that gains an entry every batch, and DW's own entry broke it. That was CD §1's fault written for the sixth time, so it is a construction rule now rather than a sixth trap:

Never assert an equality against a collection that grows. Changelog entries, corpus size, pool depth, suite counts, call-site counts — assert a floor, or assert a property. An equality against a growing set fails on the next batch that does its job, and the failure looks like a regression.

THE SWEEP FOUND FORTY-ONE SITES ACROSS THIRTEEN FILES, ALL PINNING ONE THING: THE DRAFT. The spec half at 125 (fifteen sites), each class pool at six (eleven), the whole draft at 149 (nine), the class half at 24 (four), the per-spec depth table (one) and the Beastmaster's boss pool at five (one) — and >= appeared nowhere. DO added twenty-two cards, DR a net +1 and DS six, so each of the last three batches to author a card had to hand-bump a dozen files at once, and a batch that missed one would have read as a regression rather than as a bump owed. Thirty-five assert a FLOOR now, across twelve files, each with a message that names the live figure and the direction of travel.

THE REMAINING SIX ARE KEPT ON PURPOSE, ALL SIX IN ONE FILE, AND THAT IS THE RULE'S OWN FIRST CORRECTION. A floor cannot see a card arriving, and a card arriving unannounced is exactly what test_batch_cd.PER_SPEC_DEPTH exists to force a batch to state. So the equality survives in test_batch_cd alone — beside the table a new card must move anyway, where the failure costs one edit in one file instead of thirty-five across twelve. The sharpened rule: a staleness tripwire is a SINGLE site whose message says the ground moved and names what to re-derive. Thirty copies of one is not a tripwire, it is a tax. Four other single-site tripwires were swept, examined and deliberately left standing for the same reason — check_di's CALL_SITES, check_dv's two boss-pool census pins and its Holy-pool pin, and check_cz's SHIELD_SPECIALS registry.

AND THE ONE SURVIVING EQUALITY COULD NOT SAY WHAT HAD MOVED. Its failure message read "the draft stands at %d of %d" % [DRAFT_TARGET, DRAFT_TARGET] — the target printed twice, so the single assertion left to announce a moved draft would have reported 149 of 149 while the draft stood at 150. That is the second-copy-of-a-count defect sitting inside the tripwire written to catch drift, and DW found the identical shape in two test_batch_cp messages one batch earlier. Three messages print live figures now.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE PROVEN ON DEMAND. Remove one card from the Warden's pool and every floor reds — check_dr 2, test_batch_cd 5, cp 2, bt 1, ce 4, each naming 124 and 148. Add one and all twelve floor files stay silent while test_batch_cd alone reds with four messages, the sharpest being warden drafts 10 (want 9) — the batch is told which pool moved and where to record it. A floor that can never fail is the hollow check this project has spent twenty batches removing; these fail.

§2 — THE SECOND UNSEEDED FLAKE IS SEEDED, AND IT SETTLED AT ZERO. test_run_harness gate 2 walks a randomly generated map by taking reachable()[0] at every step and asserts each of six node types was crossed; seed() was called zero times in the file. Thirty seeded runs, thirty byte-identical walks, 165 checks and 0 failures every time — so it was a flake and not a finding, which is the half that had to be measured rather than assumed.

DW'S CHARACTERISATION WAS TOO NARROW IN BOTH HALVES. Over 400 unseeded walks the length is 49 every time and fight, elite and miniboss never come close to zero — but blacksmith reached zero once, and merchant and event each came within one of it. So three of the six types are at risk, not the one that happened to fail, and the rate is well under DW's estimated 3%: two observed in roughly 474 readings, counting DW's own and 40 clean standalone re-runs at HEAD.

THE ASSERTION IS NOT WIDENED AND THE SEED GOES AT EVERY BOARD GENERATION, NOT ONCE. Relaxing six types to five would delete the check rather than repair it — the six being present is the question. Both seeding shapes were measured and both are exactly repeatable; the per-generation one is repeatable for a reason that cannot be broken from a distance, because seeding once would leave zones 1 and 2 drawing off whatever the loop consumed before them. The three boards stay different from one another (_generate_map reads zone_idx), so this buys determinism without buying one map walked three times. The negative control is a seed that misses a type: seed(101) fails gate 2 on the walk crossed a event — DW's own red, reproduced on demand.

test_batch_at §1's ratio is the last unseeded flake in the project — AND THE SWEEP THE BRIEF ASKED FOR CANNOT ESTABLISH THAT, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL ANSWER. A source sweep fails in both directions: twenty suites and gates make unseeded random draws and are perfectly stable (bk and an generate whole maps), so seed()-count is not evidence of a flake — and test_batch_at calls no RNG function at all. Its one seed() is at line 603 and every use is DOWNSTREAM of the check that flakes; the noise itself comes from battle.gd's randf_range(0.9, 1.1) in the strike loop, which no sweep of the suite tree can see. Only readings find a flake, and the readings are in baselines.json: three rows carry a flake band, and after this batch two of the three are seeded and closed — test_rune_battle at DF §0 and harness_2 here. The claim is true and it rests on the readings, not on a grep.

§3 — CLASS_POOLS: THE SEVEN ARE THE VAULT, AND OPTIONS ARE PRICED WITH NOTHING AUTHORED. DV established it is a lost feature rather than scaffolding. The sharper diagnosis is that the seven unreachable entries are not orphans of a pool — they are the contents of Classes.vault_ability(), and CLASS_POOLS is its manifest. That function holds 38 definitions kept deliberately, its header saying they "return as earnable picks without a line of new mechanics"; later batches re-homed 31 of them into spec draft pools and boss pools, and AN §4 closed the class draw, which was the vault's only remaining exit. Full options, prices and card text in docs/reports/DX.md; nothing was authored and no ruling was taken.

ONE OF DV'S PREMISES IS CORRECTED AND IT CHANGES A PRICE. DV recorded that deleting the container "would delete the last listing of seven finished abilities". The definitions survive deletion: Classes.pool_ability() resolves by name through a chain that reads the vault and never consults CLASS_POOLS at all, so all seven still resolve with the container gone. What deletion actually costs is the manifest — the only place they are enumerated as a group — and their membership in ability_corpus(), which would fall 227 → 220. That is a real cost and a smaller one than recorded.

AND THE ORPHANS ARE NOT INERT — THEY HAVE BEEN ABSORBING MAINTENANCE FOR FOUR BATCHES. DK §1 widened sanctuary's heal to _hero_side() and measured it on a live bear (1200 off a 10000 body); DL §1 widened Rallying Shout's Pressure clause and measured 30 shed on a summoned Ursus, authoring a new guard on its resource loop; DM §3 read Divine Wrath's two clauses in its hero/ally audit. Two of the seven also sit inside Ability.PURE_BUFFS and two inside HEAL_SPECIALS, so CY's and CZ's cap passes priced them too. Three recent batches spent measured, documented engineering on cards no player can obtain, and nothing said so. That is the cost of leaving the question open, stated as what has already happened.

AND THE CURATION DEBT UNDER "restore the draw is one line" IS MEASURED. run_state.gd's own comment says re-opening it is one line, and that is true of the code. Across the twelve specs, 56 of the 183 hero-and-entry pairs a reopened draw could offer duplicate something that hero can already reach, and 27 of those are the hero's own protected core — a card held on turn one. The Mystic would see 8 of 17 duplicated, the Holy Cleric 2 of 14. The line is one line; the curation behind it is 61 entries against twelve specs.

VERIFICATION. Documents written before the run. Baseline movements predicted in baselines.json before it. Parse checked by grepping stderr after every edit, never a tally and never an exit code, with a deliberate func _dx_negative_control(: proving the check bites. Every backed-up file restored by cp and md5-verified, never by git checkout. Two runs of six suites were discarded and re-taken because the negative controls were mutating scripts/classes.gd underneath them — the tree has to be frozen for a reading to mean anything, which is DL's lesson met again.

2026-08-29 — Batch DW: THE WALK, THE FINGERPRINT THAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, AND THE OVERRUNS

Three items. The brief named one hand-rolled corpus walk and two holes in the rule that should have caught it; there were THREE walks and THREE holes, and in both cases the one nobody had named was the worst. Two populations that had been pinned as equalities over a short walk are corrected to their real size, and one text overrun turns out to have been authored twice.

§1 — THE FINGERPRINT HAD THREE HOLES, AND THE THIRD WAS IN THE POPULATION IT WAS ALREADY SWEEPING. check_da §3 has asserted since Batch DA that no gate hand-rolls the ability corpus. DV §5 found test_batch_cp._corpus() doing exactly that while the gate read 37/0, and diagnosed two reasons: the sweep read check_*.gd only, and its fingerprint matched the two draft-pool ACCESSORS where that walk read the pool CONSTANTS. Both held. The third was larger than either and no population axis would ever have found it: the fingerprint took "a corpus walk reads the draft pools" as a premise rather than as an assumption. check_cl_resolver._every_ability() is a walk in a gate — inside the swept population, read on every battery run since DA — and it reads only Classes.kit() and Classes.spec_abilities(). It reached 43 of 227.

THREE WALKS, NOT ONE, AND THE TWO DV HAD NOT FOUND WERE THE TWO THAT REACHED LESS.

  • check_cl_resolver::_every_ability — 43 of 227. It feeds CL §1's asserted unexpanded-token sweep, which was therefore running over 19% of the game. Re-run over all 227 it still reads ZERO, so nothing was hiding — the instrument was blind and the thing it was blind to was not there, which is worth saying plainly rather than counting as a catch.
  • test_batch_bh::_all_ability_names — 91 of 227, and it reads neither draft pool, so no fingerprint built on those two calls could have accused it whatever population it swept. It feeds §1's "Certain reaches exactly 2 abilities game-wide". Over the real corpus it still reaches exactly two. The claim was true and the instrument behind it could not have known.
  • test_batch_cp::_corpus — 207 of 227 (211 names; the four class basics it reaches do not resolve through pool_ability and fall out). This is the one DV found.

THE WIDENED RULE ASKS WHAT A WALK IS RATHER THAN WHICH CALLS IT MAKES. A function that RETURNS a collection built out of two or more of the game's seven ability-source families is answering "what abilities exist?", and Classes.ability_corpus() is the one authorised answer. The RETURN is the discriminator and it is doing real work: a body that reads a pool and ASSERTS on it returns void and is not a walk. A flat union of marks across gates and suites accuses sixteen files — and sixteen exemptions is not a rule, because an exemption granted to a genuine violation is worse than the violation it covers. Sharpened, it carries ONE exemption: check_cz::_cl_only_corpus, the deliberate Batch CL negative control. It is keyed file::func, never by file — a file-scoped exemption blinds the rule to a new walk arriving in that file later. Comments are stripped before the match, because check_ds once took a red for a header comment that named two accessors while explaining that it does not call them.

THE OLD SWEEP AND BOTH ITS EXEMPTIONS ARE UNTOUCHED. This is an added instrument, not a loosened one: loosening a rule to cover a new case re-argues every case it already settled. check_da goes 37 → 39, and the source scanner both gates need is authored once in gate_fixture.gd rather than copied — DA/DB/DD's own lesson.

§2 — TWO POPULATIONS PINNED AS EQUALITIES OVER A WALK THAT COULD NOT SEE THEM. test_batch_cp walks the real corpus now, and both of its named populations were wrong.

  • The literal-digit rule pinned ["Shatter"]. The true population is EIGHT — Arcane Explosion, Detonation, Hymn of Hope, Resurrection, Shatter, Summon Aguila, Summon Canis and Summon Ursus. Seven were always invisible; DU's corpus fix added the eighth and the walk could not see that either. They are recorded, not rewritten: a parenthetical digit is legal in prose that is not a resolved value, so this is a named population a human has read, and a NINTH has to be a decision.
  • The checked-but-Perfectless biconditional pinned SIX. The true population is EIGHT — Arcane Explosion and Death Ray join the six. Authoring a Perfect for any of them is a design decision and none was taken.

ARCANE EXPLOSION IS IN BOTH, AND IT IS THE ARCANIST'S LIVE BASIC ATTACK. It entered the corpus at DU §4 and broke both rules on arrival with nothing going red. It runs a skill check, so the player gets a timing bar, and it advertises no Perfect at all — on the card a hero casts most. Reported; authoring one is the designer's. Both rules print their live figure now, and the failure messages count the table instead of naming a number: one read "the recorded fourteen" against a table holding one, and the other "the named six" — the second-copy defect sitting inside the assertions meant to catch drift.

§3 — THE 49-CHARACTER OVERRUN WAS AUTHORED TWICE, AND THE OLDER COPY WAS NEVER HIDDEN. DV recorded Shadowrend's rendered Perfect at 49 against the measured 44-character ceiling as the one thing DU's corpus fix made visible. It was not. "Cleric recovers {mhp:5}" is authored at two sites — on Shadowrend and on SMITE, the Cleric class basic — and ability_corpus() has walked kit("cleric") since long before DU. The identical breach was already in the corpus under Smite's name; DU added a second instance of a breach that was always visible. PROVED MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN ARGUED: repairing both drops check_cl_width's perfect_text overrun count 56 → 48, and 8 is four render contexts × two abilities — had only Shadowrend been over it would have fallen by four.

BOTH SITES READ {mhp:5} NOW, WHICH RENDERS AT 33. That is the file's own dominant idiom for a bare magnitude ({mhp:35}, {mhp:20}, {mhp:8} per stack); "Cleric recovers …" was the outlier, and the Perfect label plus the card it sits on already say whose recovery it is. Rewording to fit a measured ceiling is repair; nothing else was touched. check_dv §5's pin is inverted rather than deleted — it asserted the overrun and asserts the fit now, because a deleted check lets it come back silently — and check_dw §3 asserts the two strings AGREE, since fixing one of two copies is how two copies start.

AND THE COMPLETE RESULT FOR ALL FOUR ABILITIES DU MADE CHECKABLE, WHICH NOBODY HAD READ. Fireball (description 35, Perfect 33) and Frostbolt (40, 33) are inside the ceiling on every field. Arcane Explosion (34) is inside it too and breaks the two rules above instead. Shadowrend was the only width breach and it was never only Shadowrend's. Three of the four were clean, and that is only visible because all four were measured rather than the one that failed.

VERIFICATION. FOUR NEGATIVE CONTROLS, ALL FOUR BIT. Re-hand-rolling test_batch_cp._corpus() failed three targets at once (check_da 2, check_dw 2, the suite itself 2). The sharpest was a single character: with the smallest walk restored, changing the family threshold from 2 to 3 returns check_da to a clean 39/0 with a 43-of-227 walk standing in the tree — the exact defect DV found, reproduced on demand — while check_dw stays red, which is what proves the two gates are not redundant. Diverging Shadowrend's Perfect from Smite's to a string that still FITS failed exactly one check, the divergence guard alone. And the legitimate side: a void function added to a gate reading both pool constants is not accused, so the convention axis widened without a false positive. Every file was backed up to the scratchpad and restored by cp, never by git checkout, with md5s verified identical afterwards.

ONE CLAIM IN THE BRIEF DID NOT SURVIVE MEASUREMENT. It predicted §2 would move test_batch_cp's check count because its walk grows. The count did not move — it holds at 697. The walk grew from 207 to 227, but the two populations are asserted as equalities and the added abilities produce no new checks. Its "211" is the NAME count, not what the walk returns, which is 207.

2026-08-29 — Batch DV: THREE THINGS DU FOUND, AND THE CHANGELOG CUT

Four items. Three are DU §5's boss-pick findings and the fourth is a threshold the project's own rule says to act on. ONE THING CHANGED IN THE GAME — a door that was letting the player waste a turn the bot already refused — and the other three resolved to measurement, because the brief withheld the ruling each of them needed.

§1 — CLASS_POOLS IS A LOST FEATURE, NOT SCAFFOLDING, SO NOTHING WAS DELETED. The standing rule is that dead code is deleted rather than zeroed, and the brief made the deletion conditional on establishing WHY it is dead: a structure orphaned by a change is a lost feature, and one that was never wired is scaffolding. It was wired, and it was live. Three independent sources agree: classes.gd's own header describes the Batch AH award as "1 from its SPEC_POOLS entry and 2 from its class's CLASS_POOLS entry (Run.roll_ability_offer)"; run_state.gd records that Batch AN §4 re-pointed the award at the spec pool alone and left the structure standing; and test_batch_an §1 asserts roll_ability_offer() is deleted, so the function that read the class pools is gone and the pools are not. The AN changelog entry says the same in its own words. Per the brief, that makes it a design question rather than a deletion, and this batch has no ruling on it.

AND THE AUDIT SHARPENS DU'S FIGURE RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. CLASS_POOLS is 61 entries across four classes, 61 distinct names, and every one resolves in the corpus — DU's count is exact. What DU did not measure is where those names live otherwise, and the answer splits three ways: 27 are some spec's OPENING KIT (Heal is the Holy Cleric's, Blizzard the Cryomancer's), so what AN really retired was cross-spec acquisition inside a class; 27 are reachable through a live pool; and SEVEN ARE REACHABLE NOWHERE AT ALL — Rallying Shout, Mana Shield, Arcane Surge, Reality Fracture, Dawnbreak, Sanctuary and Divine Wrath. Each is authored, resolving, and fully implemented down to its handler, its status chip and its glossary prose, and the dead class pool is the only list in the game that names it. Checked against every other channel: no rune grants any of them (runes.json), and Classes.talent_granted_names() is empty. Deleting the structure would delete the last listing of seven finished abilities, which is a second and independent reason the brief's conditional lands where it does. Classes.ability_corpus() walks class_pool(), so the corpus of 227 counts all seven.

§2 — TWO OF HOLY'S THREE ZONE-BOSS AWARDS ROLL EMPTY, AND THE FIX IS PRICED RATHER THAN AUTHORED. The award count is THREE, derived rather than recalled: Run.SLOT_COUNT is 3 and _resolve_boss's own comment reads "THREE ZONE BOSSES, THEN A FOURTH BOSS AFTER ZONE 3 … the END BOSS awards NO ability pick". Measured against it, every spec's boss pool and the shortfall it carries before a single card is drafted:

  • holy 1 — also draftable 1, boss-only 0. SHORTFALL 2, and 3 if he ever drafts Divine Plea.
  • inquisitor 2 — both draftable, boss-only 0. SHORTFALL 1, up to 3.
  • berserker 3, pyromancer 3, cryomancer 3, occultist 3 — two draftable apiece, so up to 2 can roll empty.
  • warden 4, swordmaster 4, arcanist 4 — the Warden's three boss-only entries mean all three of his always land.
  • beastmaster 5, sharpshooter 5, mystic 5 — no overlap with their draft pools at all, so 3 of 3, always.

42 entries, 40 distinct names. Both channels write the same bm_abilities list, which is why a drafted card removes itself from the boss offer. The shape is the draft's inverted: the three Hunter specs DS had to deepen because their DRAFT pools were the shallowest in the game hold the DEEPEST boss pools, and the two Cleric specs hold the shallowest.

THE FALLBACK IS A DESIGN DECISION AND THE BRIEF WITHHELD IT, SO FOUR CANDIDATES ARE PRICED AND NONE IS TAKEN. A card from the spec's own draft pool it does not hold — costs nothing to build (bm_abilities already takes both channels) and is the closest thing to what the award promises, but it dissolves the distinction between the two channels and hands the boss the draft's job. A class-wide card — draws on CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS, which is live at 24, and would give the class channel a live purpose for the first time since AN, which is the only candidate that touches §1's finding; the cost is that class-wide cards are authored WEAKER than spec cards on purpose, so the fallback reads as a consolation prize. A rune — mechanically the cheapest of the four, because roll_rune_candidates and rune_picks_owed already exist and the map's owed-pick overlay already resolves them; it changes what the reward IS, which is either the point or the objection. Gold — free to build and the weakest, since a zone boss already pays randi_range(110, 130) and more of the same is not a reward the player will remember.

AND ONE THING THE PRICING TURNED UP THAT MAKES THE CARD-SHAPED OPTIONS WORTH LESS EXACTLY WHERE THE HOLE IS WORST. ABILITY_SLOT_CAP is 7 and the Holy Cleric carries FOUR protected cores — the only spec that does — so he has three earnable slots, the fewest in the game. The spec whose boss pool is emptiest is also the one with the least room to put a card in. Gold and a rune cost no slot; both card options do.

§3 — THE PLAYER MAY NO LONGER RECAST AN ARMED PHOENIX, AND THE REFUSAL IS EXACT. _resolve_special writes attacker.ashes_return = ASHES_RETURN_PERFECT unconditionally, so a hero who had already armed Ashes of Al'ar could recast it for 30 Mana and a turn, write the same constant and change nothing — every turn, at cooldown 0. The autoplay heuristic has refused exactly that since BB (u.ashes_return <= 0 and not u.ashes_used) and the player's door did not, so the bot was playing better than the player was permitted to. It is refused at _ability_usable now — the one door every other refusal uses — and the darkened button says which of the two reasons applies, because a greyed button with no reason is the bug CO §3 exists to prevent.

IT IS NOT IN RECAST_GATED, AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The brief called for membership; membership there is INERT and would have shipped as a change to nothing. That system reasons about STATUS writes — _recast_refused asks _recast_targets for a pool and _recast_writes for the chips a cast would lay — and ashes writes an integer FIELD. Driven live on an armed Mage: _recast_targets returns an empty array, so the loop never runs and _recast_refused returns false with the card fully armed. Adding the string to the list changes no behaviour whatever; it would only have taught check_co to report the card as never exercised. Inventing a pseudo-status to carry the field would put a name in _recast_refusal_note that STATUS_INFO cannot render and the player holds no chip for — a second path wearing the first one's clothes.

THE TEST COMPARES AGAINST WHAT THE CAST WOULD WRITE, NOT AGAINST ZERO, AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL PROVES THAT MATTERS. CO §1's rule is that a refusal blocking a cast which would in fact have done something is strictly worse than the waste being fixed. Written as ashes_return > 0 the gate refuses a genuine 25 → 40 improvement the day ASHES_RETURN acquires a caller; written as >= ASHES_RETURN_PERFECT it does not. Both forms were driven live and they disagree exactly there — see §6. ashes_used is its own arm because unit._ashes_guard() returns early forever once the phoenix has risen, so re-arming after that is inert whatever the field says. Reported and not collapsed: ASHES_RETURN (25) has no caller at all — the handler writes ASHES_RETURN_PERFECT (40) unconditionally — so it is a dead constant of exactly FIREDRAW_TAKE's shape, and collapsing it would move a magnitude.

THEN THE REVERSE, ACROSS THE WHOLE POPULATION, BECAUSE THE BOT'S REFUSAL LIST IS A READY-MADE ORACLE AND NOBODY HAD COMPARED THE TWO. Every guard in _autoplay_pick_kit and _bot_drafted_pick of the form "only when the target does not already hold it" was read against the player's door. ashes was the only genuine gap of its exact shape, and the rest of the comparison is worth as much as the finding was:

  • ALREADY COVERED BY THE GENERAL RULE, which is the rule working: Immolate, Rime, Hunter's Instinct, Venom Coating, Consecrated Ground, Divine Shield and Mantle are all in RECAST_GATED, and the bot's guard and the player's door already agree.
  • NOT A NO-OP, so correctly ungated — the bot's guard there is POLICY, not a waste refusal: Hold Breath also pays +40 Focus every cast; Renewal's Perfect pays a burst heal and its tick power is recomputed from the caster; Snare Trap also fires _hit_and_run; Fortified Spirit's recast genuinely unwinds and re-lays the loan. Refusing any of these would be the strictly-worse bug arriving through the fix for the first one.
  • UNGATED, ALL-ZERO ON ITS OWN FIELDS, AND A REAL CANDIDATE: Mark of the Hunt (a flat 7-turn hunt_mark) and Intercession (a window on every living hero) are both abilities whose whole payload is a status, and neither is in RECAST_GATED. The general rule would handle both correctly — refusing only when the standing one is already at least as long. Ruled on nowhere, per the brief.
  • AND ONE NARROW GAP THE BOT'S GUARD POINTS AT WITHOUT MATCHING: Deadfall SETS deadfall_armed, so recasting a full one writes the same number. The trap cap already refuses it at a cap of 1 — but under Deadfall Network (cap 3) the door permits it. The bot's deadfall_armed <= 0 is not an exact oracle here either: it also refuses a part-spent or DORMANT deadfall, and a recast on one of those genuinely restores charges and clears the rest. Reported, not taken.

§4 — THE CHANGELOG IS CUT AT THE DF/DE BOUNDARY. The live file crossed CW's 400 KiB threshold at DU exactly as DU predicted, and this executes the rule rather than deciding anything. With this entry in place the file held 34 entries; 17 stay and 17 move, which is the older half by count and leaves the live file at the ~150 KiB CW's rule aims for. The live file now starts at Batch DF and the archive ends at Batch DE; both headers name the other file with its full path, and nothing was deleted. THE VERIFICATION IS THE POINT, AND IT IS IN §6 — headings counted two independent ways, sets proved disjoint, order preserved, and the two bodies re-joined asserted byte-identical to the original. No file size was asserted anywhere, because sizes agreeing is entirely consistent with a duplicated entry and a dropped one. Every changelog-reading target was enumerated before the cut and NONE needed re-pointing — all fourteen (bb, bn, bo, bp, bq, br, bs, bt, bu, bv, bw, bx, cb, ce) anchor on their own <h2> heading, reach the archive by following the path out of the live file's own header, and name batches that were archived at CX; CX's re-pointing is what makes this cut cost nothing.

§5 — WHAT DU MADE VISIBLE, AND THE RULE THAT STILL CANNOT SEE IT. Four abilities entered the corpus at DU, and the brief asked whether any breaks a rule that could not previously reach it. Three findings, and the largest is not the one the brief named.

  • DU'S "THE FOUR MAGE SPECS" IS WRONG, IN THREE PLACES, AND IT MATTERS. There are only three Mage specs. apply_kit_overrides covers pyromancer, cryomancer and arcanist — all overriding Magic Bolt out of kit("mage") — and the fourth is SHADOWREND, the OCCULTIST's, which is a CLERIC spec and overrides Smite out of kit("cleric"). The sentence stands in docs/reports/DU.md, docs/state.md and classes.gd's own comment. It is not cosmetic: anyone re-deriving which kit the old walk misread would look at the Mage kit and never learn that the Cleric kit was misread too. Corrected in the source comment and in docs/state.md; DU's report is left as the record of what that batch believed.
  • SHADOWREND'S OVERRUN IS 49 CHARACTERS, NOT 45, AND THE TWO NUMBERS MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS. Authored it is 23; resolved with no context, 36; wearing the "Perfect: " label every surface supplies, 45; and RENDERED against a real Cleric — which is what check_cl_width counts and what a player actually sees — 49, five over the ceiling rather than one. The four extra characters are the computed (6), so this overrun is CAUSED by CL §1's parenthetical doing its job. Reported, not fixed — it joins the standing population of authored overruns.
  • AND THE FINDING THAT OUTRANKS BOTH: test_batch_cp §3's LITERAL-DIGIT RULE STILL CANNOT SEE ANY OF THE FOUR, AND IT NEVER COULD SEE TWELVE MORE. That suite carries its own hand-rolled Batch CL walk — the four pool tables plus Classes.kit(cls), with the overrides never applied and Classes.spec_abilities never read. It reaches 211 names where Classes.ability_corpus() reaches 227, and the 16 it misses are every spec-kit ability that lives in no pool: Arcane Cannon, Arcane Explosion, Death Ray, Detonation, Fireball, Frostbolt, Guard Change, Hex of Ruin, Hymn of Hope, Kill Command, Resurrection, Shadowrend, Summon Aguila, Summon Canis, Summon Ursus and Wildfire. Arcane Explosion carries (2 on a critical strike) — an ability-level authored parenthetical — and §3 pins that population as exactly ["Shatter"], an equality. Run over the whole corpus the true figure is EIGHT, not one: Arcane Explosion, Detonation, Hymn of Hope, Resurrection, Shatter and all three Summons. So the answer to the brief's question is yes — and the rule that would catch it is blind, which is why nothing went red at DU. This is DA §3's propagation-by-copy defect in the one place that rule cannot look: check_da §3 sweeps check_*.gd only, and its fingerprint matches the two pool ACCESSORS where this walk reads the CONSTANTS. Reported and deliberately not fixed — repointing that walk turns a green equality red on seven pre-existing offenders, and rewriting shipped player-facing text is authoring.

ALSO REPORTED, NOT FIXED: RECAST_GATED holds 64, and both battle.gd's own header ("THE QUALIFYING SET: 59 abilities") and CLAUDE.md's CO block ("59 abilities since DA §2") still say 59 — two copies of one number that stopped being true when DR and DS added five between them. Nothing in this batch moved that list, so neither copy is corrected here; the live count is printed by check_co on every battery run.

2026-08-29 — Batch DU: TWO TERMS A COMPANION SHOULD READ, AND A HOLE IN THE ONE AUTHORIZED WALK

Five items. One magnitude moved and it was an ENEMY's, one blind spot closed in the enumeration every gate is built on, one open ruling closed by declining to change anything, and one audit that changes nothing on purpose. No card was authored.

§1 — PYROBLAST KEEPS COOLDOWN ZERO, AND THE REASONING IS RECORDED WITH THE RULING. DQ found it was one of only two repeatable draft cards; DR gave the other one (Lunge) a cooldown for exactly that shape. The provenance is identical and the premise is not. Lunge cost 25 of a 100 bar at 3.5 delay — ordinary on both axes, so DR's "in a pool there is no price" was literally true of it. Pyroblast's 6.0 delay is the longest in the project with nothing above it (three times BASIC_DELAY) and its 45 mana is the second-highest cost in the game — the only card above it is Death Ray at 55, which carries cooldown 3. It is priced twice, just not with a cooldown, and cooldowns tick in the unit's own turns, so a 6.0-delay cast has already spent three basic attacks' worth of tempo before one would begin counting. Nothing under scripts/ changed for this section. The ruling AND its reasoning are in CLAUDE.md beside DR's framework, so the inconsistency cannot be read as an oversight later; check_dr §5 keeps printing the live list every run.

§2 — A CRIPPLED COMPANION BIT AT FULL STRENGTH, AND THAT IS AN EXPLOIT RATHER THAN A DEAD CARD. Enemies aim at _hero_side(), which holds the living companion; _apply_status lands the rider with no companion filter; and _companion_hit never read it. Two enemy abilities carry Cripple — the Wolfrider's Ride-by Slash and the Grave Totem's Grasping Roots — and in the hero strike loop Cripple is a flat quarter off. So an enemy debuff attached, chipped, logged and did nothing, in the player's favour. MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: 40 seeded blows read 30268 in both arms before, ratio 1.0000; they read 30268 against 22703 after, ratio 0.7501.

  • THIS IS THE LINE THAT SEPARATES IT FROM DK's REFUSAL TO WIDEN, AND BOTH DECISIONS ARE CORRECT UNDER IT. DK found Empower attaching to a companion and paying nothing and ruled the card's TEXT narrow rather than teaching the read, because widening a damage loop moves a balance number. A player effect that lands and pays nothing costs the player a card; an ENEMY effect that lands and pays nothing costs the player nothing. The first is a dead card, the second is an exploit, and only one of them is fixed by narrowing the words.
  • THE LOOP IS NOT WIDENED GENERALLY, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SIGNATURE. DT enumerated the attacker-side block at 84 multiplier terms, of which _companion_hit read three. 76 of the 78 genuinely absent terms are unreachable by SHAPE: the function takes a float and not an Ability (26 ability-keyed terms), a companion's passive_id is always empty (10 more), and every talent-rank field on one is always zero (20 more). A general widening would hang visible chips on a companion that change nothing, which is worse than the narrow miss because it reads as working.

§3 — CHILLED, WITH THE SAME DISCIPLINE, AND THE HALF THAT IS UNREACHABLE IS REPORTED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED AROUND. The HOARFROST battle modifier stamps a summoned companion deliberately and its branch carries no inherited guard, so a companion can hold Chilled. Both of the hero loop's chilled terms are read now — the threshold arm at three stacks and Hungering Cold's per-stack arm — and all four measured arms land on their arithmetic exactly: 1.0000 at one stack with no node, 0.8500 at three, 0.9700 at one stack under the node, and 0.7735 with both terms live.

  • ONE STACK IS THE CEILING IN PLAY AND SAYING SO IS THE FINDING. Every other application of Chilled in the file targets an enemy, so the frost bargain's single stack is all a companion can ever hold and the threshold arm is unreachable today. The stack count was NOT raised to make it reachable — that would be authoring. The arm is written anyway, because the hero loop's two terms are one rule and half a rule here is the next thing to diverge.
  • TYPED RELIC DAMAGE IS DELIBERATELY STILL UNREAD, AND IS INERT TWICE OVER. The Tinderbox modifier really can write a fire bonus onto a companion — measured — but a companion's blow carries no damage type at all, so the read would find nothing to apply. Fixing half of that would read as working while paying exactly what it pays now.
  • check_du.gd IS THE GATE THE RULING NEEDED, AND IT ASSERTS THE RATIO RATHER THAN THE READ. 32 checks. check_dk §4 and check_dm §2 already re-measure empower, wrath and battle_shout every run; Cripple and Chilled had no instrument in either direction, so removing these reads again would have been silent. Four negative controls, all four bit, and each bit on different arms — deleting the threshold arm and deleting the per-stack arm fail different assertions, which is what proves both are load-bearing.

§4 — THE ONE AUTHORIZED CORPUS WALK COULD NOT SEE FOUR LIVE BASIC ATTACKS. apply_kit_overrides replaces abilities[0] for each of the four mage specs at spawn — Shadowrend, Fireball, Frostbolt and Arcane Explosion — and none of the four sits in any pool or is returned by spec_abilities(). So Classes.ability_corpus() read kit("mage") and got the unoverridden Magic Bolt, which is nobody's live basic attack. Nothing was wrong at runtime; what was wrong is that DA §3 makes this the one walk every gate must use, so every gate built on it inherited the blind spot. The walk applies the overrides now, using protected_names's own idiom one function up. The corpus goes 223 → 227.

  • WHAT MOVED, RE-RUN THROUGH EVERY CRITERION DERIVED FROM THE WALK — AND THE ANSWER IS ALMOST NOTHING, WHICH IS THE USEFUL RESULT. Fifteen gates read the corpus. CN's population goes 223 → 227 and its "runs no timing bar" count does not move at all (121 either way): all four overrides attack, so all four correctly run a bar. CO's refusal population and CY's delay-cap population do not move — neither of the four is a pure buff or a shield, so neither table reaches them. DR's cooldown-zero census does not move either, and the brief said it would: that census walks the draft pools directly and never touched the corpus.
  • ONE BRIEF CLAIM DID NOT SURVIVE: DP's rune-field sweep is not derived through the corpus at all. It walks runes.json against the source text of five scripts. It does not move and it could not have.
  • ONE THING THE FIX MAKES VISIBLE FOR THE FIRST TIME. The width sweep now measures the four descriptions and three perfect_texts it never could. All twelve description lines are inside the 44-character ceiling; Shadowrend's perfect_text renders at 45, one over. It is pre-existing, it joins a standing population of authored overruns the gate already reports, and it is reported rather than fixed.
  • AND THE RECORDED FIGURE IS CORRECTED. "Twelve cooldown-zero abilities in the protected cores" is twelve INSTANCES across twelve specs and only SEVEN distinct names — Strike ×3, Quick Shot ×3, Smite ×2 and the four overrides. The claim the sentence makes is true either way; the number was the misleading half. check_cz §0's walk agreement is a SET IDENTITY now rather than an equality, derived off apply_kit_overrides itself so a fifth override is covered by doing nothing.

§5 — THE BOSS-PICK POOLS, AUDITED THE WAY DQ AUDITED THE DRAFT, AND RULED ON NOWHERE. check_dr §5 walks the draft pools only, so SPEC_POOLS had never been in any census. 42 entries across twelve specs, 40 distinct names. Full tables in docs/reports/DU.md §5. Nothing was changed and no ruling was taken — DQ's value was that it changed nothing, and DR then ruled on what it found.

  • THE BIGGEST THING IN IT IS NOT ON THE BRIEF'S LIST: CLASS_POOLS IS DEAD. Batch AN re-pointed the zone-boss award at the spec pool alone, and run_state.gd's own comment says nothing in a run reads the class pools any more. 61 authored abilities sit in a channel no run can reach, and re-opening it is one line.
  • THE DEPTHS ARE THE DRAFT'S SHAPE INVERTED, AND TWO POOLS CAN EMPTY. Three zone bosses award one pick per hero each, and a drafted card removes itself from the offer (both channels write the same bm_abilities list). The Holy Cleric's boss pool is ONE card and that card is also in his draft pool — so two of his three picks always roll empty and, if he drafted it, all three do. The Inquisitor's is two, both draftable. The three Hunter specs — the ones DS had to deepen because their DRAFT pools were the shallowest in the game — hold the DEEPEST boss pools at five apiece, with no overlap at all.
  • THE TWO COOLDOWN-ZERO BOSS CARDS ARE NOT THE SAME CASE, WHICH IS WHY NEITHER IS RULED ON HERE. Ashes of Al'ar rate-limits itself — ashes_used makes it once a battle by construction, which its own card text states. Sweeping Strikes does not: 20 Rage a cast while building 10, at cooldown 0, with a 3-turn Daze rider.
  • AND A CO-SHAPED FINDING NOBODY HAD LOOKED FOR. ashes is not in RECAST_GATED, and its handler writes the same constant unconditionally — so recasting it while already armed costs 30 Mana and a turn and writes nothing. The autoplay heuristic already knows not to (u.ashes_return <= 0 and not u.ashes_used); the player's door does not. check_co could not have found it: it saturates the members of RECAST_GATED, so it measures the list rather than the candidates for it.

2026-08-29 — Batch DT: LOOSE ENDS

Four items and no new play. A gate for the two DS specials that shipped with no permanent cover, the second of the three flakes seeded, and two reports — one of which came back recommending that the obvious change NOT be made.

§1 — check_ds.gd, AND THE ONE ASSERTION A STATIC CHECK COULD NOT MAKE. DS authored six Hunter cards and added no gate; check_co's saturation sweep reaches four of the six as a side effect and BRING IT DOWN and HEADS DOWN were covered by nothing at all. Both are driven through a real battle now, on two fixtures — the two cards belong to two different Hunter specs and the fixture fields one hunter slot. 57 checks, and four negative controls, all of which bit.

  • BRING IT DOWN is MEASURED, not asserted. The card is stamped in one place and read three thousand lines away, which is exactly the shape that produced DK's Empower defect. Ten seeded Warden strikes read 8526 plain against 10233 under the capped +20% — ratio 1.2002. The gate also pins the snapshot (deepening the bond after the cast moves nothing), the cap, the no-bond refusal, and that the beast does not wear the amp it earned, which is the one property the card text does not state and the handler does.
  • A THIRD ARM EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST TWO WOULD PASS A PARTY-WIDE GLOBAL READ. Stripping the amp from the striker alone, while the rest of the party keeps it, must put the ratio back at 1.0. The negative control that replaced the per-wearer read with a global one passed both other arms and failed only this one.
  • THE HEADS DOWN ASSERTION IS THE POINT OF THE BATCH. The card's first version refused any ability with cost > 0, and 46 of the 50 enemy abilities cost zero — derived on every run, not quoted — so it would have suppressed four abilities in the whole game while reading as working. A static check would have called that correct: both versions refuse abilities, both name a criterion, both log a fallback. The only assertion that separates them is live — run a real enemy's real kit through _intent_ability_usable and require that at least one REFUSED ability costs ZERO. Under the shipped identity test that is true on 14 of the 21 kits in the game; under cost > 0 it is false on all but two. The control put the fault back and the gate went red with six failures, the raider reading "2 kept, 0 refused".
  • AND THE GATE TRIPPED check_da §3 ON ITS FIRST RUN, ON ITS OWN COMMENT. The header explained that the file does not hand-roll the ability corpus — and named both of §3's fingerprint strings in order to say so, which is what the fingerprint matches. No exemption was granted: an exemption granted to a sentence blinds the rule to a real violation arriving in that file later. The names came out of the prose instead. The mirror of the comments-record-removals rule is now in CLAUDE.md beside it.

§2 — PYROBLAST'S COOLDOWN: PRESENTED, AND THE ANALOGY BREAKS. The brief asked whether DR's Lunge reasoning — at the end of a talent lane the price was the node, and in a pool there is no price — applies. The provenance is identical and the reasoning does not transfer. Derived across all 223 abilities: Pyroblast's 6.0 delay is the longest in the project with nothing above it, and its 45 mana is the second-highest cost in the game. The only card that costs more is Death Ray at 55 — which carries cooldown 3. Lunge was 25 mana at 3.5 delay, ordinary on both axes, so "there is no price" was literally true of it; it is false of Pyroblast, which is priced twice and simply not with a cooldown. Nothing was authored. The other six cooldown-zero abilities are reported with them: four are the free basic attacks where zero is correct (Strike, Quick Shot, Smite, Magic Bolt — twelve instances across the twelve specs), and two are BOSS-PICK cards that are not basic attacks and were not on anyone's list — Ashes of Al'ar and Sweeping Strikes.

§3 — THE SECOND FLAKE IS SEEDED, AND THE BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE OTHER ONE. test_rune_battle is not unseeded: DF §0 put _seeded() immediately before the forced White Flame hit, which is the exact site that flaked, and its own baseline row records it. Nothing was owed there and nothing was done. test_batch_bo was the real one — it called seed() zero times — and its §5 NULL FIELD pair is seeded now, per-pair and not per-suite, so 1104 other checks keep their own stream. The row settles at ZERO, not at a red: six consecutive readings of 1106 checks / 0 failures, and the compared pair now reads 17 against 10 EVERY time. And the documented cause was incomplete: before the seed the same pair ranged 16–28 against 9–11 over six readings, and a ±10% roll on a mean of 18 cannot reach 28. A crit is ×1.5 and reaches exactly there — so this was at's shape, a second and larger coin behind a variance roll that was taking all the blame, which is precisely why a per-pair seed was the right instrument and a wider band would have been the wrong one.

§4 — WHAT ELSE _companion_hit MISSES: 84 TERMS, THREE READ. The hero strike loop's attacker-side block runs 84 raw-mutation sites and _companion_hit reads three of them — Mark of the Hunt, the party-wide Hunter's Mark, and Necrosis. Most of the misses are unreachable by SHAPE rather than by oversight, and the shape is in the signature: the function takes a float, not an Ability, so every term keyed on a card cannot apply; a beast carries no passive_id and no talent ranks at all, which removes most of the rest. What is left is the finding. Nine terms were driven onto a live summoned bear and every one of them attached and paid ratio 1.0000 over 40 seeded blows, DK's number exactly. Two of them can reach a beast in a real run today: an enemy's Cripple, because enemies target _hero_side() and that holds the beast — so a Crippled beast bites at full strength — and Chilled, because the Hoarfrost modifier stamps a summoned companion deliberately. REPORTED AND NOT FIXED, because each is a magnitude change on beast damage and that is new play, which is the same reason DK ruled Empower to text.

2026-08-29 — Batch DS: THE HUNTER CLASS GAP

DQ's largest structural finding, ruled and paid. The three Hunter specs held the three shallowest pools in the game (eight apiece), received none of DO's twenty-two, and not one of their twenty-four spec cards was a heal, a shield or hero-side mitigation — a hunter's entire defensive option set for a whole run was two of the six Hunter class cards he had to be lucky enough to be offered. It compounded with the Sharpshooter holding no defensive node in his 27, so both halves of his progression offered him nothing. Six cards, all three pools 8 → 10, matching the Cleric class. The draft goes 143 → 149.

§1 — SIX CARDS, TWO PER SPEC, AND EACH SPEC'S DEFENCE IS SHAPED BY ITS OWN ENGINE. That is DR's standing rule applied rather than a new one: MIT-SELF is a shared AXIS and adding it dilutes nothing, because the engine still gates every one of them.

  • BEAR THE BRUNT (Beastmaster, 20 Mana, 1.0, 4cd) — the next blow that would fell him is REFUSED and his deepest bond takes all of it, and it can kill the beast. Battle-long, waits until it fires. It is BLOODBOND exactly inverted, clause for clause, and the pair is meant to be read together on the draft screen.
  • BRING IT DOWN (Beastmaster, 25 Mana, 2.0, 5cd) — for 4 turns EVERY hero deals 2% more damage per stack of Loyalty on his deepest bond, up to +20%, snapshot at cast and the bond is not spent. AMP-TEAM, absent from all twenty-four, and the answer to a pool measured 8-of-8 on one engine: it makes the other three heroes care what the Loyalty meter reads.
  • DUG IN (Sharpshooter, 20 Mana, 1.0, 4cd) — for 4 turns he takes a quarter of whatever Focus stands when the blow lands less damage, up to 25%. Read live, so it rises as he commits and falls to nothing when a switch breaks the meter. Deliberately not evasion: Camouflage and Ghillie Suit already stack, and Camouflage's own header reserves evasion as the class's shape so it never overlaps a Barrier or a Block.
  • HEADS DOWN (Sharpshooter, 25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, 20 dmg / 8 BD) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) that enemy can bring nothing but its basic attack to bear. The first silence in the project, written as a downgrade rather than a lost turn so it is not a fourth Stun.
  • THICK HIDE (Survivalist, 20 Mana, 1.0, 4cd) — for 4 turns he takes 6% less damage per DIFFERENT affliction standing on whoever is striking him, up to 30%. The first card that reads Trapper breadth on the way IN, and Stalking Horse is what fills it.
  • SALVE (Survivalist, 25 Mana, 2.0, 5cd) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) he heals 2% of maximum health at the start of his turn per DIFFERENT affliction on the enemies, up to 10%, counted once each across the field so a copied poison does not pay twice. The first heal in any of the twenty-four Hunter spec cards, and HARVEST's deliberate inverse: that one burns the board for a burst and strips his own Trapper bonus, this drinks and consumes nothing.

§2 — THE BRIEF ASKED FOR A BREAK CARD AND THE MEASUREMENT REFUSED IT. The premise was "the Hunter class has no Break generation anywhere". Twelve of the thirty Hunter draft cards generate Break — pressure IS Break, so a card generates it without ever saying the word. UNLEASH already lands Break on the Beastmaster's own pool and FAULT LINE is a dedicated Break card the audit scores as one of the Sharpshooter's five distinct decisions. The proposed card would have been a second copy of a clause already in its own pool. AMP-TEAM was taken instead, and the rule is in CLAUDE.md: before declaring an axis ABSENT from a class, derive it from the DATA, never from the card text.

§3 — THE SHARPSHOOTER RE-AUTHOR WAS MEASURED AND DECLINED. Four of his eight cards are single-target strikes, the concentration the Swordmaster had at DR. Compared at the read site rather than by shape, they are four different decisions: Crossfire converts crits into area damage and reads no Focus at all; Trophy Shot is a decay-RULE change read inside _sharpshooter_focus's victim.dead branch; Calibrating Shot and Drumfire are the only two that are alike, both being meter GENERATION on a strike — and they are not a domination, splitting on tempo (initiative 1.5 against 3.0) and on damage. Nothing was re-authored, which is what the brief's own escape clause asked for if the four turned out distinct. One thing the audit's DMG-ST label hides is recorded instead: Trophy Shot and Reacquire are near-siblings — both are "do not lose Focus when the target changes".

§4 — TWO STALE CLAIMS CORRECTED, BOTH FOUND BY THIS BATCH'S OWN WORK. FIELD DRESSING said "The only self-heal a Hunter can get" and it was already false when BR wrote it: HARVEST heals, and it sits in the Survivalist's boss pool and in CLASS_POOLS["hunter"]. Salve would have made it wrong a third way. Corrected on the card, in classes.gd's AXIS comment and in master.html — and the tree half of the claim is TRUE and is kept: no Hunter talent node heals (Field Medic cleanses). AND THE "SIX DESIGNED ABILITIES NOT YET WRITTEN" LIST IS FOUR, NOT SIX: Field Dressing was written at BR as a CLASS-WIDE draft card rather than as the Survivalist's boss-pool one, and Smoke Bomb's function shipped at BO as Choking Smoke. DS deliberately did not spend the Sharpshooter's three reserved names (Disengage, Suppressing Fire, Piercing Arrow) on its own two draft cards, which would have paid one debt by opening another.

§5 — WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. No talent node moves — the Sharpshooter's missing defensive node is real and is not this batch's, because a cell that changes row mis-prices the ledger. Pyroblast's cooldown of zero stays open, DO's last loose end. No other pool is touched; the Cryomancer's 11-of-11 and the Pyromancer's one-currency finding are still reported and unruled. And one correction in passing: Bloodbond's master.html row contradicted itself, saying a QUARTER in one clause and "the half he takes can kill him" in the next. The code pays a quarter; the sentence is fixed.

2026-08-28 — Batch DR: THE ENGINE / AXIS FRAMEWORK, AND THE SWORDMASTER'S POOL

DQ found two grade-2 dominations and measured that the pools vary enormously. This batch repairs both, widens the most concentrated pool in the game, and records the framework the audit made visible so future pools are authored against it rather than by feel. The draft moves twice and the net is +1: 142 → 143.

§1 — THE FRAMEWORK, AND ONE OF THE THREE "EXCLUSIVE AXES" WAS NOT ONE. Recorded in CLAUDE.md: an ENGINE is the spec's own currency (stances, Loyalty, Focus, Resonance, Ruin, Faith, Mercy, Burn, Chilled, Frenzy, Block) and is exclusive by construction; an AXIS is an effect type (single-target damage, area damage, healing, shielding, mitigation, control, tempo, Break, resource generation, meter manipulation) and is shared, deliberately. A pool is one exclusive engine plus a selection of shared axes, and adding axes to a spec does not dilute its identity — the engine still gates everything.

  • COMPANION SUMMONING — the Beastmaster. TRUE, verified over the whole corpus: special: "summon" exists on exactly three abilities, all of them his protected core, and _do_summon's only other caller is his own draft card Call the Wilds.
  • REVIVAL — the Holy Cleric. TRUE AMONG ABILITIES, and the brief asked this be verified and reported. BattleUnit.revive() has two callers — resurrection (hers) and the REVIVE POTION — and the revive_pct map event is a third channel. Exclusive as an ability; not exclusive as a channel.
  • COOLDOWN MANIPULATION IS NOT THE SWORDMASTER'S, AND THE ASSERTION WAS NOT AUTHORED. The brief held that Answering Steel and Battle Poise are "the only cards in the game that do it". _tick_cooldowns has SEVEN callers: those two, BLINK — a MAGE CLASS-WIDE DRAFT CARD whose own comment names tempo as its axis, BLESSING OF ZEAL — the Devout's PROTECTED CORE, and three talent nodes (Frostbound Hours, which ticks EVERY hero's; Practised Hands; Follow-Through). Five more sites clear a cooldown outright through cooldowns.erase. What is one implementation is the FUNCTION (BQ extracted four hand-written copies); what is shared is the axis. A single implementation reads like a single owner and is not the same thing — that is the rule now recorded.

§2 — FLASH FREEZE IS RETIRED, AND THE COMMENT SUSPENDING THE RULE OVER IT WAS DELETED RATHER THAN UPDATED. DQ's Finding 1: comments and cosmetics stripped, its handler and Glacial Prison's were the same three steps in the same order, and Glacial Prison is cheaper (25 v 30), shorter on cooldown (4 v 5), faster (2.5 v 3.0) and is in RECAST_GATED where Flash Freeze was not — so the dearer card was also the only one of the two that could be spent on an enemy already held. The Cryomancer's pool goes 12 → 11.

The comment suspended "no ability may be a strictly better version of another in the same pool" for two named reasons, and both were dead: the acquisition channel died at DO and the Perfect at CR, and neither batch touched the comment. A DOCUMENTED EXCEPTION THAT OUTLIVES ITS JUSTIFICATIONS IS WORSE THAN AN UNDOCUMENTED ONE, BECAUSE IT READS AS DELIBERATE — recorded in CLAUDE.md's traps. Thirteen live sites read the card by name (classes.gd ×3, battle.gd ×5, test_batch_bt ×5 including _one_shield_door's slice anchor, test_batch_cb, test_batch_ax, check_cv, CLAUDE.md ×3, master.html ×2); none in runes, talents or the glossary. The mechanic is untouched — four Chilled stacks still flash-freeze, which is _apply_status's branch and belongs to no card.

AND ONE MORE STALE COUNT OF THE SAME SPECIES, FOUND WHILE REMOVING IT. _hold_freeze's header said THREE callers while DO's Cryoclasm had quietly made it four, and named a force argument no caller has passed since CR. Corrected with its reason.

§3 — BATTLE POISE: THE DEFENSIVE GUARD BUYS A FREE GUARD CHANGE. DQ's Finding 2 was that its whole payload was a subset of Answering Steel's — cheaper (20 v 25), longer (6 turns v 4), ungated, paying the same _tick_cooldowns constant plus +20% parry and 15 Rage a parry. Its stance requirement was pure cost with nothing bought by it. ONCE A TURN, A PARRY NOW LETS HIM GUARD CHANGE WITHOUT SPENDING AN ACTION. Answering Steel cannot have it — it has no requirement to reward — so the two are no longer nested, and the stacking-partners comment at the parry site stands: it answered do these combine and never answered which do you take.

  • THE PIVOT ONLY, _swordmaster_switch. Guard Change's own payload — its 15 BD, SUNDER GUARD's 40 BD to every enemy, No Quarter, Tempo — stays on that card. A Defensive Swordmaster holding Sunder Guard and parrying twice a turn would otherwise land 80 free Break damage across the field every turn.
  • ONCE A TURN, not once a parry, and it does not bank. The cooldown tick stays and still pays on every parry.
  • IT ASKS _ability_usable ABOUT THE REAL GUARD CHANGE — the same door — which makes three promises true at once and keeps them from disagreeing: FORMLESS refuses it (there is no stance to change), Guard Change's own 1-turn cooldown is respected, and it starts that cooldown, because respecting a cooldown a use does not pay into is respecting it exactly once.
  • THE PIVOT IS NOT FREE OF CONSEQUENCE: it throws away DISCIPLINE's accumulation, like every other call to the one pivot. A Discipline build wants it refused and gets that by not holding the card.

§4 — THE SWORDMASTER GAINS FOUR AXES ON THREE CARDS, 10 → 12. DQ measured his as the most concentrated pool in the game: ten cards making four decisions — strike one enemy (four), change or hold a stance (three), buy tempo off a parry (two), execute (one) — so a player who had drafted four had seen everything it decides. Every one of the three reads the stance engine, because that is what makes it his, and BW's rule decides how: READERS BRANCH AND FLIP; GATED ONES REQUIRE AND STAY.

  • LUNGE, RE-AUTHORED ONTO BREAK — the sharpest gap in the pool. An entire BREAKER lane is built around a Break window (Punishment, Off Balance, Guard Breaker, Overpressure, No Quarter all live inside it, and Sever's cooldown clears against a Broken target so it can be swung through) and not one draft card opened it. Two changes and nothing else moved: cooldown 0 → 3 — of 142 cards only it and Pyroblast repeated every turn, where all twelve cooldown-zero abilities in the protected cores are the free basic attack, and at the end of a lane the price was the node — and the guard now decides where the Break lands: AGGRESSIVE puts 15 more into that one enemy, DEFENSIVE puts 12 on every other enemy, because he does not overreach and the recovery leaves the whole line off balance.
