Damage 35 → 30, because it is a Break card now; Shatterpoint keeps its title as his heaviest single Break blow at 40. THE BRIEF SAID SHATTERPOINT IS A TALENT AND IT IS NOT — it is a SPEC_POOLS boss pick, which is why the lane depended on an offer he may never see. The card stays an ORDINARY ATTACK (a special would hand-roll the blow and lose the crit, the armour read, the parry roll, Overwhelm, Off Balance and Whetstone), and both riders read _eff_stance beside the wound it already left.
  • WHEELING CUT — AREA DAMAGE and SELF-MITIGATION, the two axes on one card. 30 Rage, 2.5, 4cd, every enemy takes 20% of Attack and 12 Break. His pool had no area damage at all; his only field-wide option for a whole run was Cleave out of the Warrior class pool. A reader, so BP's arriving-stance principle decides both branches — the thing that would most easily be got backwards: cast from AGGRESSIVE he lands DEFENSIVE, so it hands him defence (20% less damage taken, 3 turns); cast from DEFENSIVE he lands AGGRESSIVE, so it hands him offence (+20% damage dealt, 3 turns). Perfect: both guards' gifts at once — it runs a bar, so test_batch_bo §5's biconditional requires it to state one, and this batch adds no third name to DO's two debts there.
  • COUNTER TIME — CONTROL, and his pool could not take an enemy's turn away at all. 25 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, requires the Defensive guard: one enemy loses its next TWO turns and the card deals nothing. Pommel Strike is his only Stun and it is protected core, so a whole run's control was one core ability's one-turn rider. It is not a second Pommel Strike: that card is cheaper, ungated, deals 25% of Attack, lands 30 Break, builds Rage and Stuns for ONE turn; this buys a SECOND turn for a stance and a whole action that pays nothing. The boss rule is inherited, not re-written — stunned is one of the five ids _apply_status's carve-out refuses on an unbroken boss and this passes no force. It joins RECAST_GATED (its entire payload is a status, so a recast onto a saturated field buys nothing); Wheeling Cut deliberately does not, because a card that deals damage is never a wasted cast.

PRECISION STRIKE AND FEINT ARE UNTOUCHED — BW's original readers, and the branch-and-flip pattern is the spec's signature. His pool now makes eight decisions across twelve cards where it made four across ten.

§5 — WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. No other pool is touched: the Beastmaster's 8-of-8 companion binding, the Cryomancer's remaining 11-of-11 ice and the Pyromancer's one-currency problem are reported and unruled. The Hunter class gap is not addressed — three shallowest pools, none of DO's twenty-two, and not one of its twenty-four spec cards is a heal, a shield or mitigation. It is bigger than the Swordmaster's and it is next, not now. NO TALENT MOVES. No cell changes row or lane, so no migration is needed, and no save version moves. Pyroblast is still cooldown-zero and that ruling stays open.

§6 — VERIFICATION. check_dr.gd joins GATES (22 now) and asserts the exclusives as PROPERTIES, never as counts — DN's gate asserted two and there were five, DO's brief nine and there were twenty-two, and this batch's own brief asserted three exclusive axes when one of the three was false. It drives all three cards and Battle Poise's free pivot on a live board. FOUR NEGATIVE CONTROLS WERE RUN AND ALL FOUR BEHAVED: a summon authored onto the Sharpshooter, a third revive call site, a cooldown site removed, and the comment-stripping trap controlled from BOTH sides — the retired card's name put back as a COMMENT left the gate GREEN, the same name put back in CODE turned it RED. The BR §1 name sweep was run for both new names against 1,127 labels (every ability, talent node, status and rune) and both come back clean on exact match, containment and shared word.

2026-08-28 — Batch DQ: DO THE DRAFT POOLS ACTUALLY CONTAIN DIFFERENT BUILDS?

A REPORT. NOTHING WAS RETIRED, RE-AUTHORED OR RETUNED. All 142 draft cards compared against every card they can be offered beside, against the protected core kit of the hero who would be offered them, and against that hero's talent tree. The comparison is on what the card DOES — handler bodies lifted out of _resolve_special with comments and every cosmetic call stripped, plus the read sites of the 27 cards whose whole handler is a self-flag. The audit is docs/draft-audit.html; this entry is the summary.

§1 — TWO GRADE-2 FINDINGS, AND BOTH ARE THE STANDING RULE NOT BEING ENFORCED. classes.gd already says "NO ABILITY MAY BE A STRICTLY BETTER VERSION OF ANOTHER IN THE SAME POOL", so these are correctness rather than taste.

  • GLACIAL PRISON AND FLASH FREEZE ARE ONE CARD AT TWO PRICES. Comments and cosmetics stripped, both handlers are the same three steps in the same order: apply 3 Chilled if the target has none, note the debuff, _hold_freeze. Flash Freeze computes one extra local and uses it only inside its log string. Glacial Prison is cheaper (25 against 30), shorter on cooldown (4 against 5), faster (2.5 against 3.0), and it is in RECAST_GATED while Flash Freeze is not — so the dearer card is also the only one of the two that can be spent on an enemy already held. Batch DO created this and nothing else did: Glacial Prison was a talent grant in no pool until DO moved it into the pool Flash Freeze had held since CB.
  • BATTLE POISE'S ENTIRE PAYLOAD IS A SUBSET OF ANSWERING STEEL'S. Both are Swordmaster self-flags; both fire at the same parry site eleven lines apart; both call _tick_cooldowns with a constant of 1. Answering Steel is cheaper (20 against 25), lasts 6 turns against 4, has no stance requirement at all, and adds +20% parry chance and 15 Rage a parry. There is no board state in which Battle Poise is the better pick. The source comment calls the two "DELIBERATE STACKING PARTNERS rather than rivals", which is a good reason to hold both and not a reason for the pool to OFFER both. This one predates DO, and the source shows why it was missed: Answering Steel's own comment names Battle Poise as "the deliberate stacking partner rather than a rival". It asks whether the two stack and never asks which of the two you take, and a three-card offer only ever asks the second question.

§2 — AND THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THAT MATTERS IS THAT THE POOLS VARY ENORMOUSLY, IN TWO MEASURES THAT DISAGREE. Each pool was scored on distinct decisions (effect axis × target shape — how many cards a player must draft before the pool stops offering anything new) and on engine dependence (how many cards read or write the spec's own system). The two disagree on the Pyromancer and both readings are true.

  • THE SWORDMASTER IS THE MOST CONCENTRATED POOL IN THE GAME: TEN CARDS, FOUR DECISIONS. Strike one enemy, change or hold a stance, buy tempo off a parry, or execute. Four cards see all of it, and his healing, area damage, control and party buff are all in the Warrior class pool — his own spec pool holds none of the four.
  • THE BEASTMASTER IS 8 OF 8 ON ONE ENGINE. Every card requires a living companion or reads its Loyalty. Not one card in his pool does anything for the hunter himself — no mitigation, no heal, no shield, no control, no Break, no tempo.
  • THE CRYOMANCER IS 12 OF 12 ON THE ICE, and none of DO's four opened a new decision — the pool already spread Chilled, already froze, already relocated and already cashed a hold.
  • THE PYROMANCER COVERS THE MOST DECISIONS (10 of 13) AND IS THE MOST NARROWLY BOUND (12 of 13 touch Burn). Overburn's multiplier is literally _total_burn_turns(), so five of the thirteen are the same lever on the passive's own input at five prices. Ten things to decide, one currency to decide them in.
  • THE WARDEN IS THE HEALTHIEST: NINE CARDS, NINE DECISIONS — no two make the same one, the only pool in the game of which that is true. But four of the nine hang off one trigger (a block), and two of those four cancel each other by design.
  • THE CLASS POOLS ARE THE HEALTHIEST THING IN THE DRAFT AND THE AUDIT SAYS SO. The authoring rule — untied and general, feeds no passive — is honoured at 0 of 24, and three of the four cover six decisions with six cards, which no spec pool does.

§3 — THE DISTRIBUTION OF DO's TWENTY-TWO LANDED ON CLASS LINES AND NOBODY ASKED FOR IT. Derived from the BATCH DO markers in classes.gd: the spec half went 96 → 118, the Mage took nine of the twenty-two and the Hunter took none. The deepest pool is now 62% deeper than the shallowest and the three shallowest are the three Hunter specs. Not one of the twenty-four Hunter spec cards is a heal, a shield, or mitigation for the hero — which lines up with the standing note that the Sharpshooter has no defensive node in his 27, so both halves of his progression offer him nothing defensive at all.

§4 — A COOLDOWN OF ZERO MEANS SOMETHING IN THIS GAME AND TWO DRAFT CARDS HAVE ONE. All twelve cooldown-zero abilities in the protected cores are the hero's free basic attack. Of 142 draft cards exactly two are repeatable every turn — Pyroblast and Lunge — and both are DO's. That is the shape of a talent grant arriving intact: at the end of a lane the price was the node, so no cooldown was needed to bound it. Pyroblast is simultaneously the dearest card in the draft (45), the slowest (6.0), joint-hardest-hitting (55) and repeatable.

§5 — NINE READ-ONLY-ZERO FIELDS WERE RECORDED AT DO AND THERE ARE TEN. icy_resolve_ranks is read twice — Rime's duration is 4 + attacker.icy_resolve_ranks, and the recast preview quotes the same expression — and nothing in the project writes it. cr_icy_resolve still exists and DO re-pointed it onto Blizzard for exactly the right reason; the field it used to write was left behind. Nothing is wrong at runtime (zero is the base) and no gate catches it, which is the FIREDRAW_TAKE shape.

§6 — THE CORE-KIT CHECK HAD NEVER BEEN RUN AND IT IS WHERE THE SECOND-LARGEST CROP IS. docs/state.md has carried "No spec pool has ever been checked for redundancy against its own base kit" as an open item. The sharpest result is KILLING FROST against BLIZZARD: the drafted card is cheaper, faster, shorter on cooldown, higher in damage and lays more Chilled (a flat 2 against a 1–2 roll) than the core ability the Cryomancer can never drop. Its one limitation is that it touches only already-Chilled enemies, and his free basic attack applies Chilled. Mind Flay against Hex of Ruin is the same story one spec over: the core card is cheaper, faster and hits one more enemy, and the whole difference is Exposed against Psychosis. Arcane Bolt, Unmaking and Death Ray are three cards on one decision and Resonance has no maximum, so the drafted one overtakes the core one at 15 stacks.

§7 — AND THE TALENT HALF CAME BACK CLEAN ON THE SHAPE THAT MATTERED, DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Thirty-six nodes carry an "ability" payload and ZERO point at a drafted card — all thirty-six name a protected core ability, including the nine whose node id still names the ability DO moved. The finding there is smaller and is player-facing: three of the five nodes named after live abilities share a draw space with their namesake and do something different from it — a Cryomancer can hold a talent called Killing Frost and a card called Killing Frost at once.

§8 — NO CLAUDE.md RULE WAS ADDED AND NO GATE WAS WRITTEN. Nothing is settled until the report is read, and a gate encodes a ruling. No .gd file was touched at all, which is why the parse floor is met by construction and the battery is a regression check on the documentation rather than on the code.

2026-08-27 — Batch DP: THE MADNESS LANE COMES OFF THE DRAW

DO's OWN COST, PAID. Mind Flay and Mass Hysteria are the only appliers of Psychosis and Hysteria in the game, and DO moved both into the draft — so four Occultist Madness cells read a status he can no longer guarantee. Before DO those dependencies were TREE-INTERNAL, which the charter explicitly permits: a ruling created this without anyone making a mistake. All four are re-pointed onto RUIN, his own passive, guaranteed in every run. NO CELL CHANGES ROW OR LANE, so no save migration is needed and Profile is still v2.

§0 — THE BRIEF SAID "THE OTHER EIGHT" AND THERE ARE SIX, WHICH IS WHY EVERY BRIEF IS TOLD TO DERIVE. check_do §4 printed twelve node/status pairs across eight nodes, and the Occultist's four cells account for six of the twelve, not four — oc_delirium and oc_permanent each read TWO un-guaranteed statuses. That leaves six pre-existing pairs, which is what docs/state.md said and what the brief did not. The sweep is 12 → 6 now.

§1 — AND FOUR OF THE SIX SURVIVORS ARE INSTRUMENT ARTEFACTS RATHER THAN BETS. The sweep matches a rendered WORD, so it cannot tell a node READING a status from a node APPLYING one: sv_virulence ("Your Poison applications … apply Exposed for 3 turns") and ss_exposed_nerve ("Critical hits apply Exposed … and you deal +15% damage to Exposed enemies") are each their OWN source. Nor can it tell an enemy's debuff landing on the HERO from a hero's landing on an enemy: ss_no_cover is an IMMUNITY ("Blind and Dazed do not affect you"). Only sm_guarded is a real bet, and it is a bonus clause gated on sm_punish — a TREE-INTERNAL condition the charter permits — sitting beside an unconditional "vs Broken" base clause, so the node cannot go dead. Ruled on: none, as the brief instructed. Each of the six is carried in check_dp.KNOWN_PAIRS with the reason it is tolerated.

§2 — THE FOUR, AND THEY READ FOUR DIFFERENT THINGS ON PURPOSE. Four cells all reading "stacks of Ruin" would flatten a lane authored as a theme into one idea repeated four times, so each reads a different quantity — and none of the four reads a DETONATION, because Grim Focus (Ruin 5), Unraveling (Ruin 7) and Avatar of Ruin (Ruin 9) already own that event. check_dp §2 asserts the four are distinct.

  • Spread of Madness (row 1) — reads an APPLICATION, probabilistically. Was: Psychosis leaps to a fellow at 60% a turn. Is: "Each mark of Ruin the Occultist lands has a 60% chance to leap to another enemy, which catches 2 Ruin." It fires on a mark LANDING where Unraveling fires on a DETONATION, so the lane's two propagation nodes never read the same event.
  • Whispers (row 2) — reads an APPLICATION MAGNITUDE. Was: +45 percentage points on Psychosis's 50% seize chance. Is: "Every debuff the Occultist applies marks 4 Ruin instead of the base 2." This is the lever AY §8 identified as the real constraint — generation, not the threshold — and the field keeps its _step name because it keeps its SHAPE: an increase on a base the kit already pays. Only the base moved, from Psychosis's 50% to OLD_GODS_MARK.
  • Delirium (row 5) — reads an EVENT, and NOT ONE LINE OF CODE CHANGED. Its text named Psychotic and Hysterical; its read site names no status and never has (not attacker.is_hero and not strike_target.is_hero). The text now says what the code does — and says it in oc_cackling's words, one row down, because the same trigger deserves the same sentence. It was NOT narrowed to "Bewitched": that would UNDER-state the payload the moment Mind Flay is drafted, which is DM's seventh family, and an absent clause does not mis-say so no test catches it.
  • Ruined Mind (row 8, was Permanent Delusion) — reads the STACK COUNT, as a threshold. Was: Psychosis, Bewitchment and Hysteria never expire — two thirds of it a bet. Is: "A boss bearing 10 or more Ruin can no longer resist the Occultist's Bewitchment." This is the row-8 shape exactly: it REMOVES THE CONSTRAINT THE LANE HAS WORKED AROUND ALL GAME, stated in the lane's own header. It is self-enabling by construction and nothing had to be added to make that true — the boss refuses the charm inside _apply_status, but the bewitch handler marks Ruin on the very next line regardless, so a REFUSED cast still deepens the mark that eventually opens the gate.

§3 — THE COST THE BRIEF DID NOT NAME: A RUNE WRITES TWO OF THESE FIELDS. The Rune of the Whispering Dark (100g, spec:occultist) writes spread_ranks AND spread_ruin and its card sells both clauses. Re-pointing Spread of Madness onto a fresh field name would have left two of that rune's four clauses paying nothing, in silence — the exact dud the rune schema exists to prevent. Both fields were KEPT and their MEANING re-pointed instead, which cost one line of card text and no payload edit at all. check_dp §4 now asserts the general property: every stat field any rune writes has a live read site in scripts/ — 116 fields across 65 runes, 0 dead.

§4 — ONE CONSTANT, FIVE CALL SITES, AND A FUNCTION BETWEEN THEM. OLD_GODS_MARK is the passive's mark and was quoted at five _gain_ruin calls, every one of them "the passive marking a debuff the Occultist applied" — the constant's own comment says so. Whispers moves that number, so the five call _old_gods_mark() now: _ruin_threshold()'s shape exactly, which Avatar of Ruin has used since AX. The base stays the one authored copy, and check_dp §3 asserts no _gain_ruin call quotes it directly, so a sixth passive site cannot be added that the node silently fails to reach. Deepening the mark inside _gain_ruin instead would have inflated Delirium, Unraveling and Spread of Madness off one node, because all three pass their OWN counts to it.

§5 — A CONTAGION THROUGH THE FUNCTION THAT MARKS IT NEEDS A GUARD, AND IDENTITY IS NOT ENOUGH. Covenant of Ash already recurses through _gain_ruin and breaks the recursion BY IDENTITY — the ash always lands on ONE known bearer, so mirror == target stops it. A contagion lands on a RANDOM enemy and has no such property, so _ruin_spreading is the equivalent. It is bounded rather than absolute and that is stated rather than glossed: a covenant mirror re-enters before the flag is ever set, so the ceiling is two contagion rolls per originating mark and no chain can run past them. The spread goes THROUGH _gain_ruin, which is the point — a caught mark arms the threshold, deepens the chip and books the AX depth reading exactly as a directly-applied one does.

§6 — THE BOSS-IMMUNITY EXCEPTION LIVES INSIDE THE REFUSAL, NOT IN ITS CONDITION, AND THAT IS NOT COSMETIC. test_batch_ah §4 and test_batch_ax §4 both pin that if line as a literal, because the boss rule is the kind of promise a later batch could dissolve by widening one condition. An exception spliced into the line would have moved the needle out from under both suites; nested inside the refusal, both literals survive untouched. The exception is scoped three ways and every one matters: to bewitch alone (the only one of the three statuses he can apply without drawing a card, and the only one his node's text names), to a HERO src holding the node (an enemy's charm still meets the boss's own immunity), and to a target already bearing the depth.

§7 — THE TWO LIVE DUPLICATIONS ARE RESOLVED, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THAT QUESTION IS ANSWERED "NO". dv_resolve and oc_mind_flay no longer grant, the runes keep their grants, and all four rune grants still resolve — a rune's grant goes through Classes.pending_talent_ability and NOT the draft resolver, so DO moving twenty-two card NAMES into SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS while the six grant_ability DEFINITIONS stayed put is the only reason nothing went dead. But "no rune now duplicates a draft card's grant" is FALSE, and this is a state the game could not previously reach: Binding Souls grants Sacred Resolve and the Flayed Mind grants Mind Flay, and both cards are draftable by their spec since DO. Holding both is not a wasted rune — measured, not reasoned: the grant collides, _collided finds no authored upgrade arm and no no_fallback, so the rune owes its generic and Run.apply_upgrades (which runs last) turns it into an upgrade on the very card it would have granted — Honed (×1.5 damage) for Mind Flay, Quickened (−2 cooldown) for Sacred Resolve. That is the Rune of the Last Rites' shipped behaviour since AV, now reachable by two more runes. OWED, NOT TAKEN: both descs still open "Grants …", which is wrong whenever the card was drafted — the Last Rites is the one that says so honestly ("She already knows Resurrection, so this hones it instead").

§8 — ONE NEW GATE, check_dp.gd, AND IT READS check_do's TABLES RATHER THAN COPYING THEM. GUARANTEED_STATUS and STATUS_FORMS are hand-authored maps of what each spec can reach without a draw, and a second copy would be this project's oldest recurring defect wearing a new hat. The load is asserted, so the day that file moves the gate says so rather than sweeping against an empty table. It asserts the PROPERTY and PRINTS the count, and its ratchet is asymmetric for baselines.json's reason one layer up: a pair not in KNOWN_PAIRS is an ERROR; a known pair that has GONE is a NOTICE, because that is a repair and a gate that reds on a repair teaches the next batch to leave the defect alone. It needs no check_da WALK_EXEMPT entry — it reads only the SPEC draft pool — and its header does not name the other call either, which is the self-accusation trap DO paid 37/2 to learn.

§9 — NINE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, AND ALL NINE BEHAVED. Each of the four cells had its old text restored (5, 5, 6 and 6 failures); the Ruined Mind read site was defeated (3); the Whispering Dark's spread_ruin was renamed, standing in for the dud the batch nearly shipped (5); and a sixth _gain_ruin call was made to quote the constant directly (3). THE COMMENT-STRIPPING TRAP WAS CONTROLLED FROM BOTH SIDES, WHICH IS DO's SCAR: a COMMENT naming the retired permanent_delusion left the gate green (comments are stripped, as they must be — prose recording a removal necessarily names what was removed), and the same identifier added as CODE turned it red. Every probed file was restored from a scratchpad copy and re-compared by MD5, never git checkout.

§10 — WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. No cell moves row or lane, so no save migration is needed and Profile is still v2 — DN measured a move driving a full Berserker ledger to −2 available points, silently. The 97-node restructure is not taken; three-ways-playable remains a separate, undecided goal. sm_lunge is not restored — it left the tree at DO, and sm_precision was re-pointed onto Stunned, which Pommel Strike applies. The six pre-existing pairs are reported and ruled on nowhere. No magnitude was re-derived by measurement: Spread of Madness keeps 60/2 and Delirium keeps 3, so the Whispering Dark's +15/+1 keeps its proportion, and Whispers's +2 doubles a base of 2 as its old +45 nearly doubled a base of 50. Both nodes now feed generation and they stack, which is the number most worth a sim — and no sim has been run since DK, so every sim figure in docs/state.md was already stale before this batch touched anything.

2026-08-27 — Batch DO: TALENTS STOP GRANTING ABILITIES, AND STOP BETTING ON THE DRAW

THE CHARTER IS SETTLED AND IMPLEMENTED. A talent may not grant an ability, and may not depend on an ability the hero is not guaranteed to have; a talent modifying the spec's PROTECTED CORE is guaranteed and permitted, which is the ruling that settles DN's §0-versus-§1 contradiction and is worth 83 nodes. NO LANE IS RENAMED, NO TREE IS RESTRUCTURED, AND NO NODE CHANGES ROW OR LANE — DN's 97-node restructure is NOT taken here, and because nothing moves a cell, no save migration is needed and Profile is still v2.

§0 — TWENTY-TWO NODES GRANTED AN ABILITY, NOT NINE, AND THE BRIEF'S OWN RULE IS WHAT CATCHES THE OTHER THIRTEEN. DN reported "nine grant a new ability outright" about the 36 capstones; the brief generalised that to the whole layer. Talents.LANE_TREES holds 22 ability-granting nodes — nine in row 9 and thirteen in rows 2, 3 and 4. All twenty-two are taken, on the designer's ruling.

§1 — THE RUNE CHECK, RUN BEFORE ANYTHING MOVED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO BY ONE ROW. Four runes grant an ability and the brief names all four correctly: Comet carries a new_ability; Binding Souls, the Last Rites and the Flayed Mind carry a grant_ability. NOT ONE OF THEM NAMES A CAPSTONE GRANT. But two name a grant from the thirteen the brief's list does not reach: Binding Souls and dv_resolve both granted Sacred Resolve, and the Flayed Mind and oc_mind_flay both granted Mind Flay — two live duplications, and the Flayed Mind's own lane field says "Madness", the lane its twin sits in. Both are resolved by the move: the rune keeps its grant, the talent does not. Runes may still grant, and that is the distinction the charter is built on — a rune is BOUGHT with knowledge of the run in front of you; a talent is chosen before the run knowing nothing.

§2 — THE TWENTY-TWO ABILITIES MOVED INTO THE DRAFT, VERBATIM, AND THE DRAFT WENT 120 → 142. SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS is 118 (was 96) and the whole draft is 142 of 142. The floor is still EIGHT and no pool lost anything: nine specs are deeper than eight, and the Beastmaster, Sharpshooter and Survivalist still read exactly eight because their trees granted nothing to move. Per spec — berserker 10, warden 9, swordmaster 10, pyromancer 13, cryomancer 12, arcanist 10, holy 10, inquisitor 10, occultist 10. SIXTEEN DEFINITIONS ACTUALLY MOVED AND SIX DID NOT: the six grant_ability nodes named a card defined in Classes.pending_talent_ability already, outside the tree. The sixteen new_ability nodes carried their whole definition INSIDE the payload — and eight of those were reachable ONLY through pool_ability's fall-through to the trees, so deleting a payload would silently have emptied a SPEC_POOLS entry the zone boss offers. They were lifted out whole: not one number, special, perfect_id or line of description was re-typed. The ability corpus is still 216 and nothing became unresolvable.

§3 — TWENTY-FIVE CELLS RE-AUTHORED, EVERY ONE KEEPING ITS ID, ITS LANE AND ITS ROW. Twenty-two are the granting nodes; three more read a drawn ability outright (bm_devoted_fury on Bestial Wrath, bm_reserves on Spirit Bond, and cr_icy_resolve, which read Rime — a card that left the tree in this same batch). EVERY REPLACEMENT MODIFIES THE SPEC'S PROTECTED CORE, ITS PASSIVE OR ITS RESOURCE, AND NOT ONE NEEDED A NEW battle.gd READ SITE — apply_payload's {"ability": …, "add"/"set": …} branch has been the mechanism since Batch AI and nine nodes already used it. ar_wrath lost almost nothing: its step-doubling was an also payload beside the grant and is the whole node now, with wrath_step_double's name, unit and single read site untouched, so AU §4's negative control still bites.

§4 — FOUR CLAUSE-CUTS, AND THE PAYLOAD TERM GOES WITH THE TEXT EVERY TIME. sm_blade_dance loses its Shatterpoint rider, wd_stomp_drill its War Stomp rider and wd_bannerman its Interpose rider — each named a SPEC_POOLS trophy, so each paid only a hero who had DRAWN one. sunder_guard_bd, rallying_stomp_ranks and bulwark_line_ranks are deleted outright, field and read site together, and check_do §3 asserts all three are absent from the whole of scripts/. Four more cuts came from the move itself: dv_waters and dv_pulse stop reading Sacred Resolve's banner (Consecrated Ground is protected core and is the whole condition now), sm_seasoned_node stops sharpening Lunge, and ar_conduit's clause is RE-POINTED rather than cut — its partner is still a node in its own tree, one row up, renamed Unchained. bm_ancient_pact is the one where the brief's blanket rule does not apply: it names Spirit Bond in an illustrative list, its single ancient_pact term carries both halves, and battle.gd refuses ALL healing rather than naming a source — so the text is corrected and there is no payload term to remove.

§5 — sm_precision WAS WORSE THAN THE BRIEF THOUGHT, AND THIS BATCH IS WHY. It read "Dazed, Crippled and Exposed" and the Swordmaster guarantees none of the three: Dazed comes only from Charge (class draft) or Sweeping Strikes (a SPEC_POOLS trophy), and Crippled and Exposed came only from sm_lunge — which left the tree in this same batch, taking the last non-drawn source with it. So cutting Dazed alone was never the whole repair, and by the end of the batch it was none of it. Re-pointed onto STUNNED, which POMMEL STRIKE applies and Pommel Strike is protected core; the battle.gd read site moved with the text.

§6 — THE STATUS SWEEP: TWELVE PAIRS, REPORTED AND RULED ON NOWHERE, AND SIX OF THEM ARE THIS BATCH'S OWN. check_do §4 prints every node reading a status its own spec cannot guarantee. Six are pre-existing — sm_guarded (Crippled, Exposed), sv_virulence (Exposed), ss_exposed_nerve (Exposed), ss_no_cover (Dazed, Blind). SIX WERE CREATED BY THIS BATCH AND ARE NAMED AS SUCH: Psychosis and Hysteria have no applier in the game but Mind Flay and Mass Hysteria, and both moved into the draft, so oc_spread, oc_whispers, oc_delirium and oc_permanent read a status the Occultist can no longer guarantee. Before DO those were TREE-INTERNAL dependencies, which the charter permits; the move converted them into draws. The brief says "report the list; rule on nothing", so nothing is ruled — but the cost is the ruling's, not an oversight, and it is in the open queue.

§7 — WHAT THE MOVE COSTS, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: nine abilities lost their upgraded variant. An upgrade arm fires only where a node's grant COLLIDES with an earned copy. No node grants, so battle_shout_node, lunge_upgraded, execute_upgraded, hold_line_upgraded, rampage_upgraded, overcharge_extra, intercession_long, resolve_extra_turns and bulwark_extra_turns are read-only-zero. The fields and read sites are LEFT STANDING — each reads a base beside it, deleting a branch is deleting a mechanic, and two are in runes.gd's coercion list already. ONE CARD TEXT MOVED AND IT CLOSES A DEFECT DM RECORDED: Battle Shout's description promised "+12% … Lasts 3 turns", which were battle_shout_node's magnitudes — index 1 of [8, 12, 18]. There is one magnitude now and the card states it: +8%, 2 turns.

§8 — A HOLE THE PROJECT HAS CARRIED SINCE BATCH CL IS CLOSED AS A SIDE EFFECT, AND check_cz's OWN FAILURE MESSAGE IS THE ONE THAT CAME TRUE. The Batch CL enumeration reached 211 of 216; the five it missed — Backdraft, Pyroblast, Glacial Prison, Cryoclasm, Intercession — were talent grants living in no pool. All five are in a draft pool now, so the two walks agree. §0's assertion read "%s IS in the CL walk — §0's premise has changed and the report is stale", had never fired in eight batches, and is INVERTED rather than deleted: it fires as its opposite now, so a batch that put one of the five back outside every pool is still caught.

§9 — ONE NEW GATE, check_do.gd, AND IT ASSERTS THE PROPERTY AND PRINTS THE COUNT. DN's own gate asserted a NUMBER and its first battery caught it, costing a second frozen run; this one asserts no node grants and no node names an ability outside its protected core, and prints 324 nodes / 0 granting / 98 naming a protected core / 1 naming its own tree / 0 naming something drawn beside them. It deliberately does not call Classes.class_draft_pool(, so it needs no check_da WALK_EXEMPT entry at all — which is better than having one, and is DN's lesson paid forward. It is in GATES and owes a baseline row.

§10 — NAMING, AND THE TRAP THAT WAS AVOIDED RATHER THAN HIT. A node named "Overcharge" beside a draft card called Overcharge is exactly the wd_spiked/Spite collision DN documented. The Arcanist's row-4 Resonance cell is Overdraw for that reason. Five nodes were already named after live abilities before DO — Second Wind, Spite, Rally, Killing Frost, Divine Presence — and DO added no sixth.

2026-08-27 — Batch DN: THE TALENT NODES AGAINST THE NEW CHARTER

A REPORT. NOTHING WAS RE-AUTHORED, NO TREE WAS RESTRUCTURED, NO NODE MOVED. The charter under audit: twelve trees, each Offense / Defense / Utility, where a talent may be general in only two ways — a STAT, or the spec's OWN resource and passive — because a talent chosen blind that depends on what you are later DEALT is a bet, not a build. DN reads all 324 nodes a second time (CU read them for text-against-code; this reads them for guaranteed-against-drawn) and the two halves of the answer disagree, which IS the finding. THE CONTENT IS ALMOST CLEAN: six of 324 depend on something drawn, and only TWO are dead without the draw (bm_devoted_fury and bm_reserves, both whole nodes about a SPEC_POOLS ability). THE SHAPE CANNOT BE BUILT FROM THEM: ZERO of twelve specs can fill three nine-cell lanes, and 97 new nodes — 30% of the talent layer — would have to be authored. Two specs hold a lane at zero: the Cleric has no offensive node and the Sharpshooter no defensive one, so even a three-cell tree leaves them short and no shrinking rescues it. TWO OF THE BRIEF'S COUNTS ARE WRONG AGAINST THE REPO — there are 36 capstones, not twelve (row 9 is three lanes wide), and CV cut THREE dead Perfect clauses, not four, this document's own disposition table having ruled dv_bulwark's heal unconditional rather than dead. The charter contradicts itself about 75 nodes: its §0 permits only a stat or the passive, its §1 permits a protected-core ability too, and the gap between those readings is 235 clean versus 318 clean. The saved-allocation risk was MEASURED rather than reasoned about — moving one node from row 1 to row 9 drives a full Berserker ledger to −2 available points, silently, with version still stamped 2. One new instrument, check_dn.gd (read-only, not in GATES, like check_cu and check_cv). No CLAUDE.md rule is added: the charter is not settled until the audit is read. The audit is a new §8 inside docs/talent-audit.html rather than a second document, so both readings of the same 324 sit together; the report is docs/reports/DN.md.

2026-08-23 — Batch DM: THE SIX SPLIT-CLAUSE CARDS, AND THE ALLY/HERO THREAD CLOSES

DL listed six more cards carrying clauses of two different shapes under one word and ruled on none of them. DM reads all six clause by clause — sixteen clauses, fourteen of which carry a collection — and ALL FOURTEEN COLLECTIONS WERE ALREADY CORRECT. The two clauses that mis-said were of a third scope this thread had no word for: Battle Shout and Hold the Line each hand five Rage to the CASTER, one body, and Battle Shout's card put it inside "A roar every hero answers:". Hold the Line already worded the identical payload correctly, so the fix was to copy the sibling card rather than invent a phrasing. Every hero ruling on the six now carries its structural reason in the source beside it, and DL's own Consecrated Ground correction had left four prose copies behind — three in master.html, one in the glossary — still saying ally for a clause _gain_faith refuses outright. NO GAME CODE MOVED: the diff to battle.gd is comments. No save version moves (still v10). One new gate, check_dm (92 checks). The ally/hero thread is CLOSED. The full report is docs/reports/DM.md.

§1 — The six, clause by clause

  • THE FOURTEEN COLLECTIONS WERE RIGHT AND THAT IS THE BATCH'S PRINCIPAL MEASUREMENT. Bulwark of Fortitude 4, Consecrated Ground 3, Divine Wrath 2, Battle Shout 1 group, Hold the Line 2 group, Sacred Resolve 2 — each says what its read site walks. A batch that finds nothing to widen has still measured something, and this is what lets the thread close rather than be abandoned.
  • BATTLE SHOUT'S RAGE CLAUSE WAS THE ONE REAL DISAGREEMENT, AND IT IS A SCOPE NEITHER WORD COVERS. The card read "A roar every hero answers: +12% damage, plus 1% per 20 blood buildup on the warband, and 5 Rage." — the Rage sits in the group clause's colon-list and is paid to exactly one unit. It now reads "Refunds 5 Rage." as its own sentence, which is Hold the Line's existing wording for the identical payload. check_co and check_cy have both recorded it as "hands the caster +5 Rage" since CO; the card was the only surface that disagreed. Measured: one shout, one unit paid, caster +5.
  • AND CV §1's DURATION RULING HAD REACHED HOLD THE LINE'S NODE TEXT AND NOT ITS CARD. CV moved wd_hold_line's no-death window 1/2 → 2/3 — and the description inside that node's own payload still said "for a turn" and "for two turns" against the 2 and 3 the code applies. That is cr_rime's shape exactly, the one CU found. Both card lines now state the applied number. No code moved and no sweep was opened — this is CV's ruling reaching the one surface it missed, on a card this batch was reading clause by clause anyway.
  • EVERY hero CLAUSE NOW CARRIES ITS REASON AT ITS SITE. Five reasons and no sixth: no resource bar to refuel; _companion_hit reads none of the hero strike loop's multiplier block; stamped once where the four are built, before a companion exists; per-turn — _next_unit() walks heroes + enemies and a summon carries next_time = INF; and _gain_faith refuses companions outright.
  • TWO OF THE SIX ARE NARROW BY CHOICE AND SAY SO, RATHER THAN IMPLYING AN IMPOSSIBILITY. Bulwark's Break immunity, armor and cast heal, and Consecrated Ground's mitigation and reflect, are all plainly receivable. Bulwark is the sharpest case: widening its loop would ship three quarters of a card, because the 10%-a-turn regen — the sustain the card is named for — can never arrive. A partial arrival reads as working, which is Tank and Spank's failure in a new shape.
  • FOUR PROSE COPIES OF ONE CLAUSE WERE STILL SAYING ally. DL corrected Consecrated Ground's Faith kindle on the card; master.html kept it in three places and the glossary in one. The DA/DC/DG shape exactly — one surface fixed, the rest carried. When a clause moves, sweep the CLAUSE across every surface, not the card across one. Two stale Perfect claims in the same two master.html sentences went with them (Battle Shout's +5 Rage and Consecrated Ground's third turn are both unconditional since the fold), and Consecrated Ground's duration there read 2 against the 3 applied.
  • AND THE DK COMMENT ON RALLYING SHOUT WAS DESCRIBING A STATE DL ENDED. It still said the Pressure half was "a separate question ... deliberately not answered here". Replaced, not appended to. A reason recorded beside a decision is a good practice that creates a new place to be wrong — DL wrote that about DK's max_resource slip and this is the same file's second instance.

§2 — A pin must name its clause, and two of check_dk's did not

  • wd_hold_line PINNED ONE OF ITS CARD'S TWO GROUP CLAUSES AND READ LIKE A PIN ON THE CARD. It fixes hold_bd; undying is applied in the same loop, was ruled ally by the same DK decision, and could have been moved onto bare heroes with that entry still green. Proved: narrowing it reds check_dm twice, once at the chip and once at a beast that dies instead of holding at 1 HP.
  • dv_waters PINNED THE RANK-AND-ROLL GATE, WHICH KEEPS NOTHING NARROW. The table's own heading is "each by the read line that keeps them narrow" and that fragment would have stayed green with the whole turn-start block deleted. Re-pointed at _next_unit()'s walk, which is what actually excludes a companion — and which serves Bulwark's regen and the Faith drip too, so one pin replaces three copies.
  • ANCHOR ON THE CLAUSE AND SEARCH BACKWARD FOR THE WALK. FIVE sites spell heroes.filter(func(he): return not he.dead and not he.is_companion) byte for byte, so a forward find from the walk reads the wrong site four times in five — the fault that bit DL at War Stomp's guard, fixed in the direction rather than in the fragment. check_dm asserted TWO of those five on its first run and its own gate caught it; the live count is printed now and the assertion is the property, not a number.

  • THE ALLY/HERO THREAD IS CLOSED, recorded in CLAUDE.md and in text-standard.html §4.9. Rule on CLAUSES, not on abilities. "Party" is retired; hero means the four, ally means heroes and companions, and every hero ruling carries the structural reason a companion cannot receive it.
  • THE FIVE ALLY-WORDED TEXTS DL LISTED SEPARATELY ARE RULED ON NOWHERE. None is a clause-level scope disagreement of the kind §1 rules on — each is a single-shape text saying ally where its read site means hero, on an effect that already behaves correctly. They stay owed.
  • A SEVENTH FAMILY WAS FOUND AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN SWEPT: a text that under-states its own payload. Both UPGRADED cards drop "Refunds 5 Rage" while the code still pays it — Battle Shout's and Hold the Line's. An absent clause does not mis-say, so §1's test does not reach it; adding a clause to a card is authoring, and correcting a wrong word is repair. Reported and not taken. And the pool-pick Battle Shout shows the NODE's numbers: there is one description in the project and the pick pays +8% for 2 turns while the card promises +12% for 3.

2026-08-23 — Batch DL: RALLYING SHOUT'S PRESSURE, AND "PARTY" IS RETIRED

One card carried two clauses of different shape under one word, and that is how it hid from two consecutive sweeps. Rallying Shout reads "the whole party sheds 30 Pressure, and every other ally regains 30% of their resource". DJ §2 swept every ally-worded text and DK §2 ruled on eleven of them — both found the RESOURCE half, ruled it a hero's for the right reason, and never saw the Pressure half, because it carried neither of the two words. It paid four bodies for the life of the project. DL widens it: the Pressure clause reads _hero_side() and a companion sheds the 30 like anyone else, measured on a live summoned Ursus at 0 before and 30 after. And "party" is retired from every player-facing surface, kept retired by a check. No save version moves (still v10). One new gate, check_dl. The full report is docs/reports/DL.md.

§1 — The Pressure clause widens; the resource clause does not

  • A COMPANION HAS A BREAK METER, so the Pressure clause is genuinely ally-shaped. It is the same axis DK had already widened Hold the Line along — Break relief to companions on that meter — so this is consistency rather than a new principle. The site takes _hero_side(), the authored name, not a fifth hand-rolled predicate, and dead is excluded for Hold the Line's reason exactly: a corpse has no meter running.
  • MEASURED ON A LIVE BODY, NOT ASSERTED (DK §1's rule). A summoned Ursus shed 0 Pressure before and 30 after; a hero shed 30 either way. A widening that changes no measurement did not land, and DK's Tank and Spank is why that sentence exists.
  • THE CLAUSES ARE TWO LOOPS NOW, NOT ONE LOOP WITH A FILTER. Each clause's collection is visible where the clause is read. A filter hung off a shared union would put the resource clause's answer somewhere the resource clause is not.
  • resource_name == "" IS THE RULING AT THE RESOURCE SITE, AND IT IS NEW HERE. Rallying Cry and War Stomp both carried that guard and DK cited its presence as the evidence for their ruling; this was the one of the three that lacked it.
  • AND DK'S RECORDED REASON WAS HALF WRONG. It read "a companion is built with no resource_name and max_resource 0". max_resource is NOT 0 on a companion — it is unit.gd's default 100, never overridden at the summon, measured on a live one. So the resource_name guard is the only thing between that loop and a beast banking 30 points of a bar it does not have. Corrected at the site.

§2 — "Party" is retired from player-facing text

  • HERO means the four. ALLY means heroes and companions. THERE IS NO THIRD WORD. Every player-facing use of "party" is now hero or ally, decided by its read site — and where the group is the ENEMY side, warband, which the game already used.
  • THE READ SITE'S COLLECTION IS THE TEST, not the sentence's rhythm. A walk over bare heroes says hero with or without an is_companion clause; three further exclusions mean hero however the collection is spelled (stamped once where the four are built, per-turn, or Faith-flavoured); and a clause whose payload a companion structurally cannot receive says hero with its reason recorded beside it.
  • SWEPT: ability descriptions, perfect_text, node text, status chips, passive_desc, battle-log lines, the glossary, the rune, relic, item, event, map, shop and blacksmith strings, the run summary, and master.html. The surviving uses are identifiers and are named: party_mark, the party event target, spec_in_party, party.tscn.
  • THE RULE IS BINDING AND IS KEPT BY A CHECK. CLAUDE.md and text-standard.html §4.9 carry it; test_batch_bx §4b sweeps for it exactly as §4 sweeps for "beast" — same place, same construction, string literals only. It was shown to bite before it was trusted: a "party" planted in a live ability description, in the glossary and in master.html each red it.
  • THREE FALSE "ALLY"s WERE CORRECTED IN THE SAME PASS, where leaving them would have made a card newly misleading: Aegis Wall's and Exhortation's log lines and Requiem's, all three of which walk heroes. Consecrated Ground's Faith clause too — it said "every ally is kindled 1 Faith" and _gain_faith refuses companions outright.
  • PROSE ABOUT THE GAME IS NOT PLAYER-FACING. CLAUDE.md, this changelog, the design notes and the batch reports are exempt. History was not swept.

§3 — The other cards with two clauses of different shape, reported and not ruled

Six, and the brief asked for the list rather than the ruling. Bulwark of Fortitude (Break immunity and armor are receivable, the per-turn heal structurally is not, the cast's instant heal is); Consecrated Ground (mitigation and reflect are receivable, Faith is refused outright); Divine Wrath (both halves die, for two different reasons — the damage term is read in the hero strike loop and the speed term only matters to a turn order a companion is never in); Sacred Resolve (the split is receivable, the Break carve-out is already worded separately); Battle Shout and Hold the Line (a group clause and a self-clause — the +5 Rage — under one word). And one text is wrong on its own terms: the Warrior's Rally says "shout one ALLY forward" and its picker filters companions out at three sites. All seven are recorded in docs/state.md as owed.

§4 — Verification

  • THE NEGATIVE CONTROL ON §1. check_dl §3 empties companions for the length of one cast, which is precisely the pre-DL collection, and the beast sheds 0 against 30 with the union. Reverting the widening in the source reds three of the gate's checks.

2026-08-23 — Batch DK: THE ELEVEN ALLY-WORDED EFFECTS, RULED

DJ §2 swept every broad ally-worded card and node and found ELEVEN besides Harvest walking bare heroes, which holds no companion — and ruled on none of them, because an exclusion that is INTENDED wants its TEXT corrected and one that is ACCIDENTAL wants its CODE corrected. DK is that ruling, and the eleven split FOUR and SEVEN. Rally, Hold the Line, Sanctuary and the Field Medic now read _hero_side() and genuinely pay a beast; the other seven say hero, each with its reason recorded beside it. The fifth candidate to widen was Tank and Spank and it was measured, not assumed: empower lands on a companion cleanly and pays it NOTHING — a beast strikes through _companion_hit, its own damage path, which reads none of the hero strike loop’s multipliers. Measured over 40 seeded blows, ratio exactly 1.0000. Its text moved instead. No save version moves (still v10). One new gate, check_dk; check_dj’s site ratchet is retired into it. The full report is docs/reports/DK.md.

§1 — THE FOUR THAT WIDEN

Rally, Hold the Line, Sanctuary and Field Medic read _hero_side(). Healing received, Break reduction, healing and cleansing are all things a beast plainly receives, and each was verified to arrive on a live summoned bear rather than assumed:

  • Sanctuary heals it 1200 of a 10000 body — the 12% the card promises.
  • Hold the Line leaves it at 20 Break from a 40-BD blow against an unheld 40 (the base 50% cut; 8 under the upgraded 80%), and its undying half holds the beast at 1 HP through a lethal blow.
  • Rally turns a 1000 heal into 1300.
  • The Field Medic’s pool holds a poisoned beast, and the wash takes the affliction off it.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: under The Pack this reaches six units instead of four, so four party-wide effects get roughly 50% more coverage in that build alone. That is a deliberate buff to one build. “Your bear doesn’t get healed by the party heal” is a rule players discover by being confused.

ALL FOUR TAKE THE LIVING, AND THAT IS A DECISION ABOUT dead RATHER THAN A DEFAULT. Each asks who RECEIVES an effect and a corpse receives nothing, so each calls _hero_side() — the authored name for “the union, living only” — instead of a fifth hand-rolled copy of the predicate. Harvest is the counter-case and was deliberately not dragged along: it asks who opened a wound, a hero who has since fallen still opened it, and it keeps its union spelled out. Both are heroes + companions; only one filters dead. (DI proposed _hero_side() for Harvest one batch ago and it would have dropped a fallen opener’s board to 0.6664.)

§2 — THE SEVEN THAT CHANGE ONLY THEIR WORDS

No read site moves. The texts say hero, and the REASON is recorded beside each one in the source — “hero” alone is a decision the next author re-litigates.

  • Rallying Cry, War Stomp, Rallying Shout — a beast is built with no resource_name and max_resource 0, so a refuel restores nothing. Two of the three already carried a resource_name == "" guard; the word now agrees with it.
  • Cleansing Waters — it rolls per-turn on the ACTING unit, and _next_unit() walks heroes + enemies. A companion is summoned with next_time = INF and takes no turns ever. Structural: no collection anywhere reaches it, so “fixing the code” would mean moving the effect off turns entirely.
  • Devoutness and Last Hope — both are stamped ONCE in the party-spawn block, before any companion exists, so widening the collection there would reach an empty array and a beast summoned on turn four would still get nothing. The effects themselves are receivable — a beast wearing devotion at 20 banks 32 Break from a 40-BD blow — so the obstacle is the stamp’s timing, and reaching it wants a re-stamp on summon.
  • Tank and Spank — see §3.

ONE THING THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RULE ON. Rallying Shout is not the pure refuel the other two are: it also sheds 30 Pressure from “the whole party”, and a companion HAS a Break meter and can plainly shed it. Only the ally-worded resource clause moved. “Party” is not one of the two words DJ §2 swept, so ruling on it is a new ruling; it is recorded as owed.

§3 — TANK AND SPANK WAS THE FIFTH TO WIDEN, AND IT WAS MEASURED INSTEAD

It says “Empowers a random ally”, it walked bare heroes, and CLAUDE.md cited it as the proof the hero/ally distinction is worth having. It was the most obvious of the five to widen. Widening it would have been a no-op.

empower attaches to a companion perfectly cleanly — the status applies, the chip renders, the tooltip reads. The payout never arrives: a beast’s blows resolve through _companion_hit, which is its own damage path and reads none of the hero strike loop’s multiplier block. battle.gd already said so from the other side, at the last_howl_dmg site: “a beast’s blows go through _companion_hit, which never reads this block, so the companions are correctly untouched.” Measured over 40 seeded blows with the chip standing: 34392 damage against 34392, a ratio of exactly 1.0000.

SO THE TEXT WAS CORRECTED AND THE COLLECTION WAS NOT, and the ruling is pinned as a MEASUREMENT rather than an assertion — check_dk §4 re-reads that ratio on every battery run. A ruling of the form “we left this narrow BECAUSE widening would pay nothing” is a claim about a code path, and a claim about a code path rots. Pinned this way, the day somebody gives _companion_hit an empower read, the gate says the ruling is stale instead of staying quietly true.

A RULE WHOSE WORKED EXAMPLE WAS WRONG NEEDS ITS EXAMPLE REPAIRED AS LOUDLY AS THE RULE. The distinction is still worth having; this was simply never the proof of it. The proof is now Hold the Line — it says “ally”, it reads _hero_side(), and a summoned bear measurably banks 20 Break where it used to bank 40.

§4 — CV §4 IS CORRECTED, NOT JUST SUPPLEMENTED

CV moved four texts TO “ally” on the stated test that “their read sites genuinely include companions”. It was false for all four (DJ §2). After DK, wd_rally and wd_hold_line are genuinely ally and dv_devoutness and dv_waters are hero — so all four land correctly for the first time, but by a different route than CV recorded.

THE TEST ITSELF IS WHAT A FUTURE AUTHOR WOULD APPLY, SO THE TEST IS WHAT WAS CORRECTED — in CLAUDE.md, docs/text-standard.html §4.9 and docs/talent-audit.html §4.1. The new test is not “does the collection reach one”. It is “does the effect ARRIVE”, and the evidence is a live measurement on a summoned beast. There are three places a widening dies and only the first is the collection: the loop walks bare heroes; a filter downstream removes it (never actually the mechanism — all 23 is_companion filters walk heroes and remove nothing); or the read site below simply never runs for that body, which is invisible to every source grep.

AND THE GLOSSARY WAS THE ONE ACTIVELY MISLEADING A PLAYER. Its hero_vs_ally entry named five effects as examples of what “ally” pays — Tank and Spank’s Empower, Rally’s healing bonus, Hold the Line, Devoutness, Cleansing Waters — and four of the five were false when it was written. Rewritten to the live split, with the reason attached to each. master.html’s Hold the Line flag, which DJ left saying “companions NOT included”, now says they are.

The changelog and the batch reports are history and were deliberately not swept.

§5 — THE FILTERS THAT REMOVE NOTHING, AND THE QUESTION DK ASKED OF THEM

All 23 is_companion filters walk heroes, which never holds one, so not one of them excludes anything. They record intent and are kept as such. DK asked the question that count exists for: does any of them now sit on a collection that DOES hold a companion? A filter on one of the four widened sites would have stopped being decoration and started removing the beast — the widening would have done nothing and the batch would have shipped a no-op wearing a fix’s clothes.

NONE of the four carried one, so none of the 23 changed meaning, and the count holding at 23 across DK is how that is checkable rather than merely stated. The real no-op risk turned out to be somewhere else entirely — a missing READ SITE rather than a surviving filter, which is §3.

§6 — VERIFICATION

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE POINT, BECAUSE THE FAILURE WAS INVISIBLE. Four effects paid four units instead of five for the life of the project and no log, no suite and no battery ever said so — so a check that passes on the fixed tree proves nothing on its own. check_dk §2 empties companions for the length of one arm, which is precisely the pre-DK collection at these sites, and asserts the beast is untouched: Sanctuary heals it 0 and Hold the Line leaves it the full 40 Break. Field Medic’s pool gets the same treatment.

check_dj’s §5 site ratchet is retired into check_dk §1 rather than updated: DJ pinned the eleven with a message asking the next batch to rule, DK ruled, and keeping both would be two copies of one fact in two gates. Its is_companion count stays — that is DJ’s own finding and nothing else asserts it. check_dj 54 → 43 checks, predicted.

heroes does not contain the companions; companions does. Any loop implementing the ally convention must read both. A number quoted from one document into another stops being a measurement. DI’s 53/204 was a single-line grep that missed 25 wrapped calls; the true figure was 63, and it had been quoted into three documents without re-derivation. Re-derive a figure at the point of use, or cite where it was measured and when. §0 — THE RECORDED COVERAGE FIGURE WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS WRONG BECAUSE IT WAS A GREP

docs/state.md, DH’s own source comment and this batch’s brief all said 53 of 204. Counted properly — balancing parentheses across the whole file rather than reading one line at a time — the figure was 63. 25 of the 204 calls wrap across lines and TWELVE OF THOSE ALREADY PASSED A SOURCE, and a single-line grep cannot see any of them. The number had been quoted into three documents without anyone re-deriving it. check_di §1 walks rather than greps, and it skips the two COMMENTS that name _apply_status( — the same fault one layer down.

§1 — WHICH STATUSES HARVEST ACTUALLY READS, DERIVED FROM THE CLAUSE

Harvest reads a status on its target if it is in DEBUFF_IDS (33 ids), is not broken, is not sticky, and its src_name resolves to a member of heroes other than the caster. Of the 141 unstamped sites, 50 could apply one of those — 48 with a literal id and 2 computed. The narrow scope held comfortably: this was never most of the 151. The population was derived by walking _resolve_special’s call graph, not the ability fields.

§2 — 36 STAMPED, 14 REPORTED RATHER THAN GUESSED

Two of the 36 had the real source sitting unused in their own signature. _hold_freeze(target, src, force) passed null to _apply_status while holding src; _apply_poison(src, victim, turns) did the same. Both were the two sites in the file passing an EXPLICIT null, which reads as deliberate and was not.

FOURTEEN SITES ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT UNSTAMPED AND ALL FOURTEEN ARE NAMED IN THE REPORT. Umbral Mirror’s rebound (an enemy’s own debuff, reflected by a talent no single hero owns), Chain Ignition (a dead foe’s fire passed on), the Cursed Visage (an item; nobody uses it), Spread of Madness and the bewitched strike (an enemy applying to an enemy under the party’s influence), Hemorrhage (a threshold on collective bleed), the Hoarfrost modifier stamp (no unit applies it), and seven companion sites. Getting the source wrong is worse than leaving it absent: absent under-pays, wrong mis-credits.

§3 — heroes DOES NOT CARRY THE COMPANIONS, AND DH’S COMMENT SAYS IT DOES

DH’s Harvest comment reads “heroes CARRIES THE COMPANIONS, which is correct rather than incidental: Aguila’s Exposed is the Beastmaster’s work”. It does not. heroes.append is reached at exactly ONE site — the party spawn — and a companion is appended to companions. Four sites in battle.gd write heroes + companions precisely because the union is not free, and _hero_side() exists to build it. The consequence is that Harvest’s ally loop cannot resolve a companion’s name, so a wound Aguila opened pays the base rate however it is stamped — measured live at exactly 1.0000 of a self-opened board. DI DID NOT CLOSE IT. The fix is one word in DH’s loop and it MOVES A MAGNITUDE, which this batch forbids itself. check_di §4 asserts the gap so a future ruling changes an assertion rather than a belief.

The parse check was proved to bite too: a deliberate syntax error appended to battle.gd produced a Parse Error line and none once removed — and the gate’s own first run exited 0 while printing two Parse Error lines, which is the trap the project has a rule about.

Harvest rolls randf_range(0.9, 1.1), so an unseeded ally-versus-self comparison would differ in the roll as well as in the term being measured. Both arms draw the same stream and the ratio reads 1.5000 exactly, over seven readings.

2026-08-22 — Batch DH: CROSS-SPEC SYNERGY

Nine clauses on nine existing cards. No new abilities, no new statuses, no pool depth change — SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS stays at 96 and the draft stays at 120 of 120. Every one of the 120 draft abilities was authored inside its own spec, so the pools never referenced each other and drafting was a decision about one hero rather than about the party. Two accidental exceptions proved the shape worked — Fault Line hands the Sharpshooter the Break that Breaking Darkness amplifies, and Downwind copies whatever debuff an ally applied. These nine are deliberate. Three of the brief’s own claims were wrong against the repo and are corrected below. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/DH.md.

§0 — THE FOUR RULES, AND THE ONE THAT BIT

Every coupling is named in the card text (the draft screen is the only place the decision happens); hub and spoke, not pairs (a run fields four of twelve specs, so a clause that needs a named partner is dead most of the time — every one of the nine is a bonus on a card that already works alone); any status a feeder applies must be in DEBUFF_IDS, or it applies, logs, reads as working and feeds the Survivalist’s breadth term nothing; and no clause may duplicate an existing talent.

THE FOURTH RULE BIT, AND IT BIT ON THE CARD THE BRIEF WAS MOST CONFIDENT ABOUT. The brief asked for “Canis’s strikes apply Bleed”. Summon Canis already reads “attacks with you for 20% of your Attack, building 20 Bleed”, its arrival lays Bloodhowl’s 15 on every enemy, and its Loyalty gift is +2 Bleed a stack — shipped, and _companion_strike’s canis branch has carried it for many batches. Writing that clause would have been BD’s Deadfall/Snare Trap duplication exactly: fourteen batches of a duplicate nobody read. The gap is the other two companions — Ursus builds no Bleed and Aguila lays Exposed — so the clause moved to the card instead.

§1 — FEEDING THE SURVIVALIST

His Trapper counts different statuses from any source, allies’ included; he is the one spec already built to be fed. Choking Smoke also sets every enemy Burning 2 turns — one clause, two couplings: it widens his own breadth (burn is in DEBUFF_IDS) and it arms the Pyromancer’s Ember Debt and Funeral Pyre, which consume Burn and have never had a second applier in the party. Snare Line’s spring holds a Chilled enemy 2 turns instead of 1; the Cryomancer lays that ice and nothing in the Survivalist’s own kit does. The clause is written at the line’s spring site and not inside _spring_trap, which is shared with the placed deadfall and Snare Trap — a clause in the helper would have moved a magnitude on two existing effects.

HARVEST IS THE HUB STATED OUTRIGHT, AND THE BRIEF EXPECTED IT TO BE UNAFFORDABLE. It now pays up to 18% of Attack a status against its base 12, scaled by the share of the reaped board that somebody else opened. The brief asked for the cost of knowing who applied each status to be reported before building it, on the assumption statuses carry no source. They have carried one since Batch W: _apply_status stamps src_name onto the status it just applied so later mitigation can credit its caster. The clause cost a read, not a signature change across 244 call sites. The caveat is real and is recorded rather than hidden: only sites that pass src stamp it — 53 of 204 single-line _apply_status calls do — so an unstamped status reads as “not an ally’s” and pays the base rate. That is the safe direction (a missed bonus, never a false one), but it is an under-payment.

§2 — FEEDING THE PYROMANCER

Emberkeep extends Burn any HERO applies, not only his own, which makes him the party’s Burn amplifier and the consuming end of §1’s Choking Smoke. The whole mechanic is still one clause at _apply_status’s eff_turns block. src.is_hero is the guard and it is load-bearing: “anyone” means anyone in the party, or the card would double the fire eating the heroes. The old scoping did that work by accident, because only he could ever hold the status. Firedraw draws 9 turns instead of 6 from an enemy already carrying another spec’s debuff, read off the curated DEBUFF_IDS list minus his own vocabulary (burn, slow_burn) and minus broken, which is a Break-meter state rather than an affliction anybody applied.

§3 — FEEDING THE OCCULTIST

Breaking Darkness names its partners in the text, and nothing mechanical moves. The card already amplified every source of Break by 25%; it now says so, and names the Sharpshooter’s Fault Line and the Warden’s Turn the Blade. The combo existed and was found by accident — this is discoverability. Suffering’s drip pays 3 Ruin a turn against a Broken enemy instead of 2, tying his Madness gate to whoever is generating Break; CR made hard control Broken-gated, so Broken is already the axis the party works toward.

§4 — THE TWO THAT COUPLE PLAYSTYLES RATHER THAN STATUSES

Savage Sweep’s run opens 12 Bleed on each enemy it reaches, whichever companion runs it. The consuming end is a Berserker card that exists today: Battle Shout pays +1% party damage per 20 of the enemy party’s bleed buildup, summed across every living enemy, so three bleeding bodies is the widest single contribution to that sum in the game. It feeds Trapper too — the chip log_bleed_chip synthesizes carries id bleed, which is in DEBUFF_IDS. It goes through _add_bleed_with_burst and never _apply_status: Bleed is a meter, and its STATUS_INFO row was deleted at BJ §1 as unreachable, so an _apply_status(_, "bleed", …) would index a table with no such key. That is the brief’s second wrong claim — it described Bleed as a status Battle Shout reads; Battle Shout reads bleed_buildup.

SHARED GRIEF READS HOW MANY ALLIES STAND BELOW HALF, AND IT IS THE BEST COUPLING IN THE BATCH FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON. Mercy accrues only on the crossing below half (_check_below_half fires once, on was_above), so a hero who parks in that band pays her exactly once and then nothing — and the Berserker’s entire Blood Frenzy band lives down there on purpose. The two specs whose engines are inverted from each other become each other’s fuel. She gains +1 Mercy per other living ally below the window, on top of her 4. It reads mercy_threshold rather than a literal half, because Guardian Angel raises that stamp party-wide and a literal would silently disagree with the passive the card is named after. Companions are excluded, and so is she — paying her for her own wound would let the card fund its own price.

§5 — THE ONE SUITE MOVEMENT, AND IT IS AN INVERSION PLUS A GUARD

test_batch_cb goes 1184 → 1185, and it is the only check count in the project that moves. That suite asserted “a SECOND applier’s Burn is not doubled” — exactly the rule §2 inverts — so the assertion is INVERTED rather than deleted, on ce’s idiom: the question (whose fire does the window reach?) is still worth asking and only the answer moved. That edit is count-neutral. The +1 is a new assertion beside it: an ENEMY’s Burn is still not doubled, which pins the src.is_hero guard. The old src-scoping hid that question because only he could ever hold the status, and without the pin a later batch could drop the guard silently. Predicted in baselines.json before the battery ran, and the battery agreed.

baselines.json was written with the PREDICTED after-values BEFORE the verification battery ran, so the run tests the prediction instead of merely recording it: a row that disagreed would be check_de’s error, not a note in a report. The prediction is 47 → 10 across 7 suites — as 2, at 3, aw 1, bj 1, bo 1, bx 1, ce 1 — a fall of exactly 37, which is the STALE count, with every check count in the project unmoved. THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS TWO-SIDED and the second half is the one that matters: a fall SMALLER than 37 means a repair did not land, and a fall LARGER than 37 means something was repaired by accident — which would be reported rather than banked, because an improvement nobody aimed at is a change nobody understands. The measured result is in docs/reports/DF.md and docs/state.md, which are written after the run for the reason DE established: a run that did not supervise the final tree cannot certify it, and those two files are read by nothing and by check_de alone respectively, so writing them last costs a seconds-long re-read of the logs rather than another battery.

test_batch_an FELL TO 6046 ON THE BEFORE-BATTERY, ON UNMODIFIED HEAD. That is one below a floor which was itself the lowest of thirteen readings, and check_de reported it as an error, which is exactly the asymmetry DE built. It is drift, not a fault: 0 failures, 0 throws, and all thirteen of the suite’s section headers printed, so nothing stopped running. Comparing this run’s counts to recorded ones is a property of the RUN. The differ is a post-pass now (check_de.gd) over the logs run_battery.sh already writes; the baselines are one machine-readable file (baselines.json); and the nesting is structurally impossible rather than merely avoided, because reading a file is not running a suite. §0 — WHAT DOES cd DO THAT THE RUNNER CANNOT? FOR HALF OF IT, NOTHING

test_batch_cd did two unrelated jobs. It diffed check counts against a recorded table, and it detected that another suite threw — which it did by spawning child Godots with stderr captured, because a script error is invisible to the suite it happens in. Both jobs were redundant, and twice over.

run_battery.sh already spawns every target, already captures every stream including stderr (>"$log" 2>&1), already greps the same three count shapes and already counts the same two throw markers. test_batch_cd’s matcher is that grep, transcribed; its throw count is that grep, transcribed. The only thing the runner did not do was COMPARE. So the honest answer for the differ half was nothing, and it is reported as nothing.

THE OTHER THREE SECTIONS STAY A SUITE, AND THE REASON IS NOT SENTIMENT. The dead-symbol sweep, the draft-target sweep and the pool measurement read the project’s SOURCE and its DATA — they resolve Classes, they walk the twelve spec pools, they read prose in four documents. A shell runner has no Classes and no opinion about prose. Those are assertions about the tree and they belong in a suite; only the differ moved.

§1 — THE BASELINES ARE DATA, IN ONE FILE, AND A BAND CARRIES ITS OWN EVIDENCE

baselines.json at the repo root, beside run_battery.sh and the gates. One place, and nothing duplicates it — docs/state.md and CLAUDE.md point at it rather than restating it, because a second copy of a number is this project’s oldest recurring defect and the instrument built to catch drift must not be the thing that seeds it.

Per target it carries the expected check count (a number, or a band where the count legitimately varies), the expected FAILURE count, the known flake and its observed rate — and THE NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS EACH BAND RESTS ON. That last field is the one worth arguing for: an’s nine-observation band was exceeded on its tenth reading, inside the batch that widened it. A band is a claim about a distribution nobody has characterised, and the number of readings behind it is part of the claim. A row written from four readings and a row written from twelve are not the same assertion, and until now nothing recorded which was which.

A BASELINE MOVES ONLY IN THE BATCH THAT CAUSES THE MOVEMENT, AND THE CHANGELOG SAYS WHY. Otherwise the table drifts into whatever the code happens to do, which is CQ §3’s failure arriving in a new place.

§2 — THE DIFFER IS A POST-PASS, RUN ONCE, AND IT SPAWNS NOTHING

check_de.gd runs last of all, reads $OUT/*.log and baselines.json, and reports. It is written in GDScript and not in shell, for the reason the batch keeps re-learning: bash string handling is how the battery’s count grep came to be too narrow three times, and how a message spelling a throw marker out in full would make the battery accuse the differ of throwing. The count-differ has been mis-instrumented twice. It is not a place to be clever — so the parser carries positive controls for all three log shapes, including bm’s scar as a regression case (written [ \t]+ instead of a single space, the matcher reads sections: 8 checks: 1891 as 8 checks and 1891 failures).

A FALL AND A RISE ARE NOT THE SAME EVENT, AND THE POLARITY INVERTS BETWEEN THE TWO HALVES. A falling check count is this project’s signature failure — bb 172→168, bo 505→495, harness gate 2 at CA, and the seven SCRIPT ERRORs that hid 2,714 assertions — and it is an ERROR. A rising one is usually a suite’s own loop walking new content and is a NOTICE. So the FLOOR of a band is asserted and the ceiling is not, which turns out to be the same asymmetry an’s band rule already had written into it. A rising FAILURE count inverts it: that is the 48th failure among 47, and it is an ERROR; a falling one means something was repaired, and it is a NOTICE. The instrument’s own asymmetry is driven through the real functions by four probes, so a control cannot pass by accident.

AND THE HAZARD THE NEW SHAPE INTRODUCES, NAMED AND CLOSED. Reading logs instead of spawning means a target that failed to launch would be blessed by its previous run’s log — run_battery.sh does not clear $OUT. So the runner writes a manifest ($OUT/.ran) naming each target immediately before launching it, and the differ trusts that rather than the directory listing. A log named in the manifest is always this run’s, because run_one truncates it at spawn. A subset invocation writes a short manifest and the differ says so instead of reporting a clean tree.

§3 — THE FAILURE BASELINES, WHICH ARE THE REAL PRIZE

With 47 known failures across 20 suites, a 48th is invisible. That is not hypothetical: DC found that test_batch_bi was right and the game was wrong for four batches, and it hid because that suite was already red for an unrelated reason. A red check does not announce a second problem underneath it.

Every target now carries an expected failure count, so a suite going from 6 red to 7 is reported exactly as loudly as one going from 0 to 1. This is the fix for the exact failure mode that let a lying passive survive four batches, and it is worth more than the check-count diffing that prompted the batch.

§4 — THE MARGIN CAVEAT, GENERALISED FROM AN ANECDOTE INTO A METHOD

The brief asked for a caveat that DD had already half-recorded, and the half that was missing is the useful half. CLAUDE.md already carried the arithmetic for at specifically — a blow rolls randf_range(0.9, 1.1), so one blow carries ±10% and a ratio of two carries up to 22%, against bands of ±20% and ±7%. What it did not carry was the instruction to do that arithmetic BEFORE choosing the band rather than after the flake.

Recorded beside the recommendation: a margin only works if it is WIDER than the noise it sits on, and a ratio of two rolled quantities carries roughly twice the variance of either. Compute the propagated noise first. If it is wider than the band the question needs, THE BAND IS NOT AVAILABLE — seed the pair and assert exactly. The recommendation to assert ratios with margins must not stand unqualified: followed on its own, it produced both of at’s flakes.
