What each repair actually asks now

THE ELIGIBLE BAND FOR COMMUNION MOVED DOWN WITH THE THRESHOLD. The walk skips a hero at faith_stacks >= FAITH_RELEASE, so the band was 1–4 under a threshold of five and is 1–2 under three. The roll is (15 × stacks)%, so the peak chance is 30% at two stacks, not 60% at four, and the cliff sits at three. Measured after the repair: 29.8% over 1200 trials.

THE THRESHOLD IS NAMED RATHER THAN SPELLED, IN EVERY SUITE THAT TOUCHES IT. Each of the five now carries const RELEASE := 3 and const HELD_MAX := RELEASE - 1 once, and the checks are written against those. The next threshold ruling costs one line a suite instead of a dozen literals — which is the same lesson the master.html stamp gate learned at CP when it stopped being a literal.

THE SOURCE CHECKS NOW NAME THE CONSTANTS TOO. bh and bi both grepped battle.gd for _gain_faith(u, 1, "ground") and for h.faith_stacks >= 5; CZ replaced those literals with FAITH_PER_GROUND_TURN and FAITH_RELEASE, so the assertions name the constants.

AND ONE REPAIR IS A mini() RATHER THAN A SHORTER LOOP, DELIBERATELY. bi §1 ratchets the peak over four gains and asserted peak == i + 1; the third gain now releases, so the fourth cannot lift the peak past three. Dropping the fourth iteration would have made it pass and stopped it asking its question. It asserts peak == mini(i + 1, RELEASE) and still runs four times.

§2 — TWO PIECES OF PROSE DA’S REVERT LEFT BEHIND

THE ASSERTION WAS RIGHT AND THE GAME’S OWN TEXT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE ONE CASE “REPAIR THE ASSERTION” MUST NOT BE APPLIED TO. test_batch_bi asks that Conviction’s passive block state “2 a hit”. It read “3 a hit”, and so did the Faith status chip:

  • scripts/classes.gd — the Devout’s passive_desc: “allies build Faith whenever Divine Shield absorbs damage for them — 3 a hit”
  • scripts/battle.gd — the faith status default, the chip a player reads mid-fight: “Divine Shield absorbs build Faith, 3 a hit”

battle.FAITH_PER_ABSORB IS 2. CZ tripled the builders to 3 and DA rolled the CODE back to 2 and did not roll the TEXT back with it, so the Devout’s passive and his status chip have both been overstating his own rate by half since DA. Both now read “2 a hit”. docs/master.html already said (2 a hit), which is how the two disagreed without anything noticing: the documentation was right and the game was wrong, and the suites that would have caught it were the ones already red for the threshold.

THE SWEEP FOR OTHERS WAS RUN AND IS EMPTY. 3 a hit appears nowhere else in .gd, .md, .html or .json, and only bg and bi read that passive_desc at all. Both edits are a single digit and are length-neutral, so check_cl_width’s wrapping measurements are untouched by construction.

§3 — WHEN THE THRESHOLD MOVES, THE DETECTOR MOVES WITH IT

THE ONE REPAIR THAT DID NOT WORK FIRST TIME, AND IT IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING. test_batch_be’s Communion rate check was repointed from three stacks to two and still read 0.0% — against a node measured at 29.8% one line later.

THE ASSERTION WAS RIGHT AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS BROKEN. _measure has two detectors: the ally’s stack count going up, or a SECOND release being banked. At three-of-five an advance left the ally at four and the stack count saw it. At two-of-three an advance takes the ally TO the threshold, which releases and resets him to zero — so the stack-count detector reads every single fire as a miss.

A MOVED THRESHOLD DOES NOT ONLY INVALIDATE THE NUMBERS AN ASSERTION PINS; IT CAN INVALIDATE THE WAY THE ASSERTION LOOKS. test_batch_bf had written that rule down when BF moved the same band — “the release counter is the only honest witness there” — and be was repaired without reading it. Both suites now say so at the function that needs it.

§4 — THREE THINGS INTO THE RECORD, AND TWO OF THEM WERE ALREADY THERE

test_batch_at IS A SECOND FLAKE AND IS RECORDED BESIDE bo. It reads 3 failures or 4, the fourth flaking in 2 of 5 dedicated runs — far worse than bo’s roughly 1 in 13. The flaking check is “Cannon at 8 stacks scales by the PASSIVE alone”, a damage-scaling assertion; test_batch_at.gd calls seed() zero times and its check count is rock steady at 470, so only the FAILURE count moves. A count-diffing rule reads at 3 → 4 as a regression and it is not one. It is NOT repaired here — the fix is to seed the suite or to assert a ratio with a margin instead of a bare comparison, and that is its own small job.

an’S BAND WAS ALREADY CORRECTED AT DB; WHAT WAS WRONG WAS THE OBSERVATION COUNT. The brief asked for 6047–6054 to replace 6052–6054, and state.md has carried 6047–6054 since DB. Its sentence said “five observations” and then listed six readings — 6047, 6051, 6052, 6054, 6048, 6054. The band rests on six, and it says six now, because a band written from too few readings reads a normal run as a regression.

AND A FOURTH, FOUND WHILE CHECKING THE FIRST THREE: cd FLAGS TWO SUITES, NOT ONE. state.md carried CW’s knock-on as “FAIL: test_batch_bb.gd reports zero failures”, naming one suite; cd reports two and always has — bb and bj. cd’s REPAIRED table holds FIVE suites only (ah, an, bb, bj, test_runes). That subset is also why repairing be–bi did not move cd’s count: none of the five Faith suites is in it, so the count-differ never saw the largest single family of failures in the project. It watches five suites, not forty-five — worth knowing before the next batch leans on it as a safety net.

THE --script BASE-CLASS TRAP NEEDED NOTHING: DB ALREADY RECORDED IT, TWICE. CLAUDE.md carries it in the traps — with the reproduction, the exits 0 and the note that throws= is the only thing standing between the fault and a green report — and again in the fixture rule, including that a preloaded RefCounted with no class_name is the working form. Nothing was added, because a rule written twice is not made truer by writing it a third time.

2026-08-21 — Batch DB: ONE _spawn FOR THE GATES

One consolidation and one battery. The battle fixture and the tally are authored once, in gate_fixture.gd, and all seven gates go through it; the battery ran for the first time since CS and the bill for five implement-only batches is 72 failing assertions across 26 suites, zero throws; and two rules go into the traps. Behaviour did not change and the proof is the counts. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/DB.md. DC is owed and is ten times larger: the suites.

§1 — ONE FIXTURE, SEVEN GATES

_spawn was copied into seven gates as four divergent bodies (check_cm_live, check_co, check_cs, check_ct, check_cy, check_cz, check_da). It is authored once now. 345 lines deleted, 135 added. check_da §3 no longer COUNTS the copies — it ASSERTS there are none: a gate that authors its own _spawn, or that instantiates the battle scene by hand, fails it by name.

THE THREE DIFFERENCES THAT WERE REAL ARE NAMED ARGUMENTS NOW rather than invisible edits inside a copy: deterministic (the AK/AL/AR damage forcing — check_cm_live and check_cs), items (check_ct’s held empty slot) and run. No gate needed an exemption; CZ’s _cl_only_corpus remains the one deliberate copy in the project.

AND THE ONE THAT WAS NOT REAL WAS RULED DEAD RATHER THAN AVERAGED. Five copies hand-set skill_check_taught and defensive_check_taught; two did not. _nobody_can_press() is sim or autoplay or headless and a gate is always headless, so the read site is never entered and the defensive brace always takes the bot branch: the flags could not affect any check any gate ran, and had not been able to since CQ. Their one live effect was Profile._save() — five gates writing the player’s user://profile.json on every run, two hundred lines from check_ct asserting it leaves the player’s save as it found it. They are gone, and profile.json’s mtime is now unchanged across a gate run, measured before and after. DA recorded this divergence as “two other copies”; it was five.

_report HAD DRIFTED INTO FOUR SHAPES, NOT TWO — N failures with no count at all (cm_live, co), N checks, M failures (cs), N checks / M failures (ct, da), and no _report at all, printed and quit inline (cy, cz). ok() had to come with it: four gates’ copies never incremented a check counter, which is why check_cm_live, check_co, check_cy and check_cz have read checks=? in every battery ever run. A count that reads ? is the one thing a count-diffing rule cannot compare. The tally is one object now and not one of the several hundred ok(...) call sites moved.

THE SCAR, AND WHY IT STAYS. The brief asked for run_battery.sh’s hand-rolled grep -E "checks," to be narrowed to the one format now that _report is single. That grep does not exist — the only occurrence of checks, in the file is the header comment recording it as a scar CP already fixed. The live matcher is general, and it must stay general: it also reads 45 SUITES, which print at least four other shapes. Narrowing it would re-open BQ’s scar and CS’s — the third time that grep has been too narrow. One shape for the gates; a grep that reads everything for the battery.

THE SHAPE THAT WOULD NOT COMPILE, WHICH IS ITSELF A TRAP. A base class (extends GateBase) is the right design and would have changed zero call sites. A --script SceneTree target cannot resolve its own base class, in either spelling, with the class cache present — it prints Parse Error, runs not one line, and exits 0. The fixture is a preloaded RefCounted, and it carries no class_name: that registration lives in the gitignored .godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg, so it would resolve here and fail on a fresh clone.

§3 — TWO THINGS INTO THE TRAPS

THE EXIT CODE IS NOT A SIGNAL, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS load() RETURNING A BROKEN SCRIPT. 2026-08-21 — Batch DA: ROLL BACK FAITH’S BUILDERS, REFUSE GLACIAL PRISON

Two corrections and one standing rule. Faith’s two builders go back to their pre-CZ rates and the release threshold stays at 3; Glacial Prison joins CO’s recast refusal, the first talent-granted ability in that set; and a helper copied between gates is recorded as a named failure mode, with the sweep for others reported and nothing consolidated. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/DA.md.

§1 — FAITH’S BUILDERS GO BACK; THE THRESHOLD STAYS

FAITH_PER_ABSORB 3 → 2 and FAITH_PER_GROUND_TURN 2 → 1. FAITH_RELEASE is untouched at 3. The named constant for the ground drip is CZ’s and it stays — naming the rate was the durable half of that change, since a bare literal at a call site can be neither measured nor moved. The revert moves the number and keeps the name.

WHY THE THRESHOLD WAS THE HONEST HALF AND THE BUILDERS WERE NOT. CZ sized the builders against CY’s arrival measurement and then, in the same batch, proved that measurement was answering a different question: the conviction row samples the DEVOUT’S OWN meter, which holds at the threshold and never releases by rule. The figure that answers “does a release fire” is releases/battle, and it read 0.81 a battle at rung 2, not 1.6 of 5. Tripling the builders on top of a halved threshold took it to 4.24 — a fivefold change sized against a number that was wrong. The threshold was sized against structure instead (a bar of five in a fight lasting three to five turns per hero), and that argument never depended on the arrival figure at all.

AND IT REMOVED A MECHANIC, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT DECIDED IT. At 3 per absorb against a threshold of 3, one absorbed hit was a whole release: a shielded ALLY filled and paid out on the same blow and never held Faith at all, so faith_peak — the high-water mark the entire lane pays its mitigation and damage on — stopped existing for allies. The card stopped being a ramp and became a per-hit heal. CZ recorded that concern in full rather than burying it; it was a larger change than the one that was asked for and nobody chose it.

RE-MEASURED AT EVERY RUNG. Releases a battle, before CZ → CZ shipped → now: rung 1 0.51 → 3.83 → 1.93; rung 2 0.81 → 4.24 → 2.60; rung 3 0.75 → 5.28 → 2.48; Sharpshooter party 1.49 → 6.39 → 3.62. The threshold alone lands between the two at every rung and is nowhere near 0.81 — it is roughly a TRIPLING of the pre-CZ rate. So the threshold was the half that mattered: it does most of the work the builders were also asked to do, without changing what the card is. Devout healing a battle comes back about a third from CZ’s peak and stays well above where the lane started (rung 2: 69 → 178 → 133).

ELEVATION AND BLESSING OF THE FAITHFUL ARE REPORTED AND UNCHANGED, AS INSTRUCTED. Elevation grants 2 against a threshold of 3 — 67% of a release, party-wide, in one cast. Blessing of the Faithful still needs 3 held of a possible 3, the whole bar, and is still castable only by the Devout since an ally reaching 3 releases on the spot. Both are printed by check_cz and check_da every run so neither can drift silently.

A CZ DOCUMENTATION MISS THE REVERT EXPOSED, FIXED HERE. master.html still described the release threshold as 5 in two places — Elevation’s card (“reaches the cap of 5 and RELEASES”) and the Faith status row (“At 5 the bearer heals 15%”). CZ moved that number in three code sites and in three of five prose sites. Both are corrected, along with the builder rates in the status row, the spec block, Consecrated Ground’s card and the glossary.

§2 — GLACIAL PRISON IS REFUSED WHEN IT WOULD WRITE NOTHING

Its whole cast-time payload is Chilled plus _hold_freeze, and that function returns immediately on an already-frozen target — so a recast onto a held enemy writes nothing while costing the turn, the resource and the cooldown. Three edits and no fourth: RECAST_GATED gains it (59 now), _recast_targets adds it to the living-enemies pool, and _recast_writes gains its case. The refusal is _recast_refused called from _ability_usable, the same door every other refusal uses. check_da counts the occurrences of _recast_refused in battle.gd and fails on a fourth, so a second path cannot be added quietly.

IT IS THE FIRST TALENT-GRANT IN THE SET, AND THAT IS WHAT THE ENUMERATION HOLE ACTUALLY COST. CO’s criterion could not be applied to an ability no walk in the project could see, so the defect was invisible rather than merely unfixed.

THE ONE MEMBER WHOSE HANDLER GUARDS ITS OWN WRITE, SO THE TABLE MIRRORS THE GUARD AND NOT THE VALUE. Every other member calls _apply_status unconditionally and lets add_status’s max() discard the weaker value; Glacial Prison reads if not target.has_status("chilled") and never calls it at all. So the Chilled half is proposed only when it would land — proposing it on an already-Chilled target would have the gate read its own optimism as an improvement, CR §3 from the other direction — while the freeze half is proposed unconditionally and _status_write_improves decides it, exactly as every other member works. The duration comes out of one authored copy: _freeze_turns() is new, _hold_freeze now calls it for the number it writes, and CR §3’s defect was precisely a duration authored in the handler and again in the table.

WHICH HALF DECIDES IT: NEITHER. The Chilled half saves the cast approximately never, and that is a proof rather than a sample — _hold_freeze is the only site in the project that writes frozen, and every path through it that lands the freeze also writes Chilled (4 stacks for a real hold, 1 for ordinary ice), so a frozen body always carries Chilled. What decides the button is the POOL: the rule darkens a BUTTON rather than a PICK, so it fires only when every living enemy is frozen, and one unfrozen enemy anywhere keeps it lit. That is the honest scope of the rule and not a defect in it — Rime, Bola and Hysteria have carried the same scope since CO, and a per-pick refusal would be the second path §2 forbids by name.

ONE KNOWN INEXACTNESS, ERRING TOWARD ALLOWING. A NON-BOSS carrying a one-turn freeze while a Cryomancer stands would read the proposed permanent hold as an improvement while the handler wrote nothing. _apply_status(_, "frozen", …) has exactly one call site and cannot produce that pairing; it needs a Cryomancer who died, let the ice land timed, and was resurrected. Allowing a wasted cast is the safe error; refusing a live one is not.

HOW OFTEN IT FIRES CANNOT BE READ OFF THE SIM, AND SAYING SO IS THE FINDING. DOD_SIM_BUILDS defaults to each tree’s FIRST lane, which for the Cryomancer is Winter — so the sim’s Cryomancer has never held Glacial Prison, Second Prison or Absolute Zero, and no figure in any prior report speaks to this card at all. A fifth run was made on cryomancer:Deep Freeze as a live smoke test: it freezes less often and holds far longer (holds lasting ≥3 turns 2.65 a battle against the default’s 1.75), and it is the build that takes Absolute Zero, which removes the hold limit — so that is the build in which an all-enemies-frozen board is genuinely reachable. 25 runs, no throws, Faith figures steady across the build change.

§3 — A HELPER COPIED BETWEEN GATES INHERITS ITS BUGS SILENTLY

Recorded as a standing rule in CLAUDE.md:

Enumerate the ability corpus through Classes.ability_corpus(). Never copy another gate’s walk. A talent can grant an ability that lives in no pool, and a hand-rolled walk misses five. A helper copied between gates inherits its bugs silently and diverges from its origin without anything reporting it.

THIS IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM EVERYTHING ELSE IN CLAUDE.md’S TRAPS, AND THE FIRST CONFIRMED CASE IN THE PROJECT. The rest are DRIFT — one authority, edited, a stale copy left behind. This is propagation by copy: five gates wrong in five places from birth, because four copied check_cl_width’s walk rather than deriving one. Fixing the origin leaves four. Drift leaves one wrong copy and a chance a diff notices it; a copy leaves N, all born wrong, none of them compared against anything. check_da asserts the rule rather than only stating it, with CZ’s _cl_only_corpus named as the one exemption — being a copy is its job there, and the gate asserts it is still a copy so a later reader cannot consolidate it into uselessness.

THE SWEEP FOUND ONE MORE AND CHANGES NOTHING. _spawn, the battle fixture, is copied into SEVEN gates as FOUR divergent bodies — and the signature diverged too (_spawn(specs: Array), _spawn(), _spawn(run: Node)). It has already cost twice. The copied _report drifted into "N checks, M failures" and "N checks / M failures", and run_battery.sh’s own header records the scar: a grep -E "checks," that silently missed every suite printing the second form. And CQ §1 deliberately deleted the two hand-set Profile.set_flag lines from check_cm_live’s copy and left them standing in check_co’s and check_ct’s, with nothing anywhere reporting the divergence. check_da prints the census every run so the number cannot rot into a sentence nobody re-checks. CONSOLIDATION IS ITS OWN BATCH: a shared fixture has to serve four legitimately different needs (a party parameter, check_cs’s determinism forcing, check_ct’s pre-loaded pouch, check_cm_live’s deliberately absent flags), and getting it wrong breaks every gate at once.

THE SAME DEFECT IS FAR LARGER IN THE SUITES, REPORTED AND OUT OF SCOPE: the same sweep over the 47 test_batch_*.gd files finds _spawn in 37 suites as 34 distinct bodies, _run in 39 as 39, and _kill copied byte-identically into 14.

§4 — CY’S TWO HEADLINE MEASUREMENTS WERE BOTH INSTRUMENT FAULTS

Recorded so that a later reader does not cite either figure as evidence. Neither finding is new — CZ reported both against its own interest — but they are scattered across two reports and they belong together in the record.

  • THE FAITH ARRIVAL ROW SAMPLED A METER THAT NEVER RELEASES. “Faith reaches 1.6 of the 5 a release needs, so the average fight ends without a Devout release ever firing” is not what the number says. The conviction row samples the Devout’s own meter, and his Faith holds at the threshold and never releases by rule (Batch BH §2). It has never been a measure of release frequency. The row that answers that question was in the same report all along: releases/battle, reading 0.51 to 1.49 on unmodified HEAD. Releases were firing.
  • THE BLOOD FRENZY REGRESSION SAT INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT’S OWN ERROR BAR. The 12.2 → 11.8 movement that motivated CZ §1 is smaller than the ±1.5 points of band this instrument carries at n=25 on an unseeded sim. The number was not the evidence.

CZ §1 REMAINS CORRECT ON ITS STRUCTURAL REASONING AND IS NOT REVISITED. A passive paid in damage TAKEN really does invert against every batch that improves party survivability; that mechanism is real, it is a standing rule in CLAUDE.md, and it was worth fixing. The fix was worth making for the mechanism, not for the number — and the Rage term it added is untouched here, measuring 17.1 / 20.7 / 22.6 / 26.2 across the four arms against CZ’s 17.4 / 20.9 / 22.8 / 26.2, which is the control that says this batch moved Faith and nothing else.

Seven gates, zero failures, zero throws. check_parse 0 (stderr grepped for Parse Error, never the tally — and it caught a real error in this batch that the tally did not: check_da’s first run exited 0 with two Parse Error lines on stderr), check_da 30 checks / 0 failures (new, and added to run_battery.sh’s GATES array, now fourteen), check_co 0 at 59 gated abilities with the new member driven live, check_cz 0, check_cn 0, check_cm 0, check_flow 0.

FIVE COMPLETE RUNS OF THE GAME — 25 runs each, ~2,500 battles a pass. Completions CZ → DA: rung 1 100→100%, rung 2 72→80%, rung 3 52→56%, Sharpshooter party 72→76%. Depth: 48.00→48.00, 46.56→47.12, 42.84→44.76, 47.04→46.12. NO ARM MOVED FURTHER THAN ITS OWN COMBINED STANDARD ERROR, so taking a third of the Devout’s healing back off did not make the game measurably harder — the expected result for a change aimed at what a card IS rather than at difficulty.

NO SUITE AND NO FULL BATTERY WAS RUN; DA is implement-only under the standing convention. One piece of good news for the batch that owes one: test_batch_bi asserts const FAITH_PER_ABSORB := 2 and an ally holding 2 after one absorb, so CZ had turned it red and this revert turns it back green without the suite being run.

2026-08-21 — Batch CZ: TWO RAMPS THAT DO NOT ARRIVE, AND A HOLE IN THE ENUMERATION

CY measured four ramp specs and found two arriving and two not. This is the repair for the two that do not, plus the enumeration gap CY reported and did not close. Blood Frenzy gets a second term the Berserker controls, Faith’s release threshold falls from 5 to 3 and both its builders rise, the six shields take the buff delay cap, and up_speed is revived from a floor CY’s cap had made unreachable. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/CZ.md.

§0 — THE ENUMERATION REACHES 216 NOW, AND IT IS ONE FUNCTION

Classes.ability_corpus() is the only enumeration in the project. It walks the kits, the class pools and the spec pools exactly as the Batch CL enumeration did, then walks Classes.talent_granted_names() through Talents.granted_ability — the one resolver both grant shapes go through. FIVE gates carried five copies of the same hole, not the two the brief named: check_cm, check_cn, check_co, check_cy (which had built the complete walk inline for its own use) and check_cl_width — the ORIGINAL, the one the other four copied. All five read the shared function now. It lives on Classes rather than in a gate because the question is about the game’s data rather than about testing it.

THE CL WALK REACHES 211; THE COMPLETE WALK REACHES 216. check_cz.gd re-derives the old walk as a negative control — its whole job is to still be missing the five, so a later batch cannot let the gap close itself and leave this report stale.

CN OWES NOTHING. Its criterion, re-run over the five, already answers all of them correctly: Backdraft, Glacial Prison, Cryoclasm and Intercession deal no damage and no Break damage, so the grade has nothing to multiply and the bar is correctly off; Pyroblast is an ordinary attack and correctly keeps its bar. Only CN’s printed population was short.

CO OWES ONE RULING, ON ONE ABILITY — GLACIAL PRISON. Its whole cast-time payload is Chilled plus _hold_freeze, and that function returns immediately on a target that is already frozen, so a recast onto a held enemy writes nothing at all — precisely the waste CO exists to refuse. The other four do not qualify: Backdraft is additive (Interpose’s shape, so a recast always improves), Cryoclasm moves state between two enemies and reschedules one, Pyroblast attacks, Intercession is an ally buff already inside CY’s cap. REPORTED, NOT TAKEN — CQ §6’s rule, and the _recast_writes half has to be right before the table entry goes in.

ONE THING THE REPAIR SURFACED FOR FREE: check_cl_width had never measured those five descriptions at all. Re-pointed, it now does, and all five are clean — zero authored lines over the 44-character ceiling, corpus figure unchanged at 8.

§1 — BLOOD FRENZY GETS A SECOND TERM HE CONTROLS

+2% per 5% of health missing, AND +2% per 5% of Rage spent. The same rate off either bar. The inversion was the problem rather than the number: Blood Frenzy is paid in health MISSING, so every improvement to party survivability weakens it — CY’s cheaper mitigation buffs made the Berserker take less damage and his own band got shallower, in a batch aimed at helping him. Rage spent is the only term genuinely under his control, and his pool already moves Rage constantly.

TWO TERMS, ONE BAND, AND THE BAND DOES NOT GROW. FRENZY_MAX_STEPS = 20 is not a new ceiling — it is the one the health term always had at zero health. The steps are SUMMED and then CLAMPED, so the second term can only fill the band sooner, never make it deeper. His identity as the spec that fights better hurt is not rewritten; he is given a floor a well-played party cannot take away, and a Berserker already in the red gets nothing from it.

THE RATE IS FLAGGED AND THE FIGURE IS REPORTED: FRENZY_RAGE_PER_STEP = 5. A Berserker’s Rage maximum is 100, so five Rage IS 5% of the Rage bar — the health term’s own rate off the other bar, which makes it a rule rather than a tuning constant. Measured Rage spent a battle across four 25-run sims: 37.3 / 39.5 / 47.9 / 57.8 at rungs 1/2/3 and the Sharpshooter party — 7.5 to 11.6 of the 20 steps.

CY’S FOUR SIMS, RE-RUN. Blood Frenzy’s peak, of 40 points: rung 1 6.2 → 17.4, rung 2 13.4 → 20.9, rung 3 12.1 → 22.8, Sharpshooter party 13.9 → 26.2. At rung 2 that is 33% → 52% of the band, and the regression CY reported is closed in every arm.

THE LEDGER BOOKS WHAT LEFT THE BAR, NOT ab.cost. One function (BattleUnit.note_resource_spent) and three callers — the one line in _resolve where every ability in the game pays, Reckless Abandon’s bar dump, and Last Rites. Measuring the bar rather than a field is what makes it un-farmable: Battle Shout costs 15 and refunds 5, so it books 10; Snap Shot and Twin Hunt waive the cost outright and book nothing. A judgement call recorded rather than buried: Last Rites is counted, because it is Rage a talent he chose converts into survival and excluding it would mean the deeper he invests in the Fury lane the less his own passive notices. Reckless Abandon is the extreme case and is named rather than discovered later — a full 100 books all twenty steps at once, for a turn and every point of his resource, and the clamp means it cannot take him past a band a dying Berserker already reaches.

§2 — FAITH REACHES ITS RELEASE

THE THRESHOLD FALLS FROM 5 TO 3, AND IT WAS A LITERAL FIVE IN THREE PLACES — the cap on the count, the release branch and Communion’s “still building” guard. battle.FAITH_RELEASE is one number now. Both builders rise with it, because a meter filling at a third of the rate it needs is not fixed by shortening the bar: Faith per absorbed hit 2 → 3 (FAITH_PER_ABSORB) and Faith per ally turn on Consecrated Ground 1 → 2 (FAITH_PER_GROUND_TURN, which was a bare literal at its one call site).

MEASURED, AT EACH RUNG, BESIDE CY’S ORIGINALS. Peak Faith: rung 1 1.9 of 5 (39%) → 2.5 of 3 (85%), rung 2 2.3 (46%) → 2.4 (81%), rung 3 2.4 (47%) → 2.4 (80%), Sharpshooter party 2.8 (56%) → 2.5 (84%). Faith releases per battle: 0.51 → 3.83, 0.81 → 4.24, 0.75 → 5.28, 1.49 → 6.39.

FLAGGED HARD, BECAUSE IT IS A LARGE POWER SWING: releases rose five- to seven-fold and the Devout’s total healing roughly TRIPLED (69 → 178 a battle at rung 2). Four combinations were measured before one shipped: the threshold move ALONE already takes releases to 2.71; 3 absorb / 1 ground reads 2.81; 2/2 reads 3.17; the shipped 3/2 reads 5.31. FAITH_PER_ABSORB := 2 is the measured alternative and is one character away.

A CONCERN IN THE SHIPPED NUMBERS, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED: three per absorb against a threshold of three means ONE ABSORBED HIT IS A WHOLE RELEASE. A shielded ally never HOLDS Faith now — he fills and pays out on the same blow, and the held half of the meter stops existing for him. Nothing is lost (the peak keeps paying), but the card stops being a ramp and becomes a per-hit heal. And raising the absorb rate does not move the figure the batch is measured on: the Faith arrival row samples the DEVOUT’S OWN meter, which is fed by the ground drip on his own turns rather than by absorbs.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS MEASURING SOMETHING ELSE, AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING. CY’s “Faith reaches 1.6 of the 5 a release needs, so the average fight ends without a release ever firing” is not what that number says. The conviction row samples the DEVOUT’S OWN meter, and his Faith HOLDS at the threshold and never releases by rule (Batch BH §2) — it has never been a measure of whether a release fires. The number that answers that was in the same report all along: the Faith decomposition’s releases/battle, which read 0.51 to 1.49 on unmodified HEAD. Releases were firing. Both rows are reported now rather than one standing in for the other, and the caveat is written into CY_METERS beside the row.

TWO INTERACTIONS CHECKED AND REPORTED, WITH NOTHING CHANGED. Blessing of the Faithful needs 3 Faith held, which was most of a bar and is now exactly the bar — so the card is castable precisely when the meter is full, and only by the Devout, since an ally reaching 3 releases on the spot and can never be holding three when the button is read. Elevation grants 2, which was 40% of a release and is now 67% of one, to every ally at once — and it is the one magnitude in this lane with a history of being moved by accident. A third the brief did not name: the held half lost two stacks of ceiling. Faith pays on the highest count held and the count caps at the threshold, so the deepest benefit an ally can hold fell from 5 stacks (10% mitigation, +7.5% damage) to 3 (6%, +4.5%). The lane trades depth of hold for frequency of release, deliberately.

§3 — SHIELDS TAKE THE SAME DELAY CAP

THE RULE, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE SECTION: A SHIELD TAKES THE BUFF DELAY CAP; A HEAL DOES NOT. A shield is played BEFORE the blow; a heal answers what just happened. Divine Shield 2.5 → 1.0, Mantle 2.5 → 1.0, Interpose, Magic Barrier, Mirror Image and Vespers all 2.0 → 1.0. Nothing else about any of them moved.

THEY ARE A SEPARATE POPULATION AND STAY ONE. Ability.SHIELD_SPECIALS is a second list rather than five names appended to PURE_BUFFS, so CY’s table can still be checked as the thing CY derived and the criterion that excluded them — a consumable absorb pool or charge count — is still correct. They are capped on the TEMPO rule rather than on the payload one, and Ability.takes_delay_cap() is the one function that unions the two so make() and every gate ask the same question.

ONE OF THE SIX IS ON CR’S DURATION LIST: VESPERS, whose 4-turn duration meets its own 4-turn cooldown. CR accepted that on the reasoning that holding it costs an action and its resource every cycle; at half delay that maintenance is now half price. Nothing is changed — the same fold CY reported for 28 of the 52, surfacing now rather than in an audit five batches out.

THE FIFTEEN HEALS ARE UNTOUCHED FOR A SECOND BATCH, AND NOW BOTH HALVES ARE ASSERTED. check_cz.gd fails if any drafted heal is caught by the cap or sits at or under it: a rule with only its positive half checked would let a later batch halve every heal in the game and still pass.

§4 — up_speed IS REVIVED, AND THE SWEEP FOUND ONE MORE

Swift’s floor was a literal 1.0 — exactly CY’s cap — so it was a DEAD PICK on all 52 pure buffs. maxf(1.0 × 0.75, 1.0) is 1.0: the reward was live on every one of them the day before and bought nothing the day after, in silence. Ability.DELAY_FLOOR is BUFF_DELAY_CAP × 0.5 = 0.50 today, so the ladder reads a swing 2.00, setting up 1.00, and the cheapest an upgrade can buy 0.50 and all three move together on a retune.

FLAGGED: half the cap is a judgement call. It is the only value that keeps Swift meaningful on the cheapest card in the game without making it free — 25% off a capped buff is 0.75, which clears 0.50 with room, so one Swift always does something and no stack of them reaches zero. Zero is reachable elsewhere and deliberately not here: Instinctive Rotation sets the delay to 0.0 as a talent’s whole payload, and an upgrade should not buy what a node exists to grant.

upgrade_fits("up_speed") now asks a question. It fell through to return true on the note that “Swift is the one that fits everything — every ability has a delay”, which was true for eight batches and stopped being true without a line changing there. It changes no offer today and is what keeps the dud closed if a later batch authors something cheaper.

THE SWEEP FOUND EXACTLY TWO SITES AND THE SECOND IS A FINDING: Mana Shield’s minf(eff_delay, 1.5) IS NOW INERT. Mana Shield is a pure buff, so its delay IS the cap and the clamp can never bind. It is reported and KEPT, not deleted — it is a clamp, and what it does is keep the discount unable to RAISE the cost, which is the exact failure CY caught it in the act of. Its description still says “It is quick to cast”: true, and no longer distinguishing. Nothing else in the project floors or compares a delay against a literal; no rune, relic or talent modifies delay at all.

§5 — GATES

ELEVEN GATES, ZERO FAILURES, ZERO THROWS. check_parse 0 (stderr grepped for Parse Error, never the tally), check_cm 0, check_cn 0, check_co 0, check_cs 104/0, check_ct 113/0, check_cu 0, check_cv 0 (324 nodes), check_cy 0, check_cz 0, check_flow 0. check_cz.gd is new and joins the battery’s gate list, which is now thirteen. It covers all five sections and the two halves only a live battle can settle: a real cast has to reach the Rage ledger with what actually left the bar, and an ally walked to the threshold has to release while the Devout’s own meter, driven to the same count, holds — the negative control that stops §2’s rule passing for the wrong reason.

Eight complete runs of the game, four before and four after — 25 runs each, three difficulty rungs, ~2,500 battles a pass. Completions before → after: rung 1 100 → 100%, rung 2 60 → 72%, rung 3 44 → 52%, Sharpshooter party 68 → 72%. Depth reached: 48.00 → 48.00, 45.64 → 46.56, 43.04 → 42.84, 44.68 → 47.04. Only the Sharpshooter arm’s move is bigger than the combined standard error, and completions are the noisy secondary the harness says never to quote alone. The honest summary is that the batch did not make the game measurably harder or easier, which is the right outcome for a change aimed at two specs rather than at difficulty.

NO SUITE AND NO FULL BATTERY WAS RUN. CZ is implement-only under the standing convention. The next dedicated test batch owes one against CW’s eleven unrepaired assertions, CY’s 52 moved delays, and this batch’s six more plus a Faith threshold three suites may quote.

FOUND WHILE WORKING, REPORTED AND NOT FIXED. check_cu and check_cv are NOT in run_battery.sh’s GATES array — CY’s report lists both among the nine gates it ran and the battery runs neither. Both were run by hand here (0 failures each). And CY’s printed after-figures do not reproduce on unmodified HEAD: re-measured at the same settings the same instrument reads Frenzy 6.2 / 13.4 / 12.1 / 13.9 against CY’s 7.4 / 11.8 / 12.7 / 12.7. That is n=25 noise on an unseeded sim — roughly ±1.5 points of band — and it means the 12.2 → 11.8 regression that motivated §1 is smaller than this instrument’s own error bar. The inversion it revealed is real and structural; the number was not the evidence.

2026-08-21 — Batch CY: A BUFF COSTS HALF A SWING

One systematic rule applied to 52 abilities: a pure buff’s initiative delay is capped at half the basic attack’s. 51 came down to 1.0; one was already there. Nothing else about any of them moved — no cost, no cooldown, no duration, no magnitude. §0 measured the thing the fix is aimed at and nobody had ever measured: a fight is 3.0 to 5.5 turns per hero. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/CY.md.

§0 — THE TWO MEASUREMENTS, BOTH TAKEN BEFORE A LINE OF §1 WAS WRITTEN

HOW LONG IS A FIGHT? THREE TO FIVE TURNS PER HERO. Four --run 25 sims across three difficulty rungs, ~2,300 battles: trash 3.5 / 3.8 / 4.1 rounds at rungs 1/2/3, boss 3.8 / 4.3 / 4.5, and elite 3.0 / 3.3 / 3.6 — the SHORTEST of the three kinds at every rung, which is the finding nobody would have predicted. Spending a turn on setup is 20–33% of everything a hero will do in the fight.

Rounds are counted as turns per living party member, and that is a correction. The standing report line divides hero_actions by three; the party has been FOUR since the class draft, so that line has been reading a third high. Companions are excluded from both halves of the fraction — a summoned beast takes turns the hero did not spend, which would have made a Beastmaster’s fights look longest when he is the spec least able to afford a setup turn.

DOES THE RAMP ARRIVE? TWO OF THE FOUR DO, AND TWO DO NOT. Each meter is banked as a per-battle peak and reported as a fraction of what the spec is built around, at rung 2: Blood Frenzy 12.2 of 40 points = 31%; Faith 1.6 of the 5 stacks a release needs = 32%; Loyalty 20.0 of 5 = 400%; Focus 131.3 of 100 = 131%. Loyalty and Focus are uncapped meters that tick on a timer, so they arrive and keep going (deepest observed 66 and 460). Blood Frenzy and Faith have to be EARNED out of what the fight does to you, and both land near a third. 1.6 of 5 means the average fight ends without a Faith release ever firing.

The sampler is read-only by construction — frenzy_bonus() is deliberately not called, because it ratchets the floor as a side effect and an instrument that moves what it measures is not an instrument.

CONFOUNDER, NAMED: every sim party is FULLY TALENTED (rows=9 of 9), which is stronger than a real player at zone 1. Weakening the party does not lengthen the fight — the rung-1 row is the closest thing to an under-equipped party and it is the SHORTEST fight in the table, because the enemy budget falls with the rung.

§0a — AND WHAT IT DID: THE SAME FOUR SIMS, RE-RUN AFTER THE CAP

Beyond the brief’s ask, and here because “half is the designer’s first guess” is a decision that wants evidence. Read with the harness’s own warning attached: at n=25 completions are a noisy secondary and depth reached is the primary, SE 0.5–2.8 slots; the runs are not seed-paired. Completions: rung 1 100→100%, rung 2 52→84%, rung 3 12→36%, Sharpshooter party 48→52%. Depth reached: 46.32→46.80, 33.16→39.88, 41.12→42.60. Depth rose in all three measurable arms and only rung 3’s move exceeds the combined standard error. The change helps, it helps most where the party was losing, and n=25 cannot size it more precisely than that.

FIGHTS GOT LONGER, NOT SHORTER — trash at rung 2 3.8 → 4.4 rounds. A cheaper buff does not end fights faster; it buys a party that survives to take more turns. FAITH IS THE METER THAT ANSWERED: peak Faith rose at every rung (1.6 → 2.1 at rung 2, roughly a third more) and is still short of the 5 a release needs. AND BLOOD FRENZY WENT THE OTHER WAY, WHICH IS NOT A BUG: peak Frenzy FELL at every rung (12.2 → 11.8 at rung 2, 14.4 → 12.7 at rung 3). Blood Frenzy pays for health already lost, and the cap made Spite, Ironclad and every other mitigation buff cheaper to hold, so the Berserker takes less damage and his own band gets shallower. Cheaper defence is a nerf to the one passive that is paid in damage taken. Flagged for the designer; no number was changed to hide it.

§1 — THE RULE, AND IT IS WRITTEN AGAINST BASIC_DELAY

Ability.BUFF_DELAY_CAP := BASIC_DELAY * 0.5. The design statement is setting up costs less tempo than swinging, so the cap is expressed against the baseline rather than as the 1.0 it evaluates to today — retune the baseline and the rule stays true instead of silently becoming a different rule. BASIC_DELAY itself moved onto Ability and battle.gd now aliases it: the delay is an ability’s property and Ability.make is where the cap has to be applied, so that is where the one authored 2.0 lives. All twelve of battle.gd’s sites read the alias and there is still exactly one 2.0 in the project.

THE CAP IS APPLIED IN TWO PLACES AND THEY CANNOT DISAGREE. Ability.make() clamps it — one function, so the draft card, the tooltip, the timeline preview and the cast all get the same answer. The 52 authored definitions were rewritten to Ability.BUFF_DELAY_CAP so the data does not lie about what the card costs, which is CR’s own rule: a change to a value is finished when every site that QUOTES it is updated, and an authored literal is a quoting site. The clamp is therefore a no-op on today’s data and check_cy.gd asserts that it is — it is what keeps the rule true for content a later batch adds.

THE POPULATION WAS DERIVED BY WALKING _resolve_special’S CALL GRAPH, NOT BY READING damage AND pressure. Those two fields are zero on 137 of the 216 abilities, Feint, Guard Change and Kill Command among them, and every one of those hits hard from inside its handler. CN paid for that lesson on the timing bar, CO paid for it again on the recast refusal, and this is the third table derived the same way. The criterion, stated so a later batch can apply it rather than guess: a PURE BUFF is an ability whose ENTIRE cast-time payload is one or more statuses (or status-backed flags) written to the CASTER or to LIVING ALLIES — no damage, no Break damage, no heal, no resource, no Pressure, no cooldown, no initiative, no summon, no revive, no purge, and nothing at all written to any enemy.

Cast time is the whole of it, because the delay is paid at cast. What the status goes on to do afterwards — Venom Coating poisoning every later hit, Tripwire springing on an enemy’s turn, Arcane Arrows striking a second body — is what the buff IS, not a second payload.

§1a — A CORRECTION TO THE CORPUS ITSELF, AND IT CHANGED THE ANSWER

The Batch CL enumeration that check_cn.gd and check_co.gd both walk MISSES FIVE ABILITIES, and always has. It walks the kits, the class pools and the spec pools; a talent node that GRANTS an ability which is in no pool is invisible to it. The five are Backdraft, Pyroblast, Glacial Prison, Cryoclasm and INTERCESSION.

Intercession is a pure buff — a party-wide death-save whose whole payload is a status on every living hero — so a CL-only sweep would have left it at 2.0 while its fifty-one neighbours came down to 1.0. check_cy.gd walks Talents.LANE_TREES through Talents.granted_ability on top of the CL enumeration, so the corpus it checks is 216, not 211. CN’s and CO’s tables were derived over the smaller corpus and are NOT re-derived here — whether either needs re-running against 216 is a decision, not a detail. Four of the five are enemy-facing and could not join either table.

§1b — THE COUNT, AND THE THREE POPULATIONS THAT DID NOT MOVE

52 pure buffs. 51 came down to 1.0; FEIGNED GUARD was already at the cap and did not change. The distribution: 2 fall by 2.0, 10 by 1.5, 24 by 1.0, 15 by 0.5. The largest single moves are Consecrated Ground and Rite of Return, both 3.0 → 1.0.

Reported and untouched: 15 HEALS, 6 SHIELDS, 66 that do more than buff, and every enemy ability. SHIELDS GO TO THE DESIGNER AS A LIST, exactly as the brief asks — Divine Shield, Magic Barrier, Mantle, Interpose, Mirror Image and Vespers. The line is mechanical: a shield is a consumable absorb pool or charge count that eats incoming attacks. Percentage mitigation running for N turns is not one, which is why Immolate, Ironclad, Camouflage and Consecrated Ground are buffs and those six are not. For the heals the answer to is this card a heal is HEAL_SPECIALS plus the heal fields — CN §2 authored that question once and this batch does not ask it a second way.

TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED, in ability.gd beside the table. The death-saves are IN — Rite of Return, Bloodbond, Intercession, Ashes of Al’ar and Undying Vigil are each armed BEFORE the blow they answer, which is setup by every test the rule states, and none is an absorb pool; if the designer rules them shields they leave as one group. The heal-over-time buffs are IN — Consecration, Aegis Wall and Battle Trance heal through a status they set, none heals a point at cast, and HEAL_SPECIALS says none of the three is a heal card.

§2 — THE CONSEQUENCE THAT REACHES BACK INTO CR

CR accepted 40 buffs whose duration meets or exceeds its own cooldown, on the reasoning that holding one costs an action and its resource every cycle. At half delay that maintenance is half price, and 28 of the 40 are in §1’s population. All 28 are tabled with their duration, cooldown and new delay in docs/reports/CY.md, and NONE OF THEM CHANGED beyond the delay every other member got. The twelve that are not in the population are excluded for reasons this batch did not touch: ten write to enemies, zeal ticks cooldowns and vespers is a shield.

The sharpest row is IMMOLATE: a 4-turn window on a 2-turn cooldown that now costs half a swing to hold. CR’s maintenance argument was already thinnest there.

A SECOND, SMALLER FOLD, FOUND WHILE APPLYING THIS ONE. The up_speed ability upgrade reads ab.delay = maxf(ab.delay * 0.75, 1.0). Its floor is a literal 1.0, which is now exactly the cap — so up_speed on any of the 52 is a DEAD PICK, and it was live on all of them yesterday. Reported, changed in no way.

AND CO’S RECAST REFUSAL WILL FIRE MORE. Cheaper buffs get recast more often, so the gate that refuses a recast which would not improve gets asked more often. That is correct behaviour and needs no change; a later reader should not read the increase as a regression.

§2a — THE ONE MECHANICAL CONSEQUENCE THAT HAD TO BE TAKEN

MANA SHIELD’S FLAT DISCOUNT IS CLAMPED RATHER THAN ASSIGNED. CN §3 made it unconditional (eff_delay = 1.5 at the cast site) and §1 brings its authored 2.0 down to 1.0. Left alone the discount would have been a penalty dressed as a bonus — the one card in the game where it is quick to cast made it slower. It reads minf(eff_delay, 1.5) now, which is what the discount always claimed to do.

§3 — WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO

Buffs are not free and do not stack onto another action — the cost is reduced, not removed, and every one still spends its resource, its cooldown and half a swing. A free buff would make every buff strictly correct to cast and would delete the decision across the whole category. No ramp spec starts a fight with meter on the clock; that is still available, and §0’s Faith measurement is now the argument for it. No enemy health changes and the turn structure does not change.

§4 — THE GATE

check_cy.gd is new and joins the battery’s gate list. It asserts the rule against BASIC_DELAY, the table’s shape, the excluded populations BY NAME (CO’s lesson: a gate that can only pass is a gap), the mechanical half against each ability’s own fields, CN’s criterion from the other side (a pure buff runs no timing bar) — and then the live half: it spawns two real battles across two parties, casts all 52 through _resolve_special, and asserts every enemy’s health, resource and status set and every hero’s health, resource, second resource and Faith are exactly where they were. 104 casts, 0 failures. The derivation is executed, not read.

Nine gates run clean: check_parse 0, check_cn 0, check_co 0, check_cs 104/0, check_ct 113/0, check_cu 0, check_cv 0, check_flow 0, check_cy 0. Eight complete runs of the game finished end to end (four before the change, four after; 25 runs each). NO FULL BATTERY WAS RUN — implement-only under the standing convention, and the next dedicated test batch still owes one.

2026-08-20 — Batch CX: THE CHANGELOG CUT, AND THREE RULINGS

Four items, and one of them was deliberately not implemented. §1 executes the archive rule CW wrote and did not use: the live changelog goes 494.2 KB → 148.7 KB, 23 of its 32 entries move out of the repo, and 11 suites are re-pointed at the archive on CD’s pattern. §3 and §4 are one-line design rulings with real code behind them. §2 is reported and STOPPED — per-hero relics is a save-format change and the brief said to say so rather than spend the week. No save version moves (still v10). The full report is docs/reports/CX.md.

§0 — WHAT RUNNING THE SUITES FOUND, AND IT WAS NOT THIS BATCH’S DOING

CW left ELEVEN red assertions across EIGHT suites and nobody knew, because CT, CU, CV and CW were all implement-only and no battery has run since CS. CW’s CLAUDE.md split dropped every batch narrative, and seven suites assert against text that went with it: BATCH BB, BATCH BQ, BATCH BR, BATCH BX, rot_hp_lost, _releasing, TRANCHES 2 AND 3, “rungs 2 and 3 were not touched”, “naming the twelve” and “SECOND CLASS COMPLETE”. The eleventh is a knock-on: test_batch_cd is the count-differ — it re-runs other suites and asserts each reports zero failures — so FAIL: test_batch_bb.gd reports zero failures is CW’s damage arriving a second time, through the one gate built to notice exactly this. None of them is a changelog check and none was caused by §1 — they are recorded in docs/state.md as owed, not silently repaired, because deciding what those assertions should ask INSTEAD is CW’s decision to make and not a detail to guess at.

Two of them pass by accident and are worse than the eight that fail. contains("BATCH BN") and contains("BATCH BS") still match — not a batch block, but a passing mention inside two of the surviving rules. That is the “check that has stopped asking its question” pattern exactly, arriving through a document this time instead of through the changelog.

An eleventh red is older and unrelated: glossary.json still reads “beast” once in prose — “pay the four and not the beast”, in CV’s own hero/ally entry — which test_batch_bx §4 catches. One word, and it belongs to the prose rename, so it is reported rather than taken here.

§1 — THE CHANGELOG IS CUT AT CN/CO

486 KB was the figure on record; re-derived it was 494.2 KB, against CW’s 400 KB threshold. Cut at a batch boundary, nothing edited, and the live file does not move — which is why build_docs.py keeps working.

  • The live file starts at Batch CO and holds 9 entries: CO through CW. 494.2 KB → 148.7 KB, the ~150 KB the rule asks for, so the next cut is many batches away rather than immediate.
  • 23 entries — BP through CN — moved to DoD-archive/changelog-archive.html, which grows 108 entries to 131. 140 entries before, 140 after. Nothing deleted.
  • THE VERIFICATION IS THE POINT. Every <h2> was extracted from the original and from both halves: counts sum (9 + 23 = 32), zero overlap, order preserved, and the two bodies rejoined are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original. A second script re-derived all of it from untouched backups rather than from the splitter, and asserted that every one of the 140 headings appears exactly once across the two files and that none was invented. No file size is asserted anywhere — sizes agreeing is entirely consistent with a duplicated entry and a dropped one.
  • One heading does not fit on one line. Batch BF’s wraps, so a ^<h2>.*</h2>$ extractor counts 107 where the archive holds 108. Caught because the two counting methods disagreed; the extractor reads across lines now. A split that drops one entry of 140 is invisible, and this is the shape of the thing that hides it.

ELEVEN SUITES RE-POINTED, AND MOST OF THEM WOULD HAVE GONE ON PASSING. bp, bq, br, bs, bt, bu, bv, bw, bx, cb and ce each asserted their own entry against the LIVE file, and eight did it with a bare contains("Batch XX") — satisfied by a later entry naming the batch in prose, so it passes with its subject in a different file entirely. That failure has now happened three times here (BZ’s in test_batch_bb, CD’s in test_batch_bo), so this time it was repaired in the same batch that caused it. CD’s pattern throughout: anchor on the <h2> heading, which prose cannot reproduce, and reach the archive by following the path out of the live file’s own header, never by hardcoding it — so the next cut moves all eleven with it.

test_batch_ce got one thing more: its contains("102") ran against the whole file, and against a 1 MB archive three digits turn up in any document with enough numbers in it — a check that can only pass. It reads inside the CE entry now.

Both headers rewritten to name each other, and the live header’s “see the Batch BZ entry below” was pointing at an entry this cut moved out; it points at CX now. Fifteen suites were run — the fourteen stamp-gate suites plus cb — zero throws, and every changelog assertion passes.

§2 — RELICS PER-HERO: THE SCOPE, AND THE STOP

Relics are party-wide throughout, and the ruling is a save-format change. Reported rather than started, which is what the brief asked for. What it touches:

  • Storage and the save. Run.active_relics is a flat Array of ids. Per-hero makes it a mapping, and run_state.gd reads it back as a hard key (data["active_relics"], no default), so every existing v10 save breaks without a migration. The run save would go v10 → v11.
  • 25 read sites — battle.gd 12, run_state.gd 8, run_sim.gd 4, shop_screen.gd 1 — plus the two aggregators (Relics.hook_add / hook_dict) and the two accessors (Run.relic_add / relic_dict) — every one of which changes signature, because none of them currently knows which hero is asking.
  • Two acquisition sites. The draft screen’s three-slot toggle needs a hero picker per relic; the relic_grant event verb appends mid-run and would have to choose a hero. The draft assigns relics before specs are chosen, which is the point where “which hero gambles” has the least information behind it.
  • 25 relics, and 13 of their descriptions are worded party-wide — “All heroes”, “Every hero”, “The party”, “party recovers”, “Heroes open every battle”. Per-hero ownership makes every one of those strings wrong.

THE AMBIGUOUS ONES, REPORTED RATHER THAN GUESSED (the brief asked). The clearly party-wide hooks keep their effect as ruled — start_items, start_gold, gold_find_mult, shop_discount, loot_extra, victory_gold. The clearly per-hero ones are the eleven battle-spawn hooks, which already run once per hero. Four sit in between and need a ruling:

  • victory_heal_pct (Chalice of Dawn, Cracked Hourglass, Martyr’s Knucklebone) and victory_mana_pct (Cracked Hourglass) — the party heals after a victory. Does the owner heal, or does everyone?
  • rest_heal_add (Cairnmoss Poultice, Martyr’s Knucklebone) — a rest node heals the party, not a hero.
  • resource_floor_pct (Bottled Storm) — reads per-hero naturally (“heroes open every battle with at least 35%”) but was authored as all of them.

§3 — REGALIA POINTS AT ITSELF, AND CAN FINALLY BE CAST

Both halves changed, because either alone leaves it broken.

  • IT IS SELECTABLE NOW, AND THAT WAS THE ACTUAL FIX. _enemy_support_action names its candidates literally and Regalia was not among the six; the attack list filters on damage > 0 and Regalia has none. Re-pointing the target alone would have changed nothing. It enters that list, gated on the caster not already carrying the ward.
  • IT WARDS THE CASTER, AND THE JSON STILL SAYS "target": "ally" — that is correct and must not be “fixed”. Ability.Target is {ENEMY, ALLY} only; “ally” means OWN SIDE, and a caster is on its own side. Regenerate, Cleansing Rite and Dark Vigil are all self-casts tagged "ally" for exactly this reason. An unmapped "self" would fall through to Target.ENEMY and the boss would ward a hero. The re-point belongs in the chooser, not in the data.
  • The description named a mechanic the payload does not implement. “Wards an ally against the next blow” is shield_charges; the payload is enemy_shield. It reads “The Crown wards itself: 25% less damage taken for 3 turns” now, which is what it does.
  • AND THE PAYLOAD LOGGED THE WRONG ABILITY’S NAME. The shared enemy_shield branch printed the literal string “Shielding”, so the moment a second ability used it, a Regalia cast announced itself as the Shieldmaster’s card. It reads ab.display_name now, and a self-ward no longer says the caster’s name twice. Same fault as the description, one layer down.
  • battle.gd’s Dispel comment claimed Regalia as a live shield source and it never was — “two of nineteen kinds” should have read one. Annotated rather than quietly corrected: it is true only as of this batch, and a comment that believes something the code does not do is the trap CU exists to avoid. master.html carried the same claim in the Dispel row and now carries the same correction.

IT COSTS THE TURN, so this is not a free 25% on the end boss: a support cast returns instead of attacking and the ward runs 3 turns, so the Crown trades roughly one turn in four. A taunt still forces it to attack and a Dispel still strips the ward. Verified in a real battle, not by reading: the chooser returns Regalia @ The Hollow Crown, declines to re-pick while warded, the fight resolves, and the log reads “The Hollow Crown: Regalia — it takes 25% less damage (3 turns)”. The Shieldmaster’s ally branch was re-checked on the same payload and is unchanged.

One thing found on the way: _psychotic_support matches on special rather than on the display name, so a maddened Crown could always cast Regalia on the party. The normal fight was the only place it could not happen.

§4 — THE ORC CHIEF’S CRUSHING BLOW IS CHIEFTAIN’S MAUL

Three things shared the stem: the Orc Chief’s ability (damage 34, BD 56), the Warrior’s earnable ability (damage 43), and the Warrior talent Crushing Blows. The enemy one is renamed — least invested, no draft pool, no talent node, no player expectation. What remains is an ability-against-node label collision, which BR §1 says ships and is flagged; the ability-against-ability half is gone.

  • THE SWEEP RAN AGAINST 700 NAMES — every ability (enemy and hero), every talent node, every status and every rune. “Chieftain’s Maul” is clean: no exact match, no stem match, no shared word.
  • It rejected three candidates, and a near-miss was treated as a hit every time. Bonebreaker collides exactly with the talent node Bone Breaker. Chieftain’s Wrath collides with Magi’s Wrath, Bestial Wrath, Divine Wrath, Roots of Wrath, Rune of Old Wrath and the wrath status. Skull Splitter shares “Skull” with the Goblin Slinger’s Skull Crack — and Skullsplitter as one word slips past a word-level sweep while reading identically in a combat log, which is the near-miss the rule is about.
  • The sweep found a fourth sharer the brief did not name: the Ash Brute’s Overhead Crush. Left alone — it shares the stem and nothing else.
  • The brief said the combat log is the only place any of them is named. It is not. master.html’s Orc Chief row lists the ability by name, and it is renamed there too.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED — master.html already confuses the surviving two. The Elemental Weakness row credits “the Warden’s Crushing Blow talent”, and there is no such talent: Crushing Blows is a Berserker node, and Crushing Blow is an ability. That is the collision doing damage in the documentation already, and it is about the two things this batch did not rename, so it wants the designer rather than a guess.

2026-08-20 — Batch CW: THE CLAUDE.md SPLIT, AND REPORTS MOVE INTO THE REPO

DOCUMENTATION ARCHITECTURE ONLY. Nothing the game does changed — no code, no magnitude, no player-facing text, no save version (still v10). CLAUDE.md goes 883.5 KB / 11,066 lines → 144.2 KB / 1,796 lines, an 83.7% cut, and the knowledge sync goes 6.15 MB → 5.46 MB (739 KB off that file; 706 KB / 11.2% net, after this batch’s own new files). It was doing two jobs and doing both badly: standing rules and a narrative block per batch, and the rules were buried among sixty of them. The full report is in docs/reports/CW.md — the first batch report written into the repo instead of a chat window, which is this batch’s own §3.

§0 — THE FILE WAS NOT SHAPED THE WAY THE BRIEF DESCRIBED

Every measurable claim was re-derived before anything was edited. The brief’s premise was right in the way that counts — the rules were buried — but the shape was different, and one error would have caused real damage if followed literally.

  • §5 says the test suites are “the bulk of the scripts folder’s 36%”. They are not in scripts/ at all — all 44 live at the repo root. scripts/ is 34.9% of the sync and holds zero suites: it is battle.gd, unit.gd, classes.gd, talents.gd, run_state.gd and the screens, every one of which §5 itself lists under “stays selected”. Deselecting “the scripts folder” would drop the game code and keep every suite — the exact inverse of the intent. The suites are their own block: 1,700 KB, 27.0%.
  • It was not larger than the changelog, master document and design notes combined — 883.5 KB against their 1,073.1 KB. Larger than any one of them, and than master + design-notes together. The 15% figure measured 14.0%.
  • The suites are not “one per batch since BN” — 44 spanning ah to cp with gaps, starting twenty batches earlier.
  • The flake is in bo, not br, and the four hanging suites were closed two batches running — both corrected in docs/state.md.
  • There were 60 batch blocks, not the ~40 estimated, and they were 8,894 of the 11,066 lines. The bulk was one Current systems snapshot section holding 86% of the file.

§1 — CLAUDE.md IS STANDING RULES ONLY

Rules that govern future behaviour, in the file’s own voice, dateless. Kept: the working agreement, the skill check and its profile rule, the duration and hero/ally conventions, the pouch, item effects, the clamped call sites, hard control, the recast refusal, the text standard, the seventeen standing subsections, the tooling reference and the architecture map. Dropped: every batch narrative, the older snapshot, and two sections still marked open that had been closed for batches (the four hanging suites, and CN’s fold debt closed at CQ).

THE GATHER IS THE POINT OF THE BATCH. A new section, THE TRAPS, collects the rules that were stated inside a narrative and would have been lost with it — the brief named five and the sweep found more: the inquisitor pool key that fails silently, the mystic spec id, the wild_communion_ranks naming trap, the _step float that STAT_INT_KEYS would round to 1, the gate rules (a gate reports its count not a verdict; a gate running zero checks must fail; a count nobody diffs is a word), grepping stderr for a parse rather than trusting a tally, the battery destroying the player’s in-progress run, zsh not word-splitting unquoted expansions, and \n in a GDScript string being two characters so \bword\b silently fails on every hand-wrapped tooltip.

THE STAMP-GATE RULE WAS WRITTEN WRONG FIRST AND CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING, which is worth recording because it is the same fault the section exists to prevent. A grep for batch codes matched comments and reported seven suites. The real gate is in fourteen — and none is a literal any more: each reads the two-letter code out of (Batch XX) and asserts it is no older than its own batch, so no bump is owed on a re-stamp. What carries forward is the prohibition and one live caveat: the comparison leans on two-letter codes sorting lexically, and a three-letter batch code needs one more line in each of the fourteen.

ONE DOCUMENTATION FAULT CORRECTED TOWARD THE CODE: the architecture section said the run save was v7. It is v10.

§2 — docs/state.md

New, and overwritten every batch rather than appended to, so it cannot grow. Where the project is, the open queue, live counts and constants, and known-broken. The battery counts, the drift bands, the flake and the one red moved here out of CLAUDE.md, where they had been sitting among the rules. Anything that reads as “what happened” was left out.

§3 — REPORTS GO INTO THE REPO

From CW each batch writes docs/reports/<CODE>.md and commits it. The copying is what this replaces, and it had already lost things: CL’s overflow measurement was written into text-standard.html §4.8 and then reported as missing. A report that says something is absent when it is present is harder to catch than an absence — nobody goes looking for a thing they have been told is not there. Retrofit nothing.

§4 — THE CHANGELOG ARCHIVE IS A RULE, NOT AN EVENT

Threshold 400 KB, cut at a batch boundary, leaving the live file around 150 KB — the size BZ’s own cut produced. Archive means move out of the repo, never delete; the live file never moves, which is why build_docs.py keeps working. The verification is the part worth having as a rule: assert the <h2> counts sum with zero overlap and order preserved, and that the two bodies rejoined are byte-identical to the original. Never assert file sizes — sizes agreeing is consistent with a duplicated entry and a dropped one. CD’s pattern is binding on anything that reads the changelog: anchor on the <h2> and follow the path out of the live file’s own header.

THIS FILE IS 486 KB — ALREADY OVER THE NEW THRESHOLD, AND THE CUT IS NOT TAKEN HERE. The brief scoped §4 to writing the rule, and a cut is a content operation that wants its own verification pass. It is owed at CX and is the first thing the next batch should take.

§5 — WHAT COMES OUT OF THE SYNC

Not a repo change — a list for the designer to apply in the connector’s file picker, and deselecting is not deleting. Take out 1,702 KB (30.4%): the 44 suites at the repo root (Claude Code reads them off disk; they cannot be archived, since they must be in the repo to run) and docs/build_docs.py; plus the two audit documents (75 KB) once their findings are confirmed applied. The archived changelog is already outside the repo and was never synced. Applying it takes the sync to 3.80 MB from 6.15 MB before this batch — a cumulative 38.2%, none of it by deleting anything.

VERIFIED

The floor is that it parses and it runs, which is the point of doing this now. check_parse.gd headless with stderr grepped for Parse Error|SCRIPT ERROR — 0 matches, which is the authority rather than the tally (the tally agreed at 0). The game launches and runs to --quit-after 150, exit 0, nothing on the stream. No file under scripts/, scenes/ or data/ was touched.

2026-08-20 — Batch CV: THE TALENT AUDIT CORRECTIONS

IMPLEMENT ONLY. CU audited all 324 nodes and changed nothing; this batch applies the rulings. 52 node texts moved and NO read site did — every disagreement was settled in the code's favour, which is what "the code is authoritative and the document is corrected toward it" means when the document is a tooltip. Two conventions settle most of it (a duration is stated as APPLIED; HERO and ALLY are different words), six nodes were individually wrong, and two mechanical sweeps plus the Mystic's 27 by hand close the coverage gap CU declared. docs/talent-audit.html now carries a per-finding disposition table.

§0 — WHERE THE BRIEF WAS RIGHT, AND THE THREE COUNTS THAT MOVED

Every mechanical claim in the brief was re-derived against the repo before anything was edited, and the six wrong nodes, the four dead Perfects, the three surfaces and both known sweep cases all check out exactly as described. Three counts came back larger:

  • §1's duration sweep found FIVE nodes, not four. wd_hold_line states its undying window as 1 and 2 turns where battle.gd applies 2 and 3 — and the comment above it was the one place in the codebase where the acting-turn reading was written down as a rule ("so 'one turn' is 2 and 'two turns' is 3"). That comment is where the convention now lives, stating the ruling instead.
  • §4's vocabulary sweep found 28 nodes shorting companions, not 16, plus 4 more worded the other way round. CU's scope sweep asked 20 nodes; this one asked all 41 that use ally/party language. Of the 28: 23 are shorted by an explicit is_companion filter, 2 (hl_guardian, hl_resurrection) by unit.gd:1320's is_hero and not is_companion gate on below_half_cb — a Mercy generator rather than a filter, which no battle.gd grep would surface — and 3 (dv_apostle, dv_fervor, dv_oath) because _gain_faith refuses companions outright, so no beast can ever hold the stack those nodes are written around.
  • §3's orphan sweep ran over all 220 ability definitions rather than the 37 CU named, because a NAMED list cannot audit itself — the list is the thing under suspicion. It found one beyond Intercession: Backdraft, carrying "3 turns each instead" on a card runs_skill_check() reports as barless.

§1 — A DURATION IS STATED AS APPLIED

"N turns" is the number the code passes to _apply_status — the calendar count, not the acting count. tick_statuses() decrements at the start of a unit's turn, so a status applied with 4 covers four calendar turns and three of the bearer's own actions; both readings were in use across the trees and cr_rime used both in one sentence.

THE CHIP DECIDES IT. The chip counts down the raw value, so a node saying 3 while the chip shows 4 contradicts something the player is looking at. The acting-turn reading also makes every text a TRANSLATION of its own code, and translations rot — which is exactly how the corpus came to hold both at once.

§3 — DEAD PERFECT CLAUSES, AND THE ABILITY CORPUS SWEPT FOR MORE

Measured, not inferred: check_cv.gd loads the live Ability objects and asks runs_skill_check().

  • CUT: dv_resolve "Perfect: 4 turns", oc_hysteria "Perfect: 3cd" (CQ already recorded Mass Hysteria's Perfect as never implemented at all), wd_shieldwall "or 5 on a perfect cast".
  • NOT CUT — dv_bulwark. CQ's fold made the 5% party heal UNCONDITIONAL and CR §7 accepted it, so the text must say the heal happens. Losing the clause would have deleted a shipped effect from the description of the ability that has it.

Intercession's handler still adds + (1 if is_perfect else 0), which is dead code in the same way. It is left standing: deleting a mechanic is a design change; deleting a claim the game cannot honour is a correction.

§4 — HERO AND ALLY ARE NOT SYNONYMS

HERO — the four party members. ALLY — heroes and companions together.

A Beastmaster's beast stands in heroes, is visibly on the player's side, and receives none of what 28 nodes promised it. The exclusion itself is intended — under The Pack a party-wide buff would otherwise reach six units — so no read site changed. Only the words did.

Precision runs both directions. wd_rally, wd_hold_line, dv_devoutness and dv_waters said "party" while their read sites genuinely include companions, and now say ally. Two words that only ever narrow are one word with extra steps. wd_tank_spank was already right and is the proof the vocabulary is worth having: it says "ally", and heroes.filter(func(h): return not h.dead) is the whole of its filter.

Targeting was checked rather than assumed, and it splits the same way: _hero_side() includes companions, so Divine Shield can legally be cast on the bear and dv_layered's "an ally who already holds one" is correct as written — while dv_aegis's echo filters companions out and is not.

Both terms are added to the glossary (hero_vs_ally, the 97th entry), the text standard (§4.9) and CLAUDE.md.

§5 — TWO SWEEPS, AND THE MYSTIC'S 27 BY HAND

CU machine-checked magnitudes on all 324 but gave the line-by-line semantic read to only 68. Its own recommendation was the model — ask one mechanical question of all 324 at once rather than reading nine more specs by hand — and this batch asked two.

SWEEP 1, UNDECLARED CAPS. Four nodes are bounded at their read site and never said so: sm_dominant (unbounded multiplicative armor growth against effective_armor()'s minf(a, 0.85) ceiling — with Endurance one line below documenting its own +75% cap), cr_winters_depth and ss_sunder_shot (both thin the same divisor, capped at 75% with a floor of 10 Constitution), and wd_iron_will (maxf(1.0 - 0.01 * iw_pct, 0.1) — a 90% ceiling reachable at eight debuffs). Nodes that already state their caps correctly — py_forge_body, oc_soul_leech, ss_unwavering, wd_endurance, Heavy Plating's own passive line — are what made the question answerable mechanically.

SWEEP 2, UNDECLARED EXCLUSIONS. Three nodes count through _status_count, which walks DEBUFF_IDS and skips broken — the one affliction the Breaker lane exists to produce: sm_momentum_sm (Overwhelm, the known case), sv_cocktail and sv_vulture. All three now say so. _unique_enemy_debuffs does NOT skip it, so oc_pleasure's "every UNIQUE debuff" is correct and was left.

THEN THE MYSTIC'S 27 WERE HAND-READ — the spec that produced zero automated hits, so not one node had ever been opened, which is real evidence about magnitudes and none at all about scope. It produced two findings neither sweep could reach:

  • sv_creeping — FIXED. "Applying any status to a Poisoned enemy refreshes its Poison" — _creeping_refresh returns early when the status applied IS the poison, so the one application a player would most expect to work does not.
  • sv_hitrun — REPORTED, NOT REWORDED. "Whenever you apply a status to an enemy, you gain Elusive" — _hit_and_run is called from four sites (any poison application, Hamstring, a Snare Trap set, a trap spring) and does not re-arm while Elusive already stands. Narrowing the text and widening the code are both design answers, so it goes to the designer under the brief's own rule.

§6 — SURFACES THAT CONTRADICTED A CORRECT NODE

  • party_screen.gd hardcoded the Blood Frenzy floor at half. Scar Tissue makes it 85% and 100% with Unstoppable, and the in-battle chip has read the same [50, 85, 100] table off the same counter since AL — so two surfaces disagreed in front of the player, on the number the party sheet exists to compare builds by. The sheet reads the table now.
  • dv_apostle promised double and paid triple. With dv_fervor the stacks count TRIPLE (_faith_stack_mult is written as a sum on purpose) and only Fervor's text said so — a player taking the capstone first was told double. Stated on both.
  • ar_wrath and ar_conduit add to a 3.5% step (RESONANCE_DMG_STEP 1.5 + Conduit 0.5 + Wrath's second 1.5) and neither mentioned the other. Both do now.
  • Guard Change's fixed perfect_text cannot know about sm_swordsmanship: reported, left. That is a surface problem, not a text one.

§7 — THE STALE NOTE, STRUCK

"92 nodes state a number their own payload cannot produce" was a FALSE ALARM and stops being quoted as an open defect. What CU actually measured: the census is 107, not 92 (the difference is incidental numbers set by a handler rather than by the payload), and the finding is that the flag payload is an IDIOM, not a fault — a talent payload is mostly a flag whose magnitude lives in battle.gd or unit.gd, so a node quoting a number its payload does not contain is the normal shape of a node. The real work was always the read-site check, which CU did on all 324 by machine and CV finished by hand. CLAUDE.md now records that instead.

§8 — WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED

  • Battle Shout's code and its own documentation disagree about intent. The loop is for h in heroes with no companion filter, so a companion DOES hear it — while the read-site comment says "Companions don't hear it" and the chip legend says "to every hero and no companion". A node whose behaviour looks wrong rather than undocumented goes to the designer, and reporting it is the whole answer here: fixing the comment would endorse a behaviour, and fixing the code would delete one.
  • Intercession's dead is_perfect branch — see §3.
  • The Trapper passive's own line ("+8% damage per DIFFERENT status effect") carries §5's Broken omission on a SPEC PASSIVE rather than a node. The sweep's mandate was the 324; the passive is reported here.
  • Every read site. 52 node texts moved and zero code paths did, other than the party sheet's hardcoded floor — which is a surface reading a table, not a rule changing.

2026-08-20 — Batch CU: THE TALENT AUDIT

REPORT ONLY — nothing was fixed. All 324 talent nodes compared three ways (node text, payload, read site), delivered as docs/talent-audit.html on text-audit.html's pattern. This closes the LAST of the four populations Batch CJ named as unreached, deferred by CJ and again by CK §4. Bucket 1 is an open queue awaiting the designer's rulings; Batch CV applies them.

§0 — WHAT THE BRIEF GOT RIGHT, AND THE ONE NUMBER THAT MOVED

The brief's factual claims check out against the repo: CLAUDE.md records exactly 324 nodes, 92 stating a number their payload cannot produce, deferred by CJ and CK §4, with the other three populations closed by CK. One divergence: re-running that census under this batch's own method (every number in the rendered text vs every number the payload can produce) returns 107, not 92 — the difference is incidental numbers such as durations that come from a handler rather than the payload. The population is slightly larger than recorded and the conclusion is unchanged: almost all of them are correct.

§1 — THE HEADLINE: THE TREES ARE SOUNDER THAN THE DEFERRAL IMPLIED, AND THE ERRORS CLUSTER

Six nodes state a number or condition the read site does not produce, and four of the six were broken by one event — Batch CN's removal of skill-check bars, which turned a perfect's number into the base and left the talent quoting the old base behind. That is the useful result: not 92 scattered errors but one systematic aftershock, plus two isolated magnitudes.
