It is CJ's mana_shield/hysteria shape — an advertised bonus no handler implements — and it is the reason the brief's separate NO READ SITE category earned its place.

§2 — ONE RULING SETTLES A DOZEN NODES: WHAT DOES "N TURNS" MEAN?

tick_statuses() runs at the START of a unit's turn, before it acts (unit.gd:2171, battle.gd:2844), so a status applied with value N is on the calendar for N turns and gives N-1 ACTING turns. Both readings are defensible and the corpus uses both — Tempo (2 applied, "1 turn"), Immolate (4, "3 turns") and Sacred Resolve (4, "3 turns") assume one; Battle Shout (3, "3 turns"), Swordsmanship (2, "2 turns") and Bulwark of Fortitude (3, "3 turns") assume the other. cr_rime uses both conventions in one sentence, for two statuses set by one handler — which is what proves this is a genuine inconsistency rather than a reading. Filed apart from bucket 1 deliberately: it is one design question, not a dozen typos, and roughly a third of the trees' duration statements move by one whichever way it goes.

§3 — BUCKET 2's LARGEST POPULATION: SIXTEEN NODES PROMISE THE PARTY AND MEAN THE PARTY MINUS COMPANIONS

Of 20 nodes whose text says "every ally", "the whole party" or "every hero", 16 have read sites that explicitly skip is_companion units and not one says so. Every exclusion was opened and confirmed individually. A Beastmaster's beast stands in heroes, is visibly on the player's side, and receives none of it. One ruling on whether "ally" includes companions closes all sixteen — the consistency across every site reads as intent that was never written down.

Also reported: caps and exclusions the text omits (Overwhelm's "every debuff" silently excludes Broken, the one affliction its own lane exists to produce; Dominant Presence's unbounded armor growth meets a hard 85% ceiling that Endurance, one line below it, DOES document), an interaction stated on a row-6 node but not on the capstone that shares it, and a party-screen line that contradicts a correct node — party_screen.gd:119 hardcodes "Half the highest bonus" for the Blood Frenzy floor while Scar Tissue makes it 85% or 100%, and the in-battle chip gets it right, so the two surfaces disagree.

§4 — THE COVERAGE GAP, STATED IN THE DOCUMENT RATHER THAN GLOSSED

All 324 got extraction from the live trees, a read site opened and confirmed non-comment (319/319 stat fields), a machine magnitude comparison, and three targeted sweeps (52/52 base-quoting nodes hand-verified against the constant they quote; 8/8 Perfect claims measured; 20/20 scope claims checked). Only 68 of 324 got the line-by-line semantic read that catches caps, exclusions and interactions — berserker, swordmaster and half the warden. The Mystic is the thinnest spot: zero of its 27 nodes were hand-opened, because it produced no hits in any automated pass, and zero flags is evidence about magnitudes and nothing about scope. CJ reported 120/120 clean and was later found to have had no check for stated bonuses with no code path at all; an audit that overstates its reach is worse than a narrow one that admits its edges, so §0 of the document names the gap and §7 puts it in the queue.

§5 — WHAT WAS NOT DONE

No node text was rewritten, no magnitude moved, no payload changed. CQ's fold audit is the precedent: it examined 105 changes and altered exactly one, because ability and talent values reach the designer as options. A batch that quietly corrected six magnitudes on its own judgement would repeat the fault it was sent to find and would destroy the evidence — after the fix nobody can tell which way the disagreement pointed. The one thing that was run rather than read is check_cu.gd, under the brief's own carve-out.

2026-08-20 — Batch CT: THE POUCH GETS SLOTS, AND THREE ITEMS TO COMPETE FOR THEM

The pouch becomes a slotted inventory that grows with the run (4 → 5 → 6 by zone), three items join the list, and the three flat potions become percentages. Save version moved to v11 — tolerant, a v10 save loads. Five claims in the brief were wrong and are corrected here rather than implemented as written; each is listed in §0 below with what the repo actually contains.

§0 — WHAT THE BRIEF GOT WRONG

Recorded first because four of the five changed what was built.

The brief saidThe repo saysWhat shipped
§1: follow the rune equip-slot precedent, which "grows 2 → 3 → 4 by zone and announces each new slot on the zone-victory screen" That ladder was deleted by Batch AN §9. rune_slots() has returned a flat 3 ever since, and the reason is written above it: a growth ladder means a run that dies in zone 2 never owns the last slot. There is no announcement anywhere to copy. The 4/5/6 ladder ships as briefed — it is right here for the opposite reason it was wrong for runes — and the announcement was written from scratch in _resolve_boss, beside the talent-point line.
§1: "Six buttons fit the existing row… the slot cap removes the layout problem rather than requiring a fix for it" They do not fit. At VIEW_X + 4 + i * 190 with width 182, button six spans x=1270–1452 on a 1280-wide viewport — 172px and its whole label off-screen. Five fit at that pitch, not six. Pitch and width re-derived from the space that exists (158/150; rightmost edge x=1260). check_ct_map.tscn measures it, and fails at the old pitch.
§5: add a new status crippled, "Crippled", −15% damage dealt cripple already exists — "Cripple", −25% damage dealt, already in DEBUFF_IDS, applied by three abilities and two enemies. The glossary entry for it reads "A crippled unit deals 25% less damage", and battle.gd's Corrupted Channeling comment says "a Crippled enemy". Shipped as hexed / "Hexed", chip "Hx". Every number and rule of §5 is unchanged; only the name moved. Two chips a player cannot tell apart, and twelve has_status("cripple") call sites one typo from a silent bug, was not worth the homonym.
§3: "reuse the elite cache and rune offer pattern… declining is always a button" There is no "elite cache" — the spoils call it a rune cache. And the offer screen states in its own header: "There is NO decline." It cannot be the model for an interaction that requires one. Built on the owed-pick overlay — the pattern the rune cache and the draft picks actually use, which map_screen.gd's header calls "an owed pick opens its own overlay". It declines.
§4: battle-only items sit in the pouch and say why "exactly as the Bomb and Defense Potion already do" Those are two different mechanisms. The Bomb is refused by _usable_on_map so its button never lights. The Defense Potion's button is enabled and refuses with a toast after the press. The three new items follow the Bomb. A button you cannot press, that says why on hover, beats one that looks live and then declines. The Defense Potion is left exactly as it was.

§1 — SLOTS

A slot holds one item TYPE and its whole stack. Six Health Potions occupy one slot. 4 → 5 → 6 by zone, announced on the zone-victory screen.

THE OPENING RESOLUTION, WRITTEN DOWN AS §1 REQUIRED: five starting types against four slots does not fit, and the opening drops to four types — the Defense Potion is the one dropped. A choose-four screen before the run has begun asks the player to price five items they have never used; the shop asks the same question later with a run's worth of context behind it. Of the five, Defense is the only pure hedge — Health, Mana and Revive answer states a party cannot otherwise leave, and the Bomb is the pouch's only offense. It is sold at every merchant. Nothing starts over capacity, and check_ct.gd asserts it.

A stack falling to zero does NOT free its slot — otherwise the cap stops binding the moment a stack empties, exactly when it should be biting. Only a discard or a sale releases one.

An ordering bug was found and fixed on the way: new_run assigned zone_idx = 0 after filling the pouch. Nothing read the slot count before this batch, so the stale read was harmless; a second run in one session would now have sized its opening pouch off the previous run's zone.

§2 — FREEING A SLOT: DISCARD AND SELL

Discard from the pouch at any time, from its own small button under each slot — because the button above it is disabled for every battle-only item and every empty stack, which is exactly when a player most wants the slot back. Confirmed, not instant.

Sell back at the merchant for 40% of the listed price (SELL_FRACTION), read off the same _price the buy button shows, so a Peddler's Lodestone discount cuts both and the two cannot be arbitraged. An even trade would make the shop a free locker. A sale pays on an empty slot too, and pays the same: the slot is the thing being sold.

§3 — A DROP WITH NO ROOM IS A SWAP OFFER

A grant with no slot queues on the run and the map puts it to the player: give up a named stack, or leave it behind. Offers resolve one at a time. Saved with the run — an offer is a reward already earned.

The two walls are kept apart, which §3 was emphatic about: NO ROOM IS A CHOICE, A FULL STACK IS A WALL. A drop over a per-type stack cap is still refused with a message.

§4 — THE THREE NEW ITEMS

ItemPriceStackEffect
Cleansing Draught (cleanse)35g4 Removes every debuff from one chosen hero. Reads DEBUFF_IDS through _cleansable_debuffs — the Rite's own derivation, so it can never strip a buff and never outdoes the Cleric ability it stands in for. Closes a real hole: a party without a Cleric had no answer to a debuff at all. Drops as loot, at a light weight.
Cursed Visage (visage)100g2 Hexes every living enemy for the rest of the battle. FLAGGED, NOT TUNED — nothing else applies a permanent party-wide debuff from one button that costs no turn. Shop-only.
Resonating Hourglass (hourglass)90g2 Any living hero — not only the one acting — acts next, initiative delay waived. Written through next_time on Watchtower's idiom; no second scheduling path. Followed by _rebuild_turn_bar(). Shop-only.

All three are battle only and sit in the map pouch with a disabled button saying why.

§5 — THE hexed STATUS

−15% damage dealt, battle-long via the negative-duration convention. In DEBUFF_IDS (a Survivalist's Trapper counts it), and therefore out of the derived _dispellable_buffs set, so a Mage's Dispel can never strip the party's own hundred gold of work back off — the rule CE set for anathema and penance. Multiplicative with Cripple rather than replacing it: separate statuses from separate sources, and stacking is the only reading that leaves neither silently free. Chip, log line and glossary entry on the usual pattern. See §0 for why it is not called crippled.

§6 — FLAT POTIONS BECOME PERCENTAGES

  • Health Potion — 20% of maximum health. FLAGGED: this is a nerf at run start, not a wash. Base class HP is 154/99/121/110, so 20% is 31/20/24/22 against the old flat 40 — it only overtakes 40 once maximum HP passes 200. Shipped as §6 specified; the figure is flagged because §6 was careful to keep the Bomb and Mana openings unchanged and did not say the same for this one.
  • Mana Potion — 40% of maximum resource. FLAGGED, as §6 asked. Base max_resource is 100, so 40% is the old flat 40 exactly. A run opens unchanged.
  • Bomb — 50 base, +2% per combat win, the heroes' own rate. A run opens unchanged.
  • Revive and Defense are untouched, as instructed.

Battle and map both call the same Run helpers now rather than each spelling out a literal — which is what "Run.ITEM_INFO stays the single place these numbers are written" has to mean in practice.

§7 — EVERYTHING ELSE THAT TOUCHES ITEMS

  • The item and random_item event verbs bypassed add_item entirely and wrote items[id] directly — so Batch AN's per-type cap was already leaking through every event grant, before this batch. Both now route through Run. A negative count is a take and still writes directly, because a removal has no cap and must not free the slot.
  • Spoiled Stores (removes two potions) works unchanged and no longer risks freeing a slot.
  • Waystone Shard and Packmother's Satchel cannot overflow the opening — every type they grant is already in the opening four. new_run routes them through add_item anyway, so a future relic is refused visibly rather than silently widening the pouch. Asserted per relic in check_ct.gd.
  • Gravelight Lantern's extra consumable goes down the same three-way split as any drop.
  • run_sim.gd carried a hand-copied mirror of ITEM_PRICES, which would have been a missing-key crash in every sim run the moment three ids were added — a crash no parse gate can see. ITEM_PRICES and SELL_FRACTION now live in run_state.gd beside ITEM_INFO and the stack caps, read at runtime by both the shop and the sim off the run node each already holds.
    THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS WAS WORSE THAN THE DUPLICATION AND IS WORTH RECORDING. The mirror was replaced with preload("res://scripts/shop_screen.gd").ITEM_PRICES — but that file names the Run autoload at compile time, and autoloads are not registered when a --script SceneTree compiles its dependency chain. The preload failed with Identifier not found: Run and took test_run_harness.gd down with it. The battery still printed GATE 1/2/3 PASS. The only tells were throws=3 beside them and GATE 2 reporting 57 checks against its documented 165 — it ran a third of itself and said PASS. Caught by reading the throw count and the live counts together, which is precisely what both were put there for. The sim also respects the slot cap, or its restock loop would pay for types it could never receive. Its drop policy is stated rather than implied: it DECLINES a drop that would need a slot it has not got — the conservative legal answer, so the sim's item economy is a floor on the real thing — and the declines are counted and printed (drops declined for want of a slot, measuring 1.3/run at balanced routing), because an unreported cap reads as "everything landed".
  • The shop's supplies column would have collided with the draft section at eight types (row 8 ending at y=600 through a header at y=452). Re-pitched to 36/32; nothing else on the screen moved. Not flagged by the brief.
  • LOOT_POOL gains cleanse at a light weight. Starting gold, the five old prices and per-fight gold are unchanged.

§8 — THE GATES

check_ct.gd — 113 checks, 0 failures. Drives each new item through the real _use_item on live units in a spawned battle (emitting _target_picked from the test side to walk a path that normally needs a mouse), rather than re-implementing the effects beside them. It also round-trips a real v10 save to prove the tolerance this entry claims — writing one, loading it, and asserting the pouch survives and the offer queue comes back empty. That test touches the player's actual user://run_save.bin, so it backs up any real save and restores it: a gate that eats an in-progress run to prove a point about migrations is a worse bug than the one it is testing. Proven to bite: breaking the Visage's duration produced 3 failures, breaking discard_item produced 4, raising the save-refusal floor to 11 produced 3.

check_ct_map.tscn — 83 checks, 0 failures. Renders the pouch full and empty at 4, 5 and 6 slots and asserts every drawn rect lies inside the 1280-wide viewport; then renders the shop and asserts its eight supply rows end above the draft header, and that a Sell takes two presses. Proven to bite: 3 failures at the brief's claimed pouch pitch (rightmost edge x=1452), 2 more at the old shop pitch (supplies ending at y=488 through a header at y=452).

THE GLOSSARY GREW BY TWO, AND THE THREE ENTRIES THAT DID NOT EARN THEIR PLACE WERE DELETED. test_batch_ce pins the glossary's entry count deliberately — its comment says growth "should have to be stated rather than absorbed" — so the pin was bumped with a reason, not loosened. CT adds status_hexed (a chip on the board a player has nowhere else to learn, and one they must not confuse with Cripple's) and pouch_slots (a system, which is what that category holds, whose two load-bearing rules are invisible in play: an emptied stack keeps its slot, and a drop with no room is an offer rather than a refusal). Per-item entries for the Cleansing Draught, Cursed Visage and Resonating Hourglass were written and then deleted — each is fully described by its own tooltip, the category has never held a per-item entry (there is no item_health), and three of eight items is a worse state than none. What they taught that a tooltip cannot — shop-only, and the stack caps — is folded into pouch_slots.

THE v11 BUMP BROKE TWO SUITES THAT PINNED THE LITERAL, AND THIS IS THE THIRD TIME. test_batch_bl asserted "version": 10 and test_batch_bm asserted v10 exactly. test_batch_bk already learned this — BL broke BK's pinned 8, and BK's §6 was re-pointed to "8 or later" with a comment saying "so the next bump does not fail a map test either". BK passed this batch; the other two did not. Both re-pointed IN PLACE on that precedent, to the invariant each actually owns: BL's is that the recap ledgers are in the save (now "9 or later"), BM's is that the party and its equipped talents are in the save and a pre-v10 save is refused (now "10 or later"). Neither suite owns the newest version number, and neither should assert it.

A THIRD suite, test_batch_bx, pinned the SOURCE TEXT of a guard this batch split in two. §3's chaining needed _maybe_open_party_draft's single if Run.sim_run or _draft_columns().is_empty(): to become two guards, so the pouch's own owed pick could take the screen when the draft had nothing to offer. The behaviour is identical — a sim still returns before anything opens. Re-pointed to the invariant BX owns, and SCOPED to the function body, which makes it strictly stronger than the global contains it replaces: map_screen.gd holds two if Run.sim_run: lines, and the old form would have passed on either.

Parse verified by grepping the engine's stderr for Parse Error, never a tally — Batch CN's scar. Headless runs complete at 100% with 0 script errors, and both new gates are registered in run_battery.sh.

2026-08-19 — Batch CS: THE SHARPSHOOTER'S BASIC BECOMES A SEQUENCE

His basic attack runs a multi-press skill check that grows with Focus, resolves with partial credit, and pays in Focus rather than damage. It is the first thing to use CN's presses parameter and it replaces CN's placeholder combine rather than joining it. His basic attack only — no other ability of his changes, and no other hero's bar moves at all. Save version did not move (still v10).

§1 — HOW MANY PRESSES, AND WHY FOUR IS THE CEILING

One press, plus one for every 50 Focus held, capped at four.

Focus held when the bar opensPresses
0–491
50–992
100–1493
150+4 — the cap

THE CAP IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT A ROUNDING CHOICE. Focus has no ceiling, so an uncapped rule makes 400 Focus a nine-press sequence with a tightening window on his most-used action — an ability a player without the reflexes simply cannot use. That is the failure that sank timed hits in Legend of Dragoon and Mother 3, and it would land on the attack he presses most. Four is the ceiling; Focus keeps climbing and the sequence does not. The reason is recorded beside the number in battle.gd, in CLAUDE.md and in master.html §4.2, so a later batch cannot read four as arbitrary and raise it.

The count is read at the moment the bar opens, from Focus held at that instant — after targeting, not before it.

§2 — PARTIAL CREDIT, AND IT REPLACES CN's COMBINE

Each landed press counts. A miss ends the sequence and keeps everything earned before it. A four-press attempt that misses on the second is worth one press, not zero. “Landed” means Good or better — a Sloppy is the miss that ends it.

CN's presses default returned the WORST GRADE OF THE SET, and CN's own comment called that a placeholder. It is deleted, not left reachable — _worse_grade and its _GRADE_ORDER table are gone. Two answers to “what is a sequence worth” is how they disagree silently, which is the scar no_skill_check left at CQ §5: the flag and the criterion disagreed and a test passed by reading the wrong oracle.

CN's comment also said “CO's Sharpshooter basic is the first” caller to ask for more than one press. CO did not do it — CO was the recast refusal — and the comment is corrected in place. CN's decision to leave the bar ON his basic was right: this batch replaced it where it stood rather than removing and restoring it.

§3 — WHAT IT PAYS: FOCUS, NOT DAMAGE

Each landed press grants 8 Focus. A full sequence — every press landed — grants a further 20 Focus; a partial grants its per-press Focus and no bonus. Damage resolves off the FIRST press's grade, exactly as a single-press basic does today, and presses two through four add none.

PressesFullBroken after 1Broken after 2Broken after 3
128———
2368——
344816—
45281624

That last rule keeps the change confined to the meter. A deep-Focus Sharpshooter ramps faster; he does not hit harder per swing — Focus already converts to crit chance and then to crit multiplier, so the damage increase arrives through the meter rather than beside it. The Focus is paid after _resolve, deliberately: the Focus engine dumps the meter to zero on a target switch, so paying before it would delete the points the same shot just earned. The same ordering means a KILLING sequence pays on top of the 50 a kill retains rather than being swallowed by it — a full four-press kill from 150 Focus leaves him on 102 against the next mark (the meter caps to 50 on the kill, then the sequence pays its 52), and 202 if he holds Overkill, which keeps the meter whole. That follows from “each landed press grants Focus” read unconditionally, and it is noted here rather than left to be discovered.

FLAGGED, NOT TUNED — the per-press figure of 8 is the designer's number. At 8, a full four-press sequence pays 52 Focus against a single press's 28 — 1.9× — and with the passive's own +20 for a same-target shot on top of both, the whole turn is 72 Focus at 150 against 48 at 0, which is 1.5×. It is the figure to move if that reads hot in play, and moving it means moving this entry, master.html and the glossary with it — check_cs.gd pins it for exactly that reason.

§4 — THE WINDOW TIGHTENS, BUT THE SEQUENCE DOES NOT GET HARDER

Each press is 85% of the width of the one before it, so the sequence has a shape rather than being one press repeated. At four presses the Good half-width runs 0.350 → 0.298 → 0.253 → 0.215.

AND THE OPENING WINDOW WIDENS AS THE PRESS COUNT RISES, by 1.00 / 1.31 / 1.57 / 1.86, so landing a full sequence stays about as achievable at 150 Focus as at 0. Without it, playing a Sharpshooter well would make his basic progressively harder to use.

THE MODEL IS WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE NOTHING IN THE PROJECT CAN MEASURE IT. CLAUDE.md already records why: the bot never runs the bar — it rolls a grade off fixed probabilities — so a widened window is invisible to every instrument the repo owns. The numbers therefore come from a stated model rather than from play data: difficulty is time inside the window (CN's standing rule read as an equation), the player's timing error is Gaussian with an SD of about 60 ms, a press's miss-risk is that Gaussian's tail outside the Good window, and the sequence's risk is the sum of its presses'. Under it the whole sequence lands 89.7% / 90.0% / 90.0% / 90.0% at one, two, three and four presses. The 60 ms is a guess about human reflexes and is flagged as one; check_cs.gd re-derives the table from the constants so a hand-edited row cannot pass silently, but it cannot check the assumption.

THE PERFECT WINDOW DELIBERATELY DOES NOT WIDEN WITH THE COUNT, and that is where §3 and §4 would have contradicted each other. The first press's Perfect is what sets the damage; widen it with the press count and depth would buy damage directly, which is exactly what §3 exists to prevent. Only the Good window widens, because “landed” is defined as Good or better and that is what the constant-difficulty rule is about.

His exception is a FIXED OFFSET, NOT A SLOPE: 15% less timing tolerance than everybody else's, the same 15% at one press and at four. It is taken against SC_PROFILE_DEFAULT rather than written as a literal, so it stays an offset FROM the default if a later batch moves the default. His bar also sweeps in 0.52s against everyone else's 0.72s, which is the “vary the character” half; because difficulty is time-in-window, the quicker sweep is paid for with proportionally wider zones and does not move the difficulty.

§5 — THE BOT

The bot never runs the bar and is blind to every window this batch widens. It now rolls its grade per press, stops at the first failure, and earns the same partial credit — it lands 2.69 of four on average. Without it a simulated Sharpshooter never earns the sequence Focus and his ramp reads far weaker than it is, and the sim is the only thing that plays him at volume. At one press the roll is byte-for-byte the line it has always been, one randf() against the same two thresholds, so no other hero's grade and no other part of the RNG stream moves.

§6 — THE TELL

The bar names how many presses are coming before the first one and which press is live throughout — “SHOT 1 OF 4 — THIS ONE SETS THE DAMAGE”, then “SHOT 2 OF 4 — KEEP THE CHAIN”. A sequence that ends early reads as ended: “CHAIN BROKEN 2 / 4 — Good”, with its own sound, rather than the bar simply vanishing and reading as dropped input. A full one says “FULL SEQUENCE 4 / 4 — PERFECT”. Both lines carry the first press's grade as well as the tally, because a player who sees only “2 / 4” cannot tell whether the shot that landed hit hard. This is CM's gated tell applied to a different stake — the stakes on the one surface the player is actually looking at.

The reading is keyed on the press count rather than on a new mode string: at 0–49 Focus his basic IS a one-press check and should read as the ordinary bar it is.

§7 — TWO THINGS THE BRIEF STATED THAT THE REPO DOES NOT (REPORTED, NOT SILENTLY OBEYED)

1. “The Perfect bonus, +20 Focus” is not Quick Shot's Perfect bonus. §3 describes the full-sequence reward as “the Perfect bonus, +20 Focus”. Quick Shot's actual Perfect bonus is perfect_id: "mana" — +10 Mana. The +20 Focus bonus (focus20) belongs to Aimed Shot, his spec ability. Quick Shot is a protected core the Beastmaster and the Survivalist also carry, so changing its Perfect bonus would have changed two other specs' basic attacks. The +20 Focus is therefore implemented as a NAMED FULL-SEQUENCE BONUS and Quick Shot's own Perfect (+10 Mana on a Perfect first press) is untouched. If the designer meant the other reading — that a full sequence should fire the ability's own Perfect bonus — that is a one-line change and a different feature.

2. “Worth meaningfully more than four single presses” only holds under one reading. §3's flag asks that a full four-press sequence be worth meaningfully more than four single presses. As shipped, the full-sequence bonus fires at EVERY press count including one — §3's own wording is “every press landed”, unconditional — so four separate one-press casts pay 4×28 = 112 and one full four-press sequence pays 52. The sentence holds if “four single presses” means four times the per-press Focus (32 against 52); it does not hold if it means four separate casts. The alternative is to require two or more presses for the bonus, which makes the sentence exact (4×8 = 32 against 52) at the cost of an unstated exception in an otherwise unconditional rule. Shipped literally; the ruling is the designer's.

3. A CONSEQUENCE OF §2 AND §3 THAT THE BRIEF DOES NOT ADDRESS: the gold Perfect zone is drawn on presses two through four and buys nothing there. §2 defines “landed” as Good or better and §3 puts the damage on the first press, so a Perfect on the second, third or fourth press is worth exactly what a Good is. The zone is still drawn and still graded — one code path, no special case — so a player aiming at gold on the fourth shot is aiming at nothing. Reported, not acted on. The obvious fix is to hide the Perfect zone after the first press, which would also make “the first press sets the damage” visible without a word of text; that is a design change beyond the brief and it is the designer's call.

§9 — TWO THINGS THE BATTERY TURNED UP, NEITHER CAUSED BY THIS BATCH

THE BATTERY's COUNT GREP HAS BEEN TOO NARROW FOR A THIRD TIME. Seven suites print checks: N   failures: N and two print BATCH XX: N passed, N FAILED; [0-9]+ checks matches neither, so ai, bm, bn, bo, bp, bq and br all reported checks=? fails=? — every one of them pinned with a number in CLAUDE.md. A count-diffing rule cannot see a regression in a suite whose count reads ?, which is CP's watchdog blind spot arriving through the parser instead of through a hang. All three shapes are matched now and the recovered counts are 2217 / 1891 / 81 / 1025 / 272 / 739 / 1447, every one reproducing CR's.

test_batch_bo HAS A FLAKY ASSERTION, AND IT IS A THIRD KIND OF INSTABILITY. an and bk drift in their check COUNT; bo's count is steady at 1025 and one assertion fails by chance. Its §5 NULL FIELD check resolves the same enemy attack at 2 Resonance and at 14 and requires the deeper one to hurt less; the damage carries a 0.9–1.1 variance roll, so when both land on the same integer — observed once as “16 damage at 2 stacks, 16 at 14” — it fails. test_batch_bo.gd calls seed() zero times. Measured: 1 failure in 13 runs on the CS tree, 0 in 8 on unmodified HEAD, and the test reaches none of this batch's code — it calls _resolve directly and never enters _hero_turn, _run_skill_check or the sequence. Reported, not repaired: seeding the suite or widening the gap the assertion measures are both changes to somebody else's test, and which one is right is a call for the batch that owns it.

§8 — THE GATE, AND THE GAP IT HAD

check_cs.gd is a LIVE gate — 104 checks, 0 failures — and it is live because it has to be. The bot cannot press a bar, so partial credit, the tapering windows and the tell are exercised nowhere in the existing battery. It spawns a real non-autoplay battle with a Sharpshooter, drives his bar by hand at every press count the design allows, and measures what the sequence actually paid; it also resolves the basic for real at each count, which is this batch's floor.

IT WAS THEN BROKEN ON PURPOSE FIVE WAYS AND CAUGHT FOUR. The cap raised to five, partial credit removed, the Perfect window widened with the count, and the widening table flattened all produced failures. Moving the per-press Focus figure from 8 to 9 passed clean, because every payout assertion was written as landed × SS_SEQ_FOCUS_PER_PRESS and so followed the constant wherever it went. The payout numbers are pinned now, with a failure message that says the documents quote them — a figure flagged as the designer's to move is exactly the figure that must not move without the documents that quote it moving too.

check_cn.gd failed on the first run of this batch, correctly: SC_PROFILE_DEFAULT gained a sixth field, press_taper, and that gate asserts the field COUNT. Its default is 1.0, the no-op — every press the same width, which is what the five numbers always described — so no other bar in the game moves. The gate is updated and the count assertion stays.

2026-08-19 — Batch CR: THE FOLD RULINGS

The designer's rulings on CQ's 105-fold audit. Boss immunity to hard control is BROKEN-gated now rather than Perfect-gated, because CN's fold silently deleted it; four values are reverted; and the rest of the audit stands as shipped. The census that CQ built to find the fold has been re-run against the ruling itself, and it reports that the ruling's own rule catches ten more cards than the ruling's list names — reported, not applied. Save version did not move (still v10).

§1 — HARD CONTROL LANDS ON A BOSS ONLY ONCE IT IS BROKEN

FLASH FREEZE and SNARE TRAP's Stun each spared an unbroken boss unless a Perfect landed. CN removed their bars, their Perfect became their base, and boss immunity to hard control silently ceased to exist — the Occultist's whole Madness gate rests on Broken meaning something. Neither could be restored to its old condition, because "only on a Perfect" is not expressible on an ability with no bar. So the gate moved to the mechanic that already exists:

Hard control lands on a boss only once that boss is BROKEN. Never before.

NO SECOND CHECK WAS WRITTEN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE IMPLEMENTATION. _apply_status has always refused stunned, frozen, psychosis, bewitch and hysteria on target.is_boss and not target.broken — the same broken the Madness lane reads. Both abilities obey the rule by no longer passing force: Flash Freeze's _hold_freeze(target, attacker, true) loses its third argument, and Snare Trap stops stamping sn_st["perfect"] = true on the snare it lays, so _spring_trap forces nothing. This is better than the pre-fold behaviour rather than a restoration of it: a bypass earned through play rather than through timing.

THE CENSUS OF EVERY ABILITY THAT APPLIES HARD CONTROL TO A BOSS, reported and NOT extended to: POMMEL STRIKE is the one ability left buying past the carve-out, and it is still expressible there because that card KEPT its bar (25 damage, so runs_skill_check() is true) — its perfect still lands the Stun on an unbroken boss. Whether it joins the rule is a designer's call. Everything else already conformed: Mind Flay (whose card already says "A BOSS RESISTS UNTIL BROKEN"), Bewitch, Mass Hysteria, Glacial Prison and Cryoclasm (both through _hold_freeze passing nothing), Spread of Madness (which filters not e.is_boss or e.broken itself) and Ricochet's stagger. _spring_trap's force_stun parameter survives with no caller passing true; removing a shared helper's argument is adjacent scope, so it is left and asserted.

§2 — TWO REVERTS, AND THE HALF OF ONE THAT STANDS

BEWITCH — the instant strike is REMOVED. It was the Perfect-only half, and the fold made it unconditional: a free extra ENEMY attack with no natural gate, acquired by accident. Base behaviour only — three turns of the target attacking its own, starting on its own turn. Losing the bar was still correct (there is no base damage for a grade to multiply); folding was the separate mistake. The criterion decides whether an ability GRADES; it does not decide what an orphaned bonus BECOMES, and CN answered only the first question.

RALLYING SHOUT — Pressure back to a flat 30, from the folded 50. Pre-fold it read 50 if is_perfect else int(30 * mult); with no bar there is no mult, so the old BASE is the ruling and not the old formula — the grade scaling cannot come back. The 20%→30% resource fold on the line beneath it is ACCEPTED and deliberately not reverted with it (§4, the 33 magnitude folds).

§3 — THREE DURATION REVERTS, AND THE RULE IS > NOT ≥

The ruling is duration > cooldown, not duration ≥ cooldown. A duration equal to its cooldown is a maintenance cost — holding the buff spends an action and its resource every cycle, which is a real tradeoff. A duration that exceeds the cooldown with slack is where the decision disappears. Scoped to self-buffs and party buffs only: an enemy debuff must be re-applied per target and costs an action each time.

DIVINE PRESENCE, ALMS and VESPERS all revert 6 → 4 turns against their 4-turn cooldowns. All three read 6 if is_perfect else 4 before the fold. VESPERS' ABSORB IS NOT TOUCHED — VESPERS_PCT has been 0.20 at CG, CK and HEAD and was never Perfect-gated, exactly as CQ corrected the brief.

THE BRIEF SAID "TWO DURATION REVERTS" AND NAMED THREE. §3's enumeration is the operative scope and all three were the same shape, so all three are reverted.

§3a — THE FINDING: THE RULING'S RULE CATCHES TEN MORE CARDS THAN ITS LIST NAMES

REPORTED, NOT APPLIED. The > refinement is a real improvement on CQ's ≥ classification — and re-running CQ's own census under it is what shows the gap. CQ's twenty-two "≥ cd (already)" rows are not twenty-two abilities that were already permanent. That label meant the pre-fold value was at or past the cooldown, and for seventeen of them it was exactly AT it — which under > is the maintenance cost the ruling explicitly wants to keep, and the fold pushed every one of them past it. Only FIVE of the twenty-two were genuinely past their cooldown before CN (Ember Debt, Mark of the Hunt, Blessing of Zeal, Tripwire, Immolate).

So §4 accepts a bucket defined by ≥ while §3 reverts on >, and the rows fall through the gap. Ten self or party buffs — §3's own declared scope — are in exactly the class the three reverted cards were in, and are left standing because a batch does not retune 105 magnitudes on its own judgment, and it does not retune ten either (the CQ §6 standing rule).

§4 — RECORDED AS DECIDED, SO NO LATER BATCH REOPENS THEM

All 33 magnitude folds (nearly everything moved 20–35%, so relative balance between abilities barely shifted, and the pre-fold values were themselves never validated by play). The other ten gate folds — Rage refunds, Focus on a mark, the 5% heals, Interpose covering the Warden. Anvil and Formless at 4 turns, both still shorter than their cooldowns, both to be judged in play. Threshold's lockout at 2 turns — its number had moved twice without a decision, and this is the decision. Mana Shield and Mass Hysteria, where the fold deleted tooltips for Perfects no handler ever implemented. The durations already at or past their cooldown before CN and the 18 the fold pushed to EQUAL their cooldown — with §3a's correction to what the first of those two counts actually contains.

§5 — THE ASSERTIONS, AND A CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF'S PREMISE

THE ~70 STALE ASSERTIONS WERE NOT LEFT RED. CQ REPAIRED THEM. The brief's §5 reads "CQ §3 left them red rather than repairing them to whatever the code happened to do"; CQ's own commit says "95 STALE ASSERTIONS REPAIRED TO INTENT across 20 suites", and CLAUDE.md records the CQ battery at 45 suites, zero throws, zero failures. The premise is half right and the half that matters is the qualifier: CQ repaired them to intent, which for the seven cards this batch rules on meant to the folded behaviour — the best available reading at the time, and the reading CR has now overturned.

So §5's real work was the assertions CR's own rulings invalidated, and CQ's discipline is what made them findable. The clearest case is test_batch_bt's Flash Freeze block: CQ inverted it to the folded behaviour and wrote in the file that it was "the assertion that would catch the carve-out coming back, and the magnitude behind it is UNREVIEWED." It caught it. That check is inverted back, to the ruling rather than to the code.

§6 — CQ'S LOOSE ENDS, CONFIRMED

THE FOUR HANGING SUITES RUN TO COMPLETION. al, bp, br and bw all produce counts, none times out, and the diagnosis (_defensive_brace's bot guard naming the two BOTS rather than the absence of a player) has held for a second batch. The five-batch hang is closed.

bt's FALL AND ITS 13 FAILURES WERE NOT THE SAME CAUSE, AND CQ ALREADY PROVED IT. §6 asks this batch to confirm they were the same; they were not, and the measurement is CQ's own. The 13 failures were the fold's population entirely (Slow Burn, Funeral Pyre, Flash Freeze's carve-out, Inner Arcane) — CQ's negative control reverted the four folded values in battle.gd and bt reported the same 455 checks with 13 failures becoming 5, so the fold moved no check count at all. The 457 → 455 fall is test-side and correct: _pools's tranche-3 depth loop lost 3 as CH and CI moved the Hunter and Warrior threes to the eight-deep assertion, and _docs gained 1 when CK replaced a hard-coded stamp with two durable ones. Both are resolved; the brief's hypothesis about their being one cause is the thing to record as answered.

CP'S TWO HARNESS FAULTS BOTH STILL HOLD. The per-suite watchdog (with CQ's per-target bound, so a slow gate is not reported as a stopped one) and the lock are both in run_battery.sh, and the lock was confirmed by DRIVING it rather than by reading it: a second invocation against a live log directory refuses with REFUSING: a battery is already writing ... and writes nothing.

§7 — THE STANDING RULE THIS BATCH EXISTS TO WRITE DOWN

Removing a skill check from an ability makes its Perfect-only behaviour unconditional. Any Perfect that gated a BINARY — boss immunity, an extra strike, a refund — must be ruled on BEFORE the bar comes off, not audited afterwards.

A MAGNITUDE FOLD IS VISIBLE IN A DIFF AND A CENSUS CAN FIND IT LATER; A BINARY IS NOT A MAGNITUDE. "The Stun lands on an unbroken boss" and "one of those strikes lands at once" are rules that switch from off to always-on, and nothing in X if is_perfect else Y becoming X says which kind of thing just changed. CN's criterion answered does this ability still grade? correctly 113 times. It never asked what the orphaned bonus should become, and folding was assumed because folding preserves the most. Three of the seven cards here are that gap: Bewitch's free enemy attack, and Flash Freeze and Snare Trap between them deleting a game-wide immunity rule.

§8 — VERIFIED

THE DEFECT THIS BATCH INTRODUCED AND THE GATE THAT CAUGHT IT, recorded because it is the useful part. The three §3 durations are declared TWICE — once in the cast handler and once in _recast_writes's proposal table, which the CO recast gate reads to decide whether a second cast would improve anything. Reverting only the handlers left the table proposing 6 against a standing 4, so the gate read every recast as an improvement and stopped refusing a saturated recast on Alms, Divine Presence and Vespers. check_co failed all three BY NAME on the first battery run. That gate spawns two real battles and casts all 58 gated abilities onto every unit they can reach rather than reading the table, which is exactly why it could see this — and it is Batch BP's Eye of the Storm lesson one door along: two copies of one figure. Both copies now move together, and the rule is written at the table.

FULL BATTERY, TWICE, AFTER THE FIX: 45 SUITES, ZERO THROWS, ZERO FAILURES. ah 5625, ah_battle 65, ai 2217, aj 418, ak 528, al 560, an 6054, ar 735, as 396, at 470, au 336, av 324, aw 350, ax 345, ay 484, az 519, ba 690, bb 177, bc 91, bd 71, be 34, bf 78, bg 47, bh 233, bi 91, bj 67, bk 130, bl 88, bm 1891, bn 81, bo 1025, bp 272, bq 739, br 1447, bs 263, bt 455, bu 477, bv 897, bw 548, bx 142, cb 1181, cd 86, ce 1112, runes 3121, rune_battle 97. Every count reproduces CQ's exactly except three, and all three are accounted for: ax is 342 → 345, the three assertions §1 added to pin its two closed doors and its one open one; an reads 6054, inside its documented 6051–6054 drift; and bk is the finding below.

bk IS A SECOND DRIFTING SUITE AND CLAUDE.md PINS IT AS IF IT WERE STABLE. It read 129 on the first battery run and 130 on the second, and four consecutive runs gave 129, 130, 129, 130 — always 0 failures. The cause is structural rather than flaky: bk generates real zone maps and then walks them (for j in nodes.size(), for prev in run.map[s-1], for t in out), so its check COUNT is a function of the topology it happened to roll. A count-diffing rule reads 129 as a regression, which is the one thing the drift note on an exists to prevent. Recorded as a band, not a number.

THE ONE RED IS check_cm_live's FOUR, UNCHANGED AND NOT THIS BATCH'S. They are the four CQ diagnosed and recorded as OWED inside the gate itself: _nobody_can_press() is true headless, so the defensive brace takes the bot branch and the bar cannot appear in a headless run at all, which makes two of them unsatisfiable and turns the other two into measurements of a 20%-Perfect bot mix. Identical on unmodified HEAD. Reported rather than repaired, on CQ's own reasoning: repair only what is understood, and an opt-in this harness then failed to drive would turn four known reds into a hang.

Gates: check_parse, check_flow, check_map, check_cl_resolver, check_cl_width, check_cm, check_cn and check_co all 0 failures; run-harness gates 1/2/3 pass (22/165/8); check_map_screen 0 throws. Parse verified by grepping stderr for Parse Error, never by the tally — 0 across the tree and 0 across the four edited suites, which check_parse does not cover (it walks res://scripts and res://scenes only).

NO RUN WAS DESTROYED: user://run_save.bin did not exist before the battery, so the designer had no run in flight to lose.

2026-08-18 — Batch CQ: THE BATTERY FINISHES, AND THE FOLD IS ACCOUNTED FOR

The battery runs end to end for the first time since Batch CE: the four hanging suites are diagnosed and fixed, and the deadlock behind them was NOT the one CP suspected. All 105 of CN's folded abilities are reported with the value before the fold and the value now, read at the read site. Exactly one is reverted — Elevation, where the fold overwrote an explicit CG decision. Everything else is reported and left alone. The two remaining clamp sites are closed, no_skill_check is deleted, and the eight overflowing draft-card lines are gone. Save version did not move (still v10).

§0 — THE LAST TWO CLAMPS, AND THE CENSUS STILL STANDS

BLOOD DEBT and RECKLESS ABANDON carried the identical apply-then-assign defect CP clamped on Battle Shout, Stabilize and Eye of the Storm: _apply_status MAXES the power, the update_status beneath it ASSIGNS, and the consuming site reads status_power. Both are clamped the same way — read what stands first, write the chip only when the new value is at least as strong. Five of five.

Blood Debt is the one where re-marking is ROUTINE rather than a misplay: the mark SURVIVES its own bleedout, so a re-opened wound gets re-marked as a matter of course, and a plain 25 landing on a standing Perfect 35 used to cut the debt by ten points. Reckless Abandon is the one that bites hardest: the buff scales off the Rage ACTUALLY SPENT and the cast zeroes the bar, so the second cast in a window is nearly always the weaker one — a full bar for +20%, rebuild 30 Rage, cast again, and the all-in buff fell to +6%. It is one of CM's gated five, so a Sloppy also loses it outright.

STILL NO GLOBAL CLAMP, and CP's census is unchanged: 69 sites, 29 with the shape. Countdowns written back through update_status would freeze forever under a global max — held_breath and instinct compute status_power(...) - 1 and write it back, and spite passes a CAP as the power while its chip carries the live figure. The other 24 are left alone deliberately. test_batch_cp pins all five sites by name now.

§1 — A BATTERY THAT CANNOT FINISH IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT

ALL FOUR HANGING SUITES RUN NOW — al, bp, br AND bw — AND THE CAUSE WAS NOT THE ORIENTATION CARD. CP found a latent deadlock in the two skill-check orientation cards, wrote a fix, tested it, saw that it did not unhang the suites, and reverted it. That observation was correct and is confirmed here: shipping the card guard alone leaves test_batch_al stopped in exactly the same place.

THE REAL DEADLOCK IS _defensive_brace. CM's defensive check has a bot guard — if sim or autoplay: braced = randf() < DEF_BOT_PERFECT — and that pair names the two BOTS rather than the absence of a player. A hand-driven suite is neither: it sets Run.active and clears sim, autoplay and sim_run precisely because it wants the real battle path. So it fell to the else and awaited _skill_done — a signal only a key press or click emits — with no input device in the process. Reproduced by bisection: al stops inside _live_spite_break, on the line that has an enemy strike a WARDEN, which is exactly where a defensive bar appears. Zero CPU, mid-battle, no output: CLAUDE.md's hang mode (1).

THE FIX IS ONE QUESTION ASKED IN ONE PLACE. _nobody_can_press() returns sim or autoplay or DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless", and all three awaits that wait on a human now read it: both orientation cards and the defensive brace. The display server is the honest third term — under --headless there is no surface to draw the bar on and no device to press it with, so an await on a press is an await on nothing. The fault was that three call sites each answered "is there anybody there" separately and two of them answered it wrong; asking once is what stops them drifting apart again. CP's card fix ships too, as the real defect it is rather than as a fix for the hang.

AND br HAD ONE OF ITS OWN, FOUND THE SAME WAY. br is one of the four suites that deadlocked, so its Ironclad check had not run in a battery since CM either. It compared ONE blow against ONE blow with the block, the parry, the plating ramp and the crit all driven off by hand — and then rolled randf_range(0.9, 1.1) twice anyway, because the damage variance is a literal inside _resolve with no field to zero. A 15% cut cannot clear a 22% spread on a single swing: a warded high roll is 1.1 × 0.85 = 0.935 of base against an unwarded low roll of 0.90, so the comparison inverts outright. It read 29 taken against 28 on the first battery that ever reached it. Sampled over twenty swings each way now — the answer check_cm_live already uses for its brace ratio — which keeps the AK/AL/AR rule the block states in its own comment: forced, not retried. Both of these are the deadlock's real cost: two live checks sat unexercised for five batches, and neither was a fold consequence.

A FIFTH TARGET WAS BEING REPORTED AS HUNG AND IS NOT HUNG. check_map printed *** TIMED OUT after 240s *** on every run of this batch including the baseline on unmodified HEAD, with a banner and nothing else — which reads exactly like the four suites that genuinely deadlocked. Run on its own it uses 99% CPU for five minutes and then finishes and prints its distributions. It walks 1,500 generated maps across four routing policies; that is simply what it costs. CP's watchdog is the right instrument and it could not tell a slow gate from a stopped one, which is the same class of error as the fault it was written to catch, pointing the other way. CLAUDE.md's own taxonomy is what splits them and it says CHECK CPU FIRST: ~1-2% is a deadlock or the idle throttle, 30-50% with a growing log is TextServer exhaustion, and 99% with no output is a gate doing its job slowly. The bound is per-target now (TMO[check_map]=600, the shape EXTRA already uses for flags) rather than raised globally, because a looser global bound would have blunted the watchdog for everything else.

AND ONE THING THE GUARD COSTS, REPORTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. check_cm_live.gd's two hand-set Profile flags are deleted — the cards are guarded now, so the flags have nothing left to dodge — but four checks in that gate are RED and have been since CM. The identical four fail on unmodified HEAD, so the guard did not cause them; it does, however, change what they could ever have measured. That harness is built to BE the player: it polls sc_active, writes sc_pos and calls _grade_skill_check() itself, which is why it was never one of the four that hung. With _nobody_can_press() true the brace takes the bot branch, so the defensive bar cannot appear in a headless run at all — two of the four are now unsatisfiable rather than merely failing, and the two ratio checks measure a 20%-Perfect bot mix instead of a forced brace. The repair is left undone deliberately and is recorded as owed in the gate itself. Re-pointing them at the bot's own rate, or giving the guard an explicit opt-in a willing harness can set, both need the diagnosis of the original four that this batch did not do — and an opt-in this harness then failed to drive would turn four known reds into a HANG, which is strictly worse. Repair only what is understood.

AND WITH al RUNNING FOR THE FIRST TIME, IT FAILED ONE CHECK IN SIX — A REAL DEFECT THE DEADLOCK HAD BEEN HIDING. _live_spite_break forces the blow to land before measuring Spite's reflect, and it did that with block_chance = 0.0. Zero is not off on a Warden: _live_block_chance is clampf(block_chance + _plating_slice(u), 0, 1) and _plating_slice hands a HEAVY PLATING unit a flat 0.15 before his own field is read, so he blocked roughly one hit in six, the blow landed for nothing, and Spite reflects only on final > 0. This suite already carried the warning in prose — _live_fields says in terms that a large negative field is what actually turns the roll off — and the check three sections below it did not apply it. Driven negative now, green over eight consecutive runs. Two wrong fixes were tried first and both are worth recording: zeroing armor alone did nothing, and raising the ATTACKER's damage to force a landing reintroduced the flake from the other end, because a crit on the high roll could fell a 200-health Warden.

BOTH OF CP'S HARNESS FAULTS HOLD. The per-suite watchdog reported test_batch_al as *** TIMED OUT after 240s *** on the pre-fix baseline run rather than letting it swallow the battery, and the lock is in place so a second invocation refuses instead of writing into a live log directory. Both were exercised in anger during this batch.

§2 — THE FOLD AUDIT: ALL 105 REPORTED, ONE REVERTED

THE FINDING IS THAT 105 ABILITIES GOT STRONGER AND NOBODY DECIDED THEY SHOULD. Every row below was read at its READ SITE — the handler in battle.gd — and not inferred from perfect_text history. The shape is mechanical throughout: CN removed the timing bar, which orphaned the Perfect bonus, and the fold rewrote X if is_perfect else Y as X. 99 live in classes.gd's corpus and 6 in talents.gd (Battle Shout, Hold the Line, Immolate, Phoenix Rebirth, Rime, Overcharge).

THE ONE REVERSAL, AND IT IS REVERTED: ELEVATION. The designer chose 2 Faith with a raised cost at CG, explicitly picking the conservative option over 3 when both were on the table. The fold made it 3. That is not drift, it is a decision undone. el_stacks reads ELEVATION_STACKS again rather than ELEVATION_STACKS + 1, and the description is back to "every ally gains 2". ELEVATION_STACKS_TEST := 2 in test_batch_cp was already pinning the intended value and was already red against the folded 3.

THE FOUR FLAGGED FIRST AND LOUDEST, because the fold pushed cards that were ALREADY recorded as possibly overtuned:

  • ANVIL — 3 turns → 4, against a 5-turn cooldown. Recorded at CI as "potentially the strongest card in the batch" and shipped deliberately untuned; the fold tuned it upward without anybody asking.
  • FORMLESS — 3 turns → 4, against a 6-turn cooldown. It grants BOTH stances and every stance-gated card, so the extra turn is an extra turn of the whole kit.
  • DIVINE PRESENCE — 4 turns → 6, against a 4-turn cooldown. It was flagged at CG as already running 100% uptime at 4-against-4. THE DURATION NOW EXCEEDS THE COOLDOWN BY TWO TURNS, SO THE COOLDOWN HAS STOPPED EXISTING — the buff can be refreshed two turns before it would lapse and can never be off.
  • VESPERS — 4 turns → 6, against a 4-turn cooldown, so the same. ONE CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF, MEASURED: only the DURATION was a Perfect value. The absorb is maxi(int(round(attacker.max_hp * VESPERS_PCT)), 1) and has never sat inside an is_perfect branch — VESPERS_PCT := 0.20 is byte-identical at CG, CK and HEAD. The absorb did not move.

AND THE CLASS THAT IS INVISIBLE IN A DIFF OF MAGNITUDES: 40 OF THE 57 DURATION FOLDS NOW MEET OR EXCEED THEIR OWN COOLDOWN. 18 of those were pushed over BY THIS FOLD (they sat below their cooldown before it) — Battle Poise, Feigned Guard, Covering Guard, Turn the Blade, Null Field, Undying Vigil, Battle Trance, Ironclad, Slow Burn, Hoarfrost Armor, Emberkeep, Frostbind, Resonant Field, Penance, Stalking Horse, Divine Wrath, Umbral Sigil and Consecrated Ground. The other 22 already met or exceeded it and the fold widened the gap. That class of change converts a timed buff into a permanent one and it does not look like a buff in a diff.

TWO OF THE 105 WERE NEVER IMPLEMENTED AT ALL. MANA SHIELD ("Initiative cost 1.5 instead of 2") and MASS HYSTERIA ("Cooldown becomes 3 instead") advertised Perfect bonuses that no code delivered — neither handler contains is_perfect at CK or anywhere before it. For those two the fold changed nothing mechanically; it deleted a false advertisement.

THE FULL REPORT. Before and after are read at the handler. uptime marks duration folds against the ability's own cooldown: ≥ cd (NEW) means this fold pushed it over, ≥ cd (already) means it was over before and the fold widened it.

§3 — THE STALE ASSERTIONS, REPAIRED TO INTENT

The pre-fix battery reported 95 failing assertions across 20 suites. All are repaired and every suite is green. The rule applied throughout: repair to the value §2 establishes as intended, never to whatever the code happens to do. Elevation is the case that rule exists for — test_batch_ce asserted "a perfect hands over 3 stacks", and rewriting that to 3 would have blessed the accident and destroyed the evidence. It asserts the reverted 2, and asserts that the GRADE CHANGES NOTHING, which is the durable form of the question.

NO ASSERTION WAS LEFT DELIBERATELY RED, and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming. §3 reserves a known red for a fold §2 reports as undecided. None of the four cards §2 flags loudest — Anvil, Formless, Divine Presence, Vespers — has a failing assertion, so the carve-out turned out to be empty in practice. Where a repaired assertion sits on an UNREVIEWED magnitude the comment above it says so in terms (test_batch_bt's Slow Burn and test_batch_cb's Emberkeep both name the cooldown they now meet), so the evidence lives beside the check rather than only in this entry.

THREE OF THE 95 WERE NOT THE FOLD AT ALL, AND EACH HAD BEEN RED LONGER. test_batch_bu's "Recant never writes a spec meter" read the branch's raw text for second_resource and tripped on the branch's own comment explaining that it deliberately never touches it — BU shipped both the comment and the check, so it has never been green. test_batch_ce's glossary count went stale at CO, which added "Recasting a Standing Effect" as the 94th entry. test_batch_ar's Overburn check read a clause CL deleted in its prose pass. Two more — test_batch_bg and test_batch_bi — searched the Devout's passive block for a phrase that is still there but which CL's re-wrap split across a line break; both flatten newlines before the read now.

§4 — bt: THE FALL AND THE FAILURES ARE NOT THE SAME CAUSE

THE BRIEF'S HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG, AND MEASURING IT IS THE ANSWER. The 13 failures and the two-check fall have nothing to do with each other.

THE 13 FAILURES ARE §3's POPULATION, ENTIRELY: Slow Burn 3→4 turns (3 failures), Funeral Pyre 150%→200% (2), Flash Freeze's boss carve-out folded away (4), Inner Arcane +0→+1 Resonance (4). Flash Freeze is the loudest of them: taking an UNBROKEN boss was the Perfect's reward, the handler now passes true unconditionally, and every Flash Freeze seals a boss that has not been Broken.

THE FALL IS TEST-SIDE AND DELIBERATE, AND A NEGATIVE CONTROL PROVES IT. With the four folded values reverted in battle.gd, bt reports 455 checks — the same count, with 13 failures becoming 5. The fold moves no check count at all. Running the suite section by section against a CE worktree splits it exactly: _pools lost 3 and _docs gained 1, for a net of −2. _pools's tranche-3 depth loop ran over SIX specs at CE asserting "still five — its third of tranche 3 is owed"; CH moved the Hunter three up to the eight-deep assertion and CI moved the Warrior three, leaving a THREE-spec loop. _docs gained one because CK replaced a hard-coded stamp assertion with two durable ones. CLAUDE.md already records the same loop causing bt 460 → 457 when it went twelve-spec to six; this is the same mechanism one tranche later, and it is a suite correctly following the content rather than a regression.

§5 — THREE SMALL DEFECTS

THIRTEEN OF CP'S FOURTEEN AUTHORED DIGITS ARE FIXED, AND THE FOURTEENTH WAS NEVER A DEFECT. Each of the thirteen was a parenthetical carrying a typed number that also lives in code — an armor shred, a status duration, an Empower cost — and CL's standing rule is that a parenthetical is the shape reserved for a value the renderer computes, so a typed one is indistinguishable from a rendered one. All thirteen are rephrased so the number stands in PROSE, where it is allowed, with the 44-character draft-card ceiling respected line by line. SHATTER'S (max 12) STAYS: it is a CAP, the exact "legitimate prose" shape CP's own report names alongside (max 5) and (0-100). It was swept up by the regex rather than by the rule. The corpus ceiling is KEPT at CP's 89 — it is a ceiling and not an equality, so holding the old number still catches growth without pretending the remaining prose sites have been audited one by one.

ALL EIGHT OVERFLOWING DRAFT-CARD LINES ARE GONE; the widest block line is now 256px against the 258px column. Four were multi-hit damage lines pushed 7px over by a trailing    × 3 hits; the hit count moves to the damage it MULTIPLIES (Damage: 10% of Attack ×3 (Physical)   BD: 10), which fixes all four in computed_block rather than card by card and lands 25px inside. The other four were long Perfect lines — Feint (+94px, the worst), Twin Hunt (+25), Renewal (+19) and Heal (+15) — each tightened without losing what it says; Feint's stance split is stated at length in its own description directly above, so the Perfect line only has to name what the Perfect ADDS. Every candidate was MEASURED against the font rather than guessed at.

no_skill_check IS DELETED AND runs_skill_check() IS THE ONLY ANSWER IN THE CODEBASE. Two ways to ask one question is how they disagree silently: on DEADFALL the flag said "runs a bar" (it was never set) while CN's criterion had already taken the bar away, and test_batch_ah passed by reading the flag — the right answer from the wrong oracle. DELETING IT WAS NOT FREE, and the price is recorded rather than absorbed. The flag was load-bearing on FOUR of its thirteen carriers:

  • SUMMON AGUILA / CANIS / URSUS — the table was simply WRONG. _do_summon is 139 lines and reaches no damage leaf at all: a summon puts a beast on the field and the beast strikes on ITS OWN later turns. "summon" is struck from DAMAGE_SPECIALS, which corrects a derived table rather than changing a card.
  • CALL OF THE WILD is the one real disagreement, and it is NOT this batch's to settle. It DOES deal damage at cast — _companion_strike for each beast standing, _ghost_hit for each absent one — so the criterion says it earns a bar, while the flag has always said it does not, alongside every other beast-command card in its family. Handing it a timing bar is a design change and goes to the designer as a report. Until he answers, the exception is NAMED in Ability.NO_BAR_BY_DESIGN rather than hidden in a data field, so there is still exactly one place that knows.

The result is byte-for-byte behaviour: check_cn reports 113 of 211 abilities running no check, which is CN's own number.

§6 — THE STANDING RULE THIS BATCH EXISTS TO WRITE DOWN

A FOLD, A RENAME OR A REFACTOR THAT CHANGES A MAGNITUDE IS A DESIGN CHANGE. IT GOES TO THE DESIGNER AS A REPORT AND IS NEVER APPLIED ON THE BATCH'S OWN JUDGMENT. CN's fold was mechanically correct and locally reasonable at all 105 sites — an orphaned Perfect bonus genuinely has nowhere to go once the bar comes off — and it still moved 105 magnitudes nobody chose, undid one explicit decision, and converted eighteen timed buffs into permanent ones. The batch that folds is exactly the batch least able to see that, because each individual fold looks like tidying. The rule is recorded in CLAUDE.md and is why §2 of this batch is a report with one reversal rather than a retune of 105 cards.

2026-08-18 — Batch CP: THE CLAMP, AND THE FIRST DEDICATED TEST BATCH

§0 clamps three call sites where a weaker recast was dragging a standing buff downward — worse than the waste CO was written to fix. Everything after it is verification, and the verification is the larger half: the battery had not been run since Batch CE, and running it found that Batch CN's fold of 105 orphaned Perfects into base effects left roughly seventy assertions across seventeen suites pinning pre-CN magnitudes, plus four suites that hang outright. No game magnitude moves outside §0. Save version did not move (still v10).

§0 — THE CLAMP

update_status ASSIGNS where add_status MAXES. On Battle Shout, Stabilize and Eye of the Storm the power handed to update_status is computed from live state, so a weaker recast overwrote the standing value instead of merely failing to improve it. All three carry a second payload, so CO's scope limit correctly kept them out of the refusal — the downgrade is separable from the conversion, and only the downgrade was the harm.

Each site now reads status_power BEFORE _apply_status and writes the chip only when the new value is at least as strong. status_power returns -1 when nothing stands, so a fresh cast always writes. The cast still proceeds and still pays — Battle Shout's +5 Rage, Stabilize's Mana and 5% heal, and Eye of the Storm's taunts are all outside the guarded branch, which is exactly why the refusal could not reach these three and why the fix belongs at the call site.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE EVIDENCE, AND IT SHOWS THE BUG RATHER THAN ARGUING FOR IT. With all three clamps removed, test_batch_cp trips six checks — three at the source and three live, reading eye_storm 50 → 24 and stabilized 70 → 10. battle.gd came back byte-identical by hash afterwards.

§0 — THE CALL-SITE CENSUS CO WAS ASKED FOR AND NEVER REPORTED

69 call sites (67 in battle.gd, 2 in unit.gd). 42 pass a power argument; 27 do not — power defaults to -1 and is only written when power >= 0, so at those 27 a global max would be a no-op.

AND THE CENSUS ANSWERS THE QUESTION IT EXISTS FOR: update_status MUST NOT BE CLAMPED GLOBALLY. Two sites settle it on their own.

battle.gd:10510   held_breath   var hb_left := attacker.status_power("held_breath") - 1
battle.gd:10553   instinct      var hi_left := attacker.status_power("instinct") - 1

Both read the standing power, subtract one, and write it back — they are countdowns. A global maxi(s.power, power) would freeze both at their opening value, so Held Breath and Hunter's Instinct would never be spent. Nothing would crash and nothing would log. Six more banks decrement through the same door and would break the same way: mirror, arrows, feint_guard, berserk, deadfall and loyalty.

THE SHAPE, MEASURED: 29 SITES CALL _apply_status AND THEN update_status ON THE SAME STATUS — that is the pattern that can downgrade. Of the 29: 11 pass a constant or a talent-rank product and cannot fall for one caster; 10 pass 0 or no power at all; 3 are the ones clamped here; 1 (shield_charges) reads the held value and adds, so Interpose can only grow; 1 (spite) passes a cap as the power while its chip text carries the live figure, so a naive “never write a smaller number” rule would be wrong there.

REPORTED, NOT FIXED — TWO MORE SITES HAVE THE IDENTICAL DEFECT AND §0's SCOPE DID NOT NAME THEM. blood_debt (battle.gd:9599) passes 35 on a perfect cast and 25 otherwise, so re-marking the same enemy with a non-perfect Blood Debt drops the standing share; the site's own comment says the power exists so the bleedout site need not re-derive whether the cast was perfect, which is precisely the value a weaker recast overwrites. reckless_abandon (battle.gd:15006) scales with Rage spent and the cast zeroes the Rage bar, so a second cast inside its own window is necessarily cheaper and lands smaller — CM gates it below one full step, not below the standing value. Both take the same three-line clamp. Not applied here, because widening a fix past its brief is how a batch stops being attributable.

§1 — THE INSTRUMENTS, AUDITED BEFORE BEING TRUSTED

check_parse IS NEGATIVE-CONTROLLED AND THE CN REPAIR IS REAL. With a deliberate syntax error appended to classes.gd the gate exits 1, prints check_parse: 16 failures, names PARSE FAILED: res://scripts/classes.gd explicitly, and the stderr grep reads 127. Restored byte-identical; back to 0 and 0. An instrument repaired without a control is an instrument nobody has tested — this one is tested now. The cascade to 16 files is honest: everything that depends on classes.gd genuinely cannot instantiate.

FOUR SUITES HANG, AND THE BATTERY COULD NOT SEE IT BECAUSE A HANG HAS NO COUNT. test_batch_al, bp, br and bw stop producing output and sit at roughly zero CPU indefinitely — bp was held for ten minutes with two lines of output. REPRODUCED ON UNMODIFIED HEAD, so it is not this batch's doing. Two consequences worth separating: a hung suite takes the whole battery with it, so every later count is missing rather than wrong — the one failure mode a count-diffing rule cannot catch; and because Godot buffers stdout when not a TTY, a killed suite loses its buffer and reads as a suite that printed nothing.

A LATENT DEADLOCK WAS FOUND WHILE CHASING IT, IS REPORTED, AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED. Both skill-check orientation cards await _hint_done — a signal only a real click or key press emits — behind a guard of not sim and not autoplay and Run.active and not Run.sim_run. Every hand-driven suite satisfies all four, and every one redirects Profile to a scratch file so the “taught” flag is always unset. check_cm_live.gd sets BOTH flags by hand, which is CM knowing about the trap and answering it in the one file it had just written. A PROFILE FLAG IS NOT A BOT GUARD, and CLAUDE.md's standing rule is that a new modal must bot-guard its await. The fix was written, tested, and REVERTED: it did not unhang the four suites, and shipping a product change that does not fix what it aimed at, in a batch whose §0 is the only sanctioned code change, is the scope creep CA warned about. The hang needs its own batch; this is the first half of its diagnosis.

THE BATTERY IS A SCRIPT IN THE REPO NOW (run_battery.sh), AND IT CARRIES THE THREE SCARS IT KEPT RE-LEARNING: flags in an array (zsh does not word-split an unquoted expansion, which silently under-ran test_batch_bl), a count grep that accepts a comma or none, and a ^ *FAIL grep that does not need an indent. It adds two of its own: a per-suite watchdog, because a hang must be reported as its own outcome rather than as a suite with no count; and a lock, because killing a hung suite's Godot does not kill the battery that spawned it — two invocations ran into one log directory during this batch, every count became whichever process finished last, and nothing errored. That contaminated run was discarded and re-run.

AND THE BATTERY'S OWN REPORT COULD NOT READ ITS OWN SUITES: THEY PRINT COUNTS IN FIVE DIFFERENT FORMATS (N checks, M failures / N passed, M FAILED / N checks / M failures / checks: N  failures: M / sections: S  checks: N  failures: M), so any single grep reports ? for some. CD found this once from one direction; it is wider than one grep. A COUNT THE HARNESS CANNOT PARSE IS WORSE THAN A COUNT NOBODY DIFFS.

THE THREE HARD-CODED STAMP GATES ARE RE-POINTED, AND THE PATTERN IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE BUMP. test_batch_ah, bb and bn each asserted a LITERAL stamp (Batch CM against a live Batch CO), so each passed for exactly one batch and had to be hand-bumped forever. CJ's re-stamp turned five such checks red at once and CK repaired those five while leaving these three. All three now compare against their own suite's batch code, so no bump is ever owed again. That took test_batch_bn from red to 81/0.

§1/§4 — THE FINDING THAT DOMINATES THE BATCH: CN's FOLD LEFT SEVENTEEN SUITES ASSERTING PRE-CN MAGNITUDES

CN §3 folded 105 orphaned Perfect bonuses into base effects — the ability is slightly stronger and nothing is lost — and CG through CO shipped implement-only, so the battery was last run at CE. The consequence is arithmetic rather than opinion: roughly seventy assertions across seventeen suites still pin the pre-fold base, and every one of them has been red since CN without anyone seeing it. A representative slice, all one root cause:

  • Deadfall arms FOUR springs where test_batch_bd asserts three (DEADFALL_CHARGES + 1 at the cast site, the constant left at 3 with a comment) — 13 failures, plus ah_battle's “an ordinary rig arms three”.
  • Elevation hands over 3 stacks where test_batch_ce asserts 2 — its own perfect's extra stack, folded.
  • Recant returns 40% where test_batch_bu asserts 30% (11 failures).
  • Mirror Image stands up four images where test_batch_bq asserts three.
  • Ember Debt burns 12 turns where test_batch_bs asserts 8; Slow Burn holds 4 where bt asserts 3 (13 failures); Bloodbond takes 25% where bv asserts half.
  • Resurrection returns 25% where test_batch_av asserts 20%.

REPORTED, AND ONLY THE MECHANICAL ONES REPAIRED, per §1's own instruction to report before repairing. Each of the remaining ~70 needs its own read site opened to confirm the new base is what CN intended — that is a batch, not a section, and it is the obvious next one.

TWO OF THE REPAIRS ARE INVERSIONS AND ONE OF THEM WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON, WHICH IS THE HARDER FAULT TO SEE. test_batch_ah asserted Snare Trap's and Deadfall's old perfect_text; both lost their bars at CN §2, so CN correctly CLEARED both Perfects, and the assertion is inverted rather than deleted — it asserts the fold, so a later batch that quietly took the fourth spring away trips here rather than looking like CN. Beside it, ah's “Deadfall now runs a skill check” read not deadfall.no_skill_check — the explicit opt-out flag, still false — and went on printing a pass while the parameteric criterion had already taken the bar away. no_skill_check has not been the answer to that question since CN §1; runs_skill_check() is. test_batch_ah is 5626/0.

AND test_batch_cd IS THE ONE INSTRUMENT THAT WORKED THROUGHOUT. It is the only suite that can see another suite's failures — it runs five as child processes and reads their stderr — and its three failures were, exactly, ah, bb and bj reporting non-zero. CD built the thing that would have caught all of this five batches earlier, and it did catch it; what was missing was anybody running the battery it lives in.

§2 — THE TWENTY-SEVEN UNCOVERED ABILITIES

NEW test_batch_cp.gd: 693 checks / 0 failures / 0 throws. Coverage of the twenty-seven tranche-3 cards in the standard shape: each resolves through pool_ability to itself (a card resolving to a different name is the resolver answering the wrong question — CH's Harvest collision), carries a description, a delay and a cooldown, sits in exactly one spec draft pool, and is absent from SPEC_POOLS and CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS, so a spec card cannot silently re-weight the boss draw or the class seam. SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS holds 96 across twelve specs at eight apiece.

THE TWO CG INVERSIONS WERE INVERTED, NOT DELETED — CONFIRMED, WHICH WAS THE POINT OF ASKING. A deletion is silent coverage loss and looks identical from the outside. Both carry an explicit “INVERTED BY BATCH CG §2, NOT DELETED” note with byte-identical setups: Elevation grants real Faith, driven at three depths so a floor-writing version fails at every one, and Blessing of the Faithful drops the peak, which was CE's own negative control. ELEVATION_STACKS_TEST := 2 is pinned, which is also what makes CN's fold to 3 visible as a failure rather than as a mystery.

ANVIL AND RECOMPENSE CANCEL, AND WHAT IS ASSERTED IS THE ORDERING rather than a carve-out: Anvil refuses the Heavy Plating reset, Recompense is paid by that reset, and the payment sits inside the else of the Anvil branch, so holding both pays nothing. Read positionally, so a rename cannot make it pass vacuously; both cards' own text names the other.

STALKING HORSE'S AFFLICTIONS ARE ALL IN DEBUFF_IDS, and the failure that catches is silent: Trapper's breadth term counts that curated list only, so an affliction outside it would apply, log and read as working while paying the Survivalist's multiplier nothing.

§3 — TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, BOTH MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED

THE LITERAL-DIGIT RULE IS NOT AT TWO HUNDRED SITES. IT IS AT 89 ACROSS 979 AUTHORED FIELDS, AND CL WAS RIGHT TO MAKE IT A REPORT. Swept over every authored field rather than CL's abilities-only slice, most of the 89 are legitimate prose that is not a resolved value at all — (max 5), (0-100), (2 on a crit), (cap 100) — so asserting zero would fail against correct text. It ships as a baseline instead, which is the form that bites: the fourteen ability-level offenders are pinned exactly (that is the surface CL's rule was written about and the one CK taught the draft card to render) and the whole-corpus count is pinned as a ceiling. A new authored digit trips either way, and the fourteen are recorded as owed rather than silently rewritten — rewriting shipped player-facing text is authoring, and this is a test batch.

THE PERFECT BICONDITIONAL DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE CONVERSE SHOULD NOT. CN's enforceable direction — runs no check ⇒ carries no Perfect — holds at ZERO violations over the whole corpus. The converse fails for five abilities (Called Shot, Coup de Grâce, Pinning Shot, Powershot, Rampage), and their bars are not idle: the grade still multiplies damage. Git settles it — all five have carried an empty perfect_text since long before CN, so this is an authoring pattern rather than a regression CN left behind. All five are named in the suite so a sixth trips and has to be a decision.

CK's MISSING MEASUREMENT, PRODUCED. The computed block against the 258px draft card (DRAFT_COL_W 296 less 38), measured with real font metrics at the label's own font size: 195 abilities carry a block, 725 lines, mean 3.72 lines a card — the brief's “five added lines” is 3.72 — and 8 lines (1.1%) exceed the card width, worst +94px (Feint's Perfect), the rest between +7 and +25px. So the block's cost is its line count, which CK already measured as the column going 313-389px to 557-671px against a 388px viewport; it is not a wrapping problem. Shipped as check_ck_width.gd.

Also asserted: the Ironclad rename is complete — Ironclad resolves to the ability, Iron Will resolves to no ability, the wd_iron_will node still carries the name Iron Will, and master.html carries both rows — and the draft card renders the computed block through the same Classes.computed_block builder the hero sheet uses.
