§5 — THE PUSH CHECK

Reported at the start of the batch and again at the end. Local HEAD and git ls-remote origin main agreed on e3fb49a before any work began — so the missing-credential-helper backlog that stranded four batches is genuinely closed — and the check is reported again below against this batch's own commit.

2026-08-18 — Batch CO: A RECAST THAT WOULD DO NOTHING IS REFUSED

add_status resolves a re-application as max() on duration and power. For any status whose power is a snapshot of live state, a recast could therefore cost full resource, a full cooldown and the whole turn and return nothing — the weaker new value discarded by the max, and the player never told. 58 abilities now refuse that cast at the button, and say why. Save version did not move (still v10).

§0 — THE SCOPE LIMIT, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE RULE

Refusal is only correct when the status application is the ability’s ENTIRE payload. An ability that also deals damage, heals, or converts a resource must still cast when its buff would not improve: that half is worth the turn on its own, and refusing it would be a worse bug than the one being fixed.

The set was derived by walking _resolve_special’s call graph, the way Batch CN derived its skill-check tables — not by reading the damage and pressure fields, which are zero on Feint, Guard Change and Kill Command and every other card that hits hard from inside a handler. 211 abilities → 134 with no field-level payload → 58 whose whole payload is the status.

Four of the five cards that motivated the batch are deliberately NOT in it, and each exclusion is the scope limit working:

  • Funeral Pyre pays _overburn_refund — the Burn it eats comes back as Mana, so the conversion is a real payload even when the barrier does not grow.
  • Stabilize vents Resonance into Mana and heals 5% of maximum health.
  • Battle Shout hands the caster +5 Rage.
  • Reckless Abandon spends the whole Rage bar (Batch CM already gates it below one step).
  • Blessing of Zeal ticks cooldowns through Crusader’s Tempo.

Of the named cards only Magic Barrier and Vespers qualify.

Four cards are excluded for a second reason worth recording: their status power is an OWNER INDEX, not a magnitude. Mark of the Hunt, Snare Line, Eye of the Storm and Vendetta store heroes.find(attacker) there, so a numeric “new ≤ held” test would have refused casts on the basis of a hero’s slot number.

§1 — THE REFUSAL

It lives at _ability_usable, the door the stance gates use, so the greyed button, the bot’s available pool and the cast itself read one decision — the rule Batch CI set for Formless. It is the last gate in that function on purpose: every gate above answers “can this be cast at all”, and asking the cheap question first keeps the walk off the hot path.

The test is exact and computed at cast time. A cast is refused only when every unit it could touch already holds everything it would hand out, at no less duration and no less power. The powers are recomputed live — Vespers off the Cleric’s current maximum health, Magic Barrier off the Mage’s, Divine Shield off the Devout’s — because refusing a cast that would in fact have improved something is strictly worse than the bug being fixed. Two further exactnesses the arithmetic needed: Fleeting is normalised (the target’s own mod_status_turns is applied before the comparison, as add_status applies it), and a negative turn count reads as permanence rather than as a duration, so a battle-long status can never be “lengthened”.

Picked-target cards are judged against the whole pool the picker offers, so a button never darkens while a second enemy still stands clean.

§2 — BM’S DIVINE SHIELD FIX, RECONCILED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

_grant_divine_shield’s bespoke path is Layered Faith, and reading it showed it is not a refusal at all: it pre-adds the standing pool so the max lands on the sum — it makes the recast additive. The general rule does not subsume it. Under Layered Faith a recast always improves and so is never refused; the two compose. Per §2 it stays, and the gate reads Layered Faith when it computes the power so the general rule cannot contradict the one build that had already fixed this.

The riders are part of the test. barrier is a SHARED status and _grant_divine_shield stamps divine, Blessed Barrier, Afterglow, Warded Robes and Unyielding onto it (Mantle adds its hops). A Devout casting over a Mage’s larger Magic Barrier improves it even though neither duration nor power moves — it becomes divine, which is what feeds Faith — so a duration-and-power-only test would have refused a genuinely improving cast.

A second bespoke instance was found and IS subsumed: Batch BV’s _ability_usable already refused a second Bloodbond while the first still stood. The guard is battle-long and carries a fixed share, so the general rule refuses it in exactly the same cases — the bespoke gate and its tooltip string are deleted rather than left unreachable beside it. What BV’s comment established stays true: the card is still not gated on a beast being out.

§3 — THE TELL

A greyed button with no reason is a bug from the player’s side, so the refusal names what is already standing. It is rendered inside _ability_tooltip — the one site every surface reads (the ability popup, the basic-attack button, the draft card) — rather than added to the per-card chain, which is §4’s point arriving in code. This is the whole benefit of refusing rather than silently replacing: the waste was invisible before and is information now.

§4 — ONE RULE, NOT EIGHTY-ONE STRINGS

Batch CL left 81 of 108 timed descriptions saying nothing about a second cast. No ability description was touched. With refusal the answer is uniform and systemic, so it is stated once in the glossary (recast_refused, “Recasting a Standing Effect”) and carried in the moment by §3’s tell. The glossary entry states the scope limit too, because the exception is the part a player would otherwise have to infer.

THE GATE

check_co.gd does not read the table against another table: it spawns two real battles, casts all 58 through _resolve_special onto every unit each can reach, and asserts the prediction against what actually landed. 57 of 58 refuse after saturation; Interpose is named as the one member that can never refuse, because its charges are additive and a second cast always improves. Two parties are needed and that is not optional — Alms and Divine Presence write nothing without Mercy, Mantle nothing without a living Devout — so a one-party sweep would report them as untested and read as coverage. The excluded cards are asserted out of the set by name.

Both gates were negative-controlled before being believed (Batch CN’s rule: a gate that can only pass is a gap). Gating stabilize fails the scope assertion; drifting one duration in the table (Quick Draw 6→9) fails the live assertion; a deliberate syntax error puts two Parse Error lines on Godot’s stderr where a clean tree puts zero.

KNOWN AND RECORDED, NOT FIXED

On three cards the bug is worse than described, and this batch cannot reach them. Battle Shout, Stabilize and Eye of the Storm call update_status with a computed power after _apply_status, and update_status ASSIGNS power where add_status maxes it. On those three a weaker recast does not merely fail to improve — it overwrites the standing buff downward. All three carry a second payload, so §0 puts them outside the refusal; widening the scope to catch them would delete a resource conversion the player wanted. Recorded here rather than half-fixed.

2026-08-18 — Batch CN: THE SKILL CHECK BECOMES PARAMETERIC, AND LOSES ITS FILLER

Two halves. §1 gives the bar parameters it has never had. §2 removes the check from everything it was doing nothing on, folding the orphaned Perfect bonuses into base effects. Nothing about a remaining check changes — same sweep, same 0.72s, same 0.045 and 0.16, same grades, same multipliers. The default profile reproduces today's bar exactly, and check_cn.gd asserts that against the pre-CN formulas rather than asking to be believed. Save version did not move (still v10).

§1 — THE PROFILE

PERFECT_HALF (0.045), GOOD_HALF (0.16) and the 0.72s sweep were bare constants read at two places: _grade_skill_check(), which takes no arguments, and a ColorRect built once during UI setup. That is why up_sure was never written — the window was not a parameter, so an upgrade meant to widen it had nothing to widen.

They are a profile now, handed to the check per cast: perfect_half, good_half, centre (where the Perfect window sits), sweep_time, and presses (how many windows must be landed). SC_PROFILE_DEFAULT is today's numbers and every caller uses it. Nothing overrides it in this batch; the content that will is CO onward.

The zone rects are resized PER CAST (_apply_sc_profile) instead of built once, and grading and drawing come off the same dictionary on the same line of execution. Split them and a profile that changes the window grades one thing and draws another — the worst failure available here, because the player would be aiming at a lie.

_grade_skill_check() still takes no arguments. The profile is a member, so Batch CM's rule is kept exactly: the grader is reached from a mouse button and a key press, it cannot know which ability is being cast, and it does not learn. centre and presses are wired and unused — nothing moves the window off 0.5 or asks for a second press. Multi-press returns the worst grade of the set. The grades, the multipliers and _apply_perfect_bonus were not touched.

§2 — WHERE THE CHECK COMES OFF: 113 OF 211 ABILITIES

The criterion is mechanical: remove the check wherever the grade multiplier has nothing to multiply. A pure buff has no damage and no Break damage, so ×1.15 and ×0.6 both resolve to nothing and the bar's only live effect is the Perfect bonus — consequence-free upside charged as an attention tax on a turn that was never in doubt.

THE FIELDS ALONE ARE NOT THE CRITERION, AND FINDING THAT OUT WAS MOST OF WHAT §2 COST. A first pass over damage == 0 and pressure == 0 caught 137 abilities — including Feint, Guard Change, Kill Command, Savage Sweep, Precision Strike, Harvest, Primal Surge and Call the Wilds, every one of which hits hard from inside a special handler. A field-only test would have stripped the bar off all of them, which is the exact opposite of what the criterion says. The criterion is applied to what the ability actually resolves, derived by walking _resolve_special's call graph to its damage and healing leaves.

Only the base effect counts. A handler whose only damage sits inside its if is_perfect branch is caught — that branch is the orphaned bonus, not a reason to keep grading. BEWITCH is the whole of that case: its strike was Perfect-only, so it lost its bar and the strike became what Bewitch always does.

The four overrides. HEALS KEEP THEIR CHECK — a heal's magnitude is multiplied by the grade — and that list is authored rather than derived, because “is this a heal” is a question about the card: Renewal heals through a status, so nothing heals at cast time and a purely mechanical read would have taken its bar away while Heal beside it kept one. SHIELDS LOSE THEIRS whether or not the absorb scaled with the grade. PURE DEBUFF APPLIERS LOSE THEIRS — the grade has never affected whether a status lands. BREAK DAMAGE COUNTS AS SOMETHING TO MULTIPLY, so an ability with BD and no HP damage keeps its bar: Breaking Darkness at 20 BD was the case checked against, and it keeps its bar on its fields alone.

ONE OVERRIDE THE BRIEF DID NOT ASK FOR, AND IT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN BURIED: a GATED ability always keeps its check. Batch CM's Reckless Abandon spends the whole Rage bar for a three-turn multiplier and has no damage and no Break damage, so the criterion catches it cleanly — and obeying the criterion there would have deleted a CM feature in silence. An ability whose Sloppy loses the cast cannot lose the check that produces the Sloppy. The other four of the gated five keep their bars on the criterion's own terms.

BASIC ATTACKS RESOLVE AT A FIXED GOOD, EXCEPT THE SHARPSHOOTER'S. That exception is read off slot 0 and the hero's passive, not off an ability name: his basic IS Quick Shot, the same object the Beastmaster and the Mystic carry, so there was no card to flag.

THE NO-CHECK TEST SITS ABOVE THE AUTOPLAY ROLL, AND THAT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. The bot rolls a 20% Perfect; left on top, it would still roll Perfects nobody can press for, every §3 fold would be paid TWICE in a sim, and the balance numbers would stop describing the game the player is playing.

The 113 that lost their bar: Aegis Reversal, Aegis Wall, Alms, Anointing, Answering Steel, Anvil, Arcane Arrows, Arcane Surge, Ashes of Al'ar, Battle Poise, Battle Shout, Battle Trance, Berserk, Bewitch, Blessing of Zeal, Blight the Well, Blink, Blood Offering, Blood Price, Bloodbond, Bola, Bulwark of Fortitude, Camouflage, Choking Smoke, Consecrated Ground, Consecration, Covenant of Ash, Covering Guard, Deadfall, Deep Winter, Discipline, Dispel, Divine Presence, Divine Shield, Divine Wrath, Downwind, Elevation, Ember Debt, Emberkeep, Exhortation, Eye of the Storm, Fault Line, Feigned Guard, Firedraw, Flash Freeze, Formless, Frostbind, Funeral Pyre, Ghostpack, Hoarfrost Armor, Hold the Line, Hunter's Mark, Immolate, Inner Arcane, Interpose, Ironclad, Last Howl, Magic Barrier, Mana Shield, Mana Well, Mantle, Mark of the Hunt, Mass Hysteria, Mirror Image, Null Field, Ordination, Overcharge, Penance, Phoenix Rebirth, Preparation, Quarry's Mark, Quick Draw, Rally, Rallying Shout, Reacquire, Recant, Recompense, Resonant Field, Resurrection, Retaliation, Rime, Rimebinding, Rite of Return, Sacred Resolve, Shared Grief, Shieldwall, Slow Burn, Snare Line, Snare Trap, Spite, Stabilize, Stalking Horse, Succession, Threshold, Transference, Tripwire, Turn the Blade, Umbral Sigil, Unburden, Undying Vigil, Unslaked, Vendetta, Vespers, Vow of Suffering, Warcry.

§3 — THE ORPHANED PERFECT BONUSES FOLDED INTO THE BASE EFFECT

105 abilities carried a perfect_text nothing could now trigger, and every one of those bonuses became part of what the ability always does — the ability is slightly stronger and nothing is lost. Anvil, Recompense, Turn the Blade, Formless and their neighbours hold four turns instead of three; Divine Shield absorbs 35% instead of 30%; Berserk banks four doubled strikes instead of three; Interpose now covers the Warden too; Mass Hysteria's cooldown is 3 and Mana Shield's initiative cost is 1.5 unconditionally — those two were the only orphans living outside _resolve_special.

Every perfect_text and perfect_id on those 105 was CLEARED, and their descriptions were rewritten to carry the folded value. Batch CK taught the draft card to render Perfect, so an orphan would now be visible on the screen where cards are compared, advertising a bonus that can never fire. check_cn.gd gates it over the whole corpus, and re-checks every rewritten description against the measured 44-character card ceiling.

_apply_perfect_bonus LOST NO BRANCHES and was not touched. The brief expected it to; it did not, because every perfect_id the criterion caught (rage5, on Battle Shout) is also carried by an ability that keeps its bar. Four of its branches — mana15, focus, sunder, burn — are authored by no ability anywhere and were already unreachable before this batch. Left in place: §1 says not to touch that function, and deleting pre-existing dead code is a separate decision. Recorded here so it is a decision rather than an oversight.

§4 — TWO CONSEQUENCES RECORDED, NEITHER COMPENSATED FOR

Break generation falls slightly. A Perfect basic was ×1.25 Break damage and basics now resolve at Good. The Warden leans on Break, and CI's Turn the Blade leans on it further. Not compensated for here.

Battles get quieter, which is the point. CM added a defensive bar on every attack the Warden takes; this removes the bar from filler turns, so the attention budget moves toward the presses that decide something. Whether the net is better is a playtest question, and the two batches should be felt together rather than separately.

§5 — THE RULE EVERY FUTURE PROFILE IS AUTHORED TO

Recorded in CLAUDE.md before CO writes twelve of them:

VARY THE CHARACTER, HOLD THE DIFFICULTY CONSTANT. A profile expresses a spec's identity, not its difficulty. The Perfect window is authored as a fraction of sweep time, not as a fixed width — so a fast, narrow bar and a slow, wide one are exactly as hard to land while feeling nothing alike. A spec whose bar is genuinely harder is a spec a player can lose access to through no fault of their build, which is the failure mode that sank timed hits in Legend of Dragoon and Mother 3.

Two deliberate exceptions, both opt-in: the Sharpshooter, whose bar is meant to be harder and to pay more, and the relic that swaps a hero's bar for a riskier one while held.

2026-08-17 — Batch CM: GATED SKILL CHECKS, AND THE DEFENSIVE CHECK

Two additions to the skill check. The existing bar is unchanged — same sweep, same 0.72s, same PERFECT_HALF 0.045 and GOOD_HALF 0.16, same grades, same multipliers, same 190 Perfect bonuses. Nothing about a normal cast moves, and the two constants were not touched: variable window widths are a different feature (up_sure, still parked) and mixing them in here would have put the constants in play for no gain. No magnitude moved elsewhere and the save version did not move (still v10).

§0 — THE ONE RULE BOTH HALVES DEPEND ON, AND IT WAS ALREADY TRUE

NOTHING IS CONSUMED UNTIL AFTER THE GRADE. The Cancel button already returns to the action bar “with nothing spent” even after a target was chosen, so consumption has always happened downstream of the grade. Both features are built on that, and neither needs a refund path: a gated failure is the existing cancel path with the turn spent instead of returned.

THAT IS WHAT MAKES THREE OF THE FIVE EXPRESSIBLE AT ALL. Requiem eats Ruin stacks off the enemy, Unleash eats the companion's Loyalty meter, and Boil Over drops the Berserker's live Frenzy bonus to the floor. “Refund the resource” would have been undefined for all three. Nothing is taken, so nothing needs giving back.

_grade_skill_check() STILL TAKES NO ARGUMENTS AND STILL CANNOT SEE THE ABILITY. The caller knows, so the flag is tested at the call site in _hero_turn against a grade produced identically for a gated cast and an ordinary one. The one new argument on _run_skill_check is a mode string naming what is being graded — it picks the bar's top line, its tint and which orientation card is owed, and it changes nothing about the sweep or the grading.

§1 — GATED ABILITIES: A SLOPPY LOSES THE CAST

Ability.gated is a new per-ability flag. On a Sloppy grade the ability does not resolve: no damage, no status, no consumption, nothing. Good and Perfect both resolve normally — the gate is missing GOOD_HALF 0.16, not missing the ±0.045 Perfect window; gating on Perfect would fail most casts.

AbilitySpecWhat it spends
Death RayArcanistalready gated at 8 Resonance — now two gates
RequiemOccultistevery stack of Ruin on the target
Reckless AbandonBerserkerall Rage
Boil OverBerserkerthe live Frenzy bonus down to the floor
UnleashBeastmasterthe companion's entire Loyalty meter

A GATED FAILURE COSTS THE TURN AND NOTHING ELSE. Resource unspent, cooldown not started, consumed meters untouched. _resolve is where every one of those is taken, so refusing to enter it is the whole implementation; the only thing the new _gated_failure does is book the loss, say so, and pay the initiative — next_time += ab.delay * 100 / effective_speed(), read off the ability exactly as _resolve's own scheduling line reads it. The punishment is tempo on a timeline where everything else keeps moving, which on a 6.0-delay ability is already severe.

THE TURN GOES ON ENDING NORMALLY. The end-of-turn nodes below the call — Practised Hands, Entropy's Toll, Pleasure from Pain, Divine Presence, Preparation's tick — all still run, because the turn did end. Skipping them would have stranded a pending extra turn and made the gate cost more than the turn it is supposed to cost.

NO HEALING OR REVIVAL ABILITY IS EVER GATED. Resurrection is deliberately excluded and this is a standing rule, not a scoping choice — losing a resurrection to a hand slip is the worst outcome the system could produce. It is recorded in CLAUDE.md, and check_cm.gd asserts it over the whole 211-ability corpus rather than over the five, so a later batch that gates a sixth cannot gate a heal by accident.

§1a — THE TELL, IN FOUR PLACES, RENDERED FROM THE FLAG

The player must know an ability is gated BEFORE committing to it. A cast silently lost to a grade nobody knew was lethal is a bug that reads as jank. It is on the ability button (a “⚠” prefix; it deliberately does not tint the label, because _mark_upgraded owns the font colour there and two marks fighting over one override is how one of them silently stops existing), in the battle tooltip, on the draft card through CK's computed_block, and on the bar itself while it sweeps — the one surface the player is actually looking at during the press. The Sloppy result line reads “SLOPPY — THE CAST IS LOST” there rather than “Sloppy...”.

ONE STRING, Classes.GATED_TELL, AND IT IS NEVER AUTHORED INTO A DESCRIPTION. That is CL §1's rule applied to a sentence instead of to a number: five cards each carrying their own copy is five places for the gate to outlive itself. No description was rewritten in this batch and none of the five mentions the gate in its own prose.

§2 — THE DEFENSIVE CHECK

A timing bar on incoming attacks, for defensive heroes only. PURE MITIGATION — it can only ever reduce incoming damage, never increase it.

GradeEffect
Perfectincoming damage ×0.85, incoming Break damage ×0.75
Goodnormal
Sloppynormal — identical to Good, never worse

FLAGGED, NOT TUNED: 0.85 / 0.75 mirrors the offensive bar's ×1.15 / ×1.25. Shipped as written. The guarantee is structural rather than a convention: _defensive_brace returns a boolean, not a grade, because there is no third outcome for the strike site to learn about — the only thing a defensive check can tell it is whether the blow lands for less.

Who gets one: the Warden, always — he is the most attacked unit in the game and that is the point of the first pass. The Swordmaster, only while in the Defensive guard; in Aggressive he gets none. Formless counts as both guards, so it grants one, consistent with CI's rule that it satisfies every stance gate. No other spec, no exceptions, and one function decides it (_has_defensive_check) so the bar, the mitigation, the bot's roll and the sim's count cannot disagree.

IT READS u.stance DIRECTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT THROUGH _stance_satisfies, AND THE REASON IS FEIGNED GUARD RATHER THAN FORMLESS. That helper answers “does this unit count as standing in guard X” for an ability gate, and Feigned Guard's scope is abilities and nothing else — Seasoned Fighter, Killing Edge, Bracing and Untouchable, every defensive property the Swordmaster has, all read the guard he is actually holding. A defensive check is one of those, not an ability, so a Feigned Guard does not conjure one. Formless is named explicitly, for the same reason _stance_satisfies names it: a single stance string cannot express “both”.

ONCE PER INCOMING ATTACK, NOT PER STRIKE. The bar runs at the top of _resolve, above everything, because “once per attack” is a statement about that function call — the strike loop below it runs once for a single blow and six times for a doubled three-strike, and a bar inside it would ask for six presses on one enemy action. The result is an ordinary local, so the recursive calls _resolve makes for counters and echoes each get their own: a nested attack can never inherit a brace pressed against a different blow. NO CANCEL BUTTON — cancellable is left at its default false rather than passed, because a hero cannot decline to be attacked.

IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE BLOCK OR PARRY ROLLS, exactly as the offensive bar does not touch miss, parry or crit. The damage half is applied to raw among the defender's own terms, below Vendetta and Seasoned Fighter — those rolls resolved hundreds of lines above and have already written themselves into that number, so the brace multiplies what lands. The Break half is applied last of everything that moves pr, and it is booked through _prev_bd so it appears in the Break-prevented ledger: BF §1's rule is that every line which lowers Break says so, and a defence that measures zero is a defence nobody can tune.

A LANDED BRACE WRITES ONE COMBAT-LOG LINE, AND IT IS WRITTEN ONCE PER ATTACK rather than at the two arithmetic sites — those sit inside the strike loop, where a doubled three-strike would print the same brace six times. Silent mitigation is mitigation nobody can audit; every other reduction in this file says its name.

TWO NARROWINGS, REPORTED BECAUSE §2 SAYS “EVERY QUALIFYING INCOMING ATTACK”. (1) COUNTERS DO NOT RAISE A BAR. A counter is a free swing drawn by the hero's own action rather than a declared incoming attack, and the offensive bar does not run for one either — every counter call site passes a hardcoded “good”. Excluding them keeps the two bars symmetrical and keeps a retaliation chain from asking for presses nobody chose to be in. (2) AN ATTACK CARRYING A special DOES NOT RAISE ONE, because it never reaches the ordinary strike loop, which is the only place the mitigation is applied; a bar there would pause the fight and then reduce nothing. Exactly one enemy attack in the roster is skipped by that clause today: the Bloodcaller's BLOOD TRIBUTE. The Hurler's SIEGE STONE is not skipped — its windup hoists the blow and deals nothing, and the landing comes back through a turn later as a plain attack copy with no special at all, which is exactly when the brace should be offered.

THE PACING NUMBER, WHICH §2 SAYS IS THE VERDICT. Measured over 60 headless battles per party, rung 1. With warden / arcanist / inquisitor / beastmaster: 9.4 defensive checks per battle against 27.3 hero actions. With warden / arcanist / occultist / beastmaster: 6.9 against 22.8. Either way the party's total presses rise by about a third — but that framing understates it, because the presses do not land on the party. THE WARDEN ACTS ABOUT SEVEN TIMES A BATTLE AND BRACES SEVEN TO NINE, SO THE FEATURE ROUGHLY DOUBLES THE PRESSES THAT BELONG TO HIM, which is exactly what the brief predicted, landing on the hero rather than on the party. Perfect braces came in at 18–21% (the bot's 20%), refusing 4–6 Break points a battle. A Swordmaster party measured 0.4 checks a battle, which is the stance gate working: he opens every battle Aggressive and the bot rarely Guard Changes. Uncapped for this first pass; a cap is a retreat available afterwards rather than a limit to guess at now, and it is a designer's call on a number that now exists.

The sim report prints Defensive checks/battle and Gated casts lost/battle, both of them only when there was one — a zero on a party with no Warden and no gated card reads as a broken instrument rather than as a line (Batch AW §0's rule).

§3 — THE SIM BOT ROLLS A DEFENSIVE GRADE, AND HONOURS THE GATE

The bot never runs the bar; it rolls grades off hardcoded probabilities. Without a defensive roll the Warden would be untestable in sims and every incoming hit would silently resolve as if the bar had not existed. It now rolls one on the same footing: 20% Perfect, otherwise no mitigation. Sloppy and Good are identical here, so the bot's own 15% Sloppy rate is irrelevant to the outcome and is deliberately not rolled.

THE BOT'S OWN 20/15 ROLL IS UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The gate reads the grade that roll already produces, at the same call site a player's grade arrives through, so a bot Sloppy on one of the five loses the same cast a player's does — otherwise the bot would play a strictly easier game than the player on exactly the five most decisive abilities. Observed live: 0.05–0.12 Death Rays lost per battle in the sims above.

§4 — ORIENTATION

A second one-time card, on the existing skill_check_taught pattern and with its own flag (defensive_check_taught), at the first defensive check. A bar appearing on an enemy's turn is unlike anything else in the game and will read as a bug otherwise. Kept to what the existing card does: what the bar is, what the grades are worth, and that it can only help. The two are mutually exclusive per bar — whichever kind the player meets first teaches itself and the other still waits for its own first time. The gated abilities need no card; §1a's tell carries them, and all four of its surfaces are read before committing, which is the whole requirement.

§5 — VERIFICATION, AND WHAT THIS BATCH DID NOT DO

check_parse.gd clean; check_cm.gd is new and asserts the four invariants §1 promises over the whole corpus (the five names are the gated set and nothing else is; no gated ability heals or revives; the tell reaches the draft card on exactly the gated cards; the tell holds the standard's measured 44-character ceiling). 220 headless battles across four parties threw zero errors and zero warnings, a 12-run progression sim likewise, and a live non-sim autoplay battle with a Warden ran to victory clean.

check_cm_live.gd IS ALSO NEW, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE SIMS CANNOT REACH THE BAR. Every headless battle takes _defensive_brace's bot branch, so the one thing a player actually touches was exercised nowhere. It spawns a real non-autoplay battle, drives an enemy attack into a Warden and presses the bar by hand. It confirms the bar appears, that its top line names the incoming blow, that there is no Cancel button, and that no bar appears when the same blow is aimed at another hero. Measured over 40 paired samples with the rolls neutralised: damage ×0.840 (against 0.85), Break ×0.750 (exact), and — the promise that matters — Sloppy 944 against Good 943, the same blow, driven rather than asserted.

ONE HARNESS FAULT WORTH RECORDING, BECAUSE IT WILL BITE THE NEXT WARDEN TEST. The first run of that gate reported the brace taking more damage than no brace. The code was right; the harness was not. block_chance = 0.0 is the usual way these suites turn the block roll off, and on a Warden it does nothing — _live_block_chance adds _plating_slice (0.15 plus Heavy Plating's climb) on top of the field, so he was still blocking one hit in six, and a block throws the whole climb away, which makes two consecutive blocks of samples path-dependent rather than comparable. The fix is a large NEGATIVE field (the sum is clamped to [0,1]) and interleaving the two conditions instead of running them in blocks.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS THE DEFAULT PARTY. Berserker / Cryomancer / Inquisitor / Beastmaster holds neither a Warden nor a Defensive Swordmaster nor any of the five, and its 60-battle report prints neither new line — no defensive checks, no gated losses. A fight nobody in this batch touches is the same fight it was.

THE THREE HARDCODED master.html STAMP GATES WERE RE-POINTED IN PLACE — test_batch_ah, bn and bb, all three of which were already failing before this batch (they still named Batch CI while the document said CK). The other five stamp checks read the line dynamically and needed nothing. The duplication CLAUDE.md keeps predicting has now cost a repair rather than a bump, which is the case for the honest fix it names.

2026-08-17 — Batch CL: LIVE VALUES, AND THE PROSE PASS

Two halves. §1 is a render change — a percentage is followed by its computed value in parentheses, everywhere a value can be resolved. §2–§8 are the prose rewrite, scoped by text-audit.html and governed by text-standard.html. Nothing the game DOES changed: no magnitude moved, no ability changed, the save version did not move. Every edit changed what the game says.

THIS ENTRY WAS WRITTEN AT BATCH CN, THREE BATCHES LATE, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO RECORD. CL shipped its code and its two documentation surfaces (text-standard.html, master.html) and never wrote a changelog entry, a CLAUDE.md note or a design note. CM and CN were then built on top of it, so three batches sat uncommitted at once and this entry is reconstructed from the brief, the diff and the two check scripts CL left behind. The standing rule that produced the mess is now explicit: commit each batch before starting the next.

§1 — THE RENDER RULE

A percentage is followed by its computed value in parentheses: 20% of maximum health (34). The parenthetical is computed at render time and never authored into a string (Classes.resolve_values) — typing a digit into a description would have created two hundred new places for a value to drift out of sync with the code, which is the exact failure text-audit.html exists to catch, reintroduced at scale. A literal digit inside parentheses in any authored field is a defect.

This SUPERSEDES the two-tier arithmetic split that stood in text-standard.html §1. The tiers existed because mid-combat surfaces could not show arithmetic; with the value resolved on the line the player is never asked to compute anything and the formula stays visible, so scaling stays legible. §1 of the standard was REWRITTEN rather than appended to. The CLAUDE.md copy of the old rule was missed at CL and is corrected at CN — it survived its own deletion for three batches, which is precisely the failure the rewrite-don't-append instruction was guarding against.

Four resolution cases: a percentage that is already final resolves to the resulting TOTAL on chips only (+25% Block chance (→ 35%)); volatile stats resolve live and are allowed to move between reads and are deliberately not frozen or snapshotted; where there is nothing to resolve against the percentage stands alone with no placeholder and no dash; and resolution follows the owner the prose names.

§1's OWED REPORT — THE OVERFLOW COUNT

§1 warned that a parenthetical adds five to seven characters to lines already hand-wrapped to the measured 44-character ceiling, and told the batch to ship, measure, then fix only what overflowed. Measured over the whole corpus with tokens expanded against all four class bases (check_cl_width.gd, re-run at CN against a reconstruction of the corpus as CL shipped it):

  • 3,864 rendered description lines — ZERO over the ceiling.
  • Lines pushed over by the parenthetical alone: ZERO. This is the number §1 asked for, and the answer is that the parenthetical cost nothing. No rewrap was needed and none was done.
  • The widest rendered line in the corpus is 67 characters — Feint's perfect_text, "Perfect: Defensive banks a third charge; Aggressive strikes for 45%".
  • 76 of 788 rendered perfect_text lines are over 44 characters, and all 76 pre-date CL (19 distinct ability lines, measured across four class bases). The measurement corrected an assumption while it was at it: the "936 of 936 lines hold the ceiling" result is about description ONLY, and perfect_text has never been held to this ceiling. That is not the defect it looks like — the draft card's computed block autowraps, so the ceiling does not bind there, and the only surface that renders perfect_text unwrapped is the battle tooltip, which grows to fit rather than clipping. Recorded as measured, not filed as owed.

The report itself was not missing — it was filed in the wrong place. CL wrote it into text-standard.html §4.8 rather than into a changelog entry that did not exist, where nobody looking for a batch report would find it.

§5's OWED REPORT — WHERE RECAST IS GENUINELY UNDEFINED

§5 asked for recast behaviour to be stated on 53 silent abilities, for the code to be read per ability rather than inferred from neighbours, and for anything genuinely undefined rather than undocumented to be reported instead of invented. The prose half was not completed — 81 of 108 descriptions that grant a timed effect still say nothing about a second cast. The report is below and it is the more useful half, because the undefined cases turn out to share one root.

THE DEFAULT IS A STORAGE RULE, NOT A DESIGN ANSWER. BattleUnit.add_status resolves a reapplied status as turns = max(old, new) and power = max(old, new). For a status whose power is a CONSTANT that is a perfectly good answer — "refreshes, never shortens". For a status whose power is a SNAPSHOT of live state, it means a recast at a weaker moment silently does nothing while the cost is paid in full. Nothing on the card says so, and nothing at the call site says so.

  • Stabilize — the damage reduction is 10% per Resonance stack consumed. The handler sets Resonance to the floor unconditionally, so a recast on fewer stacks spends the Resonance and then has its weaker mitigation discarded by the max(). The player pays and receives nothing.
  • Funeral Pyre — the shield is worth 200% of the Burn it consumes. Recast on a smaller fire, it consumes that Burn and keeps the older, larger barrier. Same shape as Stabilize.
  • Battle Shout — the bonus is base plus 1% per 20 of the enemy party's Bleed buildup at the time of the shout. A second shout after a bleedout has cleared that buildup refreshes the DURATION but keeps the OLD magnitude. That is neither refresh nor replace, and the chip's own wording ("at the time of the shout") describes one cast, not two.
  • Vespers and Magic Barrier — power derived from the caster's maximum health, which moves in this game (the Devout grows; Fortified Spirit lends and later sheds max HP). Same mechanism, smaller blast radius.
  • Every ability that writes the shared barrier status — Magic Barrier, Funeral Pyre, Divine Shield and the Aguila's arrival barrier all land in ONE status slot, so a smaller shield cast over a larger one is silently absorbed by the max().

THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE THAT THE DEFAULT WAS NEVER A DECISION IS THAT THE PROJECT ALREADY OVERRODE IT ONCE. Batch BM's Layered Faith comment in _grant_divine_shield says it outright: "add_status MAXES a re-applied barrier's power, so seven rows of investment have always been capped at one cast's worth" — and BM fixed it by pre-adding the standing pool, for Divine Shield only, and only while the Layered Faith talent is held. The same trap at every other site is untouched. Reported, not fixed: whether a snapshot-powered status should refresh, replace, add or refuse is a design question per ability, and inventing one answer across five of them is exactly what §5 forbade.

§2–§8 — THE PROSE PASS

§2 PERSON: pronouns stripped from the ability corpus — "Loses 20% of current health", never "you lose" or "he loses".

§3 perfect_text: the bare changed value, nothing else. The 107 "instead of" comparisons went — the base is on the line above, so "60 Rage instead of 40" repeats it. CK made this urgent rather than cosmetic by teaching the draft card to render Perfect: all 190 strings became visible on the screen where cards are compared. (Batch CN has since cleared 105 of them outright, because the abilities that carried them no longer run a skill check.)

§4 DURATION VS COOLDOWN: a bare "N turns" now reads "for 3 turns" when it is a duration, and descriptions do not state cooldowns at all — the renderer prints its own Cooldown: N turns line, so a description restating it is a second copy that can disagree.

§6 THE STATUS CHIPS: the 41 rows where master.html stated a number the chip omitted — almost always the duration or the source — filled in with §1's resolution applied. Shieldwall's "bonus Block chance" and Elemental Weakness's "resistances reduced" now state and resolve their numbers. Ruin and Ironclad differed in both directions and got both halves.

§7 passive_desc: twelve blocks, rendering in an autowrapping 400px label whose budget is 61 characters, with 23 of 67 authored lines running to 71. Its authored \n breaks come OUT — unlike ability descriptions, whose breaks stay until a custom tooltip exists. The Arcanist's was the exhibit: a triangular-number formula in algebra on the hero sheet, worked through two examples. The stack count is known at display time, so §1 resolves it and the algebra is gone. One code inconsistency fixed in passing: spec_choice_screen.gd flattened \n for ability descriptions and not for passive_desc on the very next line, so the passive block hard-wrapped inside a 298px column on that screen.

§8 RATIONALE AND THE DOCUMENT: rationale clauses cut; flavor kept only where it is removable without breaking the sentence. Aimed Shot needed a description from nothing — it read, in full, "A perfect line. Patient, precise, final." for an ability that deals 45 damage and grants +20 Focus on a Perfect. The corpus was calibrated against the code's own strings, not the document's: not one of master.html's 120 rows carried the code's sentence, all were independent paraphrases running a median 3× longer, and a pass calibrated against the document's verbosity would have over-corrected cards that were already most of the way to the target. The document rows were then corrected toward the finished code strings — both copies, or neither.

2026-08-17 — Batch CK: THE DRAFT CARD, THE IRONCLAD RENAME, AND THE SECOND AUDIT PASS

Three code changes and one read-only audit. No description was rewritten — that is CL's job, scoped by CJ's report and now by this batch's. No magnitude moved and the save version did not move (still v10). CJ's two bucket-1 items are both CLOSED here, and so is its largest bucket-2 item. Under the Batch CG convention this is a content batch and ships no new test suite; five existing suites were RE-POINTED IN PLACE, four of them for a fault this batch did not cause.

§1 — THE DRAFT CARD GETS THE COMPUTED BLOCK, AND IT IS ONE BUILDER FOR TWO SCREENS

The draft card rendered ab.description and nothing else — no computed damage, no Break damage, no cost, no cooldown, no initiative and no Perfect — on the one screen whose whole purpose is comparing cards. It now renders all of them, under the description, in a second label and a cooler tint so authored prose and computed figures read as different kinds of writing.

WHAT THIS FIXES. 30 of the 66 damaging abilities never state their damage in prose, because every other surface computes it. Ice Lance was the sharpest case: damage: 35 in the dict against a card reading only "+5% of Attack per Chilled stack", so it drafted as a per-stack ability. Aimed Shot's card was, in full, "A perfect line. Patient, precise, final." — damage: 45, perfect_text: "+20 Focus", a blank card for the hardest-hitting entry in the Sharpshooter's pool. And all 190-odd perfect_text strings were invisible while drafting.

THE BRIEF SAID TO REUSE THE BLOCK blacksmith_screen.gd ALREADY BUILDS, AND THAT BLOCK DOES NOT EXIST. The claim came forward from CJ's own report and neither this batch nor CJ had checked it: blacksmith_screen.gd renders Run.upgrade_desc and ab.description and no computed values at all. The only two computed blocks in the game were battle._ability_tooltip and an inline one in party_screen. So the shared builder had to be WRITTEN rather than reused — Classes.computed_block — and BOTH the draft card and the hero sheet were pointed at it, which is what keeps the copy count at two instead of taking it to three. That was the whole point of the instruction, and it is honoured; the premise behind it was simply wrong.

THE THIRD COPY IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE AND THE REASON IS RECORDED. battle._ability_tooltip reads a live BattleUnit: Surge, Empower and the Resonance curve multiply its damage and it prints "(ready in N)" off that unit's cooldown clock. It is a mid-combat tooltip with live state in it rather than a static card, and folding it in would move numbers inside a fight.

THE CARD SHOWS THE SCALING PERCENTAGE, NOT A COMPUTED RANGE, AND THAT IS A DECISION WITH A REASON. The map screen has no live Attack to compute a range from. Only party_screen._draw_detail and the battle spawn build a hero's live Attack, each with its own sixty-line prologue (hero config, kit overrides, passive, spec stats, tree, runes, upgrades, node scaling) — and a third copy of THAT on the map screen would be a far worse duplication than the one this section exists to prevent. The shared builder takes an Attack figure and prints the real range when it is given one, so the hero sheet gets the range and the draft card gets the percentage, and when that prologue is extracted the draft card changes by one argument. Recorded as owed in CLAUDE.md. Showing the percentage is not a workaround: the draft screen is one of the two arithmetic-ALLOWED surfaces in the standard, which may show percentages and formulas outright.

THE HERO SHEET GAINED THREE LINES AND LOST NONE. Routing it through the shared builder gives it the cost, cooldown and initiative lines the block carries — every one a number that sheet already had and was not showing. Its "Scaling: N% of Attack" line stays outside the block, because on the draft card the block's own damage line IS the scaling and the card would print it twice.

THE LAYOUT RISK WAS REAL AND IT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER, EXACTLY AS THE BRIEF ASKED. Measured in a headless run of the real screen with the real theme font (Open Sans SemiBold), across three sampled draws:

MeasurementBeforeAfter
Column content height, against a 388px scroll viewport 313–389px (three of four columns already at or over it) 557–671px
Added per column—+225 to +282px, 12–14 block lines across three cards
Widest font-11 line against the 258px card— 354px — a perfect_text line ("Answering Steel")

NOTHING IS CLIPPED AND NOTHING WAS SHRUNK. The cards live in a ScrollContainer with horizontal scrolling disabled and autowrap on, so over-tall content scrolls and over-wide lines wrap. The honest cost is that the column now runs about 1.5 viewports where it ran about one, so a player sees roughly two cards at a time instead of three on the screen built for comparing three. The font was not shrunk and the block was not truncated — the brief forbade both, and the column panel itself (540px) did not grow.

A NEW MEASUREMENT, BECAUSE CK IS THE FIRST SURFACE EVER TO RENDER A perfect_text: swept all 193 of them (over 207 resolvable abilities) against the 258px card. 17 are wider than the card and wrap to exactly two rows; none reaches three. CJ's 44-character ceiling holds 936/936 description lines and never bound perfect_text, which carries no authored breaks and autowraps correctly.

CONSEQUENCE RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE: making Perfect visible exposes strings nothing has ever rendered, and 107 of them are in the "60 Rage instead of 40" shape the standard rejects. They were not wrong before; they were invisible. CL cleans them up.

§2 — THE ABILITY "IRON WILL" IS NOW "IRONCLAD" (CJ bucket 1.1, CLOSED)

Two unrelated mechanics wore the chip label Iron Will: the class-wide Warrior ability (immunity to Stun, Freeze, Daze and Broken plus a flat 15% cut) and the Warden talent (−12% damage taken per rank per debuff on him). They do not resemble each other, and master.html §4.6 had a single "Iron Will" row that described the talent — so a reader checking the ability got the other mechanic's answer.

The ability's own status id was already ironclad, so the rename made the card agree with the code and NO NEW WORD ENTERED THE GAME. The talent keeps iron_will and keeps the name Iron Will. Renamed: the CLASS_DRAFT_POOLS["warrior"] entry, the ability def and its display_name, the chip label, IRON_WILL_CUT_PCT → IRONCLAD_CUT_PCT, the float text and both log lines, and master.html.

TWO SITES BEYOND THE BRIEF'S LIST, BOTH DISCLOSED. (1) The ability's special moved too, iron_will → ironclad — an ability named Ironclad dispatching on iron_will would have left the collision alive in the code layer, where a later batch grepping for the talent hits it. Two read sites, both in battle.gd (the _resolve match and the self-target list), and after the change no iron_will string anywhere in the codebase belongs to the ability. (2) The chip tag is Ir, not Ic, because intercession already holds IC and two chips a case-change apart is the same collision in two characters.

master.html §4.6 now carries TWO status rows where it carried one, each naming which of the two it is — and the ability's row had been absent entirely.

berserk/berserk_risk and formless/formless_recoil WERE NOT TOUCHED. Those pairs share a label deliberately: each is the upside and the price of one ability, separated by chip tag and colour. Iron Will was a collision; those are a pattern. A sweep of STATUS_INFO confirms the end state — 159 rows, and the only duplicate labels left are those two pairs.

THE KNOWN FLAKE ON THIS PATH DID NOT FIRE. test_batch_br's "…really cuts the damage" check reproduces roughly 1 pass in 9 and was confirmed at CD. The suite was run four times after the rename: 1447 checks, 0 failures, every time. It was not touched and it is still BR's thread.

The last card-vs-node collision in the game is now KILLING FROST (a Cryomancer card and a Cryomancer node), and it is deliberately left: unlike Iron Will its two halves both make a held enemy colder, and no document describes one under the other's name. The reason is written beside it in classes.gd.

§3 — BATTLE SHOUT'S FALLBACK LOSES ITS NUMBERS (CJ bucket 1.2, CLOSED)

STATUS_INFO["battle_shout"] hardcoded "+8% damage, plus 1% per 20 blood buildup" — right for battle_shout_node 0 and wrong for 1 (12%) and 2 (18%), and it stated no duration while the duration also moves (2/3/4).

THE NUMBERS WERE STRIPPED RATHER THAN CORRECTED, AND THAT IS THE POINT. There is no single number that is right here: changing 8% to 12% would make it wrong for two node states instead of two. The fallback now describes what Battle Shout does and states no magnitude and no duration, so it cannot disagree with any tier and cannot drift when a later batch retunes them, which is the only reason it was worth touching — the cast path calls update_status immediately after _apply_status and overwrites the chip with a live string carrying the real total, base, turns and buildup, so the fallback is probably unreachable in play. master.html was deliberately left alone: its §4.6 row is correct and lists all three tiers.

CJ verified abilities, runes, statuses and the length ceiling and named four populations it could not reach. Same three buckets. Nothing was fixed.

THE CLEAN RESULTS FIRST, BECAUSE THEY BOUND THE WORK: all 46 event choice labels agree with their payloads, 0 mismatches; all 93 see_also pointers resolve; and every status glossary entry that quotes a constant quotes it correctly — Broken's 0.7 and +0.25, Sunder's 0.65 and the claim that the two MULTIPLY, Frostbite's 0.5, Dazed on top of the 5% base, Chilled 1/2/3/4 with the 15% cut at three, Ruin's 10 and 0.40, Glacial Hold's 15 and 30, Frostbind's 40%, Psychosis' 0.5 base.

BUCKET 1 — ONE FINDING, AND IT IS ON THE END BOSS. The Hollow Crown's REGALIA reads "Wards an ally against the next blow" but its payload is enemy_shield, which is 3 turns of 25% less damage — a one-charge ward is a different status entirely. And it can never be cast: support casts are chosen by literal display name and "Regalia" is not among them, while the attack list filters on damage > 0 and Regalia has no damage. Nothing in the game can select it — and battle.gd's own comment lists it as a live shield source, so the code's notes believe it fires. BUCKET 2 — THE STRUCTURAL ONE IS THE EVENT SCREEN, and it is CJ's §2.1 again in a different file. 17 of the 30 event choices that carry an effect state nothing about it in the label (57%), and event_screen.gd puts only the label on the button — the effect summary is rendered after the choice is made. BUCKET 3 — PROSE. The glossary and events are written in second person against the standard's no-pronoun rule (glossary long 30%, event outcomes 48%), while the ten enemy ability descriptions are ten for ten clean and are the calibration example a rewrite should use. 77 of 93 glossary entries use an ASCII hyphen where the whole rest of the game uses an em dash — one judgement call applied 77 times. And a first-ever sweep of 211 hero ability names against 50 enemy ones found "Crushing Blow" on both sides of the field with different numbers (Orc Chief 34, the Warrior's own 43), beside a Warrior talent called Crushing Blows — three things sharing a stem in one combat log, which is a worse shape than the card-vs-node collisions because both halves are abilities.

THE 324 TALENT NODES ARE STILL DEFERRED, DELIBERATELY, and are RECORDED AS OWED in CLAUDE.md so they cannot quietly disappear. 92 of them state a number their own payload cannot produce, because talent payloads are mostly flag values whose magnitudes live in battle.gd and unit.gd; each needs its own read-site checked. That is a batch by itself. §CK also states its OWN gap: the 65 non-status glossary entries were read for sense rather than traced claim by claim.
