2026-08-17 — Batch CJ: THE TEXT STANDARD AND THE FULL TEXT AUDIT

Two documents and NO REWRITES. No description edited, no ability changed, no magnitude moved, no save version moved (still v10). Not one line of game code was touched — the batch ships docs/text-standard.html (the rules all player-facing text is written to, now a standing rule in CLAUDE.md) and docs/text-audit.html (what currently breaks them, in three buckets, report only). The rewrite passes come after, governed by the first and scoped by the second.

§0 — THE COPY COUNT, AND THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE BATCH

774 authored player-facing strings, 1,846 authored lines, extracted rather than sampled: 204 ability descriptions, 190 perfect_text, 12 passive_desc, 4 class passives, 147 statuses, 324 talent nodes, 65 runes, 18 relics, 93 glossary entries.

Ability descriptions, passives and statuses are written TWICE — once in the code and once in master.html. Runes, relics and the glossary are written once.

AND THE TWO COPIES SHARE NO PROSE. Of the 120 draft ability rows in master.html, ZERO carry the code's sentence — all 120 are independently authored paraphrases, and the document's copy is a median 3.0x longer (118 of 120 longer, widest 5.7x). The brief's own calibration example was quoted from the document, not from the card. Blood Offering reads one way in master.html and a different, shorter way in classes.gd, and both are true — the code does 20% of current HP floored at 1, 40 Rage / 60 Perfect. The consequence, written into the standard: the fluff problem is smaller on the cards than assumed and larger in the document, and a rewrite calibrated against master.html's verbosity would over-correct text already most of the way there.

§1 — THE STANDARD (docs/text-standard.html, linked from master.html)

Two tiers — draft screen and glossary may show arithmetic, everywhere else may not; no design rationale on a card, ever; flavor allowed as one short removable clause; no pronouns; always name whose percentage; (Perfect: X) as the value alone; keywords capitalised (Break above all); never a bare "3 turns"; state what a second cast does. A per-surface table settles which tier a string is in, because one description field is rendered by five screens and only two of them are the draft.

THE LENGTH CEILING IS 44 CHARACTERS AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. A throwaway Godot instrument asked the real theme font (Open Sans SemiBold) at the real sizes the screens set: the narrowest surface is the draft card at 258px, font 11; every observed line of ≤44 chars fits (widest 241px), and 45 is where it overflows (263px). The ability corpus already holds it — 936 of 936 lines. The existing hand-wrap discipline is correct and the ceiling records it rather than changing it.

THE "NO LITERAL \n" RULE SHIPPED WITH A MEASURED EXCEPTION, BECAUSE APPLYING IT BLINDLY WOULD BREAK THE BATTLE TOOLTIP. Nothing in the project overrides make_custom_tooltip, so every tooltip is Godot's default — which does not autowrap. The authored breaks are load-bearing there; strip them and a 322-character description renders one line ~2000px wide. The rule therefore binds passive_desc NOW (it renders in an autowrapping 400px label whose budget is 61 characters, and 23 of its 67 lines run to 71 — Arcanist, Holy, Inquisitor, Occultist, Beastmaster), and binds ability descriptions only once a custom autowrapping tooltip exists, which is a code batch.

§2 — THE AUDIT (docs/text-audit.html, report only)

THE HEADLINE IS THAT THE NUMBERS ARE SOUND. Every mechanically checkable relationship came back clean: 120/120 document stat cells (cost, initiative, cooldown) match the ability dicts; 0 damage-magnitude disagreements; 14/14 applied status durations match their prose; all 65 rune descriptions trace to their payloads; the hand-read status constants are correct (Slow 0.75, Chilled at 1/2/3/4, Burn 6, Poison 3/stack, Decay 10 BD, Ruin cap 0.40); and the Arcanist's Resonance formula is right to the decimal. That result is what makes the rewrites a prose job rather than a repair job.

BUCKET 1 — WRONG: two, and both are design questions rather than typos.

1.1 — "IRON WILL" IS THE CHIP NAME OF TWO UNRELATED MECHANICS. The ironclad status (from the ABILITY) reads "Iron Will" and means no Stun/Freeze/Daze/ Break plus 15% less damage with the Break meter capped at 99. The iron_will status (from the TALENT) also reads "Iron Will" and means −12% damage taken per rank per debuff on the Warden. master.html's status table has one row called "Iron Will" and it describes the talent, so a reader checking the ability gets the talent's answer. The game already has a deliberate same-label pattern and this is not it — berserk/berserk_risk and formless/formless_recoil are the upside and the price of ONE ability, tagged Bk/Bk! and Fm/Fm!. The fix is a rename, which is an ability change and out of scope for a text batch.

1.2 — BATTLE SHOUT'S REGISTRY TOOLTIP HARDCODES THE LOWEST OF THREE TIERS. It says "+8% damage"; the code picks 8 / 12 / 18 (and 2 / 3 / 4 turns) from battle_shout_node. Reported with its mitigation stated: the cast path overwrites the chip with a live string in the same loop, so the wrong text is a fallback not believed reachable in play — but it is the only copy of the number that does not move with the node. master.html is CORRECT here and lists all three tiers.

BUCKET 2 — INCOMPLETE. The largest single finding is one code path: the draft card renders description and nothing else — no damage, no BD, no cost, no cooldown, no Perfect. So 30 of 66 damaging abilities show no damage figure while being drafted (Ice Lance the sharpest: damage: 35 in the dict, and the card states only "+5% of Attack per Chilled stack"), all 190 Perfect bonuses are invisible on the one screen whose purpose is comparing cards, and Aimed Shot — damage: 45, the hardest-hitting card in its pool — draws as "A perfect line. Patient, precise, final." and nothing else. This cannot be fixed by rewriting prose without putting arithmetic back on the mid-combat tooltip; the draft card wants the computed block the blacksmith card already builds. Also: 53 of 61 timed abilities never say what a second cast does (87%, confirming the brief), and of 78 matched status rows 41 have a number in the document that the chip omits — usually the duration — against 0 the other way.

BUCKET 3 — PROSE ONLY. Person is split in both directions (86 second person, 44 third, of 204); 97 carry a bare "N turns"; perfect_text is one field in four shapes (107 of 190 use "instead of", restating a base the line above already gives) and four abilities state the Perfect condition in the description as well, so the tooltip says it twice. The Arcanist's passive_desc is the worst string in the game — correct to the decimal, and it puts a triangular-number formula in algebra (N(N+1)/2) on the hero sheet with two worked examples, when the stack count is known at display time and the live value is computable.

ONE CODE INCONSISTENCY FOUND IN PASSING, REPORTED NOT FIXED: spec_choice_screen.gd flattens \n to a space for ability descriptions and does not do the same for passive_desc on the very next line, so the passive block hard-wraps inside a 298px column there.

COVERAGE IS STATED IN THE REPORT RATHER THAN IMPLIED. Whole-population mechanical checks cover all 204 abilities, 120 document rows, 65 runes, 78 status rows and all 1,846 lines. NOT exhaustively verified: the 324 talent nodes against runtime behaviour (their payloads are mostly flags whose magnitudes live in battle.gd, so 92 state a number their own payload cannot produce — expected, but each needs its own read-site checked), the 93 glossary entries, and enemy/event text. That is the honest gap and the obvious follow-up scope.

§3 — VERIFICATION

The content-batch floor (standing since CG): it parses, it runs, a live battle throws nothing. No suite shipped. No game code was modified in this batch, so the surface at risk was documentation only; the parse gate and a live battle were run regardless and are clean. The measuring instrument was a throwaway and was deleted after it reported.

2026-08-16 — Batch CI: tranche 3, the WARRIOR nine (THE DRAFT IS COMPLETE)

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Warrior spec. The Warrior pools go 5 → 8, and the draft goes 111 → 120 of 120. TRANCHE 3 CLOSES AND THE ABILITY DRAFT IS FINISHED — all twelve specs draft from eight, all four class pools hold six, and the asymmetry that has shaped every batch since BO is gone. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, no save version moves (still v10). TWO new unit-side fields for nine abilities, and both are cases a status genuinely cannot hold.

§0 — THE NAME SWEEP, AND THE ONE COLLISION IT FOUND

No key trap this time, and it is the first class where that is true. berserker, warden and swordmaster are the real pool keys AND the real display names — unlike the Devout (inquisitor) and the Survivalist (mystic), each of which cost an earlier tranche a §0 warning.

The Batch BR §1 sweep ran against all nine names, over every ability, talent node, status and rune. Seven came back clean: Unslaked, Boil Over, Anvil, Recompense, Turn the Blade, Answering Steel and Formless. Two did not.

  • SPITE IS A LIVE WARDEN TALENT NODE — wd_spiked, named Spite, Threat row 5, with spite_ranks and spite_break behind it. The card is a BERSERKER card, so unlike BW's Grudge (same spec, same lane, mechanically adjacent, and therefore moved) the two can never appear on one hero's sheet: no Berserker can hold a Warden node. It is a LABEL collision by BR §1 — a node's name is not an ability name, nothing resolves it, and pool_ability is keyed on display_name, where no ability answers to Spite. It SHIPS AS SPECIFIED AND IS FLAGGED, on the Iron Will / Precision Strike / Shared Vigil precedent. Renaming either is the designer's call and one string.
  • DISCIPLINE sits one word from PLATE DISCIPLINE, a Warden talent node. Different spec, different string, nothing resolves either. Reported, not resolved.

§4's three named near-misses were checked deliberately and all three are clean: Bulwark is the VAULTED Warden passive and was not revived as a card name; Battle Poise is a live Swordmaster draft card and Discipline is a different string in the same pool; and Perfect is the skill-check keyword, which is why the both-stances card is Formless. His pool already holds Covering Guard and Feigned Guard, so there is no fourth “Guard” card.

§1 — BERSERKER: the ratchet, the band, the payout

These are the first cards in the game that read frenzy_floor at all. Blood Frenzy has two halves — a live bonus that scales with missing health, and a FLOOR that keeps half the peak he reaches — and until now nothing anywhere had a lever on the second.

  • UNSLAKED (30 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) the floor captures the FULL bonus he reaches rather than half. The play pattern is the point: cast it, then dive with Blood Offering, and the floor locks in at double its usual value for the rest of the battle. It lives inside frenzy_bonus(), the ONE place the floor is decided, so the strike multiplier, the nameplate readout and the spec chip all answer it for free. It uses maxf rather than an assignment, so a Scar Tissue Berserker already keeping 100% is never quietly lowered to it — the card can only ever raise what is kept.
  • SPITE (20 Rage, 1.5, 4cd, self) — for 4 turns (Perfect: 6) he takes 1% less damage per 5% of maximum health missing, up to 30% (Perfect: 40%). MITIGATION, NOT HEALING, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: a card that healed him here would fight his own passive, taking back the missing health Blood Frenzy pays for, so it would cancel itself. This keeps him inside the frenzy band instead of lifting him out of it.
  • BOIL OVER (40 Rage, 2.5, 5cd, one enemy, 15 BD) — one strike for 30% of Attack plus 2% more per POINT of his live Blood Frenzy bonus. For 2 turns afterwards (Perfect: 1) he receives only the FLOOR, not the live bonus. The floor itself is untouched, and the ratchet still runs inside the window — which is exactly what makes Unslaked pair with it: a high floor makes the recovery cost small.

THE ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE THING THIS CARD COULD MOST EASILY GET WRONG. Boil Over's per-point term is read at the raw-damage block, ABOVE the strike; the recovery status is applied AFTER the strike loop. Applied first, the term would have read the floor it was about to impose — the card quietly paying a fraction of what it promises, with nothing to announce it. It also draws no variance roll of its own: raw already carries one, and a second randf_range would shift every later roll in the battle (the draw-order gotcha Batch AQ spent a bisect on).

§2 — WARDEN: deny the reset, get paid for it, or turn it outward

Heavy Plating climbs +8% Block per unblocked hit and a BLOCK throws the whole climb away. That sawtooth is the passive's central cruelty and nothing had ever answered it. These are three answers, and two of them are deliberately incompatible.

  • ANVIL (25 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4), Blocking does NOT reset the Heavy Plating bonus. The sawtooth becomes a staircase. FLAGGED, NOT TUNED: with the bonus free to climb to its +40% ceiling and stay there, this is potentially the strongest card in the batch. It ships as written and play prices it.
  • RECOMPENSE (20 Rage, 1.5, 4cd, self) — for 4 turns (Perfect: 6), whenever Blocking resets his Heavy Plating bonus he gains Rage equal to the percentage points lost: a reset from +32% pays 32 Rage. The figure is read BEFORE the reset, in the unit the card advertises; read after the write it would always be zero, which is the class of mistake that reads exactly like the card doing nothing.
  • TURN THE BLADE (25 Rage, 2.0, 4cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4), each Block deals Break damage to the attacker equal to half the damage the block refused. A blow that gets THROUGH pays nothing.

ANVIL AND RECOMPENSE ACTIVELY FIGHT EACH OTHER AND THAT IS INTENDED. Anvil prevents the reset; Recompense is paid by it. A Warden holding both gets nothing from the second while the first is up — and that falls out of the ordering rather than being a carve-out anybody has to remember: with no reset there is nothing to pay for. They are two answers to the same cruelty, not a stack, it has not been smoothed over, and both card descriptions say so outright rather than leaving a player to discover it.

TURN THE BLADE MAKES THREE SPECS ACROSS THREE CLASSES generating Break that the Occultist's BREAKING DARKNESS amplifies — the Warden here, the Sharpshooter's Fault Line, and the Occultist himself. That web is deliberate. Its number it scales on is the one Batch W already defined for exactly this question: the nominal blow through the blocker's armor, because final was zeroed by the block and a hit that was never rolled has no crit, variance or riders to read.

THE RATE IS THIS BATCH'S OWN AND IS FLAGGED. §2 says “scaling on the damage negated” and names no figure; 50% is chosen here and shipped untuned. It rides an UNCAPPED count — Batch BJ measured 6.3 blocks a trash battle and 9.2 on a boss — so a rate chosen high would out-Break a Warden's whole Threat lane off a 4-turn card, and one chosen low would leave the third Break source §2 sells it as inert.

§3 — SWORDMASTER: dwell, parry, and neither stance

  • DISCIPLINE (25 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, self) — for 5 turns (Perfect: 7), each consecutive turn held in the same stance strengthens that stance's effect by 3% (Perfect: 4%), to a cap of 15%. A Guard Change resets the accumulation to nothing. It fights his own readers and his own gated cards, which is the tension worth having: the spec is built on switching, and this is the first card that pays him for refusing to. The reset lives in _swordmaster_switch, the ONE pivot with three callers, so Guard Change, Precision Strike AND Feint all throw the accumulation away by doing nothing at all — a list at the card's own site would have gone stale the first time a fourth switcher was authored.
  • ANSWERING STEEL (20 Rage, 1.5, 4cd, self) — for 4 turns (Perfect: 6), parry chance +15% (Perfect: 20%), and each successful parry grants 15 Rage and reduces his cooldowns by 1. THE RIPOSTE TALENT ALREADY GRANTS A COUNTER-ATTACK ON PARRY AND THIS DOES NOT DUPLICATE IT — Answering Steel pays TEMPO, never damage, so a hero holding both gets the counter AND the tempo off one turned blade and the two stack cleanly. He is the only parry-stat character in the game and this is the first card that reads it.
  • FORMLESS (35 Rage, 2.5, 6cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) he holds both stances' upsides and neither downside (+15% damage dealt AND 15% less damage taken). When it ends he suffers both downsides for 2 turns (+10% damage taken, −10% dealt).

FORMLESS'S TWO IMPLEMENTATION CALLS, BOTH DELIBERATE AND BOTH WRITTEN DOWN. He counts as BOTH stances for stance-gated abilities, so every gated card in his kit is usable during the window — that is what makes it a build-enabler rather than a stat buff. And Guard Change is REFUSED while it holds: there is no stance to change. Both are decided at _ability_usable, the same door BW's gated cards are refused at, so the greyed button, the bot's pool and the cast itself cannot disagree. _stance_satisfies is the one answer to “does this unit count as standing in guard X”, and it is deliberately SEPARATE from _eff_stance — that helper returns ONE guard, and a single string cannot express “both”.

REPORTED, NOT EXTENDED: PRECISION STRIKE AND FEINT STILL CAST during the window. §3 names Guard Change and only Guard Change. Both of those are READERS — they branch and flip — and they stay legal: the flip moves his underlying stance, which Formless is not reading, so nothing breaks and he simply leaves the window in whichever guard he last flipped to. Refusing them as well would delete two more cards from his pool for three turns, which is a larger change than §3 asks for. It is the designer's call and it is one condition.

Formless's four numbers are SEASONED FIGHTER'S OWN, read at the passive's two read sites rather than at a third, so the card cannot drift from the thing it is quoting; the recoil is the exact pair of downsides it refused. Its debt is armed at the cast on formless_pending and paid the moment the window lapses, in the turn loop beside Vigor's and Vengeance's own just-expired checks — the one position where the status has genuinely gone, so the two windows can neither overlap nor leave a turn's gap between them.

The nine, and what they carry

TWO NEW UNIT-SIDE FIELDS FOR NINE ABILITIES (BQ's standard: anything with a duration is a STATUS, which expires by itself and cannot leak past a battle). discipline_turns is a COUNT of consecutive turns held, which is not a duration and does not tick down; and formless_pending is a FLAG recording that a recoil is owed. TEN STATUSES, AND EVERY ONE SITS ON A HERO, so all ten are correctly ABSENT from DEBUFF_IDS — this is the first Warrior tranche with nothing to put on an enemy at all, which is what a class third made of self-buffs and passive-readers looks like.

EIGHT OF THE NINE CARRY A special; BOIL OVER DELIBERATELY DOES NOT, and that looks like an omission which is why it is recorded (the BV five-of-nine / CB Cold Iron pattern). _resolve sends any ability holding a special down _resolve_special, which means hand-rolling the blow and losing the whole attack pipeline with it — crits, armor, resists, Break, the parry roll AND Blood Frenzy's own multiplier. Boil Over is an ordinary strike with two riders and NEEDS that pipeline.

BREAK DAMAGE ASSIGNED DELIBERATELY (the BO rule, applied up front). ONE of the nine carries it and EIGHT do not, and each of the eight is a decision rather than an omission: Boil Over 15, flat, sitting between Blood Debt's 10 and Gut Rip's 20 on the same hero — flat because the DAMAGE term is the one that scales, and a Break term riding the same uncapped-looking multiplier is the squaring trap three earlier tranches each refused from their own side. The other eight land no blow at all, so Break would have nothing to ride. Turn the Blade is the interesting zero: it is the batch's largest Break source and carries none of its own, because every point of it is dealt at the BLOCK rather than by the cast.

Glossary

Two entries added (91 → 93) and two corrected toward the code. Two of the nine read Blood Frenzy's floor and three read Heavy Plating's climb, and the glossary taught neither — a player meeting Unslaked or Anvil had nowhere to learn what the card was talking about. frenzy_floor explains the ratchet and names all three things that change it (Scar Tissue, Unslaked, Boil Over); plating_climb explains the sawtooth, why he wants the blocks that reset it, and that Anvil and Recompense cannot be used together. Corrected: stance said he “is always in one of two”, which Formless makes false, and stance_gated named Feigned Guard as the answer to being locked out, where Formless is now the wider one.

§5 — THE FILL-SHORT CHECKS HAD NOWHERE LEFT TO GO, SO THE ARITHMETIC MOVED INSTEAD

Batch CH moved the “an offer fills SHORT rather than padding” constructions onto a Warrior, because he was the last spec still drafting from five. This batch takes him to eight, so after CI no pool in the game is thin and those checks cannot be moved again.

Three of the four (test_batch_bo, bq, br) refused the whole class pool plus a HARDCODED three of the hero's own cards — an arithmetic that assumed a five-deep pool. At eight that leaves FIVE standing and the offer comes up FULL: the checks would have gone on measuring something, and it would no longer have been the fill-short rule. There is no hero left to relocate to, so the REFUSAL is written relative to the LIVE pool size instead — refuse everything but two. That is test_batch_bx's shape, which was already pool-size-relative and needed no repair at all, and it is the only form that cannot go stale again: a later tranche that deepened a pool would move the setup and not the answer.

A check that silently stops asking its question is this project's signature failure, and this is the last batch where it could be prevented rather than discovered. It was prevented.

§6 — THE ASYMMETRY PROSE IS DEAD EVERYWHERE IT APPEARED

master.html §6b, the SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS header comment and CLAUDE.md all framed the draft around “the Hunter and Warrior six draft from five”. All three were rewritten rather than patched: the draft is complete at 120 of 120, twelve specs at eight apiece plus four class pools of six, and nothing is owed.

Every draft suite's per-spec depth loop inverts for the SEVENTH and LAST time. It has asserted, in order: each earlier tranche's own asymmetry, then the flatness tranche 2 achieved, then CB's new asymmetry, that asymmetry halved at CE, quartered at CH — and now gone. What it guards from here on is the FLATNESS rather than a debt: a pool that quietly empties trips, where before it would have read as the old asymmetry coming back.

2026-08-16 — Batch CH: tranche 3, the HUNTER nine (the Hunter is the third class complete)

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Hunter spec. The Hunter pools go 5 → 8 and the draft goes 102 → 111 of a target 120. THE HUNTER IS THE THIRD CLASS COMPLETE and CB's asymmetry is quartered: nine specs draft from EIGHT and only the three WARRIOR specs draft from FIVE, so all that is owed is the Warrior third — nine cards, and it is the last of the debt. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, no save version moves (still v10). FOUR new unit-side fields for nine abilities, and every one of them is a case a status cannot hold.

§0 — THREE OF THE BRIEF'S NINE NAMES COLLIDED WITH LIVE CONTENT, AND ALL THREE MOVED

The brief predicted a crowded Hunter vocabulary and said to run the Batch BR §1 sweep anyway and treat a near-miss as a hit. The sweep came back with three hits, and one of them was not a near-miss at all.

  • HARVEST IS A LIVE ABILITY, IN THE VERY POOL THIS SPEC DRAWS FROM AT A ZONE BOSS. It sits in SPEC_POOLS["mystic"] and CLASS_POOLS["hunter"] and has since Batch 33. Classes.pool_ability is keyed on display_name, so a second Harvest makes the resolver answer the wrong question — a REAL BREAK by BR §1, not a label collision to be flagged — and the mechanic duplicated too (consume every status on one enemy for damage scaling on the count), which is the Deadfall/Snare Trap failure this batch's own §1 warns about. So the name moved AND the shape did: the card is CULL, and it throws the reaping at the WHOLE FIELD where Harvest empties one body and heals him. Neither dominates.
  • KINDRED IS A LIVE BEASTMASTER CAPSTONE (bm_kindred, devotion row 8) reading the same Loyalty depth, in the same spec, and mechanically adjacent to the card. That is closer than BW's Grudge, and BW's precedent decides it: the node's id is save-bearing and its ranks travel with it, while the card was unshipped, so the CARD moved. It is SUCCESSION.
  • TRIPLE TAP sits one word from TRIPLE SHOT, the same spec's live boss-pool ability and also three strikes on one target. Nothing breaks (pool_ability reads the whole name), but a player holding both would see two nearly identical names on one sheet. It is DRUMFIRE, and the two now point opposite ways: Triple Shot spends a deep meter, Drumfire builds one.
  • UNLEASH KEEPS ITS NAME AND CHANGED SHAPE. The name is clean against every ability, node, status and rune — it appears only as prose inside Bestial Wrath's description, which is reported rather than resolved. What was NOT clean is the mechanic: PRIMAL SURGE (Beastmaster boss pool) already spends Loyalty for a companion strike, and the brief's version was a strict subset of it. Unleash is one companion at a steeper rate carrying Break on a longer cooldown, against the Surge's pack-wide conversion plus a lasting damage buff.

The other five names — Last Howl, Reacquire, Fault Line, Stalking Horse, Downwind — are clean against every ability, talent node, status and rune.

§1 — BEASTMASTER: keep it, move it, spend it

LAST HOWL (20 Mana, 1.5, 4cd, self): for the rest of the battle, every companion that falls pays him +2% strike damage per stack of Loyalty it had earned (Perfect: 3%). IT IS NOT VENGEANCE AND MUST NEVER BE WRITTEN AS "KEEP THE DEAD BEAST'S BOON" — that is the bm_vengeance node, which inherits the boon. This carries the meter to the hunter, and a hero holding both gets both. It reads the meter as it stood when the beast fell, above Steadfast Bond's rewrite three lines below, because the whole card is that the meter outlives the body. PER-COMPANION: under The Pack two beasts falling pay twice, each for what IT earned. It is the fifth user of the one implementation of "this unit deals N% more damage", so it composes additively with Battle Shout, Warcry, Resonant Field and Reckless Abandon.

SUCCESSION (20 Mana, 1.5, 4cd, self): for 4 turns (Perfect: 6) a swap hands the bond on — the arriving companion starts holding half the Loyalty of the one it replaces. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS HALF STALE AND THE CODE IS RIGHT (the AR §6 / BU / CB precedent): a swap has NEVER cost Loyalty (Batch BO §5 corrected exactly this), because the meter lives on the hunter's dict per kind and only a DEATH breaks it. So a returning beast already keeps its depth, and what "starting it at nothing" truly describes is a kind never fielded. It RAISES, never assigns — rotating into a deeper bond must not cost depth, which is the one way a card sold on carrying the bond forward could be worse than not holding it. Under The Pack the swap evicts the SHALLOWER bond, so what it carries forward is the smaller meter.

UNLEASH (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy, 12 BD): his deepest companion strikes immediately for 20% of Attack per stack of its Loyalty (Perfect: 25%), and that meter resets to zero. Under The Pack it reads the ACTIVE companion only, resolved through _deepest_bond — BX §3's ONE implementation of which companion an ORDERED action goes to, and also the bigger meter, which is the right read for a card whose subject is the meter. ITS BREAK IS FLAT AND MUST STAY FLAT: the stack count is uncapped, and a per-stack Break term on an uncapped meter is the squaring trap Arcane Bolt, Requiem and Pyre Wake each refused.

§2 — SHARPSHOOTER: the exception, the threshold, the depth

REACQUIRE (20 Mana, 1.5, 4cd, one enemy): names one enemy for the rest of the battle. Leaving it BANKS his Focus instead of clearing it; returning hands the bank back whole. Switching between any two OTHER targets still clears. Perfect: 25 Focus on the mark at once. It is written as a BANK rather than as a refusal to clear, so every Focus reader in the game sees an honest zero while he is away; and it reads the mark's own src_name, so a second Sharpshooter can never collect on the first one's quarry.

FAULT LINE (20 Mana, 1.5, 4cd, self): for 4 turns (Perfect: 6), while his Focus stands ABOVE the conversion point, every attack he lands also deals 20 Break damage. Two gaps at once: the first card in the pool to read the conversion threshold at all, and the only Break lever the HUNTER CLASS has anywhere. IT READS focus_convert() AND NEVER A LITERAL 100 — Deep Focus moves the split point down, and a card watching a hardcoded hundred would silently stop agreeing with the passive in exactly the build that bought the node (Vespers learned this against mercy_threshold). It is added ABOVE Broken Will and the Breaker runes, so every existing Break multiplier answers it — and so does the Occultist's Breaking Darkness, which is the cross-roster reach §2 sells it on.

DRUMFIRE (25 Mana, 3.0, 3cd, one enemy, 6 BD a shot): three arrows at one mark, 14% of Attack each, and EACH ONE counts separately for Focus (Perfect: a fourth arrow, counted like the rest). THIS IS BR §1'S HITS-NOT-CASTS RULE ARRIVING AT THE FOCUS ENGINE FOR THE FIRST TIME: that engine has been called once per CAST since AZ, so every existing multi-hit ability builds ONE stack of Focus however many arrows it throws. It counts inside the hit loop and shares the splash's final > 0 gate, so a missed or blocked arrow feeds nothing. THE STREAK IS ROLLED BACK BETWEEN HITS — same_target_turns is what UNWAVERING's ramp reads and it counts TURNS, so letting three arrows advance it three times would silently triple a shipped node's magnitude off a card that never mentions it.

§3 — SURVIVALIST (mystic): draw it, spread it, spend it

THE POOL KEY IS mystic, exactly as the Devout's is inquisitor. SPEC_INFO["mystic"] carries the display name "Survivalist" and master.html prints "Survivalist", so the docs and the code disagree BY DESIGN; a "survivalist": key would raise nothing, resolve nothing, and ship three cards no hero could ever be offered.

STALKING HORSE (25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, self): for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) enemies are drawn to swing at him, and every attacker takes a DIFFERENT affliction — Poison, Cripple, Slowed, Exposed, Dazed, Blind, in turn. It REUSES the existing draw (the site Savage Presence, Threatening Presence and Ghillie Suit already live on) rather than inventing a second taunt. EVERY ID IN THE CYCLE IS IN DEBUFF_IDS, and that is load-bearing: Trapper's breadth term counts that curated list ONLY, so an affliction outside it would apply, log and read as working while paying his multiplier nothing — the card would do exactly half of what it says with nothing to announce it. It pays out when a blow LANDS, not when one is declared (BL §1 declares a turn early and re-validates at resolution), and its poison goes through _apply_poison so it is HIS poison rather than a bare status wearing the name.

DOWNWIND (25 Mana, 2.0, 5cd, self): for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every harmful effect any hero lands on an enemy is copied onto a second enemy, preferring one that does not already carry it. He is the one spec in the game whose passive an ally can feed — Trapper's breadth counts statuses from ANY source — and nothing had ever exploited it. It covers every hero, himself included, and that is ONE RULE rather than a carve-out: excluding the caster would make the card read as inert on every turn he spent applying his own board.

CULL (30 Mana, 3.0, 5cd, one enemy): consumes every affliction on one enemy, and EVERY enemy takes 10% of Attack in nature damage per status removed (Perfect: 12%). It deliberately fights his own passive — the breadth he spent the fight building is what it eats — and that tension is intended. It reads _harvest_yield, the ONE answer to "what would this reap", so it and Harvest can never disagree about what a sticky poison is worth, and it MEASURES the purge rather than predicting it (BA §7's repair, inherited). Its Break is ZERO on a card that genuinely deals damage, because the multiplier is an uncapped count of afflictions and a Break term riding it is the squaring trap from a fourth direction (Pyre Wake's precedent).

§4 — six statuses, and the split between the two lists

Five sit on a HERO (last_howl, succession, fault_line, stalking_horse, downwind) and are correctly ABSENT from DEBUFF_IDS. reacquire sits on an ENEMY and is a MARK, so it is absent from DEBUFF_IDS too — a battle-long entry there reads as 999 turns remaining and a mender's longest-first Cleansing Rite would take it every single time — AND it is in DISPEL_NEVER, because _dispellable_buffs is DERIVED from that absence and would otherwise let a Mage's own Dispel strip the Sharpshooter's mark FOR the enemy wearing it. That is BU's Suffering trap and BW's mark trap meeting at one card. Unleash, Drumfire and Cull resolve inside the cast that fires them and carry nothing.

§5 — the fill-short constructions moved off the Hunter, and two faults the repair found

TWO fill-short constructions were built on a Hunter hero and both moved to a WARRIOR, who is the only class still at five: test_batch_bq's onto a Berserker and test_batch_br's onto a Swordmaster. Each refused its hero's whole CLASS pool plus three of his own spec cards to leave exactly two standing; with the Hunter pools at eight that leaves FIVE and the offer comes up full, so the check would have stopped asking its question. This is the same forced move test_batch_bo made at BW, and the same honest signal: a construction that has to relocate is how a paid debt announces itself. test_batch_bo's and test_batch_bx's versions already stood on a Berserker and a Warden and needed nothing. WHEN THE WARRIOR THIRD LANDS there will be no five-deep pool left in the game and both have to move a third time, onto a hero worn down by draft_refused alone.

THE REPAIR PASS FOUND TWO FAULTS IN THIS BATCH'S OWN CODE, AND THAT IS WHY RE-RUNNING THE OLDER SUITES IS NOT A FORMALITY. test_batch_bo walks every draft entry and asserts each carries a perfect: REACQUIRE SHIPPED WITH AN EMPTY perfect_text, and it now takes 25 Focus on the mark. Writing that fix surfaced the second: DRUMFIRE CARRIED perfect_extra_hit: false WHILE ITS PERFECT TEXT PROMISED A FOURTH ARROW — copied from Triple Shot, whose perfect is a guaranteed crit instead. The flag is back at its default and the promise is true.

§6 — documentation, and a stamp-gate count corrected

docs/master.html carries the nine new rows, the summary table and the corrected count (111 of 120, 9 owed) and is stamped Batch CH; CLAUDE.md and this changelog carry the same. THE MASTER.HTML STAMP GATE IS DUPLICATED FOURTEEN TIMES, NOT THIRTEEN, AND BOTH CE'S AND CG'S COUNTS WERE WRONG IN DIFFERENT WAYS — CE said fourteen and named test_batch_cd, which carries no stamp gate at all; CG corrected it to thirteen and dropped test_batch_ce, which does carry one. The fourteen are ah, bb, bn, bo, bp, bq, br, bs, bt, bu, bv, bw, bx and ce, and all fourteen moved to Batch CH.

§7 — flagged and shipped untuned, to be watched in play

FAULT LINE'S 20 BD is the number this batch trusts least (Threshold's 15 and Breaking Darkness's 50 are the precedent). It is the only Break the Hunter class has, so too low and the lever does not exist; too high and one draft card outdoes a Warden's whole Threat lane, which AL measured at 320 BD a battle. LAST HOWL'S 2% A STACK reads a meter with no ceiling: at the 50 Loyalty Batch AY measured on a DEVOTION build, a single companion's death is +100% strike damage. UNLEASH'S 20% A STACK has the same property from the other side. DO NOT PRE-TUNE ANY OF THE THREE.

2026-08-16 — Batch CG: the CE revision (seven changes to the Cleric nine)

Seven changes to the nine Cleric cards Batch CE shipped: two renames with new mechanics, one card deleted and replaced, one card re-specced, one rename with a re-spec, one magnitude halved, and one mechanic replaced outright. No new ability, no talent node, no save version moves (still v10). SPEC_DRAFT_POOLS stays at 78 and the draft stays at 102 of 120 — what is owed is still the Hunter and Warrior thirds of tranche 3.

§0 — the letter CF is spent

A batch document CF (the Hunter nine) was authored and deliberately never run. Nothing of it is in the repo and nothing of it will be. The gap between CE and CG is not a lost or failed batch and there is nothing to look for — the same shape as CC, recorded at Batch CD §3. The Hunter third of tranche 3 will land as CH.

§1 — HOLY: Matins becomes Divine Presence, and Observance is replaced by Vespers

MATINS → DIVINE PRESENCE. The ability, its status id (matins → divine_presence) and its display name all move. The watch condition is exactly as it was — a fall below the window breaks that turn's watch and the passive pays instead — and cost and cooldown are unchanged at 20 Mana / 4cd. Two things change about how it pays:

  • 2 Mercy per payout, at the start of every SECOND turn of hers, rather than 1 every turn.
  • Duration 4 turns (Perfect: 6), so it fires twice for 4 Mercy or three times for 6.

The 2-per-payout shape is the point rather than the rate: it can overflow the Mercy cap into ALMS, which is the first time two of her own draft cards feed each other. A drip of one a turn could only ever reach the ceiling one stack at a time and had nothing to hand on; two arriving together cross it from below, and the spare stack becomes a ward. Grace is deliberately NOT fired by that overflow — at _on_hero_below_half the two spill together by design, but the card this batch names is Alms, and paying a talent node off a second trigger is a power change nobody specified. Reported for the designer; it is one line if wanted.

FLAGGED, NOT TUNED: a 4-turn duration on a 4-turn cooldown is 100% uptime, where Matins ran at 75%. Left as the designer chose it; it is a playtest question rather than a batch's.

FLAGGED — A LABEL COLLISION ON HER OWN SHEET. hl_presence is a HOLY TALENT NODE already named Divine Presence (Vigil row 2, the end-of-turn drip to the most wounded ally). Per the Batch BR §1 sweep rule that is a label collision and not a break — a node's name is not an ability name, nothing resolves it, and the two carry different fields (divine_presence_pct against the card's divine_presence special) — so it ships as specified and is recorded. It is closer than BP's Precision Strike / Precision Strikes (same spec, and an exact match rather than a plural); renaming either is the designer's call and one string.

OBSERVANCE → REPLACED BY VESPERS. Observance and its status are deleted entirely, and the Empower-keeps-the-perfect rule goes with them: _observance_pay is gone, and an Empowered cast forfeits its perfect bonus exactly as it did before Batch CE. Nothing is left for a later batch to re-arm. What survives CE and is not undone is the Hymn's ordering — its Empowered share (35%) is written LAST, so a cast that paid a Mercy for the surge can never be handed the smaller perfect share (25%) instead.

VESPERS (25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, one ally) — for 4 turns (Perfect: 6), or until it fires: the next blow that would take that ally below half health is absorbed for 20% of the Holy Cleric's maximum health. A blow bigger than the ward still crosses, still costs the health it did not catch and still pays her.

THE LAST CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE CARD AND IT IS NOT AN EDGE CASE: if the ally does not cross, the Cleric earns no Mercy for a crossing that never happened. It is the only place in her pool where helping an ally starves her own engine. It is not a rule written anywhere — the absorb sits ABOVE the subtraction and therefore above _check_below_half, so the generator simply never fires. Moving it below would leave the card working and quietly hand her the stack anyway, which is the one way to make its price disappear.

It reads mercy_threshold rather than a literal half, for the same reason: GUARDIAN ANGEL moves the Mercy line to 65%, and a ward watching a different line from the generator would make the trade false in exactly the build that cares most about it. There is deliberately no copy in take_tick_damage — the card says "the next BLOW", and Batch BS's Kiln-Forged set the precedent this file follows: a Burn tick is not a hit. Vespers is a BUFF on an ally and is correctly OUT of DEBUFF_IDS, with the other two Holy statuses; it is the first of the three that sits on an ally rather than on Holy herself, so a listing would have made it a ward a Cleansing Rite could take off the party.

§2 — DEVOUT: Elevation grants real Faith, and Jubilee becomes Blessing of the Faithful and costs the peak

ELEVATION — A PLAIN GRANT, NOT A PEAK FLOOR. The peak-floor mechanic is replaced: every ally gains 2 stacks of Faith (Perfect: 3), visible on the bar. Cost rises 30 → 35 Mana; cooldown stays 5. It goes through _gain_faith, THE ONE DOOR, so every consequence of a Faith gain follows for free rather than being reimplemented: the peak still ratchets on the way up, Blessing of Zeal still doubles, and the source table still books it (a seventh gain term, because a six-term table would stop adding up the moment the card was drafted).

The consequences are implemented rather than guarded against. An ally already holding 3 or more reaches the cap of 5 and RELEASES — healed 15% of maximum, count reset, the Devout paid 3% of his Mana. That is correct and intended. The peak is untouched by a release (Batch BI §1), so the release costs the ally nothing they were holding and the card is pure upside on a party that has been building. Binding Oath and Communion ride it exactly as they ride any other release, because it is one.

THE GATE IS GONE, AND REMOVING IT IS THE REPAIR RATHER THAN A LOOSENING. CE refused the cast once every peak stood at the floor — the right question about a card that raised a FLOOR and meaningless about one that hands over stacks; it would have darkened the button in exactly the late-fight state the card is now worth most in. A plain grant can only be a dud if nobody can gain, and an ally never sits at the cap (reaching it releases them).

_raise_faith_peak IS DELETED, NOT LEFT UNREACHABLE. It was Elevation's write and its only caller, so nothing in the game raises faith_peak without the count any more — the peak follows the count at the one ratchet in _gain_faith, which is the state BI §1 shipped. Its absence is pinned in test_batch_bi where its presence used to be.

CE's suite asserted Elevation does NOT grant Faith. That assertion is INVERTED, not deleted, and the setups are deliberately the ones CE built, because they are still what tells the two readings apart; only the correct answer moved.

JUBILEE → BLESSING OF THE FAITHFUL, AND IT NOW COSTS THE PEAK. Renamed, and the trade changes: spending his Faith drops his high-water mark to match. Everything else holds — all stacks spent, 6% of maximum health and 3% of maximum Mana per stack (Perfect: 8%), gated at 3 held, 20 Mana / 4cd — and it is still not a release (no principal growth, no Communion, no Binding Oath).

This is the point of the change: as CE shipped it he kept the peak, so the payout was free — the count bought him nothing while he held it, so emptying it cost him nothing either. Now it is burst sustain bought with permanent mitigation and damage for the rest of the fight. It is a deliberate exception to BI §1 rather than a reversal of it: BI's repair was that a RELEASE must not silently cost held value; here the surrender is named on the card and paid once by one deliberate cast, and _gain_faith's release branch still leaves every peak standing. This is the only site in the game that lowers one. CE's negative control asserted the peak does NOT drop; it is INVERTED.

THE SPECIAL ID SURVIVES THE RENAME (jubilee), which is this project's own convention for a resolver-bearing identifier — Batch BX renamed two talent nodes and kept their ids for the same reason. The label is what moved, and a moved id is what silently breaks a saved kit.

FLAGGED: the Devout's core already holds Blessing of Zeal, so his sheet now carries two abilities beginning "Blessing of…". It is not a break (pool_ability is keyed on the WHOLE display name and the two strings differ); it is the near-miss BR §1's sweep would ordinarily raise, and it was named deliberately by the designer. Recorded here rather than silently accepted.

§3 — OCCULTIST: Anathema becomes Breaking Darkness at half the amplifier, and Penance becomes a mirror

ANATHEMA → BREAKING DARKNESS, AMPLIFIER 50% → 25%. Ability, status id (anathema → breaking_darkness) and display name all move. Everything structural holds: 25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, one enemy, 20 Break damage, 3 turns (Perfect: 4), the cast's own Break lands BEFORE the mark so it cannot amplify itself, and the amplifier sits ABOVE the reducers so every defence still answers it. CE recorded 50 as the number the designer trusted least in that batch and shipped it to be watched; this is the answer to watching it.

The status abbreviation is Dk! and must NOT be BD — that is this game's shorthand for Break damage in every log line and tooltip it has, so the one abbreviation the new name fits best is the one it may not use. test_batch_ce pins both halves.

PENANCE — NOW A MIRROR. The self-Attack tick is replaced outright. For 3 turns (Perfect: 4) the enemy takes shadow damage equal to 50% of the damage it deals, whoever it hits. Cost and cooldown unchanged at 25 Mana / 4cd.

Three consequences, all deliberate:

  • It no longer reads the target's attack stat. That property, and the snapshot rule that came with it, go away. Nothing else in the game read that stat; nothing does now.
  • It pays nothing against an enemy that does not attack — stunned, charmed, frozen, holding still. The guaranteed floor is gone. Accepted: what it buys instead is that a blow landing on the whole party bills the body that threw it.
  • The bot's targeting still holds: the HIGHEST-ATTACK enemy is still the right mark, because the biggest hitter reflects the most.

It rides Batch BL's ONE damage door (_on_damage_taken), which is what makes "whoever it hits" true without a list of sources: a strike, its splash, an echo, a retaliation, a DoT tick and a reflect all arrive there, and a damage source added later cannot forget to be mirrored. It sits ABOVE that function's hero gate, because a Feint redirect, a Bewitch, a Psychosis or a Hysteria all make its victim one of its own — a mirror written below the gate would silently do nothing on precisely the turns the Occultist engineered. It carries a re-entrancy lock (_penance_mirroring) on Frostbind's pattern, and self-inflicted damage is excluded by identity: recoil and Blood Price are damage a unit deals to ITSELF, and "whoever it hits" means somebody else. The mirror is shadow-typed, so shadow resists and weaknesses both read, and it credits the Occultist who set it through the src_name the status carries — a dead caster credits nobody and the penance goes on being paid, which is honest rather than wrong.

The turn-start tick and its function are gone from the turn loop; _penance_tick no longer exists.

§4 — documentation, and the verification convention

The draft table's Cleric rows carry three renames and one replacement — Divine Presence, Vespers, Blessing of the Faithful, Breaking Darkness. The count is unchanged at 102 of 120 and master.html is stamped Batch CG. One glossary entry corrected toward the code: mercy_window named MATINS by name, and a glossary that teaches a card nobody can draw is worse than one that omits it — it names Divine Presence and Vespers now, including the overflow into Alms and the crossing Vespers refuses. Entry count is unchanged at 91.

THE VERIFICATION CONVENTION CHANGES FROM THIS BATCH, FOR CONTENT BATCHES GOING FORWARD. No new test suite, no negative controls, no smoke sweeps, no measurement. The floor is: it parses, it runs, and a live battle throws nothing. Testing moves to periodic dedicated test batches instead. Three suites were re-pointed IN PLACE regardless, because a check that asserts a deleted card has stopped asking its question rather than merely going quiet: test_batch_ce (the two inversions §2 names, plus the renames and the two replaced sections), test_batch_bi (the peak-writer pins) and test_batch_av (the Sanctified caller count, back from four to three with Observance gone).

2026-08-16 — Batch CE: tranche 3, the Cleric nine (THE CLERIC IS THE SECOND CLASS COMPLETE)

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Cleric spec. The Cleric pools go 5 → 8 and the draft goes 93 → 102 of a target 120. The asymmetry CB opened is now half what it was: the Mage and Cleric six draft from EIGHT and the Hunter and Warrior six from FIVE, so what is owed is the Hunter and Warrior thirds — 18 cards, nine apiece. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, no save version moves (still v10). ONE new unit-side field for nine abilities, and it is a door rather than a number.

§0 — the Devout's pool key is inquisitor, not devout

SPEC_INFO["inquisitor"] carries the display name Devout and the draft table above prints Devout, so the docs and the code disagree by design and have since the spec was named. A "devout" key would raise nothing, resolve nothing, and ship three cards no hero could ever be offered. test_batch_ce pins all three halves — the key present, "devout" absent, and the display name still reading Devout.

§1 — HOLY: three cards against the three things Mercy cannot do

Her pool competes for the tightest three slots in the game. Her core takes FOUR of the seven (Batch AV gave her Resurrection on purpose), so eight cards fight over three. Every one of these had to earn its place against a stiffer bar than any other spec's.

The gap all three are authored against: Mercy is entirely reactive. She gains a stack only when an ally crosses below half health, so her engine is fuelled by the party taking damage — she can play perfectly and be starved. Three consequences, one card each.

  • MATINS (20 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, self) — for 3 turns she gains 1 Mercy at the start of each of her turns on which no ally fell below the window (Perfect: 4 turns). It pays her on exactly the turns the passive did not, and the two sources are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION — a fall breaks that turn's watch and the passive pays instead, which is what makes it impossible for the card to be simply better than waiting. The flag is cleared as it is read, so one broken turn does not poison the rest of the office.
  • ALMS (20 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, self) — for 4 turns (Perfect: 6) every stack of Mercy earned at the cap wards the ally who earned it for 12% of her maximum, instead of being lost. A WARD RATHER THAN A HEAL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DISTINCTION FROM GRACE, which already turns the same wasted stack into healing: one trigger, two effects, different sheets, and they STACK on the same spill rather than replacing each other. That is what stops this being a strictly better Grace wearing a draft card's clothes (BD §4). The ward is deliberately not divine: a Mercy overflow feeding the DEVOUT's Conviction would be one spec's engine leaking out through another spec's card.
  • OBSERVANCE (25 Mana, 2.0, 5cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) an Empowered cast keeps its perfect bonus and costs 1 additional Mercy. Unpayable is not refused: with no second stack it resolves as an ordinary Empower.

§1's Empower premise is true as a rule and smaller in practice than it reads, and the accounting goes on the page rather than staying in a conversation. _resolve_special zeroes is_perfect for every Empowered cast, so the tax is real — but three of her five Empowerable casts wrote their two branches as if empowered ... elif is_perfect, which could only ever be an elif because the two were unreachable together. Splitting them is a behavioural no-op today and is what makes the card fire at all. Measured against the live kit rather than assumed (BQ's third rule), what Observance is actually worth: Heal (the perfect's 5%-of-maximum self-heal), Renewal (its instant 5% — already an independent if, so this is the one cast where the tax was always payable) and Divine Plea (its 10 Mana). NOTHING on Hymn of Hope or Resurrection, whose Empowered share is strictly bigger than their perfect. Three of five, reported rather than papered over with a new number — inventing a bonus for the two that supersede would be authoring a magnitude the brief did not ask for. THE HYMN'S ORDER IS PINNED IN THE SUITE: 35% Empowered against 25% perfect, so the Empowered share must be written LAST or the card would quietly DOWNGRADE the cast it just charged a second Mercy for.

§2 — DEVOUT: the asymmetry nobody had exploited, and one shield

Faith is paid on the highest count held this battle (faith_peak, Batch BI), so an early spike is worth exactly as much as a long grind and lasts the whole fight — and both his builders are slow drips. Nothing let him buy one. Second gap: his own Faith HOLDS and never releases (BH §2), so the release payout does not exist for him at all.

  • ELEVATION (30 Mana, 2.5, 5cd, all allies) — every ally's PEAK Faith rises to at least 3 (Perfect: 4). It writes the peak and NOT the count, which is what makes it a spike rather than a second Ordination: nobody holds another stack and nobody is walked toward a release. TO at least 3, not BY 3, and that is the governor — a card that ADDED peak would run every ally to the ceiling in a long fight, where raising a FLOOR is worth most on turn one and worth nothing once the grind has passed it. The write is a ratchet (the same maxi _gain_faith uses) and clamps at five.
  • JUBILEE (20 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, self) — spends ALL of his own Faith for 6% of his maximum health and 3% of maximum Mana per stack (Perfect: 8%), gated at 3 held. IT IS NOT A RELEASE AND MUST NEVER BECOME ONE: BH §2 took the Devout off the release branch because a releasing Devout puts the FREQUENCY LOOP straight back — his release would heal, grow the principal and roll Communion, which feeds further releases. So it pays its own payout at its own site and does not go through _gain_faith. His PEAK does not fall, so the mitigation those stacks bought keeps paying; the count is the only thing the card costs, and the gate at three is what stops it being a heal he presses every time one stack arrives.
  • MANTLE (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one ally) — a Divine Shield worth 25% of his maximum, and when it BREAKS it passes to the ally on the lowest health, twice (Perfect: three times). THE ABSORB IS THE DRY SOURCE OF HIS WHOLE ENGINE — BI §2 measured 1.5 absorbed hits a battle against the ground's 9.1 Faith — and Conviction builds ONLY on Divine Shield absorbs, so a shield that becomes three shields is three times the trigger. It never passes back to the body it just left, which is load-bearing rather than tidy: that ally is very often the lowest health, so without the exclusion the mantle would bounce in place and cover one hero three times instead of finding the fight. Every hop is a REAL Divine Shield, granted through the one door, so Blessed Barrier, Afterglow, Warded Robes and Sacred Covenant all ride each of them.

The pool's one shield variant, deliberately. Divine Shield is a bucket on one ally, Unyielding Aegis re-forms a broken one on the SAME ally, and Aegis Reversal eats one that was never spent. This one LEAVES. Unyielding Aegis is the deliberate anti-synergy: a re-formed shield has not broken, so it does not pass — and that is decided at the ONE unit-side site where a shield is removed, so the two nodes can never disagree about what "broken" means.

§3 — OCCULTIST: the gate he could not open, and the lever nothing pulled

He is the boss specialist by construction and the boss refuses half his kit. Ruin detonates on every tenth stack and never washes off, so trash dies before the mark matters; meanwhile the whole Madness lane is refused by a boss until it is Broken, which makes Break his gate — and his pool held nothing that ground it.

  • ANATHEMA (25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, one enemy, 20 BD) — 20 Break damage, and for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every source of Break damage lands on that enemy 50% harder. NOTHING IN THE GAME HAD EVER AMPLIFIED BREAK DAMAGE: Hunter's Mark amplifies damage, Iron Will and Bulwark REFUSE Break, Devoutness and Hold the Line CUT it. This is the one place it is ever raised, and it sits above the reducers so every defence in the game still answers it. The cast's own Break lands BEFORE the mark, so the card cannot amplify itself and its headline number does not depend on the order of two lines. An amplifier rather than a bigger number, because the party is where the Break is — a Warden's Threat lane deals 320 Break a battle and the Occultist a fraction of that, so the lever with leverage is the multiplier.
  • REQUIEM (30 Mana, 3.0, 5cd, one enemy, 8 BD) — consumes every stack of Ruin on one enemy for 8% of Attack each (Perfect: 10%), and the party is healed 2% of his maximum per stack. It fires no detonation: Unraveling does not seed, Grim Focus does not deepen it, the party does not feast — and the primer goes with the pile, or a mark primed at ten would detonate for a full 90% of Attack off a pile that no longer exists. It is a bad trade most of the time and that is the design: the mark it spends is +2% damage taken a stack for the rest of the battle (+5% under Deeper Hex). It is the answer to "I need it dead this turn", not a rotation piece. The damage is per stack and the Break is FLAT, which is Arcane Bolt's rule for its reason: Ruin has no ceiling, and a per-stack Break term on an uncapped count is the squaring trap.
  • PENANCE (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) that enemy takes shadow damage equal to 20% of ITS OWN Attack at the start of each of its turns. It is the only card of his that reads no Ruin at all — no stacks to build, no threshold to reach, no mark to spend — so it is the one that still works in the trash fight that ends on round seven, which is exactly where AX measured 0.00 detonations a battle. Nothing else in the game reads the target's own Attack stat; the tick is snapshotted at application, the same rule burn and poison follow.

§4 — the names, and the sweep

All nine came back clean against every ability, talent node, status and rune — the first tranche since BO with nothing to report, and BR §1's sweep ships as a test rather than as a claim. The register is priestly and old (rites, offices, practices): Matins, Alms, Observance, Elevation, Jubilee, Mantle, Anathema, Requiem, Penance. Words about what a cleric does rather than which side he is on — which is why the Occultist three sit on his tongue as easily as on Holy's, and why the batch went looking for a practice word (Penance) rather than a vice.

§5 — two checks that had stopped asking their question

test_batch_bn and test_batch_bo each held a bare changelog.contains("Batch BN") / ("Batch BO") against the LIVE file — and Batch BZ moved both of those entries into the archive. They went on passing because a LATER entry names each batch in its own prose, so both PASSED WITHOUT THEIR SUBJECT BEING IN THE FILE AT ALL. Batch CD reported them and deliberately did not repair them; this is that repair, on the pattern CD gave test_batch_bb. The anchor is the <h2> heading rather than a phrase (a phrase is something a later entry's prose can reproduce), and the archive's path is read out of the live changelog's own header rather than hardcoded, so a later split moves both checks for free. One consequence, stated rather than buried: two more suites now depend on a file that is not in version control, and on a machine without the archive they FAIL LOUDLY — which is correct, and is the exact fault this repair exists to close.

§6 — what shipped beside the nine

Five statuses for nine abilities, and the split between the two lists is BU's Suffering trap written down rather than inferred. Three sit on HOLY (matins, alms, observance) and are correctly absent from DEBUFF_IDS; two sit on an ENEMY (anathema, penance) and are genuine afflictions, so both are LISTED — which makes them cleansable by a mender's Cleansing Rite (real counterplay, and neither is battle-long so neither is taken first every time) and, the half that matters, keeps them OUT of the derived _dispellable_buffs set, so a Mage's own Dispel can never strip the party's work off the enemy carrying it. MANTLE REGISTERS NO STATUS OF ITS OWN: it rides the existing barrier, which is precisely what makes every hop a real Divine Shield. Elevation, Jubilee and Requiem resolve inside the cast that fires them and carry nothing.

ONE new unit-side field for nine abilities — barrier_broken_cb, a door rather than a number, fired when a barrier is exhausted and removed. Its position is the whole contract: it sits in the else branch below Unyielding Aegis, so a shield the Aegis re-forms has not broken and does not pass.

Break damage assigned deliberately (the BO rule, applied up front). TWO of the nine carry it and SEVEN do not, and each of the seven is a decision rather than an oversight: Anathema 20 (one Hex of Ruin's worth — the card sells the multiplier, not the number) and Requiem 8 (flat, level with Arcane Bolt). Six of the others land no blow at all, and PENANCE is the interesting zero: it genuinely deals damage, but on the enemy's own clock as a tick, where Break has nothing to ride.

The bot got no rotation, on purpose — all nine ride BO §5's wrapper, so no existing rotation is re-weighted and no measurement taken before this batch stops being comparable. Four targeting refinements, each closing a case where the default mark makes a card read as inert: Requiem aims at the DEEPEST pile (aimed at the lowest-health enemy it would eat two stacks off something about to die), Anathema at the boss or the highest-health body (a three-turn mark on the enemy about to die spends its window on a corpse), Penance at the HIGHEST-ATTACK enemy (which is the point of the card), and Mantle never at an ally already wearing a shield (a re-cast merges into the standing barrier and would overwrite a live mantle's remaining passes with this cast's).

One glossary entry added (90 → 91): mercy_window. Matins and Alms both read the same line and a player had nowhere to learn either edge of it — that Mercy pays for a CROSSING and not for a state (a party already bloodied pays her nothing), that GUARDIAN ANGEL moves the line, and that a stack earned at the cap is thrown away unless Grace or Alms catches it. Everything else the nine do is a mechanic the player already meets.

§7 — verified

Per the standing instruction, "verified" means the code landed and works. NO SWEEPS, NO BANDS, NO BALANCE MEASUREMENT WAS RUN, and none should be quoted from this batch. check_parse 0 · check_flow 0 · check_map_screen OK · run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS at 22 / 165 / 8 checks (CA's recorded counts, unmoved) · NEW test_batch_ce.gd 1063/0.

Every clause that could silently do nothing is driven live, and for most of them the obvious assertion is not the discriminating one. MATINS is driven THREE times — unbroken (must pay), immediately after a fall (must pay nothing) and again the turn after (must pay again), so a no-flag version fails the second and a LATCHING one the third. ALMS is driven BELOW the cap as well as at it, and asserted NOT to be a Divine Shield. OBSERVANCE's discriminator is Divine Plea's perfect — 10 Mana, an exact integer — measured beside the Mercy actually spent (3 against 4). ELEVATION is driven on an ally at 4 (untouched), one at 0 (raised to 3) and one at 2, and NOBODY's count may move. JUBILEE asserts everything a release would ALSO have done and this must not. MANTLE is driven with the holder made the LOWEST HEALTH IN THE PARTY, the only arrangement in which a naive pick bounces it in place. ANATHEMA drives the same 20 Break into a marked enemy and an unmarked control — 30 against 20, exact. REQUIEM builds 5 and 20 stacks on identical bodies and asserts the damage RATIO with open ground. PENANCE uses two enemies with DIFFERENT Attack stats, which is the only construction that tells the target's Attack from the caster's.

EIGHTEEN NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each applied to product code and reverted — battle.gd, unit.gd and classes.gd all came back byte-identical by hash — and ALL EIGHTEEN TRIP. Matins' watch never broken trips 2; the flag LATCHING trips 1; Alms warding on every Mercy gain trips 1; the ward made divine trips 1; Observance never keeping the perfect trips 2; the Hymn's Empowered share written FIRST trips 1; Elevation ADDING peak trips 1; Elevation granting Faith trips 4; Jubilee lowering his peak trips 1; Jubilee growing the principal trips 2; Mantle passing back to the body it left trips 3; the hop count never decrementing trips 3; Anathema's mark landing before its own Break trips 1; the Break amplifier deleted trips 2; Requiem leaving the primer trips 1; Requiem paying flat trips 2; Penance reading the CASTER's Attack trips 2; and a spec card leaking into a class pool trips 5.

ONE OF THEM PASSED ON THE FIRST RUN AND FOUND A CHECK THAT COULD NOT FAIL — which is the whole reason to run them. "Elevation ADDS peak instead of raising a floor" tripped NOTHING: the ally on 4 is skipped by the loop's own >= floor guard before the write is ever reached, and the ally on 0 lands on 3 under either reading. Only a peak BETWEEN the two discriminates — an ally on 2 goes to 3 correctly and to 5 wrongly. That third ally is in the suite now and the control trips.

LIVE AUTOPLAY CLEAN, 0 SCRIPT ERROR across four smoke battles, with the cards firing in ordinary fights — "Matins — for 4 turns she gains 1 Mercy at the start of each of her turns on which nobody fell [PERFECT]" followed by three "the office is kept — Holy gains 1 Mercy (3/5) … (4/5) … (5/5)" lines (the ABOVE-tick_statuses placement visible in the log: a 3-turn office pays three times), "Alms — for 6 turns Mercy earned at the cap wards the ally who earned it (12% of her maximum) [PERFECT]", "Elevation — 4 ally(s) raised to a PEAK of 4 Faith for the rest of the battle [PERFECT]", "Mantle — Devout is shielded for 40, and when it breaks it passes 2 more time(s)" followed by "Mantle: the broken shield passes from Devout to Pyromancer (1 pass(es) left)", "Anathema — Orc Chief takes +23 BD now, and every source of Break lands 50% harder on it for 4 turns [PERFECT]" followed by "!! Orc Chief BREAKS (Anathema)", "Requiem — 3 stacks of Ruin consumed for 29 shadow, and 3 ally(s) mended 25 in all", and "Penance — Orc Chief is set to pay 20 shadow before its resistances" followed by "Orc Chief pays its penance — 20 shadow damage".

Two log-honesty fixes found by watching the smoke rather than by a test, both the same shape as BT's Inner Arcane: Requiem announced the party heal it ASKED for rather than what landed (an ally at full health takes none of it), and Penance's cast line printed a pre-resistance figure without saying so. Both say what they mean now. Note the smoke's own artefact: DOD_SIM_ABILITIES hands every card to every hero, so a Beastmaster lays a Mantle and a Berserker keeps an office in the logs — the real draft only ever offers spec-matching cards, and it is exactly what makes the "he holds no Mercy" and "only the Devout carries Faith that never releases" lines worth having.

§7 — the numbers this batch is least sure of

ANATHEMA'S 50% IS THE NUMBER THE DESIGNER TRUSTS LEAST AND IT SHIPS UNTUNED, to be watched in play (Threshold's 15, one tranche later). Too low and a boss's Break stays out of reach whatever he spends; too high and the Madness gate stops being a gate at all. OBSERVANCE'S VALUE IS THE OTHER ONE — three of five Empowerable casts, and each of those three perfects is small. Both are flagged rather than pre-tuned.

2026-08-16 — Batch CD: seven script errors, one wrong target count

No game code changed — no ability, no talent node, no magnitude, no save version (still v10). The battery reported zero failures and SEVEN THROWS across five suites. It reports zero of both now. The finding is the arithmetic rather than the repairs: closing the throws put 2,714 assertions back into the battery — those five suites totalled 12,327 checks before and 15,041 after — and every one of them passed.

§1 — the seven throws

A count is the instrument, and five of them had been reading low for as long as twelve batches. Batch CA found the run harness printing GATE 2 PASS on zero assertions and wrote the rule that a gate reports its check count rather than a verdict. The suites were never brought under it. Each of these five was aborting a function partway and still printing a clean line:

SuiteWhat threwDeleted atBeforeAfter
test_batch_anRun.award_talent_pointsBM §636196053
test_batch_ahRun.award_talent_pointsBM §655005625
test_runesrun.start_rune_enabled()AN29733121
test_batch_bbthe changelog anchorarchived at BZ168175
test_batch_bja plateless BattleUnit.new() (×3)—6767

The shape was one shape four times and a different one once, and the difference is what decides the cost. A GDScript runtime error aborts the function it happens in and resumes in the caller. So a dead CALL in a suite's own body eats every check below it in that function — four of the five, and all 2,714 of the missing checks were theirs — while an error raised deeper, inside product code the suite called, eats only the product function. That is why bj's three cost nothing and its count did not move, exactly as Batch BX recorded. They are repaired anyway: a suite that spews stderr is a suite whose stderr nobody reads, and the seventh throw was sitting in that noise.

ah and an — the in-run talent economy. Both re-pointed in place as INVERSIONS. Batch BM §6 deleted the whole thing, so what is asserted is the deletion: no award_talent_points, no award_spec_point, no member["talent_points"], no talent_flex — with the live door (bank_zone_boss_points) asserted present. Its behaviour is deliberately not re-driven here. The run harness's gate 2 already drives it against a scratch Profile with six negative controls, and a second copy would be a second answer to one question. an's “guaranteed floor is 2 points a zone” inverted onto the board instead — one mini-boss, one boss, unduckable — because under BM the floor is a property of the route rather than of the node types.

bb — the changelog anchor Batch BZ archived, and BZ predicted this exactly. log.contains("Batch BB") went on passing, because two LATER entries name the batch in their own prose; the slice underneath then threw Out of bounds get index '1'. It reads the archive now, and it finds the archive by reading the live changelog's own header rather than by hardcoding a path — BZ made both halves carry the other's full path precisely so a reader could follow it, so the check follows the repo's own pointer and a later split moves it for free. One consequence, stated rather than buried: a suite in the repo now depends on a file that is not in version control. On a machine without the archive it fails loudly, which is correct — a check that passed quietly when its subject was missing is the exact fault this batch exists to close.

bj — three throws on a bare unit. sync_victory_state opens with expire_fortified_spirit, whose unconditional remove_status (idempotence is what makes the unconditional call safe) refreshes a chip row that only exists once a plate is built. Fixed by building the plate, which is Batch BX's own lesson that unit-side code wants a real unit. It costs one detached Node2D and keeps the suite in _initialize with no scene, no autoload and no battle.

runes — and this one had lost the most in proportion. The dead call was the FIRST line of _start_rune_pool, so the whole function aborted and its 144-triple drift alarm had not run since Batch AN deleted the opening rune pick. The name is pinned absent and the measurement re-pointed at the one live caller of roll_rune_candidates, which is the elite rune cache. The rate reads 34% against Batch AE's 36-42% — the first re-measure since AN, inside the suite's own 20-70% alarm band, reported rather than re-banded.

§2 — the draft target is 120, not ~96

96 spec (twelve specs at eight apiece) + 24 class-wide = 120. The draft stands at 93, and 27 are owed: Cleric nine, Hunter nine, Warrior nine, three per spec. The ~96 came from an older assumption of six spec cards per spec, and Batch CB completed the Mage at eight. test_batch_bt has asserted depth 8 since CB, so the tests encoded the right figure for a whole batch while the prose contradicted it.

The instruction to sweep rather than fix the two known sites is what earned its keep. The stale denominator was in master.html §6b, in CLAUDE.md (three places), in FOUR suite messages, and in THREE comments in classes.gd — and two of those comments were stale in a second way nobody had noticed, still recording the Warrior pools as sitting “at two” three batches after Batch BW took them to five. Dated batch blocks and changelog entries keep ~96 as written (Batch CA's rule — they are the record of what each batch believed); the standing reference is the correction.

One check that could only pass was found by correcting its message. test_batch_br asserted that master.html contained the string "48" — which turns up in any document with enough numbers in it — under the message “the pool count moved to 48 of ~96”. It asks BR's real question now: does master.html state the LIVE pool count against the REAL target?

§3 — the letter CC is spent

A batch document CC was authored (pixel art) and deliberately never run. Nothing of it is in the repo and nothing of it will be. Recorded so that a later reader does not take the gap between CB and CD for a lost or failed batch: there is nothing to look for.

§4 — the two flakes, and the brief was wrong about one of them

§4 recorded both of Batch CA's failures as coming back clean on this commit and asked for them to be logged as NOT REPRODUCING rather than as fixed. test_rune_battle is: 97/0 seven times.

test_batch_br is not. It reproduced on the baseline battery pass — at CA's exact check, §3: Iron Will really cuts the damage (31 taken against 31) — and then read 1441/0 eight times running. So it is roughly one pass in nine, it is the same check with the same signature (two blows landing EQUAL), and CA's diagnosis is confirmed rather than merely repeated: Batch BS §3's variance roll, a 15% cut compared one blow against one blow. Reported, not repaired. The repair is BS's own prescription — amplify the term for the measurement and assert a ratio with open ground — and it is BR's thread, not a hygiene batch's.

§5 — the suite, and why it costs what it costs

test_batch_cd.gd is the only suite in the project that can see a throw. §1 does not grep the five repairs, it RUNS them — five child Godots via OS.execute with read_stderr on — because a script error is invisible to the suite it happens in, and a grep for the dead call this batch removed would pass the day a different dead call arrives. It reads three things off each child: zero SCRIPT ERROR, zero failures, and a check count at or above a floor. A floor rather than a pin, because an and ah walk generated boards and drift by construction, and because §1's rule is “equal or higher”. The recursion hazard is named in the file. It roughly doubles the wall clock of those five suites in a battery run; that is the price of the one question.

Two of its source sweeps failed against correct code first, and the reason is Batch BS's rule re-learned twice in one batch. Every repair NAMES its dead symbol on purpose — in a tombstone comment saying why it went, and in a has_method("...") assertion pinning it absent — so a bare contains flags exactly the files that are right, and invites the next author to delete the line telling them not to bring the call back. The sweep strips comments and string literals and looks for a CALL, which is the only form that can throw, and it ships with a positive control beside it, because a stripper returning "" would make it pass forever. The same shape hit §2 from the documentation side: this batch's own correction has to WRITE ~96 in order to say it is dead, so what is banned is the phrase that STATES a target, not the string.

No new stamp gate. master.html moved to Batch CD, so all THIRTEEN duplicated stamp gates moved with it — ah, bb, bn, bo, bp, bq, br, bs, bt, bu, bv, bw, bx. test_batch_cd deliberately does not add a fourteenth; it checks the master.html CONTENT this batch is responsible for, which is the Batch CB precedent.

Reported, not repaired — two more checks that pass without their subject. test_batch_bn and test_batch_bo each hold one bare changelog.contains("Batch BN"/"Batch BO"), and a LATER entry naming the batch in its own prose satisfies it, so both pass with their entries archived out of the file entirely. It is the same gap §1 exists to close, arriving without a throw to announce it. The fix is bb's pattern applied twice and it is one line each.
