2026-08-15 — Batch CB: tranche 3, the Mage nine (THE MAGE IS THE FIRST CLASS COMPLETE)

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Mage spec. The Mage pools go 5 → 8 and the draft goes 84 → 93 of a target ~96. The Pyromancer, the Cryomancer and the Arcanist are the first specs in the game to draft from EIGHT; the other nine still draft from five, so the asymmetry tranche 2 removed is back and pointing the other way — what is owed now is the Cleric, Hunter and Warrior thirds of tranche 3. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, no save version moves (still v10). ONE new unit-side field for nine abilities — and it is not a field at all: every one of the nine is carried by a status or by an existing counter, per BQ's standard.

THE BRIEF'S FIRST INSTRUCTION WAS TO VERIFY RATHER THAN ASSUME, AND TWO OF ITS FOUR PREMISES DID NOT HOLD. Both are corrected toward the code (the AR §6 / AX §7 / BD §3 / AY §1 / BS / BT / BU / BX precedent), and one of them moved a card's name.

§1 — what the sweep found

  • BACKDRAFT IS NOT FREE, AND THE CARD WAS RENAMED. This is the first time BR §1's sweep has forced a rename since BW's Vendetta, and unlike a label collision it is a REAL BREAK. §1 asked for confirmation that BS's rebuild removed the old Kindling row-4 node. It did not: py_melt both carries the name Backdraft AND grants an ability whose display_name is Backdraft (20 Mana, 2.0, 3cd — +2 turns of Burn to every burning enemy). What BS actually renamed was the INFERNO row-5 node, to Backblast, to dodge exactly this collision. Classes.pool_ability is keyed on display_name, so a second Backdraft would make the resolver answer the wrong question. The card ships as FIREDRAW, swept clean against every ability, talent node, status and rune. test_batch_cb pins the collision in assertion form — the node still named Backdraft, the name still resolving to the TALENT's ability, and no draft card answering to it — so a later batch cannot quietly restore the brief's name.
  • NOTHING BINDS TWO ENEMIES TOGETHER, so Frostbind is the first. Three things came close and none is this: soul_bond (One Soul) links the hunter to his companions and DIVIDES a blow, covenant mirrors Ruin STACKS one-way from any enemy onto a bearer, and umbral_sigil echoes damage to a whole party rather than to a partner. Hence the new glossary entry.
  • THERE IS NO COMBINED RESISTANCE-AND-ARMOR BYPASS DOOR — THERE ARE TWO, AND NOTHING HAD EVER CROSSED BOTH. §1 suspected one hook on the strength of BP's Precision Strike. Armor has a genuine bypass arm (effective_armor = 0.0, shared by Through and Through, Held Breath, One Shot and Open Guard); resistance has NO outright bypass at all — avatar_flame is fire-only and positive-only, and rune_resist_pierce THINS a resistance by a fraction. Unmaking is written at both sites and the suite asserts both, because deleting one would leave the card's description promising something it no longer does.
  • The other eight names are clean. Two adjacencies are reported and not resolved: Resonant Field sits beside the Rune of the Resonant Core (different string, different namespace), and Threshold is a word several code identifiers use (RUIN_THRESHOLD, mercy_threshold) and no player-facing name uses.

§2 — Pyromancer: consolidate it, scatter it, and make it arrive bigger

His whole pool moves fire that already exists — Cinderfall skims it, Stoke doubles one stack, Funeral Pyre spends it, Ember Debt places it — and nothing in it changed how much arrives.

  • FIREDRAW (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy) — consumes 4 turns of Burn from every OTHER enemy (Perfect: 6) and adds all of it to this one. Axis: the bank consolidated. It takes what is there or 4, whichever is less — an enemy holding 2 gives 2, not a debt — and it never touches the target's own Burn. Builds with Total Commitment, Powder Keg and Cataclysm; the deliberate counterpart to Cinderfall.
  • PYRE WAKE (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy) — consumes ALL its Burn; for each turn consumed a random enemy is set Burning 1 turn and takes 8% of Attack (Perfect: 12%). Axis: the bank scattered rather than cashed — a twelve-turn stack becomes twelve small fires and 96% of Attack across the board. The only card in the game that converts DEPTH into WIDTH. Builds with Sea of Flame and Slow Burn.
  • EMBERKEEP (20 Mana, 1.5, 4cd, self) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every Burn he applies lands at DOUBLE duration. Axis: the multiplier on GETTING fire. Firestorm's 6–8 bolts each land 4 turns instead of 2 — 24 to 32 burn-turns from one cast.

EMBERKEEP IS ONE CLAUSE AT _apply_status's eff_turns BLOCK, SCOPED TO THE SRC EXACTLY AS PERMAFROST IS. That is what makes an enemy Ashblade's burn, a rune's burn and a second applier's burn all correctly untouched, and why there is no per-ability list to keep up to date — Fireball, Flamewave, Firestorm, Ember Debt, Cinder Trail and anything a later batch adds ride it by doing nothing. It doubles at APPLICATION and is not retroactive: fire already on the board is Stoke's subject, and the two must not collapse into each other (the Deadfall/Snare Trap duplication BD found, avoided up front). ONE GUARD IN IT IS LOAD-BEARING and is BV's full_turns lesson through a new door: it doubles only a POSITIVE turn count, because a negative one is a PERMANENCE FLAG rather than a duration and doubling −1 into −2 would quietly un-permanent a battle-long fire.

HIS TRANSFERS RIDE THE WINDOW TOO, AND THAT IS DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN CARVED OUT. Firedraw's deposit is an application of Burn by him, so under an Emberkeep it arrives doubled — a real two-card combo, and the alternative (an exemption at a shared door) is the kind of invisible special case this file keeps warning about. It is also what makes the target-exclusion TESTABLE: the transfer is otherwise CONSERVATIVE, so a version that wrongly drew from its own target lands on the same total and passes every obvious assertion. Under the window the two readings diverge loudly — 22 against 26 — and that is the check the suite ships.

PYRE WAKE IS THE SIXTH CONSUMER OF THE ONE REFUND DOOR (_overburn_refund), which is AR's rule still working: a new Burn consumer arrives and inherits the refund with no second implementation, Crucible's doubling included. The pinned call-site count goes 5 → 6. Its Overburn multiplier is read BEFORE the consume — Detonation's ordering rule since AG — so the cast is not paid for the turns it is about to destroy.

§3 — Cryomancer: copy wide, hit the prisoner, chain two bodies

  • DEEP WINTER (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, no target) — every enemy gains Chilled equal to HALF the stacks on the held enemy, rounded down (Perfect: up). Axis: the hold as a template, applied wide. Holding nothing it does nothing, and the log says so rather than fizzling silently (§3's own instruction). The stacks go on ONE _apply_status call at a time — Killing Frost's rule — so a fourth stack still flash-freezes and BN's guard covers the card for free.
  • COLD IRON (20 Mana, 2.0, 3cd, one enemy, 6 BD) — 25% of Attack (Perfect: 35%), DOUBLE against a Frozen target, and it does NOT release the hold. Axis: hitting the prisoner without opening the cell. The hold is a party-wide +15% damage window that only he can close, and until now nothing of his own could safely strike into it — Ice Lance IS the release.
  • FROSTBIND (25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, TWO enemies) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) the pair is bound: Chilled landing on either lands on both, and damage dealt to one is dealt to the other at 40%. Axis: two prisoners on one chain.

§3'S SECOND RULE WAS CONDITIONAL AND THE CONDITION WAS FALSE. It asked for an automatic most-Chilled second target “if nothing selects two enemies today”. Ability.choose_two has existed since Shrapnel Charge and Hex of Ruin uses choose_three beside it, so the UI answer already shipped and the player picks both bodies. §3's rule is kept where it actually bites — as the FALLBACK when no second target was chosen, which is the BOT's path (autoplay skips the clicks) and the one-enemy-left path. Without it _resolve's generic fallback picks a RANDOM partner, and a bond is not a card anyone wants aimed at random.

THE OTHER TWO RULES SHIP AS SPECIFIED AND BOTH ARE ASSERTED. The 40% mirror does not itself mirror (_frostbind_mirroring, a re-entrancy lock on the _rime_echoing/_bitter_echoing/_echoing pattern — a bond that recursed is the AS crash in a new costume, and each pass being 40% of the last would not even terminate on the damage running out before the stack did), and the Chilled copy has a lock of its own (_frostbinding) because the two halves recurse through DIFFERENT functions. The mirror rides BL's ONE damage-taken door, so a strike, a splash, an echo, a Burn tick, a Killing Frost and a Winter's Toll all mirror without a list of sources — and it sits ABOVE that function's hero gate, because its victims are enemies and everything below the gate is hero-side bookkeeping. It carries no Break, deliberately: a bond that doubled the party's Break output would be a second axis nobody asked for.

ONE THING FROSTBIND'S OWN TEXT PROMISED WAS FALSE BY ONE LINE, AND IT WAS FOUND BY DRIVING IT RATHER THAN BY READING IT. “If both partners reach the threshold the pair freezes together — which is how a one-hold Cryomancer comes to hold two” could not happen: the second partner's freeze pushed _holds.size() past a limit of 1 and immediately evicted the first, so the pair took turns being held. The card LOOKED like it worked, because one of the two really was frozen. The eviction loop counts CELLS now (_hold_cells()) and a frostbound pair is ONE cell. It is deliberately NOT a limit increase — that is what Second Prison and Absolute Zero buy, and bumping the limit here would make them free — and a THIRD enemy still evicts the pair, oldest first.

VERIFIED AGAINST ICE LANCE, AS §3 ASKED, AND COLD IRON DOES NOT OUTCLASS IT. Against a Frozen target the Lance lands 55% of Attack (35% + 5% per Chilled stack) and ALWAYS crits — 110%+ — for 15 Break, and it IS the release; Cold Iron lands 50% at ordinary crit odds for 6 Break. It is cheaper (20 against 25) and faster (2.0 against 3.0) on a LONGER cooldown (3 against 2), and what it is sold on is not opening the cell. The suite drives both in the same battle, because “it does not release” is trivially true of a battle where nothing releases.

§4 — Arcanist: share the curve, buy it early, make it unanswerable

  • RESONANT FIELD (25 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, no target) — for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every ALLY deals bonus damage equal to HALF his current Resonance bonus. Axis: the curve arms the party — the cross-spec card the pool does not have. At 12 stacks he is at +117%, so allies get +58%.
  • THRESHOLD (20 Mana, 1.5, 5cd, self) — his Resonance is SET to 15 at once and he can gain none for 3 turns (Perfect: 2). Axis: the late game bought early, at the cost of the ramp.
  • UNMAKING (30 Mana, 3.0, 5cd, one enemy, 8 BD) — 10% of Attack per Resonance stack, resistances AND armor ignored, and it cannot be healed for 3 turns (Perfect: 4). Axis: the curve made unanswerable.

RESONANT FIELD READS HIS BONUS LIVE, AND THE STATUS CARRIES NO NUMBER AT ALL — Null Field's rule, for its reason: stamping the value at cast time would freeze it and delete the card's whole axis, and it would read exactly like the card working. It resolves the Arcanist through the src_name _apply_status already stamps rather than by scanning for “a living hero holding Resonance”, because one Mage stands in a party today and a scan is a rule that happens to be right. A dead Arcanist pays nobody (_covering_warden's call: his body is the ward). It is the FOURTH user of the one implementation of “this unit deals N% more damage”, so it composes additively with Battle Shout, Warcry and Reckless Abandon; and he is excluded from his own field, because he already deals the full bonus and half of it again would make a card sold on SHARING the curve into a self-multiplier on it.

THRESHOLD'S LOCKOUT IS ONE LINE AT _gain_resonance, THE ONE DOOR. Every source of Resonance in the game comes through that function, so refusing there refuses all of them without naming any — the passive's own +1 a damaging cast, Kindled Mind, Inner Arcane, Cascade, Critical Mass, Backlash, On the Edge, Entropy's toll and Singularity's crit and kill builds alike. A list at the card would go stale the first time a node was added, and it would go stale SILENTLY. Threshold itself does not come through that door: it SETS the meter, which can move it DOWN, and the door only ever adds. The damage-taken penalty arrives with the stacks — the curve is read live and knows nothing about how the meter got there — so 15 stacks is +90% damage taken on the spot.

FLAGGED: 15 IS THE NUMBER THE DESIGNER TRUSTS LEAST IN THIS BATCH. Too low and the card is never worth casting; too high and it skips the spine the whole spec is built on. SHIPPED TO BE WATCHED IN PLAY. DO NOT PRE-TUNE IT.

THE UNMAKING / DEATH RAY COMPARISON WAS ASKED FOR AND THE ANSWER IS NOT THE COMFORTABLE ONE. REPORTED, NOT RE-TUNED. Death Ray is 150% of Attack flat at 55 Mana and a 5.0 delay, so the crossover is EXACTLY 15 STACKS (10 × 15 = 150) and above it Unmaking deals MORE raw damage for 25 less Mana and 2.0 less delay. Both are multiplied by the same Resonance curve, so the comparison is on the base percentage. What Death Ray keeps is a shorter cooldown (3 against 5) and a gate at 8 rather than 1; what Unmaking is justified on is the double bypass and the heal lock. And THRESHOLD, one card above it in the same pool, sets him to exactly 15 — so the two cards meet precisely at the crossover, which is worth knowing before either number is moved.

UNMAKING'S BREAK IS FLAT RATHER THAN PER-STACK, which is Arcane Bolt's own rule: a per-stack Break term is Arcane Cannon's and Magi's Wrath's axis, and duplicating it here is the squaring trap AT exists around arriving through the Break door. Its resist bypass ZEROES rather than clamping, so a WEAKNESS is destroyed along with a resistance — the honest reading of “its resistances are ignored”, and it costs the card real damage against a vulnerable target. Keeping weaknesses would make an ability sold on beating defence also the best card against no defence, which is a strictly-better card wearing a bypass's clothes (BD §4). The heal lock joins the ABSOLUTE refusals in unit.heal_amount (Bloodless, Ancient Pact, Caught Fast, Weight of Ruin, Blight the Well) rather than the multiplier block, for BM's stated reason: “cannot be healed” is a RULE, not an amount.

§5 — one card set aside deliberately

ASH WAKE — for 3 turns, every enemy that dies sets every other enemy Burning — was authored for this tranche and the designer moved it to the RUNE PILE instead. Recorded here so it is not re-authored as a draft card later, and so whoever writes the next rune batch knows it is waiting.

Break damage, assigned deliberately

The standing rule since BO, applied up front. TWO of the nine carry it and seven do not, and each of the seven is a decision rather than an omission. Cold Iron 6 — level with Killing Frost, his other tranche-2 attack, and well below the FREE Frostbolt's 15, which is BQ's floor rule (a card that supplements the free basic must not out-Break it). Unmaking 8 — level with Arcane Bolt and flat, for the reason above. PYRE WAKE IS THE INTERESTING ZERO: it genuinely deals damage and still carries none, because its hit count is UNBOUNDED (a twelve-turn stack is twelve hits) and a per-hit Break term on an uncapped count is the same squaring trap from a third direction. The other six land no blow at all.

Statuses, and the two lists

FIVE STATUSES FOR NINE ABILITIES, and the split between the two lists is BU's suffering trap written down rather than inferred. Three sit on a HERO (emberkeep, resonant_field, threshold_lock) and are correctly absent from DEBUFF_IDS. Two sit on an ENEMY (frostbind, unmade) and are genuine afflictions, so both are listed — which makes them cleansable by a mender's Cleansing Rite (real counterplay, and neither is battle-long so neither is taken first every time) and, the half that actually matters, keeps them OUT of the derived _dispellable_buffs set, so a Mage's own Dispel can never strip the party's work off the enemy carrying it. Firedraw, Pyre Wake, Deep Winter and Cold Iron resolve inside the cast that fires them and carry nothing.

The bot

NO ROTATION, ON PURPOSE — all nine ride BO §5's wrapper, so no existing rotation is re-weighted and no measurement taken before this batch stops being comparable (BP, BQ, BR, BT, BU, BV and BW each did the same). FOUR TARGETING REFINEMENTS inside that wrapper, each closing a case where the default mark makes a card read as inert: Firedraw and Pyre Wake aim at the DEEPEST burning stack (for opposite reasons — one does not touch its target's fire, so the deepest gives the deepest result; the other consumes all of it, so the deepest is the widest scatter); Cold Iron aims at a FROZEN enemy, without which a smoke measures a 25% strike and never once exercises the clause the card is sold on; Frostbind takes the deepest Chilled pile as its first body so the pair it chains is the pair closest to freezing together; and Unmaking aims at the HIGHEST-health enemy, because a three-turn heal lock aimed at the enemy about to die spends its window on a corpse (Arcane Echo's case, and Suffering's).

Documentation

docs/master.html stamped Batch CB; §6b's draft tables gain the nine with their Builds with lines, the pool summary moves to eight for the three Mage specs, and the table's intro states the count (93) and that the Mage is the first class complete. One glossary entry added (89 → 90): status_bound, because Frostbind is the first two-enemy link in the game and a player meeting the chip has nowhere else to learn that the mirror does not mirror back or that a bound pair costs one hold slot rather than two.

One more repair, found by re-reading the shipped code

Frostbind's mirror carried a comment claiming the damage frame was saved and restored “or every later hit of the same cast would book against the bond” — but nothing ever SET a bond frame, so the restore was a no-op and the sentence described a hazard the code was not handling. The code moved rather than the comment: the frame names the bond while the bond is dealing damage. Underneath it was a second fault — the mirrored damage credited nobody, which is BB's _ghost_hit finding arriving through a new door. It books to the Cryomancer who laid the bond, resolved through the src_name the status carries, so a second Cryomancer could never collect on the first one's chain; a dead caster credits nothing and the bond keeps working, because the chain is on the enemies rather than on him. The transferable half is the comment, not the credit: a comment describing a hazard the code does not actually handle is worse than no comment, because it tells the next reader the question has already been answered — and this one would have survived every test in the suite.

Verified

Per the standing instruction, that means THE CODE LANDED AND WORKS. NO SWEEPS, NO BANDS, NO BALANCE MEASUREMENT WAS RUN, and none should be quoted from this batch.

check_parse 0 · check_flow 0 · check_map_screen OK · run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS at 22 / 165 / 8 checks (Batch CA's recorded counts, unmoved) · NEW test_batch_cb.gd 1154 / 0, stable across runs. Seventeen negative controls, each applied to product code and reverted — battle.gd, unit.gd and classes.gd all came back byte-identical by hash — and all seventeen trip. None passed. Live autoplay clean with all nine firing in ordinary fights, 0 SCRIPT ERROR.

Full battery green, zero failures anywhere across 43 suites. ah 5500, ah_battle 65, ai 2217, aj 418, ak 528, al 560, ar 735, as 396, at 470, au 336, av 324, aw 350, ax 339, ay 484, az 519, ba 690, bb 168, bc 91, bd 69, be 34, bf 78, bg 47, bh 233, bi 88, bj 67, bl 88, bm 1891, bn 77, bo 832, bp 271, bq 738, br 1441, bs 262, bt 460, bu 476, bv 893, bw 545, bx 141, cb 1154, runes 2973, rune_battle 97. (an 3622 and bk 130 sit inside their documented run-to-run drift and are not pinned.) 2026-08-15 — Batch CA: twelve batches of hollow verification

THE FINDING IS THE ENTRY; THE FIX IS ITS CONSEQUENCE. From Batch BM to Batch BY, every VERIFIED block in this changelog that reads “run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS” was quoting a gate that ran NOT ONE ASSERTION. GATE 2's first statement was a call to a function BM had deleted, and it sat above every check in the function — so the error aborted the whole body, no check ran, no check failed, and the gate printed GATE 2 PASS on the way out. 129 of BM's own replacement assertions had never executed once. Twelve batches of evidence rested on a word that was never earned. No game code changes in this batch: no ability, no talent node, no magnitude, no save version (still v10), and master.html is deliberately untouched, so the stamp gate does not move.

§1 What actually happened, and why it is a shape rather than a typo

  • test_run_harness.gd:125 called run.award_spec_point, which Batch BM §6 deleted when talents became meta progression. GDScript aborts the executing function on a nonexistent-method error. That line sat above every _check in _gate_talent_conservation.
  • The verdict was computed from a failure counter that the abort had left at zero. _go printed "PASS" if fails == 0 else "FAIL" — and with the body never entered, fails was 0, which is indistinguishable from a gate that ran two hundred checks and passed them all.
  • The aborted region was exactly the half BM re-pointed in place. BM's comment says it outright — “the income half of this gate measured a purse that no longer exists; what replaces it is the half that IS still load-bearing” — and that replacement half is what never ran.
  • The count of what was skipped is 129: one loadout check, eight across the party, and thirty per hero (a talent_order pin, nine single-rank checks, nine id-is-real checks, nine one-node-per-row checks, a purse pin and a depth check).

§2 WHY THIS ONE SURVIVED WHEN ah AND an DID NOT

Because it printed a word instead of a number. The two earlier hollow-verification cases in this project were caught because a figure looked wrong — a count that did not move, a rate that read zero. Nothing looks wrong about the string PASS.

A test that reports a QUANTITY is auditable at a glance; a test that reports a VERDICT is only auditable by reading it. That is recorded in docs/design-notes.md as the finding, separately from the fix, because it applies to every gate in the harness and to every future one.

§3 The structural changes — standing rules for EVERY gate

Repairing one call site would have left the shape intact: any future deleted function called inside a gate reproduces this exactly. Three rules, all small, and all binding on gates 1 and 3 as well — they carried the same latent fault. The brief asked for two; the third is this batch's and is flagged as such.

  • A GATE REPORTS ITS CHECK COUNT, NOT A VERDICT. GATE 2 PASS (165 checks), never a bare GATE 2 PASS. This is §2's lesson applied rather than merely recorded.
  • A GATE THAT RUNS ZERO CHECKS MUST FAIL. An empty gate is a broken gate, and it is the one case where silence has to be loud. A gate printing a count of zero is visibly broken; the same gate printing PASS is not.
  • A GATE MUST REACH ITS OWN END — a THIRD rule, added because the brief's two do not actually close the shape, and flagged rather than slipped in. Every gate's last statement is _finish(), and a gate that never got there fails. Rules 1 and 2 catch an abort ABOVE a gate's first check; an abort BELOW it leaves a NON-ZERO count, so it prints PASS (2 checks) — legible to a reader who already knows the number, and caught by nothing. §4 of the brief is titled “make the failure mode impossible, not just fixed”, and two rules only made it legible.
  • Applying rules 1 and 2 to every gate cost nothing beyond writing them once, because the counter lives in _check / _check_range and the rule lives in _go: gates 1 and 3 carried the same latent fault and needed no edit of their own. Rule 3 costs one line per gate. Rules 3 and 2 are exclusive, so a gate that aborts above its first check reports one problem once rather than twice.
  • The unknown-DOD_GATE branch was routed through _check so a bad gate id is a FAILED CHECK rather than a bare failure — otherwise it would trip the zero-check rule as well and report one problem twice.

§4 The re-point, in two halves

The original subject was talent spend conservation — points earned against points paid inside one run, replayed against a price curve. Batch BM deleted the thing being conserved: talents are meta now, bought per spec on Profile out of zone-boss income and equipped before a run begins, so there is no in-run purse. This is a re-point with a reason, and the reason is written into the file above the function.

  • §1 INCOME — A RUN AWARDS NOTHING. Batch BK's map walk is kept and inverted: it drives the real generated board (49 encounters, three zone bosses, one end boss) and asserts it pays nothing at all. The node types are asserted PRESENT first, so “nothing paid” cannot be satisfied by a board nobody crossed. Then the one door, Run.bank_zone_boss_points: a SIM banks nothing (the sim_run guard, which a later batch could delete with nothing else failing), a zone boss banks 1 per spec that played, a spec that did not play banks 0, two zone bosses bank 2 (a zone-2 wipe keeps what it cleared), an un-awakened hero banks nothing, and the END boss banks none — asserted against _resolve_boss's source, which is BM's own idiom for a rule with no reachable gate.
  • §2 THE LOADOUT — WHAT A RUN WEARS IS LEGAL. BM's assertions, executing for the first time: exactly one node per row, every id real, every rank 1, no in-run purse on the member, depth exactly RunSim.rows_built. They needed a loadout and never had one — new_run installs nothing, so every one of them would have FAILED on the day BM wrote it had the function reached them. The gate installs the build first.
  • The divergence from the brief, stated because the brief asked for it. Batch CA §3 offered the income rules as a starting point rather than an instruction. Both halves ship: the income half is the brief's list, and the loadout half is what the surviving lines actually asked. That second half is the one this harness owes — gates 1 and 3 pin what a sim's units are SPAWNED with, so gate 2 pins what a sim's heroes are BUILT with, and dropping it would have left RunSim.install_builds ungated by anything in the project.

§5 A check that could only ever pass, found on the way through

BM's closing line was _check("no points were spent in a run at all", replay_total, 0) — against a local initialised to 0 on the line above and never touched again. It is this batch's own lesson arriving from the other side, and it now asks the question mechanically: Talents.can_learn, purse_for, points_spent and MAX_PER_ROW are pinned ABSENT in the source, and can_buy / can_equip pinned PRESENT — buying and equipping being separate questions is the load-bearing rule of the whole talent system.

§6 The ledger is redirected, never written

Profile.save_path points at a scratch file for the whole of gate 2 and is restored afterwards (it is a var for exactly this; test_batch_bm's pattern). A gate that wrote the player's ledger would be a gate nobody could afford to run. sim_run is dropped for exactly three statements so the real banking path can be driven at all, and re-armed immediately; nothing in that window touches the run save. profile.json, relics.json and trees.json are byte-identical by hash across the whole batch, and no run_save.bin exists before or after — the designer had no run in flight.

§7 Verification — the acceptance test is that the gate CAN FAIL

A repair that only checks the happy path proves nothing, because a gate that passes when it should fail is the entire defect.

  • All three gates run and report a non-zero count: GATE 1 PASS (22 checks), GATE 2 PASS (165 checks), GATE 3 PASS (8 checks).
  • THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, and it reproduces the original defect on UNTOUCHED gates: the deleted run.award_spec_point call was put back ABOVE gate 1's checks — GATE 1 FAIL (0 checks) — and BELOW gate 3's first checks, the case rules 1 and 2 miss — GATE 3 FAIL (2 checks). Before this batch both constructions printed PASS.
  • SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each applied and reverted (run_state.gd, run_sim.gd and test_run_harness.gd all came back byte-identical by hash): an ELITE awarding a talent point trips 13; the zone boss banking nothing trips 11; the sim-purity guard deleted, so a sim writes the player's ledger, trips 12; a row holding every node instead of one trips 80; and the two abort controls above. None passed.
  • Gate 2 is stable at 165 checks over seven runs. Its one range check reads 16–23 walked ordinary fights inside a stated band of 9–33, so the band has headroom on both sides while still failing on a board that stopped generating fights.
  • check_parse 0 · check_flow 0 · check_map_screen OK · live autoplay clean at 0 SCRIPT ERROR over 87 log lines · build_docs.py exit 0.
  • FULL BATTERY, 42 SUITES, EVERY COUNT AT ITS RECORDED VALUE (an and bk inside their documented drift). One count moved and it is not this batch's: bb 172 → 168 — see below. profile.json, relics.json and trees.json are byte-identical by hash across the whole battery, and no run_save.bin exists before or after.

§8 Two failures, both known-bad — and one standing open item closed as a diagnosis

  • test_batch_br 1441/1, AND THE FAILING CHECK IS CAPTURED AT LAST: §3: Iron Will really cuts the damage (31 taken against 31). Batch BS recorded this exact flake as “seen once, not reproduced — the failing check was not captured”, and it has sat unnamed since. It read 1441/0 on three clean re-runs here. The diagnosis is BS's own lesson arriving in the suite that documented it: a 15% cut compared one blow against one blow with the ±10% variance roll live, so noise swamps the signal. BS's prescription is the fix — amplify the term for the measurement and assert a ratio with open ground, never a bare comparison of two blows. Reported, not repaired: nothing in this batch touches the Warrior class-card path.
  • test_rune_battle 97/1, pyromancer: rune_resist_pierce never fired against a resistant warband — the standing defect diagnosed at Batch BC (the check drives _resolve by hand and no_cover is armed nowhere in that file, so the forced hit still rolls the 5% miss). Unchanged and still not this batch's.
  • FOUR SUITES THROW SCRIPT ERRORS, ALL PRE-EXISTING — AND TWO OF THEM ARE THIS BATCH'S OWN DEFECT WEARING A SUITE'S CLOTHES. test_batch_ah and test_batch_an still call Run.award_talent_points, deleted at BM, so each aborts its own section while printing a count and zero failures — the identical shape GATE 2 had, in two suites, recorded since Batch BO and still open. Not repaired here for the same reason BY reported gate 2 rather than fixing it: it means authoring new assertions about a talent economy that no longer exists. test_batch_bb throws on the changelog anchor BZ archived, which is why its count fell 172 → 168 — four checks stopped existing and nothing failed, exactly as BZ predicted. test_batch_bj throws three of its own, reproduced on unmodified HEAD at BX. Read the counts, not only the failures.

2026-08-15 — Batch BZ: the changelog is split

THE NUMBER THIS BATCH EXISTS FOR: the knowledge-base sync goes from 5.43 MB across 169 text files to 4.73 MB across 168 — a saving of 711 KB, 12.8%. (The raw split saved 744 KB; this batch's own documentation — this entry, the guide's rewritten section, the design note and the README — spent 33 KB of it back, which is the honest figure and the one recorded.) BY recommended moving the whole changelog out of the repo; that would have cost docs/build_docs.py its relative path and removed all recent context from the sync. THIS SPLITS INSTEAD. The recent entries stay exactly where they are; only the old ones leave. Most of the saving, none of the breakage. NOTHING WAS DELETED. This is a move plus a split.

§1 Where the cut falls, and where the other half went

  • THE LIVE FILE, docs/changelog.html, NOW STARTS AT BATCH BP (2026-08-13, the Warrior draft pools) and runs forward to this entry. Eleven entries, 163 KB.
  • THE ARCHIVE, changelog-archive.html, ENDS AT BATCH BO (2026-08-13, the ability draft) and runs back to Batch 1 (2026-07-09). 108 entries, 696 KB.
  • The cut is at a batch boundary and no entry was edited — the two halves re-concatenate to the original file byte for byte, which is asserted rather than eyeballed (see §5).
  • IT LIVES AT /Users/zipples/Documents/DoD-archive/, outside the repo, beside the .docx exports. docs/addendum.html moved there whole — retired and frozen since 2026-07-08, and nothing but the project guide referenced it.
  • BOTH FILES CARRY A HEADER SAYING WHAT THEY ARE AND WHERE THE OTHER HALF IS, naming the batch each one stops at and the full path of its counterpart. In a year that will not be obvious from either file alone.

§2 THE RISK, STATED PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT IS THE COST OF THE SAVING

A FILE OUTSIDE THE REPO IS NOT IN VERSION CONTROL AND IS NOT BACKED UP BY GITHUB. If this machine is lost, an un-backed-up archive is lost with it. That must be a decision rather than a surprise, so here is the state of it as measured on the day of the split:

  • THIS MACHINE HAS NO BACKUP CONFIGURED. iCloud Drive is off (no ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs) and tmutil reports no Time Machine destinations. The archive folder therefore does NOT yet meet the requirement that it live somewhere the machine backs up. Reported, not worked around — the fix is switching on iCloud Drive for Documents, attaching a Time Machine target, or putting the archive in a second private repo, and that is the designer's call.
  • WHAT IS SAFE ANYWAY, AND IT IS MOST OF IT: every archived entry is still in this repo's git history and has been pushed to GitHub (commit 3725164, Batch BY, holds the whole 868 KB changelog). So the split did not create a single point of failure for the history that existed before it — it created one for anything written into the archive AFTER today, which should be nothing, because the archive is frozen by construction.

§3 What reads these files

  • docs/build_docs.py STILL RUNS — verified, exit 0, printing built .../DoD Master Document.docx and built .../DoD Changelog.docx. It reads the changelog by RELATIVE path and the live file did not move, which is the whole reason the split was preferred to the move. It does not need the full history to run.
  • ONE CONSEQUENCE, REPORTED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: the Word export now carries the recent half only — DoD Changelog.docx went 392 KB to 74 KB. Until today that docx was the one readable copy of the full history outside git. Restoring a full-history Word export is one line in build_docs.py's DOCS dict pointing at the archive; it was NOT taken, because the batch did not ask for it and adding an out-of-repo source to that script is a decision about what the script is for.
  • THREE TEST SUITES READ HISTORICAL CHANGELOG CONTENT AND NOW FAIL. REPORTED, NOT RE-POINTED — what each assertion was for is a decision, not a repair. See §5 for what they were checking.

§4 Two things BY's reference table surfaced, both answered

BOTH ARE COMMENT MENTIONS, NOT LOADS. NO PRODUCTION CODE DEPENDS ON A TEST FILE. BY's reference count is string-match based, which is what put them on the list.

  • scripts/run_state.gd:1117 names test_runes.gd IN A COMMENT — "Asserted in test_runes.gd, not just intended", the note explaining that the DOD_SIM_RUNE_ECON/RUNE_POWER double gate on sim_run is tested. It is a pointer to where the guarantee is checked. No load, no preload, no path.
  • scripts/battle.gd:335 names sim.sh IN A COMMENT — "Difficulty sweep (DOD_SIM_SWEEP=1, sim.sh --sweep)", naming the shell wrapper that sets the env var the block below reads. battle.gd reads the ENVIRONMENT, never the script; sim.sh invokes Godot, so the dependency runs the other way round and always did.

§5 Verification

THE SPLIT IS ASSERTED PROGRAMMATICALLY, NOT BY EYE — a split that drops one entry of 118 is invisible. Every <h2> heading was extracted from the original file and from both halves: 118 original = 10 live + 108 archive; no entry missing; ZERO overlap between the two halves; order preserved; and the two bodies re-concatenated are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original body. The live file's newest entry is this one and its oldest is Batch BP; the archive's newest is Batch BO, the batch immediately before it.

Both files open and are valid HTML — each has its own doctype, head, title, body and <h1>, and the archive carries the original's closing tags while the live file gained its own. Same structure and same styling on both sides, so the archive reads exactly as the changelog does.

THE THREE SUITES THAT FAIL, AND WHAT EACH WAS ASKING. All three assert against an entry that is now in the archive; none of them is a test of game code:

  • test_batch_bb — slices the Batch BB entry off its <h2> heading and checks it carries §3's Ruin-detonation numbers in full (trash 0.07 / n=566 / deepest mark 31, boss 0.60 / n=25 / deepest mark 18) beside AX's and AY's rows so the three are comparable, and that the number leads the entry. Note the shape of the failure: the anchor is gone, so split(...)[1] indexes out of range and throws — which ABORTS the function while the suite still prints a count. That is the documented BC trap; read the COUNT, not only the failures.
  • test_batch_bn — one check, changelog.html carries a Batch BN entry.
  • test_batch_bo — one check, the changelog has a Batch BO entry.

THE OTHER NINE CHANGELOG-READING SUITES PASS UNCHANGED (bp, bq, br, bs, bt, bu, bv, bw, bx) because every entry they name is Batch BP or newer and stayed in the live file. That is the cut point doing its job rather than luck: the suites that read the changelog are overwhelmingly each batch's own, and each batch's own entry is recent by construction. The failing three are the ones that reached BACKWARD — two for a bare existence check, one for a real measurement.

§6 Two standing notes, recorded rather than acted on

  • THE TEST SUITES ARE THE SINGLE LARGEST BLOCK IN THE SYNC AND CANNOT BE ARCHIVED. 43 suites, 1.50 MB — 28% of the old sync and 32% of the new one (they did not grow; the denominator shrank, and after this batch they are larger than any single file). They must be in the repo to run, so this is a constraint of a whole-repo sync rather than a judgement about their value. Each one encodes decisions in assertion form. Written down before someone proposes deleting them for space. (BY and this file's guide both say "47"; the live count is 43.)
  • scripts/battle.gd IS 893 KB IN ONE FILE — larger than the changelog was, and now 18.5% of the sync on its own. Not this batch's subject and not a sync problem that can be solved, because it is read constantly. Recorded as a code-health observation: a file that size wants splitting eventually, and doing it deliberately is far cheaper than doing it when it becomes unworkable.

2026-08-15 — Batch BY: the repo audit, at file level

LEAD WITH THE RESULT, BECAUSE IT IS NOT THE ONE THE BATCH EXPECTED. BJ swept fields, functions and constants; this swept FILES, and it found one dead file in the whole repo — a 10 KB macOS .DS_Store. Everything else that looked dead turned out to be reached by a path a text search cannot see. The repo is 37.72 MB over 219 tracked files and it is not carrying dead weight; it is carrying its own history. So the useful half of this batch is the other half: a knowledge-base sync ingests 5.41 MB of TEXT, not 37.72 MB of repo, and the recommendation is to archive 868 KB of it — 15.7% — without deleting a byte.

§1 The inventory — 219 files, every one attributed

Path, size, modification date and inbound reference for every tracked file, sorted by size descending, with a reason recorded for every file that has no inbound reference. AFTER ATTRIBUTION THERE ARE ZERO UNEXPLAINED FILES. The counts:

  • 106 live — reached by preload/load, a .tscn ext_resource, project.godot, or a class_name global.
  • 64 .uid sidecars — Godot engine metadata, one per script, 1.2 KB in total. Each was checked for an orphan (a .uid whose script is gone); there are none.
  • 40 test suites — run by the harness via --script, never imported. §3.
  • 6 entry points — project.godot, .gitignore, docs/build_docs.py, and check_parse/check_flow/check_map, the instruments run by hand each batch.
  • 2 documentation (README.md, the retired docs/addendum.html) and 1 licence (assets/fonts/OFL.txt, the SIL licence that must travel with PirataOne — legally paired, never a candidate).

The full 219-row table is not reproduced here — it is regenerable, and pasting 219 rows into the project's largest file to save 10 KB elsewhere would be self-defeating. What is worth keeping is the reason column for the files with no inbound reference, which is §2b.

§2 What was deleted — the complete list, one file

This list is the audit trail and it is exhaustive. Nothing else was removed.

  • assets/.DS_Store — 10,244 bytes, last modified 2026-07-09. Reason: macOS Finder metadata, no function in the project, referenced by nothing and loadable by nothing. It is already matched by .gitignore:4 and was only ever tracked because it was committed before that ignore rule landed on 2026-07-27. Removed from the index and the working tree; the ignore rule keeps it out from here.

§2b What LOOKED dead and is not — the near-misses, recorded because they are the trap

A reference count of zero was wrong four separate ways, and every one of them would have broken the build. This is the part of the audit worth keeping:

  • SIXTEEN SPRITE FILES HAVE NO LITERAL REFERENCE ANYWHERE AND ALL SIXTEEN ARE LIVE. Of the 20 files under assets/sprites/, exactly two are named in source (Berserker_Portrait.png, Soldier_Idle.png). The other sixteen are built at runtime by unit.gd:1379 — "%s/%s_%s.png" % [sheet_dir, prefix, suffix] over seven animation suffixes — where sheet_dir is a directory constant (enemies.gd:10 const SHEET := "res://assets/sprites/orc", battle.gd:600 SPEC_ART, classes.gd:49). A grep-driven audit deletes every orc, soldier and berserker animation frame in the game and the parse gate still passes, because the load is a string built at runtime.
  • FOUR SCRIPTS HAVE NO PATH REFERENCE BECAUSE THEY ARE class_name GLOBALS — profile.gd (Profile, 70 uses), enemies.gd (Enemies, 30), glossary.gd (Glossary, 10), glossary_panel.gd (GlossaryPanel, 7). A global class is reached by its NAME; no preload of the file exists to find.
  • check_map_screen.gd and check_map_screen.tscn reference only each other — a closed two-file loop with nothing pointing in. Both are live: the scene is launched by hand each batch and is the only thing that executes the lattice draw.
  • assets/fonts/OFL.txt is referenced by nothing and may not be removed: it is the font's licence.

§2c Reported, not deleted — the two ambiguous files

assets/sprites/soldier/Soldier.png (13,710 B, 900x700) and assets/sprites/orc/Orc.png (12,256 B, 800x600). These are the only asset files the sweep could not resolve either way. They are not loaded: _build_sprite only ever builds Prefix_Suffix.png and neither bare name carries a suffix, so nothing reaches them. But their dimensions say what they are — the original unsplit sheets the live per-animation strips were cut from (7 rows x 100px and 6 rows x 100px against the 600x100 strips beside them). That makes them source art rather than a backup copy, and §2's rule is that an ambiguous file is reported, not deleted. The cost of keeping them is 26 KB; the cost of deleting the master art is not recoverable from the repo. They stay, and this entry is the record of why.

§4 The archive recommendation — report only, nothing moved

THE REPO IS THE WRONG NUMBER. 37.72 MB across 219 files sounds like the problem, but 32.3 MB of it is assets/ — mp3, wav, png, ttf — which a knowledge-base sync does not ingest. The sync sees 5.41 MB across 169 text files. Against that denominator:

  • docs/changelog.html — 835.0 KB, 15.1% of the sync. The strongest candidate by a distance, and an ABSOLUTE NON-DELETION: it is the project's memory, it grows every batch, and the design conversation is explicitly told not to source premises from it — valuable, but not a working file. One caveat that must travel with the move: docs/build_docs.py reads it by relative path, so archiving it breaks the docx build until that path is updated.
  • docs/addendum.html — 32.9 KB, 0.6%. RETIRED and frozen since 2026-07-08; nothing but CLAUDE.md mentions it. The definition of a non-working file.
  • TOGETHER: 867.9 KB, 15.7% of the sync — taking it from 5.41 MB to 4.56 MB, without deleting anything.

AND A RECOMMENDATION AGAINST, which is the more useful half: §4 offered old test suites as a candidate and they should not be taken while the changelog is untaken. All 47 suites together are 1.50 MB — the whole harness is barely more than the changelog and CLAUDE.md combined — and the seven oldest (ah, ah_battle, ai, aj, ak, al, an) come to 179.6 KB, or 3.2%. That is a bad trade: AV, BR and BS each re-pointed a suite in place WITH ITS REASON precisely so a later batch could not quietly reverse a decision, and 3.2% does not buy that record back.

§5 The "beast" identifiers — the list, and BX's list corrected

Reported, not renamed, per the batch: a field rename is a different risk from a file audit and wants its own pass. BX produced a list; BY re-swept it against live code and it is wrong in three places, so the corrected list now lives in CLAUDE.md's open threads. The corrections:

  • beastmaster IS NOT A RENAME CANDIDATE AND MUST NOT BE SWEPT. The spec is still called the Beastmaster in game (classes.gd "name": "Beastmaster"), so the key is a proper name — exactly the reasoning BX used to keep Bestial Wrath. That covers 143 occurrences of the key, beastmaster_pool_ability, and every pool table keyed on it. An over-eager sweep of BX's list renames a live spec key.
  • BX was RIGHT that th_beasts and ss_beasts are gone — they survive only in test_batch_bx.gd:645-649 as negative assertions proving the deletion. That is a record to keep, not a leftover to sweep.
  • BX's list missed three, all test-side: _live_two_beasts, _live_beastmaster, beast_key. And kinds_summoned — which the batch brief expected to be a candidate — is already neutral; only its comment says "beasts".

The rest of BX's list is confirmed intact: the unit fields beasts, beast_committed, no_beast_left, no_beast_left_loyalty; the battle functions _beasts, _beast_cap, _free_beast, _on_beast_death; the six locals; and the two node ids bm_beast_within / bm_no_beast_left, which are save-bearing — renaming those two moves the save format, which is the strongest single reason this is a separate pass.

§6 What a field-level sweep could not see

Both classes BJ was blind to were checked and both are clean. No whole file has become dead beyond the .DS_Store. At file scope: all four data/*.json are still reached by a live loader; all thirteen scenes are reached from a live script (relics_screen.tscn and settings.tscn hang off single call sites in main_menu.gd:88 and :92 — thin, but real); and all 21 enemy kinds in enemies.json carry both a zone list and a role tag, so no kind is undealable, with all three bosses named by a zone def or END_BOSS_KIND.

Verified

Per the standing instruction, that means the code landed and works. No sweeps, no bands, no balance measurement was run, and none should be quoted from this batch. check_parse 0 · check_flow 0 (11 screens) · check_map_screen OK (the lattice at three positions, both overlays, and the four-column draft driven to confirm) · all 13 scenes 0 SCRIPT ERROR · run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS — but see below, because one of those three PASSes is hollow · the full 47-suite battery at zero failures, and NO SUITE'S COUNT FELL. The designer had no run in flight (run_save.bin does not exist) and none was created.

THE FIND OF THE BATCH IS NOT A FILE. IT IS THAT `run-harness GATE 2 PASSES WITHOUT RUNNING A SINGLE ASSERTION`. test_run_harness.gd:125 calls run.award_spec_point(i) and line 142 calls run.award_talent_points(...) — both deleted by Batch BM §6. The error aborts _gate_talent_conservation at line 125, which is above every _check in the function, so zero checks run, zero fail, and the gate prints "GATE 2 PASS". The aborted region is precisely the half BM RE-POINTED IN PLACE — its own comment says "the income half of this gate measured a purse that no longer exists; what replaces it is the half that IS still load-bearing" — so BM's replacement assertions have never once executed, and every VERIFIED block since BM has quoted "gates 1/2/3 PASS" on the strength of it. A count of zero failures is not evidence when the count of checks is also zero, and unlike the ah/an cases this one prints the word PASS rather than a number, which is why nobody caught it. It is REPORTED AND NOT FIXED here for the same reason §5's renames are: deciding what BM's superseded lines should now assert is BM's decision to re-point, not a file audit's, and it wants its own pass with its own test. Until then, "run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS" should be quoted as gates 1 and 3.

Three previously recorded faults reproduced exactly and none is this batch's, which is the useful control: test_batch_ah (5500/0) and test_batch_an (3621/0) still call award_talent_points and still abort their reward sections while printing 0 failures; test_runes still prints its stale start_rune_enabled error at 2973/0; and test_batch_bj still throws its three _refresh_chips errors at an unmoved 67/0. Matching the last recorded run fault-for-fault is what licenses the claim that the deletion changed nothing.

AND ONE TESTING LESSON, LEARNED THE SAME WAY THE FILE AUDIT'S LESSONS WERE. The first battery reported test_batch_bl at 88 checks, 4 failures — every one of them a recap-ledger assertion that needs a real-play battle to FINISH. The cause was not the code: zsh does not word-split unquoted parameter expansions, so a battery script holding fps="--fixed-fps 12" and passing bare $fps hands Godot one token, the flag is rejected, and bl runs at the default step — reproducing CLAUDE.md's documented symptom precisely. Invoked correctly it is 88/0, twice in a row. In zsh a flag list must be an ARRAY (fps=(--fixed-fps 12)); the bash habit of a bare string silently under-runs the one suite that most needs the flag.

2026-08-15 — Batch BX: every hero drafts after an elite

LEAD WITH THE RATE. An elite victory used to hand one hero, drawn at random, a choice of three abilities. It now offers a draft to every living hero — each from their own pool, on one screen of four columns rather than four screens in sequence. Measured end to end over a walked run: 34.00 draft offers a run against BO's ~10, and 62% of them arrive at a hero already at the seven-slot cap, so most drafts are now a take-one-and-drop-one decision rather than a free addition. That is four times as much drafting, and it ships deliberately untuned — the cap, the offer size and the one-in-four class seam are all untouched, because the point is to feel this against the pools as they stand before tranche 3 lands thirty-six more cards on top of it.

No new abilities. No talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability's numbers moved, and no save version moves (still v10) — the party dict is saved wholesale and every key this needs was already on it.

§2 — The elite draft screen

Every living hero is offered a draft, and each draws their own three cards from their own spec pool and their own class pool at the established one-in-four seam. There is no shared offer and no shared ledger: Run.roll_draft_offer is called per member and reads that member's own pools and their own draft_refused, so a Pyromancer can never be shown a Warden card and one hero's decline can never hide a card from another. That ledger being per member is load-bearing — a shared refusal list is the obvious implementation and the wrong one, and it is verified rather than assumed.

ONE SCREEN, FOUR COLUMNS. Four sequential offers after every elite would slow a run noticeably, so the shape of the screen is the change and not just its reach. The rules carried over unaltered, each still owned by run_state.gd rather than by the screen:

  • Declining is per hero and independent. One hero taking a card does not commit the others.
  • A declined or dropped card enters that hero's no-return ledger and does not return that run — per member, never shared.
  • The seven-slot cap holds per column. A hero at the cap must name what the incoming card replaces before their column counts as decided, and only earned abilities can be named: protected ones are simply not in that list.
  • Offers fill short rather than padding with repeats (AP §3, unchanged). A hero with nothing left to be shown gets no column at all rather than an empty one.

THE SCREEN RESOLVES AS ONE ACTION, and that is the piece that decided the implementation. Every column is chosen, then the whole screen is confirmed — so a player who fills the Devout's last slot can still reconsider before the Warden's pick is locked. The choices are therefore staged, not committed: nothing touches the run until the confirm, which then walks the columns through Run.take_draft_ability and Run.decline_draft — the same two doors the boss pick's overlay already used. Leaving the screen commits nothing and the picks stay owed on the hero cards, so a player can go and read a hero sheet mid-draft. Clicking a staged card again unstages it, because declining costs a whole offer and must never be the only way out of a misclick.

ONE DRAFT RENDERER, NOT TWO. BO's single-hero draft branch inside the pick overlay is deleted rather than left unreachable, and the hero card's CHOOSE button now opens the party screen. A merchant or event grants a draft to one hero, and that simply renders as a one-column version of the same screen.

A FALLEN HERO DRAFTS NORMALLY, AND THE ORDERING WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ADDED. §2 asked which of two cases held — and it is the first: a post-battle revive already existed, inside BattleUnit.sync_victory_state, and it returns a hero who fell at 20% of maximum rather than at the 1 HP the brief describes. It runs in the victory branch ~50 lines above the draft award, so "they are alive when the screen opens" is a consequence of the existing order rather than a rule this batch had to write. Nothing was changed toward 1 HP: the instruction was conditional on no revive existing, and one does. The health gate in the award loop is still written and tested, so the rule is stated rather than depending on a fact that could stop being true.

§3 — Twin Hunt's companion, closed

BV established the rule — an ordered action goes to one companion, a passive strike-alongside goes to all of them — and resolved Savage Sweep by picking the highest-Loyalty standing companion. Twin Hunt went on picking by list order, which under The Pack means the earlier summon rather than the better bond. BW reported it and changed nothing (its tranche touched no existing ability); this points it at the same rule.

It is ONE implementation now, battle._deepest_bond, and not two copies of a loop — Savage Sweep's inline walk moved into it and Twin Hunt calls it. A rule written twice eventually disagrees with itself, which is exactly what happened here across two batches. Ties break on list order, so the answer is deterministic and a test can assert an identity rather than a probability.

§4 — Beast becomes companion

The prose said companion, the field said beasts, and three node names said Beast. Every player-facing string now reads companion: ability descriptions, status tooltips, the swap and summon pickers, combat-log lines, the glossary and the Master Document. Code identifiers are deliberately untouched — a missed rename in prose is a typo, a missed rename in code is a bug, and mixing the two would have made this batch's diff unreadable.

TWO NODES RENAMED, KEEPING THEIR IDS — and that is the negative control that matters, since a rename that moved an id would break every saved build silently. bm_beast_within Beast Within → The Wild Within and bm_no_beast_left No Beast Left → None Left Behind: same ids, same rows, same lanes, same payload fields. Bestial Wrath keeps its name, which reads as a proper name rather than as the common noun. Both new names were swept against every ability, talent node, status and rune before shipping (BR §1) and are clean.

THE CODE IDENTIFIERS STILL READING "beast", listed so a later batch can take them deliberately: the unit fields beasts, beast_committed, no_beast_left, no_beast_left_loyalty; the node ids bm_beast_within and bm_no_beast_left; the battle functions _beasts, _beast_cap, _free_beast, _on_beast_death; and the locals bot_beasts, cw_beasts, kc_beasts, sb_beast, sb_beasts, tm_beasts. (th_beasts and ss_beasts are gone — §3 deleted both.) No other node or rune names the word.

Verified

Per the standing instruction, that means the code landed and works. No sweeps, no bands, no balance measurement was run, and none should be quoted from this batch. check_parse 0 · check_flow 0 · check_map_screen OK (it drives the four-column screen, seats a hero at the cap so a column renders its drop step, and confirms) · run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS · NEW test_batch_bx.gd 141/0, full battery green with zero failures anywhere. Every clause §6 named is driven live, and each is built so a broken implementation still fails: the per-member ledger is driven on two heroes sharing one spec, which is the only arrangement in which a shared list is visible; the one-action rule is asserted before the confirm, where a per-column commit passes every "the card landed" check and fails this one; the cap is asserted UNDECIDED with a card staged and DECIDED the moment a drop is named; the own-pool rule is rolled 200 times a hero, because one offer would agree with a shared pool by luck; and Twin Hunt is driven by identity — the two companions carry wildly different companion_power so the blow says which one struck — then mirrored, so a version that always picks the second summon fails too.

SEVEN NEGATIVE CONTROLS, each applied to product code and reverted (every touched file back byte-identical by hash): Twin Hunt back to list order trips 2; the screen committing per column trips 6; a shared draft_refused trips 7; a capped column deciding without a drop trips 1; the elite offering one hero again trips 4; a renamed node moving its id trips 1; and the revive moved below the draft award trips 5. None passed.

One fault was found by an empirical check rather than by reasoning, and it would have shipped. Callable.bind appends its arguments after the call's, so f.bind(idx).bind(name) resolves to f(name, idx) — reversed. The drop step's staged handler was written as a double bind and would have thrown the moment a player named a replacement, in the one path no source check and no headless draw was exercising.

The drafts-per-run figure above is instrumentation, not a difficulty reading: it comes from an 8-run walk taken only to exercise RunSim's draft path, and its Matrix row is not quoted. The designer had no run in flight and none was created — no run_save.bin exists, and profile.json, relics.json and trees.json are byte-identical by hash across the whole battery.

2026-08-14 — Batch BW: tranche 2, the Warrior nine (TRANCHE 2 COMPLETE)

LEAD WITH THE DEBT BEING PAID. Since Batch BP the Warrior three have been the visible shape of what the draft still owed — two cards apiece against everybody else's five, so a Berserker, a Warden or a Swordmaster was the one hero whose offer of three came up short. That is over. All twelve specs draft from five, the asymmetry is gone, and the draft holds 84 of a target ~96. What remains is a third tranche, and it is owed by all twelve equally rather than by three of them. The mechanically new thing is the STANCE-GATED ABILITY — the first cards in the game that are refused outright unless the Swordmaster is standing in the right guard.

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Warrior spec. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, and no save version moves (still v10). ONE new unit-side field for nine abilities (Berserk's charge count) — everything with a duration is a STATUS, per BQ's standard.

STANCE-GATED ABILITIES ARE THE NEW MECHANIC, AND THE RULE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE TWO CARDS. READERS BRANCH AND FLIP; GATED ONES REQUIRE AND STAY. BP shipped the readers — Precision Strike and Feint branch on the stance and then switch it, each branch buying what the guard he is arriving in wants. A gated card is a different animal: it is refused outright in the wrong stance (unavailable, not a weaker branch) and casting it moves nothing. _ability_usable is the door, matching how Death Ray's Resonance gate and BV's nine are refused — so the greyed button, the bot's pool and the cast itself can never disagree. Getting the two card types backwards is the single easiest mistake to make on this spec, which is why it ships as a standing rule.

BERSERKER — spend the rage, take the risk, and finally get paid back. His pool was Blood Offering and Gut Rip: both single-target, both about him getting low, and nothing paid him back for being there.

  • Reckless Abandon — 0 Rage, 1.5, 4cd, self. He spends ALL his Rage; for 3 turns he deals +2% damage per 10 points SPENT (Perfect: 3%). Axis: the dump. A full bar is +20% and costs him every ability he might have cast in that window, which is the trade. It scales off what was actually spent, not off his maximum — a half-full Berserker buys half the buff. Refused outright at zero Rage (BO §5's rule). Builds with Blood Offering, Blood Tithe and Bloodied Momentum; a deliberate anti-synergy with Bloodwake, which pays him for holding Rage.
  • Berserk — 25 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, self. His next 3 strikes each land twice (Perfect: 4), and he takes 30% more damage for 3 turns. Axis: the risk dial at maximum, and the drawback IS the payoff — Blood Frenzy scales his damage with missing health, so taking 30% more drives him into his own power band. TWO DIFFERENT CLOCKS ON ONE CARD: the strikes are CHARGES and wait until spent, the 30% is an ordinary 3-turn status. Per BR §1 the charges count HITS, not casts, so Hack and Slash empties the whole bank in one cast and lands six blows. FLAGGED AS PROBABLY THE STRONGEST CARD IN THE WARRIOR SET AND SHIPPED TO BE WATCHED RATHER THAN PRE-TUNED.
  • Blood Debt — 20 Rage, 2.0, 4cd, one enemy, 10 BD. Strikes for 30% of Attack and marks the enemy for the rest of the battle; every time it bleeds out he heals 25% of his maximum health (Perfect: 35%). Axis: a reason to survive being low. THE MARK SURVIVES THE BLEEDOUT IT PAYS FOR, which is the clause most likely to be built as one-shot by accident and the whole card: Slaughterhouse drops a bleedout to 50 rather than 0, so the same marked enemy bleeds out repeatedly and one mark pays three or four times.

SWORDMASTER — the first stance-GATED cards.

  • Sever (requires Aggressive) — 25 Rage, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy, 15 BD. 40% of Attack, and if the target is Broken this ability's cooldown is cleared outright. Axis: the Break window rewards aggression — his Breaker lane opens a one-turn window and nothing let him swing repeatedly inside it. Builds with Shatterpoint, Punishment, Off Balance, Pressure Point and Guard Breaker, all of which live in that window.
  • Battle Poise (requires Defensive) — 25 Rage, 2.0, 4cd, self. For 3 turns every attack he parries takes a turn off all his cooldowns (Perfect: 4 turns). Axis: defence buys tempo. He is the only parry-stat hero in the game and all of it merely made hits smaller; this is the connection his three lanes have never had. It pays PER PARRY and goes through _tick_cooldowns, BQ's one implementation of cooldown reduction; it skips its own recast, because a defensive window that shortens its own return is a different and unbounded card.
  • Feigned Guard — 20 Rage, 1.0, 3cd, self. For 2 turns his abilities resolve as though cast from the other stance — AND satisfy that stance's gate — without switching him (Perfect: 3 turns). Axis: the only card in the game that lets a build have both halves of its own toggle. THE GATE-SATISFYING CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A CONVENIENCE: without it this is a minor modifier; with it, an Aggressive build can cast Battle Poise and a Defensive build can cast Sever. It is satisfied in _ability_usable, not merely branched at resolution — two different sites, and only the first makes the card true. IT DOES NOT SWITCH THE STANCE AND MUST NOT BE BUILT TO, and his PASSIVE keeps reading the guard he is actually in, so an Aggressive build keeps Aggressive's damage bonus the whole time.

WARDEN — his bulk as a weapon, a permanent duel, and Block that pays the party. His pool was Covering Guard and Eye of the Storm: both defensive, and he had no offense at all.

  • Shield Slam — 25 Rage, 2.5, 3cd, one enemy. Damage equal to 15% of his maximum health (Perfect: 20%) plus 40 Break damage. Axis: his bulk as a weapon, and the Break contributes to a Warrior party's central axis rather than to his own damage number. It reads the maximum LIVE, so Heavy Plating's climb and every +15 Tenacity adds during the fight feed it.
  • Vendetta — 20 Rage, 1.5, 4cd, one enemy. For the rest of the battle that enemy can attack nobody but the Warden, and he takes 20% less damage from it (Perfect: 30%). Axis: a permanent duel — Eye of the Storm taunts everything for two turns, this locks one thing forever. It reuses the taunt system rather than writing a parallel one (a mocked status at -1 turns, exactly the shape The Whole Room installs), so the lock releases if the Warden falls for free: the targeting narrow re-resolves the taunter live and ignores a dead one.
  • Aegis Wall — 25 Rage, 2.0, 5cd, self. For 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every attack he BLOCKS heals all allies 8% of his maximum health. Axis: his signature stat feeds the party. Block negates an attack entirely and paid him nothing beyond that; this is the first thing that makes a block worth something to anyone else. It reads BLOCKS, not attacks taken — a blow that gets through pays nothing — and it reads the maximum LIVE.

ONE NAME COLLISION, FOUND BY BR §1's SWEEP AND RESOLVED RATHER THAN FLAGGED — THE CARD MOVED, NOT THE TALENT. The Warden's permanent duel was authored as GRUDGE, and wd_grudge is already a Warden Threat-lane talent (row 7: +25% damage against enemies his taunt binds), with a Rune of Grudges paying into the same term. Same spec, same lane, one row apart, and mechanically adjacent — the talent's effect is precisely what the card's taunt would feed. That is closer than BP's Precision Strike / Precision Strikes and closer than BV's Ghostpack / Ghost Pack, and unlike those it was avoidable: the talent's id is save-migrated and its ranks travel with it, while the card was unshipped. The card is VENDETTA. The two still compose exactly as intended — Grudge pays +25% against a target his taunt binds, and Vendetta is a taunt that never lapses. The other eight names are clean against every ability, talent node, status and rune, and the whole sweep ships as a test.

BREAK DAMAGE ASSIGNED DELIBERATELY (the standing rule since BO), AND REPORTED. §1 names one figure; the other two are this batch's. THREE of the nine are attacks and carry it: Shield Slam 40 (the brief's), Sever 15 — 40% of Attack for 25 Rage, priced beside Feint (35% / 12) and Precision Strike's Defensive branch (15% / 15), and worth noting that its Break matters most on the FIRST cast, because it is what opens the window the cooldown clause then exploits — and Blood Debt 10, one step under Feint on the same curve with Gut Rip's 20 at the 30-Rage end of it. The other six land no blow at all, so Break would have nothing to ride: that is a decision on each of them, not an omission on any.

TWO STATUSES SIT ON AN ENEMY, AND THAT PUT THEM IN A LIST THE OBVIOUS READING WOULD HAVE MISSED. blood_debt and vendetta are MARKS, so neither is in DEBUFF_IDS — a battle-long entry there reads as 999 turns remaining and a mender's longest-first Cleansing Rite would take it every single time (feinted's reason). But _dispellable_buffs is DERIVED from exactly that absence, so leaving them out of both lists would have made them beneficial statuses in the eyes of the one ability that strips those: a Mage's Dispel would have stripped the party's own marks FOR the enemy carrying them. Both are in DISPEL_NEVER. This is BU's Suffering trap arriving through the mark door. Vendetta's taunt half is a separate mocked status and is deliberately still cleansable, because mocked always has been — that is the same exposure The Whole Room's permanent taunt already carries, and a carve-out for one card would make two permanent taunts behave differently.

BERSERK'S DOUBLING EXPANDS THE HIT COUNT RATHER THAN RE-ENTERING THE STRIKE BODY, so every doubled blow is an ORDINARY blow: it rolls its own crit, miss and parry and carries his bleed buildup, which is what feeds Gut Rip and Blood Debt twice as fast. The target-list expansion beside it looks optional and is not: the strike loop reads strike_targets[hit_i] on the area and chosen-pair branches, so raising the hit count without growing the list runs the doubled strikes off its end. multi_hits and random_hits re-pick their own target every iteration and need no expansion, which is why the expansion is gated to the other branch.

BERSERK'S 30% IS DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED INTO dmg_taken_bonus, the stat field talents and runes write. Two reasons, and the second is load-bearing: that field is permanent and this is a 3-turn status, and MEASURED RAGE zeroes dmg_taken_bonus outright to cancel Reckless Fury. Letting a talent delete a drafted card's drawback would delete the card, because the 30% is the payoff. Two effects sharing one field is how one of them silently stops existing.

THE BOT GOT NO ROTATION, ON PURPOSE — all nine ride BO §5's wrapper, so no existing rotation is re-weighted and no prior measurement stops being comparable. Four of the nine joined the self-cast list (Reckless Abandon, Berserk, Battle Poise, Feigned Guard and Aegis Wall have nothing to click); Shield Slam, Vendetta, Blood Debt and Sever each name one enemy and fall through to the ordinary target picker. The two stance gates need no bot rule at all: they live in _ability_usable, which the bot's drafted-pick wrapper already consults.

ONE GLOSSARY ENTRY ADDED (88 -> 89): stance_gated. "Requires Aggressive" is a rule the game has never had before, and a player meeting a greyed-out card needs to know why it is dark and what Feigned Guard does about it. The existing stance entry cross-links to it and now says two of his abilities REQUIRE a guard.

MASTER.HTML CORRECTED TOWARD THE CODE WHERE IT HAD DRIFTED, beside the ordinary update: the draft table's intro read "the fifty-four drafted abilities" against a table already holding seventy-five rows (BT, BU and BV each added rows without moving that sentence), and the Swordmaster group header still read "both cards read the stance and then switch it" against a lane that now holds five. Both now state what the code does.

2026-08-14 — Batch BV: tranche 2, the Hunter nine

LEAD WITH PREPARATION, because it is the first extra-turn mechanic in the game. PREPARATION (Survivalist) is 25 Mana for a plain sentence: after his NEXT turn he immediately takes another one. Nothing in Dawn of Decay has ever handed a hero a second action. Two things came close and neither is this — Rally hands an ALLY the next slot in the order (they still spend that turn; nobody gains one), and Instinctive Rotation makes one specific action, the companion swap, cost no turn. Preparation is a whole turn out of nowhere, and because it is a whole turn it carries a whole turn's costs: his own statuses tick again for it. Three rules were decided here rather than left to whichever branch the code fell into, and all three are in CLAUDE.md.

Nine spec draft abilities, three per Hunter spec. The Hunter pools go from two to five, joining the Mage and the Cleric. The Warrior three are the last third of tranche 2 owed, and tranche 3 after them. The draft holds 75 of a target ~96. Nothing else ships: no talent node, no magnitude, no existing ability changed, and no save version moves (still v10).

BEASTMASTER — the partnership protected, widened, and paid back. His pool was Twin Hunt and Call the Wilds: both about the companion striking. Nothing protected it, and Loyalty — uncapped, measured reaching 50 — dies with it.

  • Bloodbond — 20 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, self. The next blow that would fell a companion is refused, and the hunter takes half of it instead (Perfect: a quarter). Axis: protecting the single largest investment in the game. It is a placed guard, not a window — no duration, so it is never wasted on a turn nothing threatened the beast, and it holds until it fires. The half he takes can kill him, and the card says so: a guard that cannot cost anything is not a decision.
  • Savage Sweep — 25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, self. His companion strikes the three lowest-health enemies and gains 3 Loyalty (Perfect: 5). Axis: the partnership made wide. Lowest-health rather than random, deliberately: it is a finisher, and a random spread would make it a worse Cinderfall.
  • Ghostpack — 25 Mana, 2.5, 5cd, self. For 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every companion he has summoned this battle strikes alongside his attacks at 40%, including the ones no longer standing. Axis: what rotating actually buys. It is the Pack build's payoff and deliberately near-worthless to a Lone Bond build, which fields one companion and never swaps.

SHARPSHOOTER — the multiplier half, the finish, and the field. His pool was Called Volley and Quarry's Mark: both about generating and keeping Focus. Nothing read the half past 100, where Focus stops buying crit chance and starts buying crit multiplier without a ceiling.

  • Crossfire — 25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy, 10 BD. 30% of Attack, and for 3 turns (Perfect: 4) every critical hit also strikes 2 other enemies for 40% of that crit's damage. Axis: the crit build goes wide. Anti-synergy with Consistent Aim is deliberate and named — that node trades multiplier for chance, so a Consistent build wants a different card, and that is what makes this a build decision rather than a strict pick.
  • Calibrating Shot — 20 Mana, 1.5, 3cd, one enemy, 8 BD. 20% of Attack, and Focus equal to 10% of the target's missing health (Perfect: 15%). Axis: patience rewarded for finishing what he started. The reading is taken BEFORE this shot lands, so "a fresh enemy pays nothing" is literally true rather than nearly true — measured afterwards, the shot's own damage would have paid a few Focus every cast and quietly made the card's promise false.
  • Trophy Shot — 25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy, 12 BD. 35% of Attack (Perfect: 45%). If this kills, his Focus is not reduced at all and carries whole to the next enemy. Axis: the kill stops costing him. If it does not kill it is an ordinary shot and the ordinary switch rules apply — the card's own text says so, because a conditional card that reads unconditional is a tooltip lying.

SURVIVALIST — hold the breadth, cash the breadth, buy a turn. His pool was Choking Smoke and Snare Line: both wide, both one-shot. His engine is breadth and breadth decays — Cripple runs out while he is applying Slow, and the count Trapper pays him for quietly shrinks.

  • Loaded Shot — 20 Mana, 2.0, 4cd, one enemy, 8 BD. 20% of Attack, and every harmful effect on the target is reset to full duration, the uncleansable ones included (Perfect: it also lands 2 turns of Poison). Axis: craft as maintenance, on a turn he would have been attacking anyway. It reads a new full_turns ledger written by add_status itself rather than a table of defaults, so a talent that lengthened a status lengthened its full value too. It can only lengthen: a re-applied Burn already standing longer than it started is left alone, and a permanent affliction stays permanent.
  • Hunt — 25 Mana, 2.5, 4cd, one enemy, 10 BD. 15% of Attack for every different harmful effect on the target (Perfect: 20%) — 60% at four, 90% at six. Axis: the count made into a weapon. Distinct effects, never stacks, and that is a property of one implementation rather than a second rule: it shares _status_count with the Trapper passive's own breadth term, so the card and the passive can never disagree about what breadth is.
  • Preparation — 25 Mana, 2.0, 5cd, self. After his next turn he immediately takes another (Perfect: the extra turn also refunds 15 Mana). Axis: an extra action IS extra breadth, for a spec where every status costs a whole cast.

PREPARATION'S THREE RULES, DECIDED HERE RATHER THAN BY WHICHEVER BRANCH THE CODE FELL INTO.

  • The extra turn is a FULL turn and it re-ticks his statuses. Designer's call: simpler and legible. It falls out of the implementation rather than being bolted on — he re-enters the ordinary initiative loop, so his damage-over-time effects bite, his buffs shorten and his cooldowns tick, exactly as on any turn. The cost is real without being punishing because ENEMY statuses tick on ENEMY turns, so the board he just armed is untouched by his second action.
  • It must not chain. Casting Preparation on the extra turn to earn another is an unbounded loop — a hang, not a balance question — so the cast is refused while one is pending. That refusal is load-bearing rather than tidy, and it is the negative control test_batch_bv drives directly.
  • The delay is what makes it a setup card rather than "take two turns now". A counter armed at 2 and decremented at the end of each of his turns is what makes that exact: the turn he cast on burns one and grants nothing, and his next turn grants the extra one.

THE Improvised INTERACTION IS REPORTED, NOT PRE-TUNED — AND THE MEASUREMENT DISAGREED WITH THE BRIEF. Improvised (Survivalist, Guerilla row 7) stops the first two abilities of each fight starting their cooldowns, and the brief predicted a Guerilla build "opens with Preparation twice — bounded at two". Two is the bound on the FREE casts, not on the opening. Driven honestly in test_batch_bv — cast whenever the gate allows, tick at the end of every turn — such a build gets three Preparations in its first five turns: two Improvised-funded, and then a third the shortened clock already allows, because the extra turn each cast buys is a REAL turn and ticks the cooldown with it. The card accelerates its own cooldown, which nothing in the brief anticipated and no reading of the code would have shown. What IS bounded is the thing that makes the mechanic safe, and it is asserted rather than described: every cast buys exactly one extra turn, the counter never rises above 2, and two can never be pending at once. Shipped as specified and flagged; the number to watch in play is the opening cadence, and the lever if it reads hot is Preparation's 5-turn cooldown.

WHAT "HIS COMPANION" RESOLVES TO UNDER THE PACK, decided rather than left to the first beasts[0] in the file. The general rule is worth more than either card: an ORDERED action goes to ONE companion; the passive strike-alongside goes to ALL of them.
