  • One old node had no home, and it is reported rather than forced. Ashes of Al'ar — the self-revive — has no successor anywhere in the new design, because §2 removes every defensive option deliberately. Its id carries Wildfire Spread now purely because a slot had to hold it; that is the batch's one assignment made on position rather than intent. Where it should go, if the designer wants it back: not into this tree. It is a Mage-wide or relic-shaped effect, and putting it back in a Pyromancer lane re-opens exactly the escape hatch the batch closed.
  • Cauterise is the health risk put back, once, as an opt-in. The drain sits on Mana so it would not be a clock he carries; one node that lets a player choose to carry it anyway is a decision rather than a tax, and it is the sharpest thing in the tree. Taking Kiln-Forged as well is legal, and the FLOOR WINS — a Pyromancer who paid for "the drain can never take me below 10" is not then billed in blood for the same drain.
  • The magnitudes are ADDITIVE, not ranked. Two fields are fed by a rune as well as by a node (Burn tick strength and Flamewave's turns), so each node writes its magnitude in the units its read site adds up. The node pays its number, the rune pays its number, and stacked they pay the sum. That is Batch AL's repair rule applied up front instead of after the fact.

THE SPEC RUNE AUDIT (and it found what it was sent to find). Most Pyromancer spec runes ride an existing talent counter rather than carrying their own machinery, and a rune pointing at a counter that no longer exists fails silently — no error, no log line. All four Pyromancer runes and all three Mage runes were checked against the new node set:

  • RE-POINTED — Rune of the Cinder Trail. The node took cinder_trail_ranks for a new meaning, so the rune was moved onto its own term and keeps paying exactly the effect it advertises (embers onto a second enemy). Its text is unchanged because its behaviour is.
  • STILL LIVE, now rune-only content — the Rune of the Blast Radius (Detonation consumes 25% more) and the Rune of the Long Burn (softer hits from burning enemies, Detonation crit). Their nodes are gone; their read sites were deliberately kept, because a rune whose node vanished wants re-authoring, not silent death.
  • FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED — the Rune of the White Flame's middle clause is INERT. It reads "Inferno Master grants +1% per burning enemy", and Overburn has no per-turn step to raise. Re-pointing it at the cap or the drain would be inventing a magnitude the design deliberately fixed, so the rune is left exactly as authored and this is the flag. Its other two clauses (resistance piercing, the health cost) are untouched and live. A test asserts the clause is inert, so a future re-authoring has to come and change that assertion rather than discover the problem.
  • The three Mage class runes (Wellspring, Reckless Channeling, Comet) touch nothing this batch moved.
  • runes.json changed by exactly one field name. This is a dead-counter re-point, not the rune-magnitude pass the designer closed in Batch AF.

THE BOT. The autoplay mage policy ignored Mana pressure entirely, and under Overburn a bot that never detonates to relieve the drain would measure a spec no player would recognise. It now knows the one rule that matters: consume Burn when the drain exceeds Mana regeneration — Detonation onto the largest stack, Wildfire when Detonation is cooling. This is instrument honesty, not tuning.

KIT SMOKE, AND ONE THING WORTH FLAGGING. Forty battles per row against the fixed lineup, with a full 8-node build force-learned (a standalone sim spends no talent points, so an unloaded run never touches these nodes at all). Every row 40/40 wins, no script errors, and every new ability shows up in the rotation. The Kindling lane is the standout by a distance — his damage share goes 46% ungeared to 66% on a full Kindling build, against 48% for Inferno and 50% for Detonation. Firestorm, Backdraft, Accelerant's tick and Conflagration's turns all compound, and the drain that is meant to price that does not bite inside a seven-round smoke fight. Measured and flagged, not nerfed: these are the batch's own magnitudes, so it ships as written. Kit-mechanics ratios only — the smoke lineup carries no difficulty signal.

NO DIFFICULTY MEASUREMENT WAS RUN, deliberately — the same reason Batches AJ, AK and AL recorded: a single-spec re-author has no honest control row against a fixed four-hero party, and ./sim.sh carries no difficulty signal.

TWO CLAIMS IN THE BATCH BRIEF WERE STALE, and are recorded rather than quietly actioned. (1) §6 asked for the Master Document's Wildfire text to be corrected, saying it described Wildfire spreading the target's Burn at half duration. It did not — Batch AG updated that passage and the doc already matched the code. (2) §4 warned that spec runes would break "quietly"; only one clause did, and it is the one flagged above. Both are the same lesson Batch AP recorded: a note in a brief is not evidence, and has to be re-read against the code before it is acted on.

2026-08-07 — Batch AQ: the modifier pool, 6 → 19, and upgrades you can see

Two things. The bargain's modifier pool goes from six placeholders to nineteen authored ones, weighted toward the mild end. And the ability upgrades Batch AP wired become visible outside a fight.

  • Thirteen new modifiers. Severity 1: Parched (both parties open at half resource), Slick Footing (+0.5 initiative on every ability), Dull Edge (crit chance halved), Muffled (all Break damage −25%), Hoarfrost (everyone opens Chilled). Severity 2: Fleeting (every status lasts one turn less, never below one), Feverish (everyone deals 25% more), Deadened (nobody can be Broken), Miasma (healing received halved). Severity 3: Thin Air (no resource returns at turn start), Encumbered (+2 turns on every cooldown that already had one). Severity 4: Bloodletting (every attack adds 15 Bleed), Mirrorbound (a quarter of the damage you deal comes back on you). The six existing modifiers are untouched — ids, severities and text — so a save holding a pending modifier still resolves.
  • The pool is weighted low on purpose. Six severity-1, six severity-2, four severity-3, three severity-4. Every offer's first card is drawn from the 1–2 pool, so that is the end a run actually sees over and over; the harsh end already rotates. Authoring the pool evenly would have deepened the half nobody repeats.
  • The other two cards now come from the severity 3–4 pool alone. They used to draw from everything left, low and high together. At six modifiers that was fine; at nineteen — twelve of them low — 86% of sampled offers came out holding two cheap options, three cheap rewards, and no real decision. Filling from the high pool makes every offer read the same way: one safe option, two gambles. The floor still guarantees the safe one, so a wounded party is never cornered. This is the only change in the batch that is not authoring.
  • Rot was authored, implemented, and dropped — and that is the finding worth keeping. It was to halve everyone's maximum health, and the risk flagged in advance was the percentage effects that read max HP. The real problem was somewhere else entirely: the end-of-battle sync writes the battle unit's max HP straight back onto the party member, so winning a Rot fight would have carried the halving out of the battle that charged for it — the map card would show the halved maximum, the party's health would be clamped under it, and a bargain sold as "one battle" would have taken half the party's HP for the rest of the run. Undoing that needs a seventh new field read at the save sync, which is past the field budget this batch set for itself, so it was dropped rather than patched around. Severity 4 ships with three modifiers instead of four; the pool is 19, not 20. Reinstating Rot is a small, separate decision, and it should be made deliberately.
  • Companions were missing every modifier — a pre-existing bug six modifiers made nearly invisible. The modifier is stamped on everyone at spawn, and a summoned beast exists at neither of those moments, so under Hoarfrost it would have been the only unit on the field not Chilled. Fixed at the summon site, beside the lines that already copy the hunter's armor, Stability and crit. Correction to the batch brief: it cited Feverish as an example of what the beast misses — it does not. The beast's Attack is copied from the hunter's, which is already modified, so Feverish (and Dull Edge) always reached it; stamping them again would have doubled them, and the fix skips exactly those two.
  • Ability upgrades are visible outside a fight now. A run awards three upgrades to every hero, twelve across the party, and until now every one of them was discoverable only by hovering ability buttons mid-battle. An upgraded ability wears a gold ◆ on its label — on the battle action button and on the hero sheet's chip — and each map hero card carries a ◆N count beside its rune slots, whose hover lists them one per line ("Overpower — Honed"). The badge takes no click of its own; the whole card is already the button that opens the tree. The hover line itself is unchanged from Batch AP: names only, because the magnitudes are already in the numbers above them. The hero sheet was capturing nothing from the call that applies upgrades; it reads that call's return now, so it can only ever mark an upgrade that really applied.
  • Four glossary entries: Ability Upgrades (under Progression, next to boss trophies), and The Bargain, Modifier and Severity under The Run, cross-linked to each other. Nineteen modifiers is the point at which the system needs one place explaining the system rather than nineteen descriptions each explaining one face.
  • Two shapes deliberately not authored, recorded so the rules stay visible: anything that touches only heroes ("no items this fight", "the skill-check window shrinks") breaks the binds-both-parties rule and is a difficulty slider wearing a bargain's clothes; and miss-chance modifiers, which would land cleanly on the hook Dazed already uses and play as tedium rather than tension. Rejected on feel, not on machinery.
  • Unchanged and stated as such: the reward table, the bot's severity-extreme bargain policy, the offer screen's layout, and the save version — nothing new persists.

2026-08-07 — Batch AP: the mini-boss reward becomes real

Ability upgrades were offered, picked, stored on the hero and saved — and nothing read them at battle spawn. Three mini-bosses a run handed out an inert prize. This batch wires the four placeholder upgrades and nothing else; the pool stays four, and no new upgrade is authored here.

  • The four upgrades now do something. Honed multiplies an ability's damage by 1.5. Quickened takes two turns off its cooldown, floored at 0. Effortless sets its resource cost to 0. Swift cuts its initiative delay by 25%, floored at 1.0.
  • Two of the four had their text corrected, because it was written before anything read it. Effortless zeroes the ordinary resource cost only — never Mercy. Mercy is the Holy Cleric's identity resource and a free Resurrection is a different game, so the description now says "costs no Rage / Mana / Focus (Mercy is unaffected)". Swift said "+2 initiative speed", but delays across the whole roster run 1.5–4.0, so subtracting 2 would have taken most abilities to near-zero — the authored number was never checked against the field it names. It is a 25% cut floored at 1.0 instead, described as "Arrives 25% sooner". That floor-and-percentage is the one balance judgement in this batch, and it is stated here rather than buried. Honed and Quickened keep their text as written.
  • Upgrades apply after talents, and the order is not interchangeable. One helper on Run, called from exactly the two places that assemble a hero's kit: the battle spawn and the hero sheet. Both call it after the talent tree and the equipped runes, because several talents set an ability's field rather than add to it — the Swordmaster node that upgrades Lunge sets its cost to 15 — so an Effortless applied first would be silently overwritten. Upgrades go last and always win. An upgrade naming an ability the hero no longer holds is skipped in silence; that can happen across a spec reroll and is not an error. The run simulator reloads the battle scene, so it inherits the same code with no separate change. Stacking and never-twice already worked and are untouched, and upgrades already persisted, so no save version moves.
  • The offer only pairs an upgrade with an ability it can change. It used to pair a random un-taken upgrade with a random owned ability, which could offer Honed on Heal (no damage), Effortless on Blood Price (no cost) or Quickened on a basic attack (no cooldown) — a pick that reads as a reward and does nothing, which is the exact bug this batch exists to close. Each candidate upgrade now keeps only the abilities it has something to touch, and an upgrade with nothing to land on is dropped from the offer rather than paired with a dud. An offer showing fewer than three was already normal and needs no new handling.
  • The player can see it. An upgraded ability's button in battle carries a trailing line naming its upgrades — "Honed · Swift". Names only: the magnitudes are already in the numbers above them, which now reflect the upgrade. The hero sheet assembles the kit the same way, so an Effortless ability loses its cost tag there too. Nothing else in the UI changes; the pick itself already resolved on the map hero card.
  • Talent tooltips stop reading "25.00%". Every tooltip in all twelve trees rendered its number to two decimals; the dead zeros and a trailing decimal point are trimmed, so a whole 25 reads "25" and a genuine 2.5 still reads "2.5". This had been reported and not acted on since Batch AJ. The Master Document's talent tables were regenerated to match, but only where the dead decimal was the only difference from the live text.
  • Housekeeping: one test check formatted an Array into a bare %s and spewed a "String formatting error" to stderr on every run — one character. The treasure/Loot node type needed no deleting: it was already gone, taken with the whole node-map generator when Batch AN replaced it with the line. It had been listed as outstanding since Batch AC; the listing was stale, not the code.

2026-08-07 — Batch AO: map direction, offer gating, and a kill switch

Three changes from playing Batch AN. No new systems, and no balance work beyond the one gold number in the second item.

  • The road now reads LEFT TO RIGHT. Encounter 1 sits on the left edge and the boss on the right. Batch AN flagged right-to-left as unconventional and shipped it anyway; it read wrong in play, so it is flipped. It was two constants, as AN said it would be (SLOT_X_START moves to the exact mirror of its old value across the 1280-wide screen, and the step now adds instead of subtracting — the line keeps its old margins, reversed). The compass label under the road is deleted: it existed only because the direction was unconventional, and left-to-right is what a reader already assumes. The slot numbers 1–12 under the dots stay — twelve near-identical dots want a ruler whichever way the road runs.
  • The offer moves to ELITES and MINI-BOSSES; plain fights pay gold instead. A bargain screen before all eight plain fights in a zone made it a toll booth. It is an event now: four encounters a zone instead of ten. Bosses still get no offer. A mini-boss is therefore fought under a modifier, which is intended — every enemy in a mini-boss warband already carries 1.5× max HP, so a severity-4 pick there is a real gamble, and the guaranteed low-severity option is what makes it a choice rather than a trap. The mini-boss's existing spoils (elite gold, 1 talent point, the ability-upgrade pick) are untouched and now stack with the bargain's reward. Plain-fight gold covers the hole: 25–35 → 45–60. Elite/mini-boss (80–100) and boss (110–130) are unchanged. It is deliberately below the old bargain payout, because a plain fight no longer charges a modifier for it. The severity-1-or-2 floor, the no-decline rule and reward-on-victory are all unchanged, and the run sim's harness walks the same gate so a simulated run walks the road the player walks.
  • New: battle DEBUG ▾ → Kill All Enemies. A tester can reach the victory screen on demand. It is a switch, not a hit: every living enemy is set to 0 HP and killed directly rather than through the damage path, so there is no damage event, no on-hit or overkill proc and no floating number. The deliberate consequence is that on-death talent procs which read a killing blow (Seeding Embers and friends) do not fire on a nuked kill — the accepted cost of a switch. Everything after the kills is the real victory path: gold, talent points, the 15% heal, the bargain's reward, elite spoils and the run summary, which is exactly what needs testing. It inherits the existing debug gate and the debug_used honesty flag from the menu's one dispatch, so a debug-touched run still declares itself in the summary.

2026-08-07 — Batch AN: the map scaffold

Rewards and modifiers in this batch are PLACEHOLDERS drawn from content that already exists. The point is to make a full 36-encounter run playable so the pacing can be felt before 66 pieces of new content are authored against it. Nothing here is final art or final content.

  • The branching node map is gone; a run is a LINE. 3 zones × 12 encounters = 36, and every zone has the identical shape: fight, fight, ELITE, fight, fight, MINI-BOSS, fight, fight, ELITE, fight, fight, BOSS. Zone 3's boss is the end boss. The road renders right to left — encounter 1 on the right edge, the boss on the left. (Horizontal run-maps conventionally read left-to-right, so an English-reading player may parse the boss end as the start; this was flagged, chosen anyway, and is two constants if it flips.)
  • Deleted rather than left unreachable: FLOORS, NODES_PER_TIER, the deck composition constants (FIGHT_NODES/REST_NODES/SHOP_NODES/EVENT_NODES), both DECK_FALLBACK tables, MINIBOSS_TIER, the rejection-sampling deal and its swap repair, the link graph, the inbound guarantee, and the forward-DP key-route check. All rest nodes and the rest-heal path go with them. So does the edge-column adjacency rule and its documented-70%/actual-53% bug — it needed deleting, not fixing. Batch AF's starting rune pick is deleted too: heroes now begin with no runes and empty slots. A test pins each of these as ABSENT, because a constant that still resolves is a constant a later batch reads by accident.
  • New: the offer screen. Before every fight and elite — not mini-bosses, not bosses — the player is shown three bargains and takes one. A bargain is one modifier (a condition binding BOTH parties for that battle) plus one reward, both visible before choosing, with no decline. Each modifier carries a severity of 1–4 and the reward table reads it, so authoring a modifier is authoring one number rather than a pairing. Severity is flat and deliberately ignores party composition — a modifier that happens to be cheap for your build is a good deal you earned by building that way. Every offer holds at least one option of severity 1 or 2, guaranteed by construction rather than by rejecting rolls, so a wounded party always has a survivable choice. The reward pays on victory: the modifier is the price, and the "a merchant follows the fight" reward settles that a reward cannot precede the fight it follows.
  • Six placeholder modifiers, to be replaced by the authored 20 — each built out of a hook battle.gd already had, each landing at exactly one read site: Overgrown (1, both parties open at 70% health), Tinderbox (2, all fire +25%), Frenzied (2, everyone acts 30% faster, cooldowns unchanged), Brittle (3, all attacks ignore armor), Warded (3, abilities cost 25% more, basics free), Bloodless (4, no healing for anyone; Bleed and damage-over-time still tick). NOTE on Warded: basic attacks are cost 0 already, so "basic attacks are free" describes the kit rather than changing it — the multiplier is written to never add to a zero, which is the line that keeps it true.
  • Placeholder rewards, existing content only. Severity 1: 40 gold. 2: 80 gold or a random potion. 3: 140 gold or a random rune. 4: 220 gold, a random rune, or a merchant follows the fight.
  • The map screen is the party screen now. All four hero stat cards live on it — portrait, spec name, HP bar with numbers, resource bar, three rune slots (filled or empty), unspent-talent badge. Clicking a card opens that hero's talent tree; clicking a rune slot opens their pouch. Owed ability, upgrade and rune picks resolve on the card. The Party button and its separate screen are gone; the old Party screen survives as the hero sheet, entered for one hero with a four-button switcher and its list view deleted.
  • Rewards re-cut. The mini-boss now awards a generic ability upgrade chosen from three, attached to an ability the hero owns — upgrades stack on the same ability, but the same upgrade never comes twice in a run. Placeholder pool of four until the dozen are authored: Honed (+50% damage), Quickened (−2 cooldown), Effortless (no resource cost), Swift (+2 initiative speed). Zone 1 and 2 bosses award an ability pick from three, drawn from the hero's spec pool only — the class-pool draw Batch AH added is dropped, abilities are spec-locked now. (Classes.CLASS_POOLS is left standing and still resolves; nothing reads it, and reopening the class draw is one line.) The end boss awards a relic unlock, big gold, and ends the run — no ability pick, because nothing follows it.
  • The shop is scheduled, not placed. 40% chance of a merchant after any cleared fight or elite, with a floor: four encounters without one and the next is guaranteed. Plus the severity-4 reward, which guarantees one on demand. Both the merchant and the 25% event roll are made once, on the victory screen, and queued — rolling them from the map would re-roll on every redraw and the floor would mean nothing.
  • Attrition: no rest nodes. Clearing any encounter heals the party 15% of max HP, riding the same victory_heal_pct hook the Chalice of Dawn already used, so the relic's 10% stacks on top for 25% and there is still exactly one read site for "how much does a victory heal". Potions are usable on the map screen, targeting a hero from the stat cards (the Bomb and the Defense Potion stay battle-only and say why on hover). Potion cap: 6 per item type — purchases and drops above it are refused with a message rather than silently lost, and the shop greys a full stack rather than taking the gold.
  • Talent points: 1 apiece from elites, mini-bosses and bosses — the end boss included, where it used to pay nothing. Regular fights award none. That is 4 a zone, 12 a run, against an 8-node tree. The two purses became one, and the arithmetic is why: Batch AI had 8 points against 8 nodes, so an elite point had to be BARRED from second nodes or the tree could be climbed faster than intended. At 12 against 8 the shape does the barring by itself — rows are mutually exclusive and there are only eight, so a purse can open at most 8 rows and the surplus has nowhere to go but second nodes. The flex purse survives in the data and is spent first when it holds anything; ordinary points cover these picks when it is empty.
  • Runes: three slots, flat, from run start. The 2 → 3 → 4 growth ladder is gone. Heroes start with none. Rune content is unchanged in this batch — the rebuild (deleting ability-granting and talent-rank runes, authoring ~36 double-edged ones) is its own batch.
  • SAVE v7, and pre-v7 saves are REFUSED and cleared on load. A pre-v7 save holds a [tier][column] board with links, rest nodes and a mini-boss row; there is no honest way to place a party standing at tier 7 column 2 onto a line with no columns. Same call Batch AI made about ranked talent purchases — a wipe that says so beats a migration that invents state.
  • Sim harness: the map walk follows the line, the bot takes bargains by a severity-extreme policy (harshest above 60% average party HP, mildest below), and the report gains merchants-met, events-fired, bargains-taken and average accepted severity while losing the rest lines. DOD_SIM_MAP, DOD_SIM_MINIBOSS, DOD_SIM_START_RUNE and DOD_SIM_SPEC_OPENING are retired with the features they controlled; a Matrix row now reads map=line and carries none of those fields. Rows from before the road are not comparable with rows after it — even depth changed units (36 encounters, not 33 tiers). "Route agency" is retained and reads 0% forever by design: a line has no route decision, and a missing figure would look like a broken instrument.
  • Verified: new test_batch_an.gd, 5,667 checks / 0 failures, stable 3/3 — the line's shape and its one-way-forward walk, every deleted constant and function pinned ABSENT, 2,000 sampled offers for the severity-1-or-2 floor (0 misses) and for severity-matched rewards, all six modifiers stamped on BOTH parties in a live battle and checked at the read site each one implements, a no-modifier battle proving the pre-AN path is untouched, the upgrade pool's stacking and never-twice rules, spec-only ability draws, the merchant floor driven rather than sampled (no drought exceeds four), the item cap refusing rather than swallowing, and the flat three rune slots. Regression: test_batch_ah 5,416/0, test_batch_ah_battle 65/0, test_batch_ai 2,036/0, test_batch_aj 389/0, test_batch_ak 524/0, test_batch_al 556/0, test_runes 2,982/0, run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS, 11 scenes and every script compiling with 0 SCRIPT ERROR. Known-bad and not ours: test_rune_battle 91/1, the Inferno chip check Batch AK recorded as a standing defect. test_start_rune.gd and test_start_rune_ui.gd are deleted with the feature they pinned.

2026-08-06 — Batch AL: the Warden's 24 nodes

  • All 24 tree nodes re-authored for row exclusivity. The third of the four class batches Batch AI promised. Every id survives, so saved picks migrate and no save version moves (still v6). Since AI a node is not one of three ranks — it is the whole row, priced against the two doors it closes, which came out at roughly 3-4× the old rank-1 values: Unkillable 2% → 8% of the health he brought in, Richocet 5% → 35% stun chance, Toughness 5% → 25% of max HP as Constitution, Provoke +1 → +2 taunted foes, Rally +15%/2 turns → +30%/3 turns, Endurance 1% → 3% armor per unhealed turn, Iron Will 4% → 12% per debuff, Tenacity +5 → +15 max HP per block, Sundering 25% → 100% of the Break splash, Elemental Weakness 5% → 20% resist shred, Shield Mastery +1 → +2 turns of stance, Spite 8% → 30% reflected, Plate Discipline +3% → +12% on the plating climb, Bruising Guard 10 → 30 Break damage, Shared Vigil 3% → 12%, Battered Not Broken 8 → 30 Break shed, Grudge 6% → 25%, Steadfast 15% → 60% absorbed.
  • The rows are themed, not merely exclusive. 1 who your defence pays, 2 how much you hold, 3 attrition, 4 what compounds, 5 active defence, 6 the engine running, 7 the last stand, 8 the capstone. Row 1 is the model for the whole tree: one trigger, three beneficiaries — a block heals him, a block stuns them, a taunt empowers the party.
  • Two nodes were re-specced in place — same id, new effect — and for the same reason. Batch AH moved the ability each one modified into the earnable spec pool, so both were dead on a Warden who never drew it. Rallying Stomp ("War Stomp restores +5% more resource") became Rallying Cry: at the start of each of the Warden's turns every ally regains 4% of their maximum resource, and War Stomp — if he owns it — restores 20% more on top. Bulwark Line ("Interpose grants +1 charge") now keys to Shieldwall, which he has always had since Batch G promoted it into the base kit: the stance also grants every ally +10% Block chance for its duration, and Interpose — if he owns it — still hands each ally an extra charge. The refuel and the cover are Banner's real cargo; they happen on their own now, and the earnable abilities ride on top.
  • Tank and Spank is CERTAIN. It was a 15% chance to Empower an ally off Mocking Blow. Mocking Blow is free and on his rotation constantly, so a chance roll there read as noise rather than tension — nothing was ever planned around it. It always fires now.
  • Spite and Bruising Guard stopped being an exclusive fork. They sat in one tier as "reflect the damage you soak, or convert your blocks into Break". Split across rows 5 and 6 both are reachable, so taking the second welds them into one continuous Break engine instead of two unrelated numbers: with Spite taken, its reflected damage also builds Break equal to 50% of its value.
  • Hold the Line's capstone upgrades an earned copy. The ability also sits in the Warden spec pool (Batch AH), so drawing it early used to make the capstone the worst pick in its row — a second copy of a button you already have. Taken on an ability he already owns it now UPGRADES instead: the Break reduction rises from 50% to 80%, and the no-death window lasts two turns rather than one. Same pattern as the Swordmaster's Lunge and Execute and the Berserker's Battle Shout and Rampage.
  • Two Warden runes repaired in passing. The Rune of Grudges and the Rune of the Standard each added a RANK to a talent counter whose per-rank value this batch multiplies by four. Left alone, a rune advertising "+6% damage against his taunted mark" would quietly have started paying 25% — a magnitude change nobody authored, and exactly the rune-magnitude pass the designer closed in Batch AF. Both now carry their own smaller term alongside the node's, so each pays its advertised number whether it is worn alone or beside the talent. Same repair as Batch AK made to the Rune of the Still Wrist, for the same reason.
  • New status: Bulwark Line. The ally Block grant rides the same Heavy Plating slice of the block roll that Shieldwall's own stance does, so what it buys is real Block rather than a separate ward — and a block it buys is logged as "(Bulwark Line)". It does NOT feed the Warden's Tenacity or Rally, which key on his own Heavy Plating blocks.
  • Measured, flagged, not nerfed. Kit smoke test, fixed lineup, 40 battles per row, force-learned 8-node builds (a standalone sim spends no points, so an unloaded run never touches these nodes at all). All rows 40/40 wins, 0 SCRIPT ERROR. The THREAT lane is the standout by a distance: his Break damage per battle 104 → 320 and the party's Breaks per battle 1.02 → 2.35, with his damage share 17% → 30% — that is Sundering at a full 100% splash plus the newly-reachable Spite/Bruising Guard pair. The BANNER build shows up in statuses applied per battle (1.3 → 5.7) rather than damage, and the PLATE build barely moves against a lineup the party already survives at 85% health. Kit-mechanics ratios only — the fixed smoke lineup carries NO difficulty signal (Batch R). No difficulty measurement was run, deliberately: a content re-author of one spec has no honest control row, because the sim's damage-share instrument reads a fixed four-hero party.
  • Verified. New test_batch_al.gd, 556 checks / 0 failures, stable 3/3: tree shape, all 24 ids/rows/lanes/names, every magnitude in BOTH the payload and the tooltip that renders it, all three conditional halves firing / dark / inert on an empty ctx, the upgrade path in both acquisition orders, both repaired runes paying alone and stacked, and a live battle for the ally cover, the refuel, the taunt spread, the block payoffs and the upgraded capstone. 2026-08-06 — Batch AJ: the Berserker's 24 nodes

  • All 24 tree nodes re-authored for row exclusivity. Every id survives, so saved picks migrate and no save version moves. The rows have been mutually exclusive since Batch AI, which means a node is no longer one of three ranks — it is the whole row, priced against the two doors it closes. Concretely: Savagery +5 → +15 Bleed, Unstoppable 2.5% → 3.5% per step, Hemorrhage's threshold 80 → 60 bloodloss, Reckless Fury 5%/5% → 20% dealt / 15% taken, Flurry +1 → +2 strikes, Crushing Blows 3% → 9% per step, Bloodied Momentum 15 → 40 Rage, Arterial Spray 25% → a full transfer, Deathwish 6% → 25%, Relentless −5 → −15 Rage, Scent of Blood 3% → 10% per bleedout, Scar Tissue's floor 60% → 85%, Second Wind 40 → 60 Rage, Bloodcraze 3% → 12% max HP, Measured Rage 8% → 20%, Unrelenting Assault +10 → +40 Constitution, Blood Tithe 15 → 45 Rage, Enraged 3% → 12% per stack.
  • The rows are themed now. Each row asks one question and each lane answers it its own way: 1 the opening, 2 the wound, 3 what the wound pays, 4 the edge, 5 what compounds, 6 refusal, 7 the finish, 8 the capstone. Batch AI cut the old tiers into rows mechanically, which left several rows with no question in them at all.
  • Two nodes were re-specced in place — same id, new effect. Vitality (+5% max HP) became First Blood: the Berserker begins every battle with 40 Rage. A flat health dial is not an opening. Deafening Cry (Battle Shout's cooldown) became Overkill: killing an enemy clears the cooldowns of Hack and Slash and Wildstrikes. AI's mechanical row assignment had put Deafening Cry in the same row as Battle Shout itself, and two exclusive nodes where one exists only to modify the other is a row with a dead option in it.
  • Three cross-row conditions. Crushing Blows counts every 15 points of bloodloss instead of 20 if Savagery was taken. Scar Tissue's Frenzy floor holds 100% of the peak — never falling at all — if Unstoppable was taken. Measured Rage with Reckless Fury cancels that node's +15% damage taken outright rather than subtracting from it, so the pair buys consequence-free damage: two nodes for a clean +20%, or one node and eat the risk.
  • Two upgrade paths. Battle Shout and Rampage sit in the Berserker's spec pool as well as his tree. A node on an ability he does not own grants it; on one he earned from a pick it upgrades instead — Battle Shout to +18% for 4 turns (from +12% for 3), Rampage's kill-recast to twice a turn.
  • Rampage's recast is capped for the first time. It used to chain for as long as the kills kept coming, which is a capstone with no ceiling and nothing left for an upgrade path to buy. It is once per turn now, twice with the upgrade.
  • Fixed: Measured Rage has been doing nothing since Batch AI. The damage-taken read site was guarded > 0.0, which silently ate every negative value — and Measured Rage's whole payload is a negative. The node has been inert for two batches. The guard now reads any non-zero value, and the batch's own test spawns a live Berserker to prove the reduction lands.
  • Second Wind clears every cooldown as well as granting its Rage, which is what makes the near-death moment a whole turn rather than a resource top-up.
  • Relentless buys reliability permanently. Hack and Slash's bleed roll always lands with it — the Batch AG rule that a perfect on a swingy ability pays in reliability rather than magnitude, bought once instead of earned per cast.
  • Naming collision, reported not resolved: the Sharpshooter's Precision lane already has a talent called Overkill (a kill's overflow damage carries to another enemy). Different trees and different ids, so nothing breaks — but two nodes now share a name in tooltips. The engine field was named overkill_reset to keep them apart.

Known-bad and not ours: test_rune_battle 91/1, the standing Inferno-chip defect.

This is a content re-author of ONE spec, and the sim's damage-share instrument reads a fixed four-hero party, so a single-spec re-tune has no honest control row (the same reasoning Batch AK recorded). Several values are 2–3× their old rank-1 numbers by design: a hero now gets 8 nodes a run instead of a third of a 24-node tree, so per-node impact has to rise to match. Concretely: the stance nodes 3% → 12%, Sword Mastery 3% → 12% parry, Killing Edge 4% → 15% crit, Bracing +8 → +30 Constitution, Dominant Presence 5% → 15% armor per debuff, Precision Strikes 5% → 20% crit, Seasoned Fighter 3% → 15%, No Quarter 15 → 45 Rage, Overwhelm 3% → 8% per debuff, Punishment 15% → 60%, Tempo 10% → 30%, Off Balance 5% → 20%, Pressure Point +8 → +30 BD, High Guard 25% for 1 turn → 40% for 2.

The old target did not disappear so much as become a bonus — if he owns Shatterpoint anyway, that gains +40 BD too. A node aimed at a guaranteed button that pays extra on a lucky draw is strictly better than one aimed only at the draw.
  • Swordsmanship became a spike he earns rather than a number he owns. A perfect Guard Change now grants +25% parry for 2 turns (the ability's own 10% plus the node's 15). It rides the existing Parry Up chip with a live counter, and the whole value now lives in the granted status power rather than being added again at the roll — so what the chip says is exactly what the parry roll reads.
  • Riposte answers with a free Overpower instead of a basic Strike, reusing the recast machinery Opportunist already had. Opportunist now answers a parry as well as a whiff. They are the same answer bought from two different lanes and both are reachable (rows 6 and 4), so a parry fires one counter, not two; the log names the node that paid for it. The Untouchable capstone's free Pommel Strike still takes precedence in the Defensive stance.
  • Punishment and Off Balance stopped being an exclusive pair. Split across rows 6 and 7 they are both reachable, and two "+% versus Broken" numbers stacking would be redundant rather than interesting. So with Punishment also taken, Off Balance widens what counts as a window — Exposed and Crippled targets pay out too — instead of adding to the same number.
  • Lunge and Execute sit in the spec pool AND the tree, so the node upgrades a copy he already earned. Lunge drops to 15 Rage and applies both Exposed and Crippled whatever the guard; Execute's threshold rises from 20% to 35% health and it costs no Rage against a Broken target. Neither is ever granted twice, in either order of acquisition.
  • New payload machinery, two keys. also holds extra payloads applied alongside the main one, each carrying its own condition — that is how one node has two halves under different conditions (Sunder Guard's Shatterpoint hook, owns_ability; Off Balance's widening, has_node) without a second node id. upgrade holds payloads applied instead of granting when the ability is already in the kit. The batch asked for owns_ability on all three checks and it is the wrong instrument for two of them: a learned node's own grant is itself in ability_names(), so after taking the Lunge node owns_ability(member, "Lunge") is true no matter where Lunge came from. The only honest question is "was it in the kit when the tree ran", and the abilities list is what knows that. Shatterpoint's hook does use owns_ability, because no node grants Shatterpoint.
  • The Rune of the Still Wrist was repaired in passing. It wrote pommel_parry_bonus and advertised "a perfect Pommel Strike's parry blessing" — a blessing that stopped existing in Batch AH, when Pommel's perfect became the boss Stun. It has been half-dead since, and this batch's field rename would have killed it outright. It now pays into the live field and names Guard Change. That field is additive rather than a replacement for exactly this reason: a max() against the talent's value would have left the rune silently inert on its own. Rune alone = a 15% grant, node alone = 25%, both = 30%.
  • Verified: new test_batch_ak.gd, 524 checks / 0 failures, stable across three runs — the kit swap and its single-definition property, every pool entry of all twelve specs and four classes still resolving, all 24 nodes' id/row/lane/magnitude, both tooltip and payload (they are two hand-written places), both conditional halves firing and staying dark including on an empty ctx, both upgrade paths in both acquisition orders, and a live battle for the BD spread, the parry spike, the parry counter, Execute's pricing and the upgraded Lunge. Regression: test_batch_ai 2,042/0, test_batch_ah 4,284/0 (its Guard Change trim assertion re-pointed, with the reason in the file), test_batch_ah_battle 62/0, test_runes 3,130/0, test_start_rune 239/0, test_start_rune_ui 31/0, run-harness gates 1/2/3 PASS. Headless parse: all 10 scenes, 0 SCRIPT ERROR. One pre-existing failure, not caused by this batch and not fixed by it: test_rune_battle 91/1, the Inferno chip check — it reproduces 3 of 3 on unmodified HEAD in a clean worktree, so it is a standing defect in that check rather than a regression.
  • Measured, and flagged rather than second-guessed: Sunder Guard is the largest single node in the tree by a distance. On the fixed smoke-test lineup (60 battles, one node forced, everything else at default) it takes the Swordmaster's Break damage from 158 to 649 per battle and the party's Breaks from 1.33 to 5.43 per battle — 4.1x on both. His own damage share falls, 29% to 23%, because he spends those turns pivoting instead of swinging; what he is really doing is opening windows for the other three. That is the node as the batch specified it (40 BD to every enemy, on a 0-Rage 1-cooldown button), so it ships as written and this is the note rather than a quiet nerf. The smoke-test lineup carries no difficulty signal (Batch R) — these are kit-mechanics ratios, not a balance verdict.
  • Not in this batch: the other ten trees and enemy tuning, both untouched as instructed. No difficulty measurement was run — this is a content re-author of one spec, and the sim's damage-share instrument reads a fixed four-hero party, so a single-spec re-tune has no honest control row.

2026-08-06 — Fix: a rune triple could offer the same rune twice

  • The pick-of-3 rune offer could contain a duplicate — roughly one triple in a hundred, which surfaced as an intermittent test failure on the Warden and, in play, as an awakening or elite cache that presented the same choice twice. The roller drew each candidate independently and, on a collision, rerolled up to four times — then appended the result unchecked. Two ways to lose: every reroll could collide, and the last reroll was never tested at all (the check sat at the top of the retry loop, so four checks covered five draws). On a small per-rarity pool both were reachable.
  • Fixed by drawing without replacement instead of rolling and hoping. The names already in the triple now ride the same exclusion channel the owned pouch already used — a rune sitting in the offer is exactly as unavailable as one already worn — so the pool a candidate is picked from cannot contain its siblings. A duplicate is not merely unlikely, it is unreachable. Measured 0 duplicates in 4,000 triples on both the guaranteed and the ordinary path, where the old roller produced them on both.
  • The default path changed too, deliberately. It had the same defect (it just needed three unlucky draws rather than a seeded one), so the fix reaches it, and its roll sequence moves: fewer random numbers, because the wasted retries are gone, and a smaller pool for draws two and three. The Batch AF test that pinned this path against a verbatim copy of the old loop was re-transcribed to the corrected one — keeping the old copy frozen would have asserted the bug had to stay forever. Its distinctness assertion is new: the default path never had one, which is why only the guaranteed path ever caught this, and only sometimes.

2026-08-06 — Batch AI: talent tree structure — seven rows, eight decisions

  • Every tree is now seven mutually exclusive ROWS plus a capstone row. A row holds one node per lane and the player picks exactly one of the three; that pick shuts the other two permanently. They stay visible and greyed with the reason in the tooltip — the player must see the door they closed — and a node not yet taken names the two doors taking it would shut. Rows were assigned mechanically from the existing data: within each lane, nodes ordered by their old tier then by definition order, numbered 1–7. Every lane had exactly seven non-capstone nodes, so the mapping was one-to-one and nothing moved on screen. exclusive_with is gone — sixteen authored pairs across nine specs, all superseded by row exclusivity.
  • Row 1 is open from the start; row N opens when row N−1 has been picked. The capstones become row 8: open at 7/7, take one, from any lane — the lane-purity requirement is gone. Every node costs 1 point and holds a single rank, no exceptions. A complete tree is 8 nodes.
  • THE POINT SUPPLY NOW MATCHES THE TREE EXACTLY. 1 for confirming a spec (paid at the awakening, from both the spec screen and the sim's start_run — the sync_spec_hp pattern), 1 per mini-boss, 2 per zone boss, 0 for regular fights, 0 for the final boss. A three-zone run guarantees 1 + 3 + 4 = 8 points, exactly one complete tree. The question stops being "how many nodes can I afford" and becomes "which eight".
  • ELITE POINTS ARE A SEPARATE PURSE (§6 of the brief, taken rather than cut). An elite kill pays 1 — 0–3 a run. They cannot open a new row. The only thing they buy is a second node in a row already picked, forcing that one row's door back open; the third node in that row stays shut forever. This is what makes hunting elites read as "widen a choice I already made" rather than "climb the tree faster", and it keeps the guaranteed 8 honest. Normal points can never buy a second node in a row, and the sim's bot spends normal points before flex (flex can never open a row, so banking a normal point to spend flex is strictly worse).
  • Retired machinery, deleted rather than left unreachable: LANE_TIER_REQ, NODE_TIER_REQ, CAPSTONE_REQ, NODE_CAPSTONE_REQ, ROW_REQ, FIXED_TREES, LANE_CONVERSIONS, next_node_cost, node_cost, lane_nodes_bought, lane_points, points_below_row, is_node_gated, is_lane_tree, the node_gated flag, the per-node tier field, and member["talent_order"] (which existed only to replay the ceil(N/3) price curve). The party screen's classic-tree renderer went with FIXED_TREES. desc_for() stays — it already rendered {v} at rank 1 for unlearned previews, which is now the only case there is.
  • HOOKS FOR THE FOUR CLASS BATCHES (§5), built but not yet used by any node. Talents.has_node(learned, id) — was this node taken. Talents.owns_ability(member, name) — does the hero have this ability from ANY source: starting kit, kit override, mini-boss/boss pick, or talent grant. A payload may now carry a condition ({"has_node": id} / {"owns_ability": name}, or both), evaluated at ONE read site inside apply_payload; a conditional payload with no context is inert rather than silently unconditional, because an effect that fails to appear is a bug you can see. Both statics are callable from battle.gd at resolve time.
  • owned_ability_names moved from Run to Talents, and this is load-bearing. §5 asked owns_ability to read the same list the action bar reads, and it could not: GDScript does not resolve autoload identifiers inside a class_name script (the same constraint that makes RunSim take Run injected). So the implementation now lives as Talents.ability_names(member) and Run.owned_ability_names forwards to it — one list, not two copies that could drift. The Talents → Runes → Classes → Talents cycle this creates resolves fine (verified headless, not assumed).
  • Save migration: save version 6. A save from before this batch holds learned talents under the old ranked, point-priced scheme — ranks that no longer exist, bought at prices that no longer exist — so there is no honest translation. The tree is WIPED and the purse re-issued on the new schedule: 1 for the spec choice, 2 per zone boss cleared, 1 per mini-boss cleared (zone bosses counted by zone_idx, since a zone is only left by killing its boss; the mini-boss sits at a fixed tier, so "cleared" is "past that tier"). The player re-picks their eight rows with a full purse. Same-version saves keep the old behaviour.
  • Test coverage: new test_batch_ai.gd (2042 checks) pins the shape of all twelve trees, the row gating, the elite crack including that no row ever holds three, the hooks, payload conditions, the 8-point economy and the migration. The run harness's gate 2 (talent spend conservation) was rewritten for flat pricing and now also asserts a fed hero lands on a complete tree with a capstone. test_runes.gd's exclusive-pair alarm was RETIRED, with its reasoning left in the file: it watched authored pairs, and at row granularity every spec rune in the game would trip it — that is the alarm asking a question the design no longer answers the same way. Whether a rune should grant a counter whose node sits in a row the player passed on is a real question for the class batches to answer with the nodes, and then re-arm.
  • EXPECTED STATE, stated plainly: the tree is structurally correct and numerically weak. Rows are lopsided, because the 21 existing nodes per spec were authored to stack within a lane rather than compete across a row — Savagery and Hemorrhage were built to be taken together and now sit as alternatives. Several rows have one obviously correct pick. Single-rank values are the old rank-1 values, so roughly a third of their intended power. None of this was tuned or re-homed to compensate: the four class batches re-author all 252 nodes.
    Measured, 30 runs each side, same flags (route=default, map=new, standard, all shipped content on): depth 17.10±1.55 → 13.40±0.86 (bands do not overlap — runs now die a full zone earlier); wipe median z2 t7.5 → z1 t11.0; talent nodes owned entering a boss 5.0 → 2.6; points earned per hero per run 17.4 → 3.6 (partly the new schedule, partly that shorter runs collect less — a run that went the distance would bank exactly 8). ratio@z1t8 is flat, 0.97 → 0.98, and completions are 0% both sides: the party's raw stat ratio barely moved, so what was lost is the conditional and proc power the extra ranks were paying for. These are readings of placeholder content, not a difficulty signal — do not tune against them until the nodes are written.

2026-08-05 — Batch AH: ability progression — three to start, six to earn

  • Every hero now opens a run with its core attack plus exactly THREE spec abilities, and earns six more over the run. Nothing was written for this batch: every earnable ability already existed as a kit piece, a talent grant, or a vaulted one whose machinery never left battle.gd. Trimmed out of their opening kits and made earnable: the Berserker's Blood Price; the Warden's War Stomp and Interpose; the Swordmaster's Sweeping Strikes and Guard Change. Pyromancer, Cryomancer, Arcanist, Holy, Devout, Occultist, Sharpshooter and Survivalist already held exactly three and were left alone — and so was the Beastmaster, which is already at three under the batch's own counting rule: the Summon Companion picker is ONE slot however many beasts it offers (the action bar has always grouped them that way), plus Hunter's Instinct and Kill Command.
  • WARDEN AND SWORDMASTER — the judgment calls, and their reasons. The Warden keeps Mocking Blow (his only 0-cost Rage generator: without it he cannot afford his own opening), Crushing Blow (his damage and his Sunder) and Shieldwall (the Block identity Batch G deliberately promoted out of the tree and into the base kit). War Stomp is a mid-fight AoE, and Batch AB already found that Interpose and Shieldwall are the same verb pointed two ways — so the redundant half is the one that becomes earnable. GUARD CHANGE IS FLAGGED, NOT ARGUED WITH. The batch named the Swordmaster's three keepers explicitly, which leaves Guard Change earnable — and Guard Change is the ONLY way to swap stance, so until a Swordmaster earns it back he fights every battle Aggressive and half of Seasoned Fighter is inert. His tree still sells four stance nodes that would sit dead beside it. That is a real consequence of an explicit instruction, so it shipped as written and is recorded here rather than quietly reinterpreted.
  • Two pools, and a curation rule with teeth. SPEC_POOLS now covers all twelve specs: each spec's own trims, its talent-granted abilities, and its own vaulted ones. CLASS_POOLS is new — four entries holding the sibling specs' abilities plus the class's vaulted ones. An entry only reaches a class pool if it FUNCTIONS for a sibling. Excluded and why: Hymn of Hope, Resurrection, Divine Plea (faith_cost — Mercy is Holy-only, Faith is Devout-only, and a sibling has no stacks to pay with); Detonation and Wildfire (Burn consumers, and Wildfire is hard-gated with nothing alight); Shatter (hard-gated with nobody Chilled); Arcane Cannon, Magi's Wrath, Stabilize, Overcharge (Resonance — the first two scale their damage AND their entire Break contribution off stacks a sibling never builds, so they land as strictly-worse basics; the last two are outright no-ops); Bestial Wrath, Spirit Bond, Primal Surge (a living companion or Loyalty); Coup de Grâce (consumes all Focus); Lunge and Guard Change (the Swordmaster's stance — stance defaults to "aggressive" on every unit, so a sibling's Lunge could only ever Expose and never Cripple, which is half an ability); and the three named identity pieces, the summons, Kill Command and Hex of Ruin. Kept with their inert riders noted rather than excluded: Hold Breath and Aimed Shot (the Focus they grant is a rider; a guaranteed armour-ignoring crit and a 45% hit are the abilities), Arcane Surge and Reality Fracture (the +20% attack and the six-point initiative shove are the abilities; the Resonance line is a rider), Mark of the Hunt (its +25% keys on the caster's index, not on the Pack passive — only the Mana drip is Beastmaster-only), Hunter's Instinct (it empowers Quick Shot, which every Hunter spec has).
  • The vault, unsealed — and the five that could not come back. Returning as earnable picks, all on machinery that never left battle.gd: Rallying Shout (warrior), Retaliation (Warden), Mana Shield, Arcane Surge, Reality Fracture, Phoenix Rebirth (mage), Dawnbreak, Sanctuary, Divine Wrath (cleric), Umbral Sigil (Occultist). Pyroblast, Flame Surge, Frost Bolt, Death Ray and Mend Wounds did NOT: their special handlers went with them, so they exist only as prose in a comment and reviving them would mean AUTHORING them — which this batch's own opening line forbids. The three restored abilities whose full dicts survived (Mana Shield, Arcane Surge, Reality Fracture) came back verbatim; the other seven needed a cost/cooldown/initiative wrapper around effects the code already defines exactly, and those numbers are new and are the one place this batch made a balance judgment.
  • NOT DONE, and it is a contradiction in the batch, not an omission. §2 asks for six UNSHIPPED abilities to be added — Disengage, Suppressing Fire and Piercing Arrow for the Sharpshooter, Blight, Smoke Bomb and Field Dressing for the Survivalist. The batch's own first paragraph says "No new abilities are written in this batch", and no costs, damage, mechanics or descriptions were given for any of the six. Authoring them would have been six abilities' worth of undirected design, so the header rule won and the two Hunter pools ship at five entries each. Nothing is blocked by this — the cross-fill rule keeps every offer at three regardless.
  • Each award offers 3 abilities the hero does not own: 1 from its spec pool, 2 from its class pool. Either side fills for the other when its own runs dry, so an offer only shrinks below three once BOTH are nearly exhausted; measured over all twelve specs, six awards a run, every offer stays at three. THE SPEC DRAW LEADS THE OFFER and wears the trophy gold on the Party screen. That is a deliberate departure from the rune picker, which shuffles its triple: there the blindness IS the question, but the two ability pools OVERLAP by design (a spec's own talent grants sit in both), so nothing in the NAME says which pool an entry came from and hiding it would just withhold something the player has earned the right to know. The triple is rolled the moment the award drops and stored on the member (the rune-cache pattern), so re-opening the screen never rerolls it. Storage stays bm_abilities; the new bm_candidates queue is another key on the party dict, so the save stays v5 with no migration, and a run saved before this batch that owes a pick rolls its triple on the spot rather than dead-ending.
  • A SPAWN-ORDERING BUG, found by making abilities earnable. Earned abilities used to be appended AFTER Talents.apply_from_tree. Several talents MODIFY an ability rather than grant one — and Battle Shout is both talent-granted and talent-modified, so a Berserker who bought Deafening Cry and then EARNED Battle Shout from the pool would have had the -1 cooldown silently miss it. Earned abilities now go on BEFORE the tree; apply_from_tree already refuses to double-grant a name it can see, so the talent-bought path is unchanged.
  • ONE GUARANTEED MINI-BOSS PER ZONE, on the middle row. Tier 6 is now the zone's mini-boss and it occupies all three columns, so no route goes around it. It is a combat node between elite and boss: an elite warband carrying a boss-tier health pool — every enemy at ×1.5 max HP, attack untouched, which puts a chief's 250 at 375, in among the two authored bosses at 370 and 500. It pays elite gold (80–100) and 2 talent points, and its own spoil is an ability pick — no consumable, no rune cache, so the rune economy AE and AF measured is left alone. The zone boss now awards an ability pick too, on top of its existing 3 talent points. Two picks a zone, six a run.
  • The map deal absorbs it without touching the run economy. The mini-boss row is AUTHORED, not dealt, so the deck now deals 27 cards into nine tiers — and it is paid for out of the FIGHT cards alone (17 → 14). Rest 5, shop 5 and event 3 are byte-identical, which is the point: a zone trades three ordinary fight OFFERS for one guaranteed hard fight, and the economy dials that drive gold, healing and rune access do not move. The structural constraints are now stated in TIER terms and converted to card slices, so lifting a row out of the deal cannot silently shift a window; a second 27-card authored fallback (DECK_FALLBACK_MB) matches the new composition. Elites still roll at 25% on tiers 6+, which in practice means tiers 7–10 now, with the existing one-elite-per-zone floor unchanged.
  • FLAG: DOD_SIM_MINIBOSS=off reproduces the pre-AH map — ten dealt tiers, the full 17-fight deck, no mini-boss and so no mini-boss award. Shipped content, so it defaults ON and, like the AE and AF flags and unlike AD's experiment arms, it is NOT gated on sim_run. It is an honest control for the MAP half of this batch only: kit sizes still open at three with it off, because the trim is structural and has no switch. Post-AH Matrix rows carry mb=; pre-AH rows do not, so never compare across.
  • The action bar has no cap and no swap step. A hero holds every ability it earns. Abilities 1–9 keep their hotkeys — with G added as the ninth, which the batch's own worked example requires ("ability 10 = Shift+Q" only lands if nine plain keys exist) — and ability 10 onward binds to Shift + the same key in the same order, up to 18 at Shift+G. The button carries the modifier: "[⇧Q] Blood Price". Shift hotkeys route through the same _ability_usable gate and the same two fenced call sites, so they are ignored when the ability is unaffordable or gated and inactive during targeting or a skill check. A real run tops out at core + 3 + 6 = 10 abilities, so exactly one Shift slot is reachable in play; the harness stresses it to eighteen anyway.
  • Eight Perfect skill checks became RELIABILITY checks. In each the Perfect removes a chance roll instead of adding magnitude, and the old bonus is gone: Hack and Slash lands its Bleed on all three strikes (loses the 4th strike); Blizzard puts 2 stacks of Chilled on every enemy instead of 1–2 (loses the 5-Mana refund); Pommel Strike lands its Stun on an unbroken boss (loses the parry buff); Snare Trap the same (loses the extra Poison turns — Poison is a flat 4 either way now); Firestorm spreads its bolts evenly across the living instead of scattering them (loses the extra bolts); Arcane Barrage never strikes the same enemy twice while an unstruck one stands (loses the 7th bolt); Triple Shot pays out one guaranteed critical; and Deadfall gained a skill check it never had so it could have a Perfect at all — a perfect rig lets the player NAME the victim. Wildstrikes was already converted in Batch AG and was left alone.
  • Three implementation notes from that conversion. (1) The two scatter perfects — Firestorm and Arcane Barrage — are ONE mechanic under two framings: deal the target pool round-robin and refill it only once it empties. "Every enemy takes an even share" and "no two bolts strike the same enemy" are the same rule described from different ends. (2) The boss Stun immunity now has exactly one escape, an explicit force argument on _apply_status rather than a name check inside it — so the exception is visible at the call site that bought it, and Freeze, Psychosis, Bewitch and Hysteria are untouched. (3) An AIMED Deadfall waits for its mark, and releases if the mark dies first, so a perfect rig can never be worth less than an ordinary one.
  • A LIVE BUG, exposed by the rule. Triple Shot fired TWO arrows. Its multi_hits was 2 while its name, its description ("Three arrows at one target") and the master document all said three — and because perfect_extra_hit defaults to true and its perfect_text was empty, a Perfect silently added the third with no tooltip anywhere admitting it. Removing the undocumented magnitude perfect is what this batch's rule demands, and doing it would have left an ability called Triple Shot firing two arrows forever. multi_hits is now 3 and the extra hit is off.
  • Two knock-ons the conversion left behind, cleaned up. (1) Swordsmanship read "a perfect Pommel Strike grants +5%/rank more parry chance" — and Pommel Strike's perfect is now the boss Stun. The mechanic was ALREADY shared with Guard Change's perfect, so the node is re-pointed in place: same id (saved ranks migrate), same stat, wording moved to the source that still pays it. (2) The parry_up and mana5 perfect_id handlers had no callers left — Pommel Strike and Blizzard were the only ones — so they are gone. Guard Change applies its own parry buff inline and is unaffected. Nothing in runes.json or the talent trees writes a perfect_id except rage5, so the two removals are provably unreachable rather than probably.
  • Visibility. Owed ability picks badge the map's Party button in the trophy gold and pulse it (rune purple still outranks them), and the Party screen's hero list marks the owed row — the same affordance chain Batch AE built for runes, because a pick left unchosen is a hero walking into the next tier a third weaker than intended. The picker's heading is now "NEW ABILITY — choose one" with the subtitle "one from your spec, two from your class"; the map gains a WARDEN node label in a colour between the elite's orange and the boss's red, and a "Mini-boss" entry in the debug summon menu.
  • VERIFIED. New test_batch_ah.gd: 4,263 checks, 0 failures — every spec's kit counted at three, all 100 pool entries resolved to an Ability, the curation rule asserted rather than trusted (no faith_cost, no summon/Kill Command/Hex of Ruin, no passive-gated special in any class pool), pool copies proven identical to the kit and talent copies they mirror, the offer shape and the six-award sequence checked for all twelve specs, cross-fill and both-pools-dry forced, a talent-learned ability proven un-offerable, and the mini-boss row proven to be exactly one row, on the middle tier, full width, with a forward DP showing no route reaches the boss without crossing it. New test_batch_ah_battle.gd: 41 checks, 0 failures in a spawned battle — an earned class-pool ability reaching the kit, Deafening Cry finding a POOL-bought Battle Shout (the ordering fix), the action bar handing slot 10 its ⇧Q, the boss Stun immunity holding for an ordinary cast and yielding to a forced one through both routes (_apply_status and _spring_trap), Freeze immunity proven untouched by the new argument's default, and mini-boss enemies measured against their own elite selves. Regression: test_runes.gd 3,248/0, test_start_rune.gd 233/0, test_start_rune_ui.gd 31/0, test_run_harness.gd gates 1/2/3 PASS, test_rune_battle.gd 91/1 — the same single failure the unmodified code gives 6 runs out of 6 (a Batch AG Inferno-chip check that reads the chip before any Burn is on the field). That harness needed one fix, and the fix is worth recording: its White Flame check reads a LOG LINE, which made it a race against how long a fight lasts — and trimming the Berserker's kit shortened fights enough that the Pyromancer sometimes never took a turn (0 fire casts in ~50% of runs; restoring Blood Price made it 6/6 again, which is how the cause was pinned). A check that depends on the bot happening to get a turn cannot fail honestly, so the pass now FORCES one fire hit onto a resistant enemy instead of hoping for one: 6/6 stable, and the flake is gone rather than tolerated. Headless parse: all 10 scenes, 0 SCRIPT ERROR.
  • MEASURED (n=100 runs each, route=default, control = mb=off). THE ACQUISITION HALF LANDED: abilities earned per hero per run 1.18 → 3.02 (offers 3.54 → 9.06), and the ceiling of 6 is not the target — the average run only reaches 2.0 mini-bosses and 1.3 zone bosses, so 3.02 is very nearly every award a run actually survives to collect. Talent points 19.1 → 21.0 and gold 711 → 808, both exactly the mini-boss's own payout. Mini-boss nodes taken 2.0 of 2.0 offered: unroutable in practice, not just on paper.
    THE DIFFICULTY HALF DID NOT MOVE, on the metric built to see it: depth 20.15 → 20.49 = +0.34 tiers against a resolvable difference of 3.57 — nowhere near clearing, and remarkable in itself, since the treatment fights two extra hard battles a run to reach the same place. ratio@z1t8 1.00 → 0.95, flat. Wipe median moved z2 t8 → z2 t10, deeper.
    REPORTED, NOT ACTED ON — the one row that disagrees. Completions read 9% → 0%, which nominally clears its own 8.2-point threshold (z=3.07). It is recorded rather than believed, for two reasons stated together: (a) Batch AE's noise calibration measured 7% and 14% from two identical halves of one arm, so a 9-point completion swing is inside this instrument's known noise, and (b) an earlier n=100 pass over the same code — discarded because two background jobs wrote the same file and corrupted it — produced completion rows of 12% and 4%. Depth is the low-variance metric and depth says nothing moved.
    ROUTE AGENCY IS THE ONE REAL COST, and it is by design: steps offering a genuine choice 77% → 71%, and rests taken 2.3 → 1.9. A row with one node type in all three columns is a row with no decision in it — that is what "cannot be routed around" buys, and one tier in eleven is the price. Fights taken fall 14.4 → 12.7 and elites 1.1 → 0.9, both the arithmetic of three fight cards leaving the deck.
    PURITY: profile.json and relics.json byte-identical across both arms; run_save.bin never created.

2026-08-05 — Batch AG: combat tuning — reliability, Burn turns, and the tempo of self-buffs

  • Wildstrikes trades magnitude for reliability. The sweep had no bleed_chance, so it defaulted to 1.0 and put a guaranteed 35 Bleed on every enemy — 140 buildup across a four-wide field, every cast, with no roll to lose. It now carries bleed_chance 0.5 like Hack and Slash, and the Perfect changed what it buys: instead of +50% buildup on every target it now guarantees the roll on all of them (four × 35, no bonus). The skill check is a reliability check now, not a magnitude one — which is what a Perfect on a wide, swingy ability should be. The per-target roll already lived in the strike loop; the Perfect simply treats the chance as 1.0 for the cast.
  • Inferno Master counts Burn TURNS, not burning heads. The passive read the number of enemies alight, which meant a single enemy burning for six turns was worth exactly as much as one burning for one, and the Pyromancer's own build-the-fire loop (Flamewave extensions, Conflagration, Accelerant) fed it nothing. It now reads the total Burn turns standing on the enemy team: step = 1.0 + 0.2 × Pyromaniac ranks percent per turn, cap = 25 × step + 10 × Heat Haze ranks percent. Ceilings: +25% base, +40% at Pyromaniac 3, +70% with Heat Haze 3 on top (was 64%). Pyromaniac now raises the cap along with the step — the old node bought a deeper step against a fixed ceiling. Avatar of Flame still removes the cap and still burns through fire resistance.
  • Consumption ordering, which was a live bug. Detonation removed its target's Burn before the passive block ran, so the cast that spent the field was paid on the field it had already emptied. Both Detonation and the reworked Wildfire now measure the total before their own consumption: the consuming cast gets full credit, and only subsequent turns see the thinner field.
  • Wildfire is the wide payoff now. The old version copied one target's Burn to everyone at half duration — a setup tool that made the Pyromancer's own Detonation worse by diluting the deep fire he was building. It is now a special with no target selection: 20 Mana, 3cd, 2.5 initiative, 10 BD, consuming one turn of Burn from every burning enemy, each taking 18% of Attack in fire for it. An enemy on its last turn simply loses its Burn; enemies that are not burning are untouched. Perfect takes two turns from each, dealing the damage twice to anyone holding 2+. Detonation is unchanged — the two now ask different questions of the same field (one deep fire, or a wide one).
  • Wildfire cannot be cast into an empty field, on the same rule as Shatter: with nothing alight the ability does literally nothing, so it is gated out of the menu rather than eating 20 Mana and a turn. The autoplay/sim pyromancer loop was retargeted with it — Flamewave builds, Wildfire harvests at 3+ burning, Detonation still cashes the deepest single fire.
  • Battle Shout is a party-wide warcry. It was a self-buff scaling off the enemy party's bloodloss, which meant it read as a warcry and behaved as a solo cooldown — and at low buildup it was worth nearly nothing. Power is now 8 + (total enemy bleed buildup / 20) and it lands on every living hero (companions excluded — the beast's damage runs through its own path). Duration 2 turns and the +5 Rage Perfect are unchanged; Deafening Cry still takes a turn off its cooldown. The damage clause already read the status per unit, so it works party-wide untouched.
  • Razor Ice: damage 20 → 15, cost 20 → 25. Three shards, 3 Chilled stacks, 3cd and the 25%-of-Attack Perfect all unchanged. This is the first cut against the Cryomancer overtune Batch S identified and Batch U confirmed at the honest floor (38–40% damage share across every budget and every routing policy) — his numbers, not his AoE.
  • Self-buff initiative costs cut 0.5 (floor 1.5). Buffing yourself or the party costs a turn and the tempo of a long initiative delay, and the double charge was pushing whole categories of ability out of real rotations. Applied to the fifteen named: Blood Price, Battle Shout, Shieldwall, Flame Shield, Stabilize and Spirit Bond → 1.5; Interpose and Blessing of Zeal → 2.0; Divine Shield, Sacred Resolve and Hunter's Instinct → 2.5; Consecrated Ground, Bulwark of Fortitude and Hold the Line → 3.0; Bestial Wrath → 3.5.
  • The sweep for unlisted abilities matching the rule (a special handler, damage: 0, no healing, no enemy target) found five: Quick Draw and Overcharge (both named in advance) and Hold Breath → 1.5, Tripwire → 2.0, Hold the Line → 3.0. Judged out, and why: Deadfall, Snare Trap and Mass Hysteria are pointed at the enemy team even though they need no target pick; Dark Pact heals; the three Summons field a unit rather than buff anyone, and Aguila takes an enemy target, so including them would have split the trio; Guard Change already sits at the 1.5 floor. Heals were excluded by the rule — Heal, Renewal, Hymn of Hope, Divine Plea and Resurrection keep their delays.
  • Bug: Call of the Wild permanently locked a Lone Bond hunter out of summoning. Call of the Wild writes kinds_summoned[kind] = true for all three beasts as bookkeeping for Feral Momentum and Menagerie. The Lone Bond gate in _ability_usable read not kinds_summoned.is_empty() as "you have spent your one beast" — so a single Call of the Wild marked all three kinds and closed every summon for the rest of the fight. Fix: a separate beast_committed flag on BattleUnit, set only in _do_summon (a real summon), and the gate reads that. kinds_summoned is untouched — Feral Momentum and Menagerie keep reading it and Call of the Wild keeps writing it. The AI path goes through _ability_usable, so autoplay and the sims inherit the fix.
  • Verified. Headless parse clean on all four touched scripts; 40-battle sims on the standard party and on a pyromancer party — 0 SCRIPT ERRORs, Wildfire firing 0.8×/battle through the new handler. Autoplay log checks confirm the Wildstrikes Perfect landing 35 (not 52) on all four targets, and Wildfire tearing 1 turn from 6 enemies for 101 and 2 turns from 5 for 96 on a Perfect.

2026-08-04 — Batch AF: the opening pick offers a rune for your spec

  • Why — the number that prompted it. Batch AE shipped the starting rune and measured it delivering 0.49 spec runes worn per hero against the 1.18 projected. AE's own diagnosis found the cause and it was not the lever: the ordinary roller put a spec-scoped rune among the three only 36–42% of the time, and the sim's policy — which already prefers a spec candidate — took one at exactly that rate, i.e. whenever one was there. The ceiling was the roller's hit rate, not the policy's. A player sits under the same ceiling, and the opening pick is the most visible gear decision in a run. This batch raises the offer rate and changes nothing else.
  • Guarantee, not weighting — and that was the design choice. The opening triple always contains one spec-scoped candidate where the hero's spec pool has an eligible entry; the other two roll normally. A weighting nudges a probability and leaves the outcome mushy. A guarantee makes the opening pick a reliable question — do I take the rune written for my spec, or the generic one that is stronger right now? — and that question can only be asked if it is always on the table. One candidate, not two: a triple of spec runes is not a question, it is a menu.
  • Only the opening pick. Run.roll_rune_candidates is shared with the elite cache, so the guarantee is an opt-in parameter defaulted off and exactly one caller arms it. The elite cache and every other caller produce identical rolls. This is asserted, not assumed — the test seeds the global RNG and replays a verbatim copy of the pre-AF loop against the default path, because "it looks the same" proves nothing about a random roll, and it re-checks the call sites so a future batch cannot quietly arm it.
  • What the guaranteed candidate is. A normal roll within the spec-scoped subset — same rarity roll on the zone slot, same widen-on-exhaustion — not a forced Epic. Measured over 600 rolls per spec, the four specs that own an Epic draw it ~25% of the time, which is what an unconstrained draw over their four gives. The three candidates stay distinct, and the guaranteed one is shuffled into a random slot so its position is not a tell. Fallback, silent and safe: if the spec subset is empty — an unmet requires_ability, an exhausted set — the pick falls back to an ordinary roll of three. No error, no empty slot, no half-filled triple.
  • What this batch is not. Not a magnitude pass — runes.json is byte-unchanged for the third batch running, and that is the intent, not an accident. The designer has closed the rune-magnitude question; the six magnitude-proof entries Batch AE catalogued are left exactly as they are. No change to the elite cache, the shop roll or any other rune source. No second acquisition lever. No sim policy change — _pick_rune_candidate already preferred a spec candidate, which is precisely why raising the offer rate is the whole intervention.
  • Measured — the acquisition half, and it is near-deterministic. Fixed party, n=200 per row, control is specopen=off (AE's opening with the starting rune still on, so the pair isolates this change rather than re-measuring AE).
    Offer rate 41% → 100%, with ZERO fallbacks across 800 opening triples — no spec hit the fallback path, which is expected: all twelve specs have four entries and the only gates on them are core kit abilities.
    Spec runes worn per hero at run end: 0.56 → 1.15 (AE measured 0.49; the control reproduces it). The pick was spec-scoped 100% of the time against the control's 41% — the policy's rate tracks the offer rate exactly, which is AE's diagnosis confirmed from the other side.
    The finding worth keeping: this is a COMPOSITION change, not an acquisition-volume one. Runes acquired per hero barely moved (1.62 → 1.67) and slots filled barely moved (1.58 → 1.64 of 2.7–2.8 available, 59% → 58%). What changed is what fills them — spec 0.56 → 1.15 while class 0.16 → 0.10, universal 0.32 → 0.16 and stat sticks 0.54 → 0.23. The party does not wear more runes; it wears authored spec content where it used to wear filler.
  • Measured — the difficulty half, reported as information. There is no gate to fail here and no target to hit; nothing in this batch is conditional on the number. Depth 15.89 → 17.14 = +1.25 tiers against a resolvable difference of 2.72 (n=200, 80% power) — it does not clear, and is reported as movement inside noise, not as an effect. Completions 7% → 6% (resolvable 6.9 pts), ratio@z1t8 0.97 → 0.98, wipe median identical at z1 t11.0. Consistent with Batch AD's and AE's central claim that acquisition alone moves nothing detectable — and the composition finding above explains why: the party wears about the same number of runes, just better-targeted ones. Nothing was compensated, because there is nothing measurable to compensate.
  • Reported, not acted on. No spec rune in the pool is Common — all 44 are Rare plus 4 Epics. So inside the spec subset the zone-slot-1 Common lean has almost nothing to bind on, and the guaranteed slot is always Rare-or-better where it used to be ~60% Common. "The opening gift stays modest" is delivered by the pool's own composition rather than by the rarity weighting; a designer who wants the opening gift smaller would author Common spec entries, not re-weight the roll. Also still outstanding: treasure /Loot, untouched since Batch AC, six batches.
  • Flag and Matrix rows. DOD_SIM_SPEC_OPENING=off reproduces AE's opening while leaving the starting rune itself ON. Like the AE flag and unlike Batch AD's two arms it is shipped content, so it is on by default and not gated on sim_run — a control a real build cannot reach is a control nobody can reproduce. Post-AF Matrix rows carry specopen=; pre-AF rows do not and are not comparable.
